source.text: Legends of Localization is an examination of the cultural influences and differences that affect Japanese and English games. This book is an educational, history-focused exploration of the Undertale video game, but this book is not official Undertale merchandise in any form.

translation.text: Legends of Localization 探讨影响日语与英语游戏的文化因素及差异。本书以教育和历史为出发点，研究电子游戏 Undertale，但并非任何形式的 Undertale 官方商品。

source.text: Certain portions of this book’s content (and the localization information on many other games) is freely available online at: http://LegendsOfLocalization.com

translation.text:

source.text: Introduction

translation.text: 引言

source.text: Introduction

translation.text: 引言

source.text: Have you ever played a video game, watched a movie, or read a book and wondered what it was like in its original language? Or have you ever wondered how your favorite game, movie, or book sounds in a different language? Welcome to the world of Legends of Localization!

translation.text: 你有没有在玩游戏、看电影或读书时，好奇过作品在原文里是什么样的？有没有想过，自己喜欢的游戏、电影或书换一种语言，会是什么感觉？欢迎来到《Legends of Localization》的世界！

source.text: In this book, we'll take a detailed look at the popular American video game known as Undertale. We'll compare the original English version of the game with its official Japanese release. We'll also look at some of the translation challenges involved, and the solutions that were used to overcome them.

translation.text: 本书将详细介绍广受欢迎的美国游戏 Undertale，比较它的英语原版与官方日语版，看看翻译中遇到了哪些难题，又是怎样解决的。

source.text: Along the way, we'll examine other related topics, such as:

translation.text: 我们还会讨论一些相关话题，例如：

source.text: What "localization" is and how it differs from translation Undertale's history and the inspirations behind the game Undertale's localization process as seen from the inside Common problems and mistakes in entertainment localization How culture and language shape a game's localization and vice-versa How unofficial, volunteer-made localizations and official localizations interact, how they differ, and what they mean to fans

translation.text:
• 什么是“本地化”，它与翻译有什么不同
• Undertale 的历史与创作灵感
• Undertale 本地化的幕后过程
• 娱乐作品本地化中常见的问题与错误
• 文化、语言与游戏本地化之间的相互影响
• 志愿者制作的非官方译版与官方译版如何互动、有何不同，又对爱好者意味着什么

source.text: Some of this might sound like dry, boring academic material, but don't worry - it'll be a genuinely fun and enlightening journey. After all, how do bad knock knock jokes and skeleton puns even work in Japanese? Do they just get lost in translation? Let's find out!

translation.text: 有些话题听起来或许像枯燥的学术材料，不过别担心，读起来其实既有趣，又能让人长见识。那些蹩脚的敲门笑话和骷髅双关，到了日语里还能成立吗？还是会在翻译中丢失笑点？一起看看吧！

source.text: Newcomers Welcome

translation.text: 欢迎新读者

source.text: Although this book analyzes the English and Japanese versions of Undertale and touches on topics that will surely delight Undertale fans, it's also been designed with general audiences in mind. Everything in this book is explained in clear, simple English for readers who know nothing about Undertale, video games, the Japanese language, or translation.

translation.text: 本书分析 Undertale 的英日版本，也会谈到爱好者感兴趣的话题，但写作时同样考虑了普通读者。书中所有内容都用清楚易懂的英语讲解，即使不了解 Undertale、电子游戏、日语或翻译，也能读懂。

source.text: Basically, whatever your background is, you'll come away from this book with a deeper understanding of language, culture, and translation.

translation.text: 无论你有怎样的背景，读完后都能对语言、文化和翻译有更深的了解。

source.text: If you don't know the first thing about games, translation, Japanese, or Undertale, no worries!

translation.text: 就算你对游戏、翻译、日语或 Undertale 一窍不通，也不用担心！

source.text: Concerning Spoilers

translation.text: 关于剧透

source.text: Undertale is full of surprises, branching story routes, and endings. Every playthrough feels unique and memorable - especially your first one. For this reason, spoilers can greatly affect the gameplay experience.

translation.text: Undertale 充满惊喜、故事分支和不同结局。每次游玩都有独特而难忘的体验，第一次尤其如此。因此，剧透会大大影响游玩体验。

source.text: If you're already an Undertale fan, then you're probably familiar with the story's many twists. But if you've never played it before and plan to someday, keep in mind that portions of this book will naturally contain spoilers.

translation.text: 如果你已经是 Undertale 的爱好者，想必熟悉故事的种种转折。但如果你还没玩过，打算今后体验，就要注意：本书有些内容难免涉及剧透。

source.text: Although this book wasn't designed as a gameplay supplement, you probably could read through it as you play the game. Who knows, it could even add a new perspective to the gameplay experience!

translation.text: 本书原本并不是供游玩时配合阅读的，不过你也可以试着边玩边读。说不定，还会让你从新的角度体验游戏！

source.text: About Me

translation.text: 关于我

source.text: My name is Clyde Mandelin, but I'm more commonly known on line as "Tomato" or just "Mato". I'm a professional Japanese-to-English translator and have been in the industry for about twenty years. I specialize in translating Japanese movies, anime, games, and other entertainment into English.

translation.text: 我叫 Clyde Mandelin，不过大家在网上更熟悉的名字是“Tomato”，或简称“Mato”。我是一名职业日译英译者，从业约二十年，主要将日本电影、动画、游戏及其他娱乐作品译成英语。

source.text: During my journey to become a professional translator, I studied Japanese-to English translation in university, in Japan, and on my own as a hobby. As part of my hobby study, I translated old Japanese games that had never been released in English. In short, translation has been a major part of my personal life and professional life for decades.

translation.text: 在成为职业译者的过程中，我在大学、在日本，以及作为业余爱好自学过日译英。业余学习的一部分，是翻译从未推出英语版的日本老游戏。可以说，几十年来，翻译一直是我生活和工作的主要部分。

source.text: Several years ago, I started Legends of Localization, a website and a book series dedicated to explaining how popular games and movies change during the jump between languages. I've also written books about the history of bad video game translation and what happens when you try to let a computer translate an entire video game on its own.

translation.text: 几年前，我创办了 Legends of Localization 网站和同名书系，介绍热门游戏、电影跨越语言时会发生什么变化。我还写过关于糟糕游戏翻译的历史，以及把整款游戏交给电脑自行翻译会发生什么的书。

source.text: Basically, I just really like translation and showing how the translation process works. Naturally, this detailed look at Undertale's Japanese translation is another passion project for me.

translation.text: 我就是很喜欢翻译，也很喜欢向大家展示翻译的过程。如此细看 Undertale 的日语翻译，自然又是一个出于热爱的项目。

source.text: From time to time, I'll share my thoughts and insights about Undertale, localization, business experiences, personal experiences, and so on. So keep your eyes out for the little tomato! Well, not literally "out". That would be weird.

translation.text: 我会不时分享自己对 Undertale、本地化的想法，以及工作和生活中的经历。所以，请留意那颗小番茄！英语里叫 keep your eyes out，可别真把眼睛“拿出来”，那也太奇怪了。

source.text: As a professional, I translate and localize all types and genres of Japanese entertainment into English. Each project is fun, unique, and educational!

translation.text: 工作中，我把各种类型、各种题材的日本娱乐作品译成英语并做本地化。每个项目都独特、有趣，也能学到东西！

source.text: And as a hobby, I sometimes create unofficial translations of classic games never released outside of Japan

translation.text: 业余时，我偶尔会为从未在日本以外发行的经典游戏制作非官方译版。

source.text: Introduction

translation.text: 引言

source.text: A Rare Opportunity

translation.text: 难得的机会

source.text: Because I specialize in Japanese-to-English translation, I usually write about how games are translated from Japanese into English. But Undertale gives us a chance to look at the opposite side of things: how English games are translated into Japanese.

translation.text: 我专做日译英，平时写的大多是日本游戏如何译成英语。不过，Undertale 让我们有机会从另一面看看：英语游戏如何译成日语。

source.text: In Legends of Localization Book 1, we looked at how the original Legend of Zelda was translated into English. There was one key issue, though - the game is so old that nobody remembers who the actual translator was or how the game's translation process worked. As a result, we could see how things changed in translation, but there was no way to ask why.

translation.text: 在《Legends of Localization》第1卷，我们研究了初代《The Legend of Zelda》如何译成英语。不过有个关键问题：游戏太老，已经没人记得究竟是谁翻译的，也没人记得翻译是怎么进行的。因此，我们看得见翻译改了什么，却无从追问为什么。

source.text: In Legends of Localization Book 2, we looked at how the classic game EarthBound was translated into English. Luckily, through personal connections and friendships, I was able to ask the game's creator and the game's head localizer a handful of questions. Given that EarthBound was twenty years old by then, I was thankful to receive any kind of inside information at all.

translation.text: 在第2卷，我们研究了经典游戏 EarthBound 如何译成英语。幸运的是，通过私人关系和朋友帮忙，我得以向游戏创作者和本地化负责人提几个问题。那时 EarthBound 已问世二十年，能得到任何内部信息，我都十分感激。

source.text: Now, in Book 3, we'll see how Undertale was translated into Japanese. But this time, I have an unparalleled amount of inside access. I've been friends with the game's creator for years, and I've worked alongside the translation staff in the past. I was even brought on as a consultant during the game's Japanese translation. In other words, I can share firsthand and secondhand knowledge about Undertale's translation process, as well as details about the original game itself that have never seen the light of day.

translation.text: 如今到了第3卷，我们将看看 Undertale 如何译成日语。这次，我能接触到前所未有的内部资料。我与游戏创作者相识多年，也曾与翻译人员共事；游戏翻译成日语时，我还受邀担任顾问。也就是说，我可以分享 Undertale 翻译过程的一手、二手信息，以及原版游戏中从未公开过的细节。

source.text: In short, Undertale offers us a rare opportunity to see how English-to .Japanese game translation works, and in unprecedented detail. So when the game's creator suggested I write a Legends of Localization book about the Japanese version of Undertale, I jumped at the chance.

translation.text: 总之，Undertale 给了我们一个难得的机会，以前所未有的细致程度了解游戏英译日的过程。因此，当游戏创作者提议让我写一本介绍 Undertale 日语版的《Legends of Localization》时，我立刻就答应了。

source.text: The older a game gets, the harder it is to document its past. So being right there during Undertale's localization was like watching history happen!

translation.text: 游戏越老，过去就越难考证。亲身参与 Undertale 的本地化，就像看着历史发生！

source.text: My book about EarthBound ended up around 420 pages long. This Undertale book is a bit shorter, but could've easily been double the size!

translation.text: 我写 EarthBound 的那本书最终约有420页。这本 Undertale 稍短一些，但要再写一倍也不难！

source.text: I'm listed in ~ Undertale's credits under "Localization Support", and I did help with stuff, but I'd say my role was pretty minor overall

translation.text: Undertale 的制作名单把我列在“本地化支持”一栏。我确实帮了些忙，不过总体而言，我的作用相当有限。

source.text: Around the World

translation.text: 走向世界

source.text: As of the writing of this book, Undertale has only been officially translated into one language: Japanese. Even so, the game's inherent appeal, together with fan made translations into other languages, has helped Undertale grow from a tiny indie game into a global phenomenon.

translation.text: 截至本书写作时，Undertale 官方只推出过一种语言的译版：日语。不过，游戏本身的魅力，加上玩家制作的其他语言译版，帮助 Undertale 从小小的独立游戏成长为风靡世界的作品。

source.text: With this in mind, it's important to note that even though we'll be focusing on the English and Japanese versions of Undertale in this book, it's only one small view of a much larger picture. Undertale's popularity reaches far beyond these two languages.

translation.text: 因此请记住：本书虽然着重讨论 Undertale 的英语版与日语版，所见也只是更大图景中的一角。Undertale 的流行远远超出了这两种语言。

source.text: LEFT: Undertale on the cover of a Swedish video game magazine

translation.text: 左：Undertale 登上瑞典游戏杂志封面。

source.text: RIGHT: Undertale is insanely popular in Korea, where fans created and inserted their own translation into the game

translation.text: 右：Undertale 在韩国极受欢迎，玩家自行翻译，并将译文植入游戏。

source.text: Cartoon Network Latin America created and aired Undertale themed episodes of ToonTubers in Spanish and Portuguese

translation.text: Cartoon Network 拉丁美洲频道制作并播出了西班牙语、葡萄牙语的 Undertale 主题《ToonTubers》节目。

source.text: Arabic-speaking fans share videos and translation walkthroughs with hundreds of thousands of views each

translation.text: 阿拉伯语玩家分享的视频和翻译解说，各有数十万次观看。

source.text: Introduction

translation.text: 引言

source.text: What is Localization?

translation.text: 什么是本地化？

source.text: What is Localization?

translation.text: 什么是本地化？

source.text: Before we dive into Undertale's English-to-Japanese localization, there's one big question that needs answering: what exactly is localization, anyway?

translation.text: 在深入探讨 Undertale 的英译日本地化之前，先得回答一个大问题：本地化究竟是什么？

source.text: The word "localization" is actually relatively new in the translation world, so different people use it to mean different things. Here's how I would define it in simple terms, though:

translation.text: “本地化”在翻译界其实还是个相对年轻的词，不同的人用它表达不同的意思。简单来说，我会这样定义：

source.text: Basically, localization is translation. Localization just changes things a bit when a literal translation doesn't quite work.

translation.text: 本地化说到底就是翻译，只是在直译行不通的时候，稍微改动一下。

source.text: If you're unfamiliar with translation, this idea probably sounds odd at first. Why should anything be changed at all? Shouldn't a literal translation work all the time? Let's find out.

translation.text: 如果你不熟悉翻译，乍听之下可能觉得奇怪。为什么要改？难道不是任何时候都能直译吗？我们来看看。

source.text: Getting Literal

translation.text: 只按字面理解

source.text: Imagine you're talking to a grumpy genie who takes everything literally. You want to be rich, so you immediately wish to be "made of money". Unfortunately, instead of becoming rich, you transform into a pile of coins. Oops, that's not what you meant at all!

translation.text: 设想你遇到一个暴躁、凡事照字面理解的精灵。你想发财，立刻许愿让自己 made of money（富得流油，字面为“由钱构成”）。结果却变成了一堆硬币。哎呀，这可不是你想要的！

source.text: "Ugh, whatever! I just wish I had lots of dough!" you somehow say. You expect to become rich for sure this time, but instead, you suddenly find yourself covered in bread dough. Oops again!

translation.text: “唉，随便吧！我只想要一大堆 dough！”不知怎么，你又开口了。dough 可以指“钱”，也可以指“面团”。你以为这次总该发财了，结果浑身糊满了面团。又糟了！

source.text: These examples, as ridiculous as they are, show how a literal interpretation can completely miss the point of what's being said.

translation.text: 这些例子虽然荒唐，却说明了按字面理解可以完全错过说话人的意思。

source.text: When we communicate, words are our tools. They're like paintbrushes that we use to paint pictures for others to see. The problem is that if you focus too hard on someone's tools, you risk missing the full picture of what they're actually saying.

translation.text: 交流时，词语是我们的工具，好比画笔，用来画出图景让别人看见。问题在于，如果你一味盯着别人的工具，就可能看不见他们真正想表达的整幅图景。

source.text: Literal translation can • have hilarious side effects. In this scene, the English sentence "this work is killing me" was translated literally into Japanese as "this work of art is murdering me" (Game: Girls and Quiz)

translation.text: 直译可能产生滑稽的副作用。这里的“this work is killing me”（这工作快累死我了）被直译成日语，成了“这件艺术品正在杀我”。（游戏：Girls and Quiz）

source.text: A literal translation can miss the original, intended meaning, which would have been "Make sure the stove is turned off!" in this example (Game: Harvest Moon)

translation.text: 直译可能错过原文真正的意思。这里原本想说的是“确认炉子已经关掉！”（游戏：Harvest Moon）

source.text: Even advanced machine translations tend to miss what's being said by translating too literally. A better translation of this Japanese idiom might've been "Quit loafing around here!" (Game: Final Fantasy IV machine translation experiment)

translation.text: 即使先进的机器翻译也常因过于字面而误解意思。这句日语惯用语更适合译成“别在这里磨蹭了！”（游戏：Final Fantasy IV 机器翻译实验）

source.text: Literal translations can sometimes end up feeling "off" or incomplete (Game: Fate/Grand Order)

translation.text: 直译有时会让人觉得“不对劲”，或像是话没说完。（游戏：Fate/Grand Order）

source.text: Literal translations can still sound like a foreign language despite being translated (Game: Kitty Love)

translation.text: 即便已经译过，直译读起来也可能仍像外语。（游戏：Kitty Love）

source.text: What is Localization?

translation.text: 什么是本地化？

source.text: The Need for Localization

translation.text: 为什么需要本地化

source.text: Every language has its own unique rules and quirks. Every culture has its own unique values and expectations. Because of this, not every word has a perfect, 1-to-l equivalent in other languages. So when a straightforward, literal translation isn't possible, one alternative is to use completely different words to say the same thing. And that's precisely what localization is: preserving the creator's intended meaning but with completely different words. As the acclaimed translator John Ciardi once put it:

translation.text: 每种语言都有自己的规则和特点，每种文化也有自己的价值观和预期。因此，并不是每个词都能在另一种语言中找到一一对应的词。无法直接照字面翻译时，一种办法就是换一套完全不同的说法，表达同样的意思。这正是本地化：用完全不同的词，保留创作者想表达的意思。正如著名译者 John Ciardi 所说：

source.text: '' When the violin repeats what the piano has just played, it cannot make the same sounds and it can only approximate the same chords. It can, however, make recognizably the same "music," the same air. But it can do so only when it is as faithful to the self logic of the violin as it is to the self logic of the piano.

translation.text: 小提琴重复钢琴刚弹过的旋律时，发不出同样的声音，和弦也只能近似。不过，它仍能奏出听得出是同一段的“音乐”、同一支曲调。但要做到这一点，它既要忠实于钢琴自身的逻辑，也要同样忠实于小提琴自身的逻辑。

source.text: In short, languages are weird, messy, and complicated. It's easy for people to misunderstand each other in one language, so translating between two can sometimes be impossible. In this chapter, we'll examine a few situations in which straightforward, literal translations don't quite work.

translation.text: 总之，语言古怪、杂乱而复杂。用同一种语言，人们都容易误解彼此；在两种语言之间翻译，有时甚至是不可能的任务。本章将介绍一些直接照字面翻译不太行得通的情形。

source.text: Humor

translation.text: 笑点

source.text: There's a famous joke in English that goes:

translation.text: 英语里有个著名的笑话：

source.text: Why was 6 afraid of 7? Because 7 8 9!

translation.text:
Why was 6 afraid of 7? Because 7 8 9!
6为什么怕7？因为7把9吃了！

source.text: Of course, this joke only works because the number "8" and the word "ate" share the same pronunciation in English. This isn't necessarily true in other languages, so a literal translation of the joke might sound like this:

translation.text: 这个笑话能成立，是因为英语里的数字“8”（eight）与“吃了”（ate）同音。其他语言未必如此，所以直译出来可能变成：

source.text: Why was the sixth digit afraid of the seventh digit? Because seventh digit eighth digit ninth digit!

translation.text: 第六个数字为什么怕第七个数字？因为第七个数字、第八个数字、第九个数字！

source.text: As we can see, the result is meaningless nonsense that loses the original intention entirely. The joke is lost in translation.

translation.text: 结果成了毫无意义的胡话，原本的用意完全丢失了。笑话就这样消失在翻译中。

source.text: Similarly, consider this Japanese joke:

translation.text: 再看一个日语笑话：

source.text: ashi nihon aru kara nihonjin da

translation.text:
ashi nihon aru kara nihonjin da
我有两条腿，所以我是日本人。

source.text: This joke, translated literally, means "I have two legs, so I'm Japanese". Even though it's an incredibly simple, straightforward joke in Japanese, we can see how it makes zero sense when translated into English.

translation.text: 直译就是“我有两条腿，所以我是日本人”（“两条”和“日本”都读 nihon）。它在日语里是很简单直接的笑话，译成英语却完全莫名其妙。

source.text: In short, humor rarely translates easily between languages.

translation.text: 总之，笑点很少能轻易跨越语言。

source.text: So, as a translator, what do you do when you run into an untranslatable joke? The most common solution is to take out the original joke and replace it with a similar joke that works in the target language. And that's precisely what localization is all about: retaining the original intent even if it means changing the original words.

translation.text: 那么，译者遇到译不过去的笑话该怎么办？最常见的做法，是撤下原来的笑话，换上目标语言里能讲通的类似笑话。这正是本地化的要点：即使得改换原词，也要保留原本的用意。

source.text: "The other day, someone mistook the word 'hospital' for 'hair salon' and asked for a shampoo and haircut. We speak in hiragana, so I guess that sort of thing is bound to happen sometimes."

translation.text: “前几天，有人把‘医院’听成了‘理发店’，要求洗头、剪发。我们说的都是平假名，想来偶尔会有这种误会吧。”

source.text: "One person requested a 'shampoo and cut.' They must have thought that a 'bad hair day' could be treated at the hospital. Either that or they wanted their medical insurance to cover their grooming."

translation.text: “有人来要求‘洗头剪发’。他准以为医院能治‘头发糟透了的一天’。要不就是想让医疗保险替他报销理发费。”

source.text: ~ The original joke in this scene only makes sense if you understand how the Japanese language works. Because a literal translation wouldn't make sense to most players outside of Japan, the joke was replaced with a different, but similarly-themed joke in English (Game: EarthBound)

translation.text: 原来的笑话只有了解日语的人才懂。直译会让日本以外的大多数玩家摸不着头脑，因此英语版换成了另一个主题相近的笑话。（游戏：EarthBound）

source.text: This imprisoned character plays with the Japanese words for "prison cell" and "candle" to make a simple joke. The translators replaced this untranslatable wordplay with a different prison-themed joke that makes sense in English (Game: The Legend of the Mystical Ninja)

translation.text: 这个被关起来的人用日语里“牢房”和“蜡烛”的读音玩了个简单的文字游戏。译者把这个译不过去的双关换成了英语能讲通的另一个监狱笑话。（游戏：The Legend of the Mystical Ninja）

source.text: ~ This Japanese pun on the words for "go bald" and "encouragement" was replaced with an English pun on the word "scalping" (Game: Yakuza 0)

translation.text: 日语中“秃头”与“鼓励”的双关，被换成英语 scalping（剥头皮）一词的双关。（游戏：Yakuza 0）

source.text: What is Localization?

translation.text: 什么是本地化？

pages.title: 惯用语、谚语与多层含义

source.text: Idioms, Proverbs, and Multi-Layered Phrases

translation.text: 惯用语、谚语与多层含义

source.text: Every language has its own unique set of colorful phrases that have a literal meaning and a functional meaning. For example, the English phrase "I'm in a pickle" literally means "I am inside of a pickle" but functionally means "I'm in a difficult situation".

translation.text: 每种语言都有一套生动的说法，既有字面意思，也有实际含义。例如英语 I’m in a pickle，字面是“我在一根酸黄瓜里”，实际却是“我陷入了困境”。

source.text: These problematic, multi-layered phrases come in all types. Idioms, for example, are notorious for having very different literal and functional meanings:

translation.text: 这种棘手的多层表达有很多种。惯用语的字面意思与实际含义往往相差很远，就是出了名的例子：

source.text: Imagine this title being translated literally - it'd still be kind of silly to see this weird guy in a pickle suit, but the reason for the suit would be lost

translation.text: 想象一下把这个标题照字面翻译。看到这怪人穿着酸黄瓜服，或许仍觉得好笑，却不知道他为什么这样穿。

source.text: Japanese idiom: nodo kara te ga deru Literal meaning: to have your hand coming out of your mouth Functional meaning: to want something very much

translation.text:
• 日语惯用语：nodo kara te ga deru
字面意思：手从嘴里伸出来
实际含义：非常想要某样东西

source.text: Finnish idiom: heittää lusikka nurkkaan Literal meaning: to throw the spoon in the corner Functional meaning: to die

translation.text:
• 芬兰语惯用语：heittää lusikka nurkkaan
字面意思：把勺子扔到角落
实际含义：死去

source.text: Proverbs are another source of tricky phrases with multiple meanings:

translation.text: 谚语也是这种棘手的多义表达的来源：

source.text: German proverb: Morgenstund hat Gold im Mund Literal meaning: the morning hour has gold in the mouth Functional meaning: early risers get the best opportunities

translation.text:
• 德语谚语：Morgenstund hat Gold im Mund
字面意思：早晨嘴里有黄金
实际含义：早起的人能得到最好的机会

source.text: Japanese proverb: hiza to mo dangō Literal meaning: consult even your knees Functional meaning: consulting others can be unexpectedly useful

translation.text:
• 日语谚语：hiza to mo dangō
字面意思：连自己的膝盖也不妨商量一下
实际含义：向别人请教，可能意外地有用

source.text: Slang, jargon, and other multi-layered phrases provide a similar challenge for translators:

translation.text: 俚语、行话和其他多层表达，也给译者带来类似的难题：

source.text: Japanese slang: denpa Literal meaning: electromagnetic wave Functional meaning: a person with a wildly incoherent and delusional mindset

translation.text:
• 日语俚语：denpa
字面意思：电磁波
实际含义：想法极度混乱、充满妄想的人

source.text: Choctaw phrase: oka mali hashi akuchaka itintakla Literal meaning: head towards water wind while heading towards the sun’s home Functional meaning: southeast

translation.text:
• 乔克托语短语：oka mali hashi akuchaka itintakla
字面意思：朝着水风，同时朝着太阳的家前进
实际含义：东南方

source.text: As we can see, idioms, proverbs, and other multi-layered phrases are rarely meant to be taken literally, so it doesn't always make sense to translate them literally. Instead, it's usually more helpful to focus on preserving their functional meanings, even if it means ignoring their literal wordings.

translation.text: 可见，惯用语、谚语等多层表达很少是让人按字面理解的，因此照字面翻译未必合理。通常，着重保留实际含义更有帮助，即使这意味着放下原来的字面措辞。

source.text: ~ The Japanese phrase "to drink the brewed dirt from under XX's fingernails" sounds bizarre when translated literally, but functionally means "to take a lesson from XX" (Game: Refreshing Sideways Puzzle)

translation.text: 日语里“把某人指甲缝里的污垢煎来喝”，直译听着很古怪，实际却是“向某人学习”的意思。（游戏：Refreshing Sideways Puzzle）

source.text: This Japanese proverb could be literally translated as "doing life laundry while the ogre is away". This doesn't make much sense in English though, so the localized script uses a completely different proverb to say roughly the same thing (Game: Final Fantasy IV)

translation.text: 这句日语谚语可以直译成“趁鬼不在时洗涤人生”。这在英语里没什么意义，因此本地化采用了一句完全不同的谚语，表达大致相同的意思。（游戏：Final Fantasy IV）

source.text: This Japanese battle cry was translated literally into English as "I will turn you into a beehive", resulting in a bizarre, hilarious, non- threatening threat. In English, we'd probably say something like ''I'll fill you full of holes!" or "I'll turn you into Swiss cheese!" instead (Game: Star Ocean: The Second Story)

translation.text: 这句日语战斗台词被直译成英语“I will turn you into a beehive”（我要把你变成蜂巢），成了古怪又好笑、毫无威慑力的威胁。英语里大概会说“I’ll fill you full of holes!”（我要把你打得满身窟窿），或“I’ll turn you into Swiss cheese!”（我要把你打成瑞士奶酪）。（游戏：Star Ocean: The Second Story）

source.text: What is Localization?

translation.text: 什么是本地化？

source.text: Cultural Knowledge and Expectations

translation.text: 文化知识与预期

source.text: Have you ever heard someone tell an inside joke that you weren't in on? Even though you understood the literal words that were being said, the intended meaning was lost on you. This same thing happens in translation.

translation.text: 你有没有听过自己不懂的圈内笑话？每个字都听懂了，却不明白想表达什么。翻译也会遇到同样的情形。

source.text: Cultures are basically their own giant in-groups: they have their own histories, customs, rituals, traditions, folk stories, foods, and more. A reference to any of these might sound meaningless to an outsider when translated literally. In this situation, understanding the literal words isn't enough - the actual "inside joke" needs to be explained too. It basically needs to be translated twice instead of only once.

translation.text: 每种文化都像一个巨大的圈子，有自己的历史、习俗、仪式、传统、民间故事、食物等。提及其中任何一项，直译给圈外人听都可能毫无意义。这时，理解字面还不够，也得解释那个“圈内笑话”。相当于要翻译两遍，而不是一遍。

source.text: This type of in-group obstacle comes in many forms. Here are a few common examples.

translation.text: 这种圈内知识造成的障碍有很多形式，下面是几个常见例子。

source.text: Cultural and Historical References

translation.text: 文化与历史典故

source.text: Imagine someone says in Japanese:

translation.text: 想象有人用日语说：

source.text: pussuma de nagisuke o osotta egashira 2:50 mitai da! (Literally: It's just like when Egashira 2:50 attacked Nagisuke on Pussuma!)

translation.text:
pussuma de nagisuke o osotta egashira 2:50 mitai da!
直译：就像 Egashira 2:50 在《Pussuma》上袭击 Nagisuke 时一样！

source.text: The above translation, despite being literal, is probably still meaningless to most people outside of Japan. It only makes sense as intended if you're already familiar with Japanese celebrities and television. You have to be part of the "in group'', in other words.

translation.text: 上面的译文虽然忠于字面，对日本以外的大多数人来说，可能仍毫无意义。只有熟悉日本艺人和电视节目，才能理解它的用意。换句话说，你得是“圈内人”。

source.text: Cultural Facts, Stats, and Practices

translation.text: 文化中的事实、数字与做法

source.text: Imagine someone says in Japanese:

translation.text: 想象有人用日语说：

source.text: watashi no nenshū wa 530,000 en desu (Literally: My annual income is 530,000 yen.)

translation.text:
watashi no nenshū wa 530,000 en desu
直译：我的年收入是530,000日元。

source.text: At first glance, this literal translation seems fine. But for people unfamiliar with Japanese economics, it's unclear just how much money this is. Is it a lot? Is it very little? A literal translation still leaves questions for those outside the in-group.

translation.text: 乍看之下，这样直译没问题。但不了解日本经济的人，不知道这到底是多少钱。算多吗？还是很少？对圈外人而言，直译仍留下了疑问。

source.text: Culture-Specific Food

translation.text: 特定文化的食物

source.text: References to culture-specific foods can become meaningless when translated literally or left untranslated. Imagine someone says in Japanese:

translation.text: 提到特定文化的食物时，照字面翻译或干脆不译，都可能让人摸不着头脑。想象有人用日语说：

source.text: kinō shirako to funazushi o tabeta (Literally: I ate shirako and funazushi yesterday.)

translation.text:
kinō shirako to funazushi o tabeta
直译：我昨天吃了 shirako（白子）和 funazushi（鲋寿司）。

source.text: For people not familiar with Japanese food, this translation probably doesn't mean much at all. As we can see, a literal translation can only go so far when crossing the cultural divide.

translation.text: 不熟悉日本饮食的人，看到这句译文大概仍不明所以。可见，直译能跨越的文化距离是有限的。

source.text: In rare cases, translators will simply leave cultural references untranslated and leave an explanation in parentheses immediately afterward (Game: Mysterious Stars: The Samurai)

translation.text: 极少数情况下，译者会保留文化典故不译，紧接着用括号解释。（游戏：Mysterious Stars: The Samurai）

source.text: There are several ways of handling cultural matters in translation. In academia, it's standard practice to translate everything literally and include lots of explanatory footnotes. In entertainment, it's more common to localize foreign cultural references by replacing them with something similar, but more familiar to the target audience

translation.text: 翻译处理文化问题有几种办法。学术作品通常照字面翻译，再附上大量解释性脚注。娱乐作品则更常进行本地化，把外国文化典故换成目标受众更熟悉、又相近的事物。

source.text: A Japanese line about "Hanako" was translated literally into English, making it completely meaningless for most players outside of Japan. For players in Japan, it's an obvious reference to the famous urban legend of Hanako, the ghost girl who haunts bathrooms (Game: Breath of Fire II)

translation.text: 一句提到 Hanako 的日语台词被直译成英语，对日本以外的大多数玩家毫无意义。日本玩家却一看就知道，它指的是著名都市传说中出没于厕所的幽灵女孩 Hanako。（游戏：Breath of Fire II）

source.text: Originally, this character delivered food from a generically named Japanese-style Chinese restaurant. Because the name's significance would've been lost on players outside of Japan, the package was replaced with a generic pizza box for the English release (Game: Tricky Kick)

translation.text: 这个角色原本给一家名字很普通的日式中餐馆送外卖。日本以外的玩家不容易看懂店名的意义，因此英语版把包装换成了普通的披萨盒。（游戏：Tricky Kick）

source.text: Japanese players are asked to hold the controller like a traditional okappiki. But because most players outside of Japan wouldn't understand this reference, the English version asks players to hold the controller like a boxer instead (Game: WarioWare: Smooth Moves)

translation.text: 日版让玩家像传统的 okappiki（捕吏）那样握住控制器。但日本以外的大多数玩家不懂这个比喻，因此英语版改成让玩家像拳击手那样握住控制器。（游戏：WarioWare: Smooth Moves）

source.text: What is Localization?

translation.text: 什么是本地化？

source.text: Speech Patterns

translation.text: 说话方式

source.text: Naturally, a translator should strive to preserve what's being said. But it's often just as important to preserve how it's being said. Otherwise the resulting translation might become "flattened". A flattened translation lacks the original text's unique traits, can lead to confusion, and can cause key information to be lost.

translation.text: 译者自然应尽力保留“说了什么”，但保留“怎么说”往往同样重要。否则，译文就可能被“磨平”：失去原文的独特之处，造成混淆，乃至丢掉关键信息。

source.text: Language-specific speech patterns are particularly tricky - and sometimes impossible - to preserve when jumping between languages. Here are a few speech patterns that can easily be lost in a literal translation.

translation.text: 某种语言独有的说话方式尤其难以跨越语言，有时根本无法保留。下面几种就很容易在直译中消失。

source.text: Accents and Dialects

translation.text: 口音与方言

source.text: Some speech patterns have their own histories, backgrounds, and deep ties to specific regions of specific countries. These speech patterns convey extra information that give off a specific vibe not found anywhere else.

translation.text: 有些说话方式有自己的历史、背景，并与特定国家的特定地区紧密相连。它们能传达额外信息，带出其他地方没有的独特感觉。

source.text: For example, there is no "Boston accent" in Japanese. There's no cowboy dialect, nor is there a "Southern belle" speech pattern. Similarly, there's no "Heian era" speech pattern or "Kyoto accent" in English. These speech patterns simply become flattened in a literal translation.

translation.text: 例如，日语里没有“波士顿口音”，没有牛仔腔，也没有“美国南方淑女”的说话方式。同样，英语里没有“平安时代”的说话方式或“京都口音”。直译只会把这些特点磨平。

source.text: Pronouns

translation.text: 代词

source.text: Different languages use pronouns in different ways. For example, in English we only have "I/me" when referring to ourselves, but there are dozens of ways to say "I" in Japanese, each with a different connotation.

translation.text: 不同语言使用代词的方式不同。例如英语用来指自己的只有 I/me，而日语说“我”的方式有几十种，各有不同意味。

source.text: Similarly, there are dozens of Japanese pronouns that mean "you" in the singular, but it's just as common to restate the listener's name every time instead of using a pronoun. In fact, it's perfectly normal to drop pronouns entirely in Japanese if it's clear who's being referred to. The Japanese phrase for "I love you'', ai shiteiru, literally contains no pronouns, for instance.

translation.text: 日语同样有几十个单数“你”的说法，但每次直接叫对方的名字、不用代词，也很常见。只要指的是谁足够明确，日语完全省略代词也很正常。例如 ai shiteiru（我爱你），字面上就没有任何代词。

source.text: Because every language uses pronouns in such different ways, dialogue and conversations risk being flattened when translated literally.

translation.text: 由于各语言使用代词的方式差异很大，直译对白和对话就可能磨平它们的特点。

source.text: Grammar

translation.text: 语法

source.text: The same sentence can flow very differently in different languages. For example, English sentences generally go subject-verb-object, as in "Bob ate a monkey". But in Japanese, sentences tend to go subject-object-verb, as in "Bob a monkey ate". This difference can make a literal translation fall apart when a sentence is incomplete - which is extremely common in Japanese - or when timing is important.

translation.text: 同一句话在不同语言里的行进顺序可能大不相同。例如英语通常是主语—动词—宾语，像 Bob ate a monkey（Bob 吃了一只猴子）；日语则通常是主语—宾语—动词，相当于“Bob 一只猴子吃了”。遇到不完整的句子——日语里极为常见——或讲究时机的台词，这种差异就可能让直译失效。

source.text: Other aspects of grnmmar, such as gendered speech and politeness levels, also get flattened in a literal translation. Basically, grammar is a language's rulebook, but not every language plays by the same rules.

translation.text: 带有性别色彩的说话方式、礼貌程度等其他语法特点，也可能在直译中被磨平。语法就像一种语言的规则手册，但不是所有语言都按同一套规则行事。

source.text: Originally, this boss in Pocky and Rocky spoke with a heavy Japanese regional accent. This trait was left unlocalized in English, resulting in flattened dialogue

translation.text: 《Pocky and Rocky》的这个头目原本带有浓重的日本地方口音。英语版没有处理这一特点，台词的特色便被磨平了。

source.text: In some Japanese translations of the Harry Potter series, Voldemort uses the first-person pronoun ore-sama, the same pronoun that Wario uses

translation.text: 一些《Harry Potter》的日语译本让 Voldemort 用 ore-sama（本大爷）自称，与 Wario 用的一样。

source.text: This Japanese line features a strong "rural, country bumpkin" speech pattern. The localized line, despite being in a completely different language, uses a roughly similar English dialect to provide the same vibe and details that would've otherwise been lost in a literal translation (Game: Blaster Master Zero 2)

translation.text: 这句日语带着浓重的“乡下土包子”口吻。译文虽然换了一种语言，却使用了大体相似的英语方言，传达同样的感觉和细节，免得它们在直译中流失。（游戏：Blaster Master Zero 2）

source.text: ~ In the Japanese Animal Crossing games, Mr. Resetti speaks with a very thick Osaka dialect. Because this dialect doesn't exist in English, the localization team approximated it by giving him a distinctive, gruff New York accent instead

translation.text: 日版《Animal Crossing》中，Mr. Resetti 操着极浓的大阪方言。英语里没有这种方言，因此本地化团队改用鲜明、粗犷的纽约口音，近似传达原来的感觉。

source.text: Imagine someone asked you to translate this game into English. What happens when you run into text like this?

translation.text: 想象有人请你把这个游戏译成英语。遇到这样的台词，你会怎么办？

source.text: If a bilingual character sometimes speaks a foreign language, a literal translation of their dialogue into that foreign language will flatten their speech and effectively turn the character monolingual (Game: Tokimeki Memorial)

translation.text: 如果一个双语角色偶尔说外语，而你又要把对白译成那种外语，直译就会抹平这种特点，让角色实际上变成只说一种语言。（游戏：Tokimeki Memorial）

source.text: What is Localization?

translation.text: 什么是本地化？

source.text: Language Peculiarities

translation.text: 语言的独特之处

source.text: Despite their differences, DVDs, Blu-rays, and VHS tapes can all hold the same movie. These formats aren't compatible with each other, though - you can't just stick a VHS tape into a DVD player. Languages are very similar - they can say roughly the same things, but you can't just shove text from one language into another and hope it'll work right.

translation.text: DVD、蓝光和 VHS 录像带虽各不相同，却都能装下同一部电影。不过，它们彼此并不兼容：你不能把 VHS 录像带塞进 DVD 播放器。语言也很相似，能表达大致相同的内容，却不能把一种语言的文字硬塞进另一种，就指望一切正常。

source.text: Here are some examples of how a language's uniqueness can cause literal translations to miss the mark.

translation.text: 下面几个例子说明，语言的独特之处如何让直译偏离原意。

source.text: Sound Effects

translation.text: 拟声词

source.text: Some sound-effect words, such as animal sounds, are generally easy to convert between languages. But some languages use sound-effect words more than others, and some languages have sound-effect words that don't even exist in other languages. For example, the Japanese language has a sound for staring. It even has a sound effect for silence. When it comes to sound effects, sometimes a literal translation isn't even possible.

translation.text: 动物叫声之类的拟声词，通常很容易在语言之间转换。但有的语言比别的语言更常用这类词，有的语言还有别的语言根本没有的拟声、拟态词。例如日语有表示盯着看的“声音”，甚至连寂静也有“声音”。碰到这类词，有时连直译都不可能。

source.text: Punctuation

translation.text: 标点

source.text: Not every language uses punctuation the same way. Some languages have similar-looking punctuation marks that serve different purposes. And some languages have punctuation marks that don't exist in other languages. Because of this, a literal translation with all of the original punctuation intact can have unintended effects.

translation.text: 不是所有语言都以同样方式使用标点。有些标点看起来相似，用途却不同；有些标点在其他语言里根本不存在。因此，直译时照搬原来的全部标点，可能产生意料之外的效果。

source.text: Writing Systems

translation.text: 文字系统

source.text: Unlike English, the Japanese language has three distinct writing systems. This lets you spell the same word in multiple ways - sometimes dozens of ways - to achieve different effects. What's more, the Japanese language even allows you to write words on top of other words to achieve various effects not possible in other languages. Unsurprisingly, these effects tend to get flattened in a literal translation.

translation.text: 与英语不同，日语有三套不同的文字系统。同一个词可以有多种写法，有时甚至几十种，能产生不同效果。日语还可以在词语上面再写一层文字，做到其他语言做不到的事。这些效果往往在直译中被磨平，也就不奇怪了。

source.text: Japanese text can have extra text on top to change meanings or pronunciations (Game: Tales of Vesperia)

translation.text: 日语文字上方还能加字，改变意思或读音。（游戏：Tales of Vesperia）

source.text: Numbers

translation.text: 数字

source.text: If you type "58008" on a calculator and turn it upside down, it makes English speaking schoolchildren laugh because it spells "BOOBS". This numberplay would make little sense to non-English speakers, however. Similarly, the Japanese language has its own unique forms of numberplay that make zero sense in other languages - November 4•h can be interpreted as "Nice Butt Day", for example. When language is involved, numbers lose their literal predictability.

translation.text: 在计算器上输入“58008”，再上下颠倒，会让英语国家的小学生发笑，因为它看起来像“BOOBS”（胸部）。不过，不懂英语的人恐怕不明白这个数字游戏。日语同样有别的语言完全看不懂的数字游戏，例如11月4日可以解作“美臀日”。一旦牵涉语言，数字也不再总能按字面理解。

source.text: Sound effect translation can lead to humorous results if done poorly. Here, the Japanese sound effect for chewing food hilariously became "CHUCK, CHUCK" in English (Game: Battle Rangers)

translation.text: 拟声词翻译得不好，可能产生滑稽的结果。这里的日语咀嚼声就莫名变成了英语“CHUCK, CHUCK”。（游戏：Battle Rangers）

source.text: In Japanese, quotation marks and similar characters are often used for emphasis. In English, however, such quotation marks often indicate sarcasm and/or dishonesty

translation.text: 日语常用引号及类似符号表示强调；英语里的这类引号却往往暗示讽刺，或所言不实。

source.text: This bit of Japanese numberplay was left unlocalized for English-speaking players. Instead, a short translation note was added for clarification for those unfamiliar with Japanese (Game: Waku Waku Sweets)

translation.text: 这个日语数字游戏没有为英语玩家改写，而是加了一条简短译注，向不懂日语的人说明。（游戏：Waku Waku Sweets）

source.text: Double-negatives are usually a no-no in proper English, but this same rule doesn't necessarily apply to other languages like Japanese. As a result, literal translations can end up breaking expected grammar rules (Game: Sword Art Online: Hollow Fragment)

translation.text: 规范英语通常不接受这样的双重否定，但这条规则不一定适用于日语等其他语言。因此，直译可能违反读者熟悉的语法规则。（游戏：Sword Art Online: Hollow Fragment）

source.text: What is Localization?

translation.text: 什么是本地化？

source.text: Creative Packaging

translation.text: 创意的表达形式

source.text: Sometimes, it's not the words themselves that are difficult to translate, but how they're presented. Literal translations tend to fall apart when this type of "creative packaging" is involved. Here are a few simple examples.

translation.text: 有时难译的不是词语本身，而是它们的呈现方式。碰上这种“创意包装”，直译往往会失效。下面是几个简单例子。

source.text: Clues and Hints

translation.text: 线索与提示

source.text: Writers sometimes include meticulously worded hints meant to guide the reader or lead the reader astray. Such hints might be used as mystery clues, as foreshadowing devices, or to say something indirectly. Naturally, a carefully crafted hint can easily break during translation.

translation.text: 作者有时会用精心斟酌的措辞引导读者，或把读者引向歧途。这些提示可以是谜题线索、伏笔，也可以用来委婉表达。这样的精巧安排，自然很容易在翻译中失灵。

source.text: Poetry

translation.text: 诗歌

source.text: Rhyme, rhythm, and syllable counts are important in poetry, but tend to get lost in a literal translation. For example, a literal translation of a Japanese haiku into English will probably have too many syllables to still be a traditional haiku.

translation.text: 押韵、节奏和音节数对诗歌很重要，却往往在直译中丢失。例如，把日语俳句直译成英语，音节通常会多到不再符合传统俳句的形式。

source.text: Songs

translation.text: 歌曲

source.text: Songs present a similar creative packaging problem. A literal translation of "Rudolph the Red-Nosed Reindeer" into Japanese, for example, will result in lyrics that no longer fit the music. The natural solution, then, is to tweak the translation until they do fit the music:

translation.text: 歌曲也有类似的形式难题。例如，将《Rudolph the Red-Nosed Reindeer》（红鼻子驯鹿鲁道夫）直译成日语，歌词就唱不进原来的旋律了。自然的办法是调整译词，直到能配合旋律：

source.text: Although these .Japanese lyrics don't fully match the English lyrics, they still tell roughly the same story with words that can be sung to the original tune.

source.text: This dying message was localized for audiences unfamiliar with Japanese writing systems. Without this change, the underlying mystery - and its solution - would've made zero sense in English (Game: Phoenix Wright - Ace Attorney: Justice For All)

source.text: This 5-7-5 Japanese haiku also contains an important gameplay clue. As such, the content of the poem was prioritized over the need to keep the syllable count intact (Game: Yakuza 6)

translation.text: 这首五—七—五的日语俳句还藏着重要的游戏提示。因此，翻译优先保留诗的内容，而非原来的音节数。（游戏：Yakuza 6）

source.text: Gato's Japanese song, which was meant to be sung to his theme music, required some minor lyrical rewrites to remain singable in the English release (Game: Chrono Trigger)
