source.text: The Japanese language has three different writing systems: hiragana, katakana, and kanji. In standard written Japanese, these three systems work together to convey information. There are approximately 50 hiragana characters, 50 katakana characters, and 2000 standard kanji characters.

translation.text: 日语有三套不同的文字系统：平假名、片假名和汉字。标准书面日语用三者共同传递信息，约有50个平假名、50个片假名，以及2000个常用汉字。

source.text: Many video games in ~ the 1990s and earlier used a simplified form of Japanese that can be considered "retro" today

translation.text: 20世纪90年代及更早的很多游戏，采用简化的日语书写方式，如今已带有“复古”感。

source.text: MOTHER 2 (1994)

source.text: During the 1990s and earlier, hardware limitations made it unwieldy to support the thousands of kanji characters. This led developers to rely more heavily on hiragana and katakana, with limited kanji support when possible. All three writing systems are commonly supported in modern games, which in turn gives the "mostly hiragana and katakana" writing style a strong retro vibe.

translation.text: 20世纪90年代及更早，硬件限制让游戏难以容纳数千个汉字。开发者因此更多依赖平假名和片假名，条件允许时才加入少量汉字。现代游戏普遍支持三套文字，也因此让“主要使用平假名与片假名”的写法带上了浓厚的复古气息。

translation.text: 两张截图说的完全一样，左图是模拟图。不过，现代写法有几个复杂的字，复古写法则整体更简单、曲线更多。

source.text: Because Toby designed Undertale as a love letter to retro Japanese RPGs, he asked 8-4 to mimic the retro style of classic Japanese games, particularly when characters speak. For this reason, the Japanese dialogue in Undertale uses this simplified writing style, while inanimate objects like plaques and signs use the more standard writing style.

translation.text: Toby 把 Undertale 当作献给复古日式角色扮演游戏的情书，因此请 8-4 模仿经典日本游戏的写法，尤其是角色说话时。所以，日语对白采用这种简化写法，铭牌、标牌等无生命物体则使用更标准的写法。

source.text: Although this simplified Japanese style has a retro feel to it, the lack of kanji also lends it an immature or "grade schooler" vibe. This combination led some fans to criticize the official translation as feeling too "kiddie" and/or old-fashioned.

translation.text: 这种简化日语虽然复古，汉字稀少也会让人觉得幼稚，像“小学生”。这两种感觉叠加，令一些玩家批评官方译版太“低龄”或太老派。

source.text: There were mixed opinions on the choice to use retro, simplified Japanese. Some fans simply said it was difficult to read. Louder fans scoffed and threw insults around. Others praised the choice by saying it made characters feel more "alive", or that it made the text feel "gentle".

translation.text: 玩家对复古简化写法意见不一。有些人只说难读，嗓门更大的人则冷嘲热讽、出口骂人；另一些人却称赞，这让角色更“鲜活”，或让文字显得“温柔”。

source.text: The Japanese Language's Many Writing Systems

translation.text: 日语的多套文字系统

source.text: The Japanese language uses three different writing systems: hiragana, katakana, and kanji.

translation.text: 日语使用三套不同的文字系统：平假名、片假名和汉字。

source.text: Hiragana and katakana are both syllabaries, which means every character is one syllable. You can write any and every Japanese word with hiragana or katakana alone. Kanji is a more complicated writing system that Japan imported from China long ago. Kanji is complex, follows multiple pronunciation rules, contains thousands of characters, and takes years to master. All three systems are used side-by-side in normal, everyday Japanese writing.

translation.text: 平假名与片假名都属于音节文字，也就是说，每个字符表示一个音节。任何日语词，都可以只用平假名或只用片假名写出来。汉字则是日本很久以前从中国引进的、更复杂的文字系统：读法规则多、字数达数千，需要多年才能掌握。日常书面日语将三套文字并用。

source.text: Early Japanese games could only support hiragana and/or katakana, but kanji became available as game hardware improved. Toby and 8-4 intentionally avoided heavy kanji usage in Undertale's dialogue to retain the game's intended "retro" vibe.

translation.text: 早期日本游戏只能支持平假名或片假名，随着硬件进步，才逐渐用上汉字。Toby 与 8-4 有意避免在 Undertale 对白中大量使用汉字，以保留游戏原本想要的“复古”感。

source.text: Just the Right Type

translation.text: 恰到好处的字体

source.text: Fonts are a big part of the Undertale experience - the game makes heavy use of multiple fonts, and it even contains font-related jokes. What's more, Toby chose many of the game's English fonts because they're generic, cheesy, and not what a serious, professional game developer would ever use.

translation.text: 字体是 Undertale 体验的重要部分。游戏大量使用多种字体，甚至有与字体相关的笑话。而且 Toby 选择许多英文字体，正因为它们普通、俗气，正经的专业游戏开发者绝不会用。

source.text: Because fonts are so important in Undertale, Toby and 8-4 searched at length for Japanese fonts that "feel" like their English counterparts, even if they aren't visually similar. In other words, cheesy English fonts were replaced with cheesy Japanese fonts, generic English game fonts were replaced with generic Japanese fonts, and so on.

translation.text: 既然字体如此重要，Toby 与 8-4 就花了很久，寻找与英文字体“感觉”相近的日文字体，外观不必相似。也就是说，俗气的英文字体换成俗气的日文字体，常见的英语游戏字体换成常见的日文字体，诸如此类。

source.text: There were two reasons for the team's obsession with finding the right Japanese fonts: a poor font choice would inaccurately represent the original game, and a poor font choice would sour the player's experience.

translation.text: 团队如此执着于找对日文字体，有两个原因：选错会误传原作，也会损害玩家体验。

source.text: In text-heavy games, fonts can shape the way a game "feels" just as much as its art and sound (note: for display purposes, the Undertale fonts here aren't to scale)

translation.text: 文字量大的游戏中，字体对“感觉”的影响不亚于美术与声音。（注：为方便展示，这里的 Undertale 字体并非按实际比例呈现。）

source.text: Sound of the Mountain

translation.text: 山的名字

source.text: Undertale begins when the main character visits a mountain known as "Mt. Ebott". It's not obvious at first glance, but this isn't some random name - it's simply "Toby" backwards, spelled in a roundabout way.

translation.text: Undertale 开始时，主角来到一座叫 Mt. Ebott 的山。乍看不明显，但这并非随手起的名字：它只是将 Toby 倒过来，再绕点弯子拼出来。

source.text: This naming choice was inspired by a similar mountain in Earth.Bound Beginnings known as "Mt. Itoi", which is a reference to Shigesato Itoi, the game's creator. In the original Japanese version of Earth.Bound Beginnings, however, this mountain was known as "Holy Loly Mountain". This difference meant that Toby's homage to the Earth.Bound series was destined to be lost in translation.

translation.text: 这个命名方式来自 EarthBound Beginnings 中类似的一座山——Mt. Itoi，指的是游戏创作者 Shigesato Itoi。不过，在该作日语原版中，这座山名叫 Holy Loly Mountain。因此，Toby 对 EarthBound 系列的这份致敬，注定会在翻译中丢失。

source.text: Even though Toby’s reference to Mt. Itoi would be lost on Japanese players, the reference to Toby’s name could still be conveyed in translation. To make the reference work, the translator took the name トビイ (to bi i, “Toby”), reversed the characters, and called the mountain “Mt. Ibito”.

translation.text: 日本玩家虽然看不出对 Mt. Itoi 的致敬，但对 Toby 名字的指涉仍能译出来。译者采用トビイ（to bi i，即 Toby 的日文写法），将字符倒过来，把山命名为“Mt. Ibito”。

source.text: By changing the mountain's name, the translator was able to preserve Toby's original intent as closely as possible. However, the change from "Ebott" to "Ibito" also meant that most Japanese players would know the mountain by a different name than the rest of the world.

translation.text: 通过改名，译者尽可能保住了 Toby 原本的用意。不过，从 Ebott 改成 Ibito，也意味着多数日本玩家熟悉的山名，会与世界其他地方不同。

source.text: It was interesting - and frustrating - to see the official localization criticized for "mistranslating" this mountain's name

translation.text: 看到官方译版因“译错”这座山的名字受到批评，既有趣，又让人无奈。

source.text: Mt. ltoi - known as Holy Loly Mountain in Japanese - is a frightful, deadly place full of monsters and darkness, so it's no wonder it served as inspiration for Mt. Ebott

translation.text: Mt. Itoi——日版叫 Holy Loly Mountain——是个怪物遍布、黑暗又致命的可怕地方，难怪会成为 Mt. Ebott 的灵感。

source.text: Undertale's option menu contains things you'd expect: screen size options, language options, controller options, and more. But the option menu also features a unique theme and text quote for each season of the year.

translation.text: Undertale 的故事发生在 Ebott 山下的一片广阔区域。英语里，这里叫作 Underground（地下世界）。

source.text: The Japanese language has multiple words that can mean "underground'', each with its own unique nuances. In Undertale's case, the localization team decided to translate "Underground" as chitei ("depths of the earth") and chitei no sekai ("world at the depths of the earth") as needed. In fiction, chitei tends to evoke the feeling of a vast underground land or realm of unseen wonders:

translation.text: 日语里有几个词都能表示“地下”，各自又带着不同的细微含义。本地化团队为 Undertale 选择了 chitei（地底）和 chitei no sekai（地底世界），视语境使用。在虚构作品中，chitei 往往让人想到辽阔的地下大陆，或藏着未知奇观的世界：

source.text: LEFT: The plot of "Journey to the Center of the Earth" (called "Chitei Journey" in Japanese) involves going inside a big volcanic mountain

translation.text: 左：《地心游记》的日语书名是“地底旅行”，故事中就有进入一座巨大火山的情节。

source.text: RIGHT: The word chitei evokes images of a fantastical underground world

translation.text: 右：chitei（地底）这个词会让人联想到奇幻的地下世界。

source.text: On a side note, the decision to use chitei in the Japanese name resulted in a minor coincidence: the vast underground world in EarthBound was originally known in Japanese as the chitei tairiku ("continent at the depths of the earth"). Given Toby's fondness for EarthBound and EarthBound's clear influence on Undertale as a whole, it almost feels like this translation choice was meant to be from the very start.

translation.text: 顺带一提，日语名称里采用 chitei，还带来了一个小巧合：EarthBound 中那片广阔的地下世界，日语原名就叫 chitei tairiku（地底大陆）。考虑到 Toby 对 EarthBound 的喜爱，以及这款游戏对 Undertale 的明显影响，这个译法简直像是从一开始就注定了。

source.text: Does Undertale actually take place in EarthBound's Lost Underworld? I asked Toby and he just said "lol"

translation.text: 难道 Undertale 的故事其实发生在 EarthBound 的 Lost Underworld（失落的地底世界）？我问了 Toby，他只回了句“哈哈”。

source.text: Inspiration Spotlight: EarthBound

translation.text: 灵感聚焦：EarthBound

source.text: In 1994, Nintendo released a Super Famicom role-playing game known as MOTHER 2 in Japan. The game sold hundreds of thousands of copies and was a hit among fans and critics alike.

translation.text: 1994年，任天堂在日本的 Super Famicom 平台推出角色扮演游戏 MOTHER 2。游戏卖出数十万份，深受玩家和评论界好评。

source.text: Hoping for similar success outside of Japan, Nintendo localized MOTHER 2 into English and released the game as EarthBound in 1995. The game sold poorly and was quickly moved to bargain bins. Despite its commercial failure, EarthBound eventually became a cult classic that continues to influence game developers around the world.

translation.text: 任天堂希望海外也有同样的成绩，于是将 MOTHER 2 译成英语，于1995年以 EarthBound 之名发行。然而销量不佳，游戏很快就进了特价区。商业失利并没妨碍它后来成为拥有忠实追随者的经典，至今仍影响着全球的游戏开发者。

source.text: The main character encounters a happy monster named Flowey. In English, Flowey uses friendly, welcoming words like "howdy", "golly", and "aren'tcha". But looks and words are deceiving - Flowey is actually sadistic and evil.

translation.text: 主角遇到一只快乐的怪物 Flowey。他在英语里用 howdy（你好呀）、golly（哎呀）、aren’tcha（是不是呀）这类亲切、热情的说法。但外表和言语都能骗人——Flowey 其实残忍而邪恶。

source.text: In Japanese, Flowey begins by speaking in a friendly way that sounds fitting for a happy flower character. He also uses the Japanese personal pronoun boku, which gives off a friendly, boyish vibe. Even after Flowey reveals his cruel, sinister side and switches to a rude Japanese speaking style, he continues to use the lighthearted boku pronoun. This early localization choice makes sense after the player learns Flowey's true identity much later on.

translation.text: 日语版中，Flowey 起初说话也很亲切，很符合一朵快乐小花的形象。他用 boku（我）自称，显得友善而有少年气。即使后来露出残忍、阴险的本性，改用粗鲁的日语说话，他仍然沿用这个轻快的 boku。等玩家在很久以后得知 Flowey 的真实身份时，就能理解游戏早期的这一选择了。

source.text: Technical Teamwork

translation.text: 技术上的协作

source.text: Flowey pretends to be friendly and helpful at first, but it becomes clear that he only wants to murder the main character.

translation.text: Flowey 起初装得友好又热心，但很快就显露出他唯一的目的：杀死主角。

source.text: The fact that this scene is literally one minute into the game is amazing - I can't think of any Japanese RPGs that are so bold right off the bat

translation.text: 这一幕居然就发生在开场后一分钟，真了不起——我想不出还有哪款日式角色扮演游戏，一上来就敢这么做。

source.text: As part of his battle system tutorial, Flowey instructs the player to catch little white "friendliness pellets", which are actually harmful projectiles. If the player dodges them, Flowey responds in English with:

translation.text: 在讲解战斗系统时，Flowey 让玩家接住白色的“友谊颗粒”（friendliness pellets），其实那些都是会造成伤害的弹丸。如果玩家躲开它们，Flowey 就会说：

translation.text:
Is this a joke? Are you brain dead? RUN. INTO. THE. BULLETS!!!
你在开玩笑？脑子坏了吗？给。我。撞。上。子弹！！！

source.text: Flowey then pauses, notices he used the word "bullets" in his text bubble, and quickly changes it to say "friendliness pellets" instead.

translation.text: 接着，Flowey 停顿了一下，发现对话框里用了 bullets（子弹）这个词，赶紧把它改成了 friendliness pellets（友谊颗粒）。

source.text: Flowey's line is easily translated into Japanese, but there were two problems:

translation.text: 这句台词本身不难译成日语，但有两个问题：

source.text: 1. The line's comedic timing was designed for the English text 2. The changed word needed to appear last to look correct

translation.text:
1. 笑话的节奏是按英语文本设计的。
2. 被替换的词必须放在最后，效果才对。

source.text: The first problem required back-and-forth testing with the localization programmer to get the timing right. The resulting Japanese scene has Flowey notice the mistake before the word tama ("bullet") fully displays. Because the word isn't fully spelled, the letter "m" is left dangling at the end, which is what happens after typing "tam" with a Japanese keyboard. For Japanese players, this joke conveys a similar sense of "whoops, that's not the word I meant to use".

translation.text: 第一个问题需要与本地化程序员反复测试，才能调准时机。最终，日语版里的 Flowey 会在 tama（子弹）显示完整之前发现失误。由于这个词还没拼完，末尾就留着一个 m——使用日语键盘输入 tam 时，正是这样的状态。对日本玩家来说，这个笑话也传达出了类似的感觉：“糟糕，我不是想用这个词。”

source.text: Incidentally, the term "friendliness pellets" was localized as "friendliness capsules" after much internal discussion

translation.text: 顺带一提，经过多次内部讨论，friendliness pellets（友谊颗粒）被译成了“友谊胶囊”。

source.text: The second problem required some creative writing, because standard Japanese grammar would usually place the word "bullets" somewhere in the middle of the sentence and not necessarily at the end.

translation.text: 第二个问题则需要在措辞上想些办法，因为按常规日语语法，“子弹”通常会出现在句子中间，不一定放在句尾。

source.text: With these new adjustments in place, the final Japanese line became:

translation.text: 经过这些调整，最终日语台词的大意是：

source.text: Are you joking around? Are you an idiot? Just get hit already! By the bu/--

translation.text: 你在开玩笑？白痴吗？快撞上去！撞上子——

source.text: This wasn't the only line that involved timing, of course - the localizers encountered many more that required this level of attentive teamwork.

translation.text: 当然，需要配合时机的台词不止这一句。本地化人员还遇到了许多同样需要细致协作的地方。

source.text: Ruins

translation.text: 遗迹

source.text: Toriel Speaks

translation.text: Toriel 的说话方式

source.text: Random trivia: Toby pointed out in his notes that the name of this place, "RUINS", is a reference to Brandish

translation.text: 冷知识：Toby 在笔记里指出，这个地方名叫 RUINS（遗迹），是在致敬 Brandish。

source.text: A kind monster saves the main character from Flowey. This character serves as a guide through the dangerous ruins, further explains how Undertale's battle system works, and offers the main character a new home in the Underground.

translation.text: 一只善良的怪物从 Flowey 手中救下了主角。她带着主角穿过危险的遗迹，继续讲解 Undertale 的战斗系统，还愿意在地下世界给主角一个新家。

source.text: In English, this character is named "Torie!", a play on the word "tutorial". Fortunately, because the English word "tutorial" is already a part of the Japanese language, there was no need to localize Toriel's name into something else.

translation.text: 英语版的 Toriel 是 tutorial（教程）的文字游戏。幸好 tutorial 早已成为日语借词，这个名字便无需另译。

source.text: In English, Torie! speaks with a polite, motherly tone. In Japanese, she uses an equivalent speaking style that conveys politeness and gentleness. She also uses the personal pronoun watashi, which portrays her as a polite, caring woman.

translation.text: 英语版中，Toriel 的语气礼貌而慈爱，像一位母亲。日语版也采用了相应的说话方式，表现出礼貌与温柔。她还用 watashi（我）自称，显得彬彬有礼、体贴关怀。

source.text: Although nobody intended it, I like how Toriel's name contains the Japanese word torie ("virtue; merit; redeeming feature"). Toriel teaches the player how to be a good person in Undertale, so it's a nice, fitting coincidence.

translation.text: 虽然并非有意为之，但我很喜欢 Toriel 的名字里恰好包含日语 torie（长处、美德、可取之处）。Toriel 会教玩家在 Undertale 里做一个好人，这个巧合既美好，又贴切。

source.text: Walk This Way

translation.text: 走这边

source.text: Note how the Japanese text here is more complicated looking than Japanese dialogue in other screenshots - that's because it uses kanji much more heavily

translation.text: 这里的日语看起来比其他截图中的对白复杂，因为这段文字使用了更多汉字。

source.text: The first sign in the game offers a hint to a nearby puzzle:

translation.text: 游戏中的第一块告示牌，为附近的一道谜题提供了提示：

source.text: Only the fearless may proceed. Brave ones. Foolish ones. Both walk not the middle road.

translation.text:
Only the fearless may proceed. Brave ones. Foolish ones. Both walk not the middle road.
唯有无畏者方能前行。勇敢者。愚蠢者。两者都不走中间的路。

source.text: While working on this line, the translator noticed that it could also be interpreted as a subtle hint about the three different ways of playing Undertale: a difficult path that leads to a happy ending, a murderous path that leads to a bad ending, and a "middle of the road" path that leads to a mediocre ending.

translation.text: 翻译这段文字时，译者发现它也可以被理解成对 Undertale 三种玩法的隐晦提示：艰难的道路通向美好结局，杀戮的道路通向坏结局，而“走中间”的道路则通向平庸的结局。

source.text: Although Toby didn't comment on this line's potential double-meaning, it so strongly parallels the literal meaning of the hint that both meanings can be inferred from the Japanese line too.

translation.text: Toby 没有评论这句话是否有这样的双重含义。不过，这层意思与谜题提示的字面含义高度吻合，因此日语台词也能让人读出这两层意思。

source.text: Japanese Personal Pronouns: watashi

translation.text: 日语人称代词：watashi

source.text: Watashi is the most neutral version of "I/me" in Japanese. In formal situations, watashi can be used by almost anyone. In informal situations, watashi is a tad more feminine. Other fictional characters who use watashi include:

translation.text: Watashi 是日语中最中性的“我”。在正式场合，几乎任何人都可以用它自称；在非正式场合，它则略偏女性化。其他使用 watashi 的虚构角色还有：

source.text: Princess Zelda (The Legend of Zelda series)

translation.text:
Princess Zelda
（The Legend of Zelda 系列）

source.text: Mitsurugi Reiji (aka Miles Edgeworth, Gyakuten Saiban!Ace Attorney series)

translation.text:
Mitsurugi Reiji（Miles Edgeworth）
Gyakuten Saiban／Ace Attorney 系列

source.text: Dracula (Akumajō/Castlevania series)

translation.text:
Dracula
（Akumajō／Castlevania 系列）

source.text: Aerith Gainsborough (Final Fantasy series)

translation.text:
Aerith Gainsborough
（Final Fantasy 系列）

source.text: Bandage Care

translation.text: 绷带护理

source.text: On an unrelated note, I have a gut feeling that the more experienced a translator is, the weirder their total search history is

translation.text: 顺便说个不相干的：我总觉得，译者经验越丰富，整份搜索记录看起来就越古怪。

source.text: The main character starts with the "Bandage" item. In English, "bandage" can refer to either an adhesive bandage or a bandage wrap. This ambiguity was intentional, but late-game text suggests "bandage wrap" was intended.

translation.text: 主角开局就带着一件叫 Bandage（绷带）的物品。英语 bandage 既可以指创可贴，也可以指缠绕式绷带。这种歧义是刻意保留的，不过游戏后期的文本表明，它应该指缠绕式绷带。

source.text: In Japanese, however, these two types of bandages go by different names: bans6k6 ("adhesive bandage") and h6tai ("bandage wrap"). Unfortunately, this language difference forced the translator to use h6tai, which removes the intended ambiguity and prevents Japanese players from experiencing the same confusion as English-speaking players.

translation.text: 但在日语中，两者有不同的名称：bansōkō（创可贴）与 hōtai（缠绕式绷带）。遗憾的是，这个语言差异迫使译者选择了 hōtai，也消除了原本有意留下的歧义，使日本玩家无法像英语玩家那样感到困惑。

source.text: "There ... are ... TWO bandages!"

translation.text: “有……两种……绷带！”

source.text: Ruins

translation.text: 遗迹

source.text: Getting Determination

translation.text: 获得“决心”

source.text: It was clear to ~ everyone involved that "determination" represented one of the biggest translation choices in the entire game

translation.text: 所有参与者都很清楚，determination（决心）的译法是整部游戏最重要的翻译选择之一。

source.text: One of the most important concepts in Undertale is known as "determination''. At first, the use of this word doesn't seem particularly noteworthy, but its sig11ificance grows as the game progresses. The word also carries several extra meanings unique to Undertale, so Toby naturally left many notes about it.

translation.text: Undertale 中最重要的概念之一叫作 determination（决心）。起初，这个词的使用似乎没什么特别，但随着游戏推进，它的重要性越来越明显。这个词在 Undertale 中还包含几层独特的含义，因此 Toby 自然为它留下了大量笔记。

source.text: There are multiple words that can mean "determination" in Japanese, but none contain the multiple meanings behind Undertale's "determination". For the localization team, this meant that certain things would be lost in translation no matter what. The term still needed to be translated into something, though, so after some discussion, the team settled on the word ketsui ("determination; resolve; decisiveness; a made-up mind") for Undertale's "determination".

translation.text: 日语中有几个词都能表示 determination，但没有哪个词能涵盖 Undertale 赋予它的多重含义。这意味着，本地化团队无论如何都会在翻译中有所损失。可它终究得有个译法。经过讨论，团队选定了 ketsui，意思包括“决心、决意、果断、打定主意”，用来对应 Undertale 中的 determination。

source.text: Generally Determined

translation.text: 一般意义的决心

source.text: Random trivia: Toby ~ noted that the term "fallen down" was a partially cut concept for describing the state someone enters just before death

translation.text: 冷知识：Toby 指出，fallen down（倒下）原本用来描述临死前的状态，但这个概念后来有一部分被删掉了。

source.text: After the localization team chose to translate "determination" as ketsui, another problem appeared: what happens when words like "determination" or "determined" are used in a general sense rather than the Undertale sense?

translation.text: 团队选定 ketsui（决心）之后，又出现了一个问题：如果 determination（决心）或 determined（坚定的）只是用于一般语境，而不指 Undertale 的特殊概念，该怎么办？

source.text: Luckily, Toby left notes about this issue too, and the localization staff double checked with him as needed. The issue didn't come up much, but both Toby and 8-4 knew it was important to handle properly.

translation.text: 幸好 Toby 也为这个问题写了笔记，本地化人员还会在必要时向他核实。这种情况不常出现，但 Toby 和 8-4 都知道，必须妥善处理。

source.text: This left one last question: how do you differentiate between general ketsui and Undertale-style ketsui in the Japanese script? The solution, which Toby also suggested, was to use eye-catching katakana for Undertale "determination", and ordinary hiragana for more general determination.

translation.text: 最后只剩一个问题：在日语文本中，怎样区分一般意义的 ketsui 与 Undertale 特有的 ketsui？解决办法也是 Toby 提出的：游戏的特殊概念用醒目的片假名书写，一般意义的“决心”则用普通的平假名。

source.text: If you're like me, reading "determination" so many times has probably turned your brain numb. Basically, Toby and 8-4 spent a lot of time on this one term to make sure it was always handled faithfully.

translation.text: 如果你和我一样，读了这么多遍“决心”，脑子大概已经麻了。说到底，Toby 和 8-4 花了许多时间研究这一个词，就是为了确保每次出现都忠于原意。

pages.title: 本地化笔记：“决心”的重要性

source.text: Localization Notes: Determination's Importance

translation.text: 本地化笔记：“决心”的重要性

source.text: Toby began by defining what "determination" is in the game and how it factors into the story in different ways:

translation.text: Toby 先解释了游戏中“决心”的含义，以及它如何以不同方式影响故事：

source.text: "Determination" - Possibly THE most important key word in the entire game. Should you change it, choosing a good word for this is really important. Meaning of the word determination as most commonly used in the game:

translation.text: “决心”（determination）——可能是整部游戏最重要的关键词。如果要换个词，选得好不好就非常关键。游戏里，这个词最常见的含义有：

source.text: • Resolve to continue • Will to live • Refusal to give up/die (appears to be related to fighting spirit in some cases)

translation.text:
• 坚持下去的决心
• 求生意志
• 拒绝放弃／死亡（有时似乎与斗志有关）

source.text: "Determination" also turns out to be Al phys' code word for an actual physical substance that she injects into monsters, one that humans produce naturally in large quantities. This substance has the following properties:

translation.text: “决心”同时也是 Alphys 为一种真实物质起的代号。她把这种物质注入怪物体内，而人类能自然产生大量这种物质。它有以下性质：

source.text: • Creatures with too much are unable to die (de - termination) • The being with the most "Determination" in the underground has the power to change fate and use the in-game save/load system

translation.text:
• 体内这种物质过多的生物将无法死亡（de-termination，把词拆成“去除终结”）。
• 地下世界中“决心”最强的存在，能够改变命运，并使用游戏内的存档／读档系统。

source.text: I think there are a few words like this in JP, right? You'll have to strike a good balance between what's the best fit. But also, "determination" is an unusual word, and thus it's really increased the quotability of the save point line ("It fills you with determination ... ") So if there's a way to get the meaning while also being a bit more iconic/quotable, go for that.

translation.text: 我记得日语里有几个类似的词，对吧？你得权衡一下，找出最合适的。不过，“决心”也是个不太常见的词，因此存档点那句“它使你充满了决心……”才变得特别容易被人记住和引用。所以，要是能找到既传达含义、又更有辨识度、更适合引用的说法，就用吧。

source.text: Toby frequently repeated the need to properly handle "determination" in translation:

translation.text: Toby 多次强调，翻译时必须妥善处理“决心”这个词：

source.text: Mentioned elsewhere, but use the same word for "determination" throughout the entire game

translation.text: 别处也提到过，整部游戏里的“决心”都要用同一个词。

source.text: Toby clarified how to handle atypical instances of the word "determination" in translation:

translation.text: Toby 进一步解释了“决心”在特殊用法下该怎样翻译：

source.text: All “determinations” are determination. However, I think depending on the context, (please tell me if this is a dumb idea) it could be put in hiragana or kanji instead of katakana instead? Because it’s literally the same thing here (foreshadowing how she will melt when defeated due to her determination) but its meaning is more in a normal, less conspicuous sense, even though it’s pronounced the same way. So just 決意 [ketsui in kanji] or whatever. 決意 vs ケツイ [ketsui in katakana] IDK if there are other instances of this.

translation.text: 所有“决心”都是同一种决心。不过，能否按语境改用平假名或汉字，而不是片假名？（若这想法很蠢，请告诉我。）这里字面上指的是同一事物，也在暗示她会因自身的决心，在被击败后融化。但这里用的是更日常、更不显眼的含义，读音却相同。所以写成「決意」之类就好；汉字「決意」与片假名「ケツイ」，都读 ketsui（决心）。我不确定还有没有其他这样的例子。

source.text: Ruins

translation.text: 遗迹

pages.title: 骷髅双关 · 诗意的念头

source.text: A Skeleton Pun

translation.text: 骷髅双关

source.text: The translator considered other puns on kotsu o tsukamu ("get the hang of") and kotsu ga iru ("there’s a trick/knack to it")

translation.text: 译者还考虑过围绕 kotsu o tsukamu（掌握诀窍）和 kotsu ga iru（需要技巧／窍门）的其他双关。

source.text: Toriel loves bad puns and shares many throughout the game. One early example is about skeletons:

translation.text: Toriel 喜欢冷双关，在游戏中讲了不少。前期就有一个关于骷髅的笑话：

source.text: English Text

translation.text: 英文笑话（释义）

source.text: Japanese Text (roughly translated)

translation.text: 日版笑话（大意）

source.text: What did the skeleton tile his roof with? SHIN-gles!

translation.text:
骷髅用什么铺屋顶？
SHIN-gles（木瓦）！

source.text: Where do skeletons live? Tekkotsu apartment buildings!

translation.text:
骷髅住在哪里？
Tekkotsu（钢骨架）公寓楼！

source.text: The original joke wouldn’t work in a straightforward translation into Japanese, as it plays with the English words “shin” and “shingles”. To compensate, the translator replaced the joke with a similar joke in Japanese that plays with the words kotsu (bone) and tekkotsu (steel frame). The result is a bad Japanese pun on par with the original English pun.

translation.text: 原笑话利用英文 shin（胫骨）和 shingles（屋顶木瓦）玩双关，直译成日文就不成立了。为此，译者换上了类似的日语笑话，利用 kotsu（骨）与 tekkotsu（钢骨架）的关系。于是，一个和英文原版同样冷的日语双关就诞生了。

source.text: Poetry in Notion

translation.text: 诗意的念头

source.text: Reader Challenge #2: Rewrite this English description to say roughly the same thing, but without using the letters E or F!

translation.text: 读者挑战 2：改写这段英文说明，大意保持不变，但不能使用字母 E 或 F！

source.text: The first real battle in Undertale takes place against a lifeless dummy. Checking this dummy in battle displays the short English description that Toby also described as a “meaningless poem”:

translation.text: Undertale 的第一场真正的战斗，对手是一个没有生命的假人。在战斗中查看它，会显示下面这段简短的英文说明；Toby 也把它称为一首“没有意义的诗”：

source.text:
A cotton heart and a button eye
You are the apple of my eye

translation.text:
A cotton heart and a button eye（棉花的心，纽扣的眼）
You are the apple of my eye（你是我的心头宝）

source.text: Because the fanciful phrase “apple of my eye” isn’t commonly used in Japanese, it was replaced with a lighthearted Japanese literary reference:

translation.text: “apple of my eye”这类富于想象的表达在日语中并不常用，于是被换成了一个轻松的日本文学典故：

source.text:
wata no hāto ni botan no hitomi (“A cotton heart and a button eye”)
kagayaitchimatta yorokobi ni (“For the shining joy”)

translation.text:
wata no hāto ni botan no hitomi（棉花的心，纽扣的眼）
kagayaitchimatta yorokobi ni（为了那闪耀的喜悦）

source.text: The second line in this description is a meaningless parody of a famous poem by Chūya Nakahara known as Yogoretchimatta Kanashimi Ni (“For the Tainted Sorrow”). This change ensures that the dummy’s Japanese description is clearly recognizable as a poem, but leaves players confused by its meaningless content.

translation.text: 说明的第二行，是对 Chūya Nakahara 的名诗 Yogoretchimatta Kanashimi Ni（《为了那被玷污的悲伤》）的一句无意义戏仿。这样一改，玩家一眼就能认出假人的日文说明是一首诗，却仍会被其中毫无意义的内容弄得摸不着头脑。

source.text: Yogoretchimatta Kanashimi Ni, first published in 1930, has since been adapted into many books, television shows, and movies

translation.text: Yogoretchimatta Kanashimi Ni 最初发表于 1930 年，后来被改编成许多书籍、电视剧和电影。

pages.title: 胜利的传承 · 怪物的口味

source.text: Victory Bound

translation.text: 胜利的传承

source.text: The 1990s JRPG references never stop in the world of Undertale!

translation.text: 在 Undertale 的世界里，1990 年代日式角色扮演游戏的梗真是无处不在！

source.text: In the English version of Undertale, the message “YOU WON!” appears after a successful battle. At Toby’s direction, this was changed to “YOU WIN!” in the Japanese game. This minor rewording is actually an intentional reference to a change made during MOTHER 2’s English localization into EarthBound:

translation.text: 英文版 Undertale 在战斗获胜后会显示“YOU WON!”（你赢了！）。按 Toby 的要求，日版将它改成了“YOU WIN!”。这点小小的措辞变化，其实是在有意致敬 MOTHER 2 本地化为英文版 EarthBound 时的一处改动：

source.text: I’ve seen long discussions on Japanese message boards about why some things say “you win” in English and other things say “you won”

translation.text: 我见过日本论坛长篇讨论：为什么有些作品的英文写“you win”，另一些却写“you won”？

source.text: Original victory message (MOTHER 2)

translation.text: 原版胜利提示（MOTHER 2）

source.text: Localized victory message (EarthBound)

translation.text: 本地化后的提示（EarthBound）

source.text: As we can see, the original Japanese version of EarthBound displayed “YOU WIN!” after each battle, but this was changed to “YOU WON!” for its English release. Toby was eager to keep this tradition alive with Undertale’s localization, just in the opposite direction.

translation.text: 可以看到，EarthBound 的日文原版在每场战斗后显示“YOU WIN!”，英文发行版却改成了“YOU WON!”。Toby 很想让 Undertale 的本地化延续这项传统，只不过方向恰好反了过来。

source.text: Monstrous Flavors

translation.text: 怪物的口味

source.text: You know how people avoid the licorice ones when eating jelly beans? The same thing happens in Japan, but with peppermint drops

translation.text: 你知道有人吃糖豆时会挑开甘草味的吗？日本也有类似的情况，只不过被挑开的是薄荷糖。

source.text: “Monster Candy” is available for free in the ruins. In English, this candy is described as having a “distinct, non-licorice” flavor. Licorice candy is popular in Western countries, but its striking flavor is also quite polarizing – some people love it, and some people despise it with a burning passion.

translation.text: 在遗迹里可以免费拿到 Monster Candy（怪物糖果）。英文说明写它有一种“distinct, non-licorice”（独特、并非甘草味）风味。甘草糖在西方国家很受欢迎，但那强烈的味道也让人爱憎分明：有人爱不释口，有人则深恶痛绝。

source.text: Licorice candy isn’t as common in Japan, however, so the translator changed the candy to a different flavor: peppermint. Just like with licorice in the West, the peppermint flavor is highly divisive in Japan – some like it, and some would rather eat trash.

translation.text: 不过，甘草糖在日本没那么常见，所以译者把说明中用来对比的口味换成了薄荷。就像西方的甘草味一样，日本人对薄荷味也很两极分化：有人喜欢，有人宁可去吃垃圾。

source.text: American licorice candies and Japanese peppermint candies. Will you eat?

translation.text: 美国的甘草糖与日本的薄荷糖。要吃吗？

source.text: Ruins

translation.text: 遗迹

source.text: Monster Picking

translation.text: 别欺负怪物

source.text: To be fair, I doubt more than a dozen people recognized the Monster Party quote in English, but Toby made the reference intentionally, so it was important to try to localize

translation.text: 说真的，能认出这句英文引用自 Monster Party 的人大概连十几个都没有。不过 Toby 是有意引用的，所以仍有必要尝试把它本地化。

source.text: A bully eyeball monster named Loox appears in the Underground. In the English script, Loox says in battle:

translation.text: 地下世界中有个爱欺负人的眼球怪物，名叫 Loox。在英文版的战斗中，Loox 会说：

source.text: Please don’t pick on me.

translation.text: Please don’t pick on me.（请别欺负我。）

source.text: This seems like a simple, unimportant message at first, until the player is literally given the menu options “Pick On” and “Don’t Pick On”. Picking on Loox will make him more difficult to defeat, while not picking on him will allow the player to spare him.

translation.text: 起初，这似乎只是句简单、无关紧要的话，直到菜单真的给出“Pick On”（欺负）和“Don’t Pick On”（不欺负）两个选项。欺负 Loox 会使他更难击败；不欺负他，则能让玩家饶恕他。

source.text: Toby pointed out in his translation notes that Loox’s line is actually a direct quote from the 1989 NES game, Monster Party. In this classic retro game, a pumpkin monster says “please don’t pick on me” when the player enters its lair.

translation.text: Toby 在翻译备注中指出，Loox 的这句话直接出自 1989 年的 NES 游戏 Monster Party。在这款经典老游戏中，玩家走进一只南瓜怪物的巢穴时，它就会说“please don’t pick on me”。

source.text: The Japanese version of this enemy, which is a parody of Planet of the Apes, roughly says “Seize him! He’s to become our slave!”

translation.text: 这个敌人的日版形象是在戏仿 Planet of the Apes（《人猿星球》），台词大意是：“抓住他！让他当我们的奴隶！”

source.text: A boss enemy in Parody World: Monster Party (Japan)

translation.text:
Parody World: Monster Party
中的头目（日版）

source.text: The same boss enemy in Monster Party (North America)

translation.text:
Monster Party 中的同一头目
（北美版）

source.text: This retro game reference presented three problems for the translator:

translation.text: 这个老游戏的典故给译者带来了三个问题：

source.text: Quoting the original Japanese version of Monster Party wouldn’t work, as it featured very different monsters with completely different text

translation.text: 引用 Monster Party 日文原版行不通，因为它的怪物大不相同，台词也完全不一样。

source.text: Although a near-complete prototype exists, Monster Party was never officially released in Japan anyway

translation.text: 虽然存在一个接近完成的原型版本，但 Monster Party 从来没有在日本正式发行。

source.text: Changing Loox’s quote would most likely break the original bullying theme

translation.text: 改掉 Loox 的这句引用，很可能会破坏原有的欺凌主题。

source.text: The localization team hoped to find a fitting Japanese retro game quote for Loox’s battle message. After some time, though, the team decided to prioritize the line’s functional purpose over its decorative purpose. Thus, Loox still says “please don’t pick on me” in Japanese, but only as a simple, straightforward statement.

translation.text: 本地化团队本想找一句合适的日本老游戏台词，作为 Loox 的战斗发言。但斟酌一番后，团队决定优先保留这句话的实际作用，而不是它作为典故的点缀作用。因此，日版的 Loox 依然会说“请别欺负我”，只是变成了一句平实、直接的话。

source.text: Toriel Asks

translation.text: Toriel 的请求

source.text: Without inside access to the localization team’s notes, I probably never would’ve noticed this difference, as it’s such a rarely seen line

translation.text: 要不是能看到本地化团队的内部备注，我大概永远不会注意到这处差别，因为这句台词实在太少出现了。

source.text: Toriel asks the player to stay in the current room until she returns from an errand. If the player stays in the room for ten minutes, Toriel will call and say:

translation.text: Toriel 请玩家待在当前房间，等她办事回来。如果玩家在房间里等上十分钟，Toriel 就会打来电话说：

source.text: It will take a little longer. Please understand.

translation.text:
It will take a little longer. Please understand.
还需要再等一会儿。请理解。

source.text: Toby noted that “please understand” is a reference to Satoru Iwata, the former president of Nintendo. In his many English-language videos for Nintendo fans, Iwata often said “please understand”, a literal translation of a common Japanese apology. He repeated this peculiar English phrase so often that it became his unofficial catchphrase in the West.

translation.text: Toby 解释说，“please understand”是在致敬任天堂前社长 Satoru Iwata（岩田聪）。在许多面向任天堂粉丝的英语视频中，岩田常说这句话；它直译自一种常见的日语致歉用语。他频繁使用这句特别的英语，使它在西方成了他非官方的标志性口头禅。

source.text: This reference would’ve been lost in a literal translation into Japanese, as Iwata was never famous for saying “please understand” in Japan. Undertale’s localizers considered potential replacement references, but eventually agreed that a natural-sounding translation took priority. Thus Toriel now says “I’m sorry” in Japanese instead of “please understand”.

translation.text: 如果直译成日文，这个梗就会消失，因为岩田在日本并不是以说“please understand”而闻名。Undertale 的本地化人员考虑过替换成其他典故，但最终一致认为，译文自然更重要。于是，日版 Toriel 说的是“对不起”，而不是“请理解”。

source.text: RIP Iwata, I wonder what he would’ve thought about Undertale

translation.text: 愿岩田安息。不知道他会怎样看待 Undertale。

source.text: Localization Notes: “Please Understand”

translation.text: 本地化备注：“Please Understand”

source.text: Toby left a very short note about this line in the localization spreadsheet.

translation.text: Toby 在本地化表格里为这句台词留了一条很简短的备注。

source.text: Iwata’s catch phrase

translation.text: 岩田的口头禅。

source.text: After some research and discussion, the translator localized the line into Japanese and left a note for reference.

translation.text: 经过调查和讨论，译者将这句话本地化为日文，并留下了一条备注供参考。

source.text: “Please Understand” = It’s a meme in English speaking regions and apparently the typical 「ご理解ください」 [gorikai kudasai] has been translated into this. The Japanese phrase doesn’t have any specific meme-related meaning and Toriel saying 「ごりかいください」 [gorikai kudasai] would break the character, so I’ve prioritized making the translation natural.

translation.text: “Please Understand”是英语地区的一个梗，似乎译自常见的「ご理解ください」（gorikai kudasai，请理解）。日语原句没有特定的梗含义；让 Toriel 说「ごりかいください」（gorikai kudasai，请理解）也不符合角色性格，所以我优先让译文自然。

source.text: Translator

translation.text: 译者

source.text: Ruins

translation.text: 遗迹

source.text: Rocky Majority

translation.text: 石头中的多数派

source.text: Juggling priorities is incredibly common in entertainment localization. Sometimes there are no perfect solutions to localization problems, only imperfect approximations

translation.text: 在娱乐作品本地化中，权衡各项优先级非常常见。有些问题没有完美的解法，只能做出不完美的近似处理。

source.text: The main character comes across four rocks sitting next to four switches. Three of the rocks are easily pushed onto their switches, but a sign on a wall suggests that the fourth rock might be a bit different. In English, this sign says:

translation.text: 主角遇到四块石头，旁边有四个开关。其中三块很容易就能推到开关上，但墙上的牌子暗示，第四块可能有些不同。英文牌子写道：

source.text: Three out of four grey rocks recommend you push them.

translation.text:
Three out of four grey rocks recommend you push them.
四块灰色石头中，有三块建议你推它们。

source.text: Toby noted that this is a reference to American medicine and toothpaste commercials that use the cliché “X out of Y professionals recommend” phrase. He also pointed out that part of the joke is about how there is always that one weird person who disagrees for some reason. Except in this case, it’s a rock.

translation.text: Toby 说明，这句话是在模仿美国药品和牙膏广告常用的套话：“每 Y 位专业人士中，有 X 位推荐。”笑点还在于，总会有一个古怪的家伙，不知为什么就是持不同意见。只不过，这次那个家伙是一块石头。

source.text: LEFT: The “X out of Y recommend” phrase really took off in the mid-1970s with Trident chewing gum

translation.text: 左：“每 Y 位中有 X 位推荐”的说法，在 1970 年代中期借着 Trident 口香糖广告大为流行。

source.text: RIGHT: “X out of Y recommend” has been copied and parodied for almost 50 years, yet it remains in regular use today

translation.text: 右：这种说法被模仿、戏仿了近 50 年，时至今日仍然经常出现。

source.text: The “X out of Y professionals recommend” phrase has been a part of Western pop culture for decades, but is largely unknown in Japan. As such, the reference would be lost in a straightforward translation. The localization team looked for a good Japanese equivalent, but nothing quite fit. So, they instead focused on the sign’s other two functions: providing a hint for proceeding in the game, and warning the player that one of the rocks might be strange. Thus, the final Japanese line became a literal, straightforward statement:

translation.text: “每 Y 位专业人士中有 X 位推荐”几十年来一直是西方流行文化的一部分，在日本却鲜为人知。因此，直接翻译就会丢掉这个典故。团队尝试寻找贴切的日语表达，却始终没有合适的。于是，他们转而关注牌子的另外两项作用：提供推进游戏的提示，并提醒玩家，其中一块石头可能有点怪。最终，日版改成了一句平实的说明，大意是：

source.text: Three out of four gray rocks wish to be pushed.

translation.text:
Three out of four gray rocks wish to be pushed.
四块灰色石头中，有三块希望被推。

source.text: As we can see, the original pop culture reference was dropped, but the sign’s usefulness within the game remains the same.

translation.text: 可以看到，原来的流行文化典故被舍弃了，但这块牌子在游戏中的作用保持不变。

source.text: As a translator, recognizing pop culture references can be a bigger challenge than localizing them. It’s not really a skill that’s taught in textbooks or classes – you just have to absorb on your own. Even then, you’ll never know as much about a country’s pop culture as a native who grew up surrounded by it. This is why it was so helpful to have Toby involved in Undertale’s localization process, along with others who grew up surrounded by the same pop culture.

translation.text: 对译者来说，认出流行文化典故，有时比将它们本地化还难。这并不是教科书或课堂能教会的技能，你只能自己慢慢积累。即便如此，你对一个国家流行文化的了解，也很难比得上从小浸润其中的当地人。这就是为什么让 Toby，以及其他在相同文化环境中长大的人，参与 Undertale 的本地化会如此有帮助。

pages.title: 石头也有脾气 · 蜘蛛的募款活动

source.text: Rock and Roll

translation.text: 石头也有脾气

source.text: So, have you been reading these captions first or the main text first? I wonder what most people do first

translation.text: 话说，你是先看这些图注，还是先看正文呢？不知道大多数人会先看哪边。

source.text: Indeed, it turns out that one gray rock doesn’t want to be pushed. In English, the rock speaks with an unusual accent and uses words like “pardner” and “pumpkin” that give off a “cowboy” or “person from Texas” vibe.

translation.text: 果然，有一块灰石头不愿意被推。在英文中，它说话带着特别的口音，会用 pardner（伙计）、pumpkin（南瓜，昵称） 这样的词，让人联想到牛仔，或是得克萨斯州的人。

source.text: Toby noted that it wasn’t important for the Japanese script to retain this rock’s rural speech – the rock just needed to sound unique. Thus the rock now uses a distinctive speaking style associated with Edokko, a class of citizens who lived in Edo (now known as Tokyo) in the late 1700s and early 1800s. This speaking style evokes a special combination of assertive brashness and cheerful straightforwardness.

translation.text: Toby 说明，日文台词不必保留这块石头的乡土口音，只要让它说话与众不同就行。于是，日版采用了与 Edokko（江户子）相关的一种鲜明腔调。江户子是指 18 世纪末、19 世纪初生活在江户（今天的东京）的一类市民。这种说话方式把强势、莽撞与爽朗、直率揉合在一起，别有特色。

source.text: An Edokko man, as depicted in a 1947 Japanese film

translation.text: 1947 年一部日本电影中的江户男子。

source.text: Arachnid Fundraising

translation.text: 蜘蛛的募款活动

source.text: It’s crazy how even a tiny thing like this shop can have such a big effect on later events in the game

translation.text: 连这样一家小店，都能对游戏后面的事件产生那么大的影响，真不可思议。

source.text: Spiders are holding a bake sale in the underground ruins, with doughnuts and cider available for purchase. Supporting the spiders here can have an effect on later events in the game, so the bake sale isn’t a simple, unimportant shop.

translation.text: 蜘蛛们在地下遗迹里举办烘焙义卖，出售甜甜圈和苹果酒。在这里支持蜘蛛，会影响游戏后续的事件，因此这场义卖并不是一家无关紧要的普通小店。

source.text: There’s one problem, though: bake sales aren’t very common in Japan. The team eventually decided to localize “bake sale” as sokubaikai (“sales exhibition”), which is roughly equivalent to the “Artist Alley” vendor areas commonly seen at entertainment conventions in the West.

translation.text: 但有个问题：烘焙义卖在日本并不常见。团队最终决定把 bake sale本地化为 sokubaikai（即卖会），大致相当于西方娱乐展会上常见的 Artist Alley，也就是创作者摆摊售卖作品的区域。

source.text: LEFT: Bake sales are generally small fundraising activities for clubs, etc.

translation.text: 左：烘焙义卖通常是社团等组织的小型筹款活动。

source.text: RIGHT: Japanese sales exhibitions are kind of like “Artist Alleys” at entertainment conventions

translation.text: 右：日本的即卖会，有点像娱乐展会上的 创作者摊位区。

source.text: Ruins

translation.text: 遗迹

source.text: The Ghost with the Least

translation.text: 最没自信的幽灵

source.text: Napstablook’s association with “Napster” is why the character owns a computer, uses the Underground’s version of the Internet, and listens to music

translation.text: Napstablook 与 Napster 的关联，正是这个角色拥有电脑、使用地下世界版互联网并且爱听音乐的原因。

source.text: In the ruins is a sleeping ghost named “Napstablook”. As Toby explains it, this name was originally randomly generated and had no actual inherent meaning:

translation.text: 遗迹里有一个正在睡觉的幽灵，名叫 Napstablook。据 Toby 解释，这个名字原本是随机生成的，本身并没有实际含义：

source.text: Basically I used the name to come up with the character. So “blook” sounds like a ghost, then “nap” --> it sleeps, with zzz. After the demo, people noticed “napsta” sounded like Napster [a popular file-sharing service in the early 2000s], so I added the Napster joke as well. Then I explained all of this simultaneously to the translator.

translation.text: 基本上，我是根据名字来构思角色的。blook 听起来像个幽灵，而 nap（打盹）就意味着它会睡觉，还会发出 zzz。试玩版出来后，有人发现 napsta 听起来像 Napster［2000 年代初流行的文件分享服务］，所以我又加上了 Napster 的梗。之后，我把这些一股脑儿都解释给了译者。

source.text: LEFT: Napstablook is often depicted wearing headphones like in the Napster logo

translation.text: 左：Napstablook 常被画成戴着耳机的样子，就像 Napster 标志那样。

source.text: RIGHT: Winny was the big file-sharing service in Japan for a while in the 2000s

translation.text: 右：2000 年代，Winny 曾一度是日本主要的文件分享服务。

source.text: Because Napstablook’s name contains an old Internet reference, the localizers considered giving the character a name with a similar Japanese reference. For this reason, early drafts of the Japanese script called Napstablook “Winnybohre”. “Winny” was a Japanese file-sharing service that was popular in the mid-2000s, and “bohre” is a play on the Japanese word bōrei, a type of ghost.

translation.text: 由于 Napstablook 的名字包含一个早期互联网的典故，本地化团队考虑过换成一个含有类似日本典故的名字。因此，早期日文稿把 Napstablook 称作 Winnybohre。Winny 是 2000 年代中期在日本流行的文件分享服务，bohre 则是在日语 bōrei（亡灵，一类幽灵）上做的文字游戏。

source.text: To Pikachu, or not to Pikachu? Whether it’s for memorability, consistency, or simplicity’s sake, there is some merit in leaving a meaningful name unlocalized for international audiences

translation.text: 要不要像 Pikachu 那样保留原名？无论是为了好记、一致还是简洁，面向国际受众时，不将一个有含义的名字本地化，也自有它的好处。

source.text: Initially, Toby wasn’t sure that “Winnybohre” suited the character. He understood the reasoning behind the choice and wasn’t against the idea of renaming Napstablook, so he waited to see if the name grew on him. It still felt off months later, so he reverted the name back to “Napstablook” before the Japanese release.

translation.text: 最初，Toby 不确定 Winnybohre 是否适合这个角色。他理解这样命名的理由，也不反对给 Napstablook 改名，于是决定等等，看自己会不会慢慢喜欢上这个名字。几个月后，他仍觉得不太对劲，便在日版发行前把名字改回了 Napstablook。

pages.title: 幽灵如何定义 · Napstablook 的说话方式

source.text: Ghostly Definition

translation.text: 幽灵如何定义

source.text: Big game companies spend tons of money to make awesome, realistic-looking characters with spiffy designs and outfits… and then Toby comes along and makes a round rectangle with eyes

translation.text: 大游戏公司花大钱塑造炫酷逼真的角色，精心设计造型和服装……然后 Toby 来了，画了个长着眼睛的圆角矩形。

source.text: Napstablook’s identity was also a concern for the localization staff. First, because the English script refers to Napstablook as “them” rather than “him” or “her”, the localization team kept Napstablook’s gender unstated and unclear as much as possible in the Japanese script.

translation.text: 本地化团队也很在意 Napstablook 的身份。首先，英文台词用 them（此处不指明性别），而不用 him（他）或 her（她），因此日文也尽量不说明或暗示其性别。

source.text: Secondly, Napstablook is referred to as a “ghost” in English, but there are many words for “ghost” in Japanese. Unfortunately, these words have their own unique nuances and definitions, none of which are a 100% match with the Western-style “sheet ghost”. As a result, Napstablook’s ghost classification changed throughout Undertale’s localization. These classifications included:

translation.text: 其次，英文称 Napstablook 为 ghost（幽灵），但日语中有许多表示“幽灵”的词。遗憾的是，这些词各有细微差别和定义，没有一个能与西方式的“床单幽灵”完全对应。因此，在 Undertale 的本地化过程中，对 Napstablook 的分类曾多次变更，考虑过的词包括：

source.text: yūrei – the ghost of a dead person with a grudge or lingering regrets

translation.text: yūrei——心怀怨恨或仍有遗憾的死者之魂

source.text: bōrei – the ghost of a dead person that can’t rest in peace

translation.text: bōrei——无法安息的死者之魂

source.text: obake – a ghost, monster, or supernatural creature that scares people

translation.text: obake——会吓人的幽灵、怪物或超自然生物

source.text: After stepping back and looking at the finished Japanese script as a whole, the localizers chose to classify Napstablook as an obake.

translation.text: 退后一步，通看完成后的日文稿，团队最终选择把 Napstablook 归为 obake。

source.text: Napstablook Speaks

translation.text: Napstablook 的说话方式

source.text: I remember when they had to explain the meaning of “:)” in movies, so it’s been fascinating to see other online speech patterns – such as using all-lowercase text – show up more and more in popular media

translation.text: 我还记得电影里需要解释“:)”含义的年代。如今，其他网络说话方式——比如全小写文字——越来越多地出现在大众媒体中，实在很有意思。

source.text: Napstablook is insecure and has little self-worth, which is partially conveyed by a unique speech style: all of their text is written with lowercase characters. This not only supplements Napstablook’s dialogue, but also allows the player to identify anonymous messages from Napstablook elsewhere in the game.

translation.text: Napstablook 缺乏安全感，也没什么自我价值感。一种独特的说话方式部分传达了这种性格：全部台词都用小写字母。这不仅补充了对话的表达，也让玩家能认出游戏其他地方来自 Napstablook 的匿名消息。

source.text: Because the Japanese language doesn’t have uppercase and lowercase letters, the translator compensated by giving Napstablook an “I’m worthless, what does anything matter” tone, along with a speaking style that mixes hiragana and katakana in an unusual manner. In this way, the Japanese version of Napstablook parallels the English version in style and substance.

translation.text: 日语没有字母的大小写之分，译者便给 Napstablook 安排了“我一无是处，一切又有什么意义”的口吻，同时以不同寻常的方式混用平假名和片假名。这样，日版 Napstablook 在说话风格和内在性格上，都与英文版形成了对应。

source.text: Ruins

translation.text: 遗迹

pages.title: 坏到根里 · 健康饮食

source.text: Rotten to the Core

translation.text: 坏到根里

source.text: Theory: Mt. Ebott is in the United States because the game references the USDA. Toby’s response when I asked: “USDA could be UNDERGROUND SALAD DEMON ASSOCIATION”

translation.text: 有人推测：游戏提到 USDA（美国农业部），所以 Mt. Ebott 在美国。我问 Toby，他回答：“USDA 也可以是 UNDERGROUND SALAD DEMON ASSOCIATION（地下沙拉恶魔协会）。”

source.text: A monster named Vegetoid lives in the ruins. In the English script, Vegetoid’s in-battle description is a parody of the text commonly seen on real-life food labels. Specifically, the description contains a reference to the United States Department of Agriculture:

translation.text: 遗迹里住着一只叫 Vegetoid 的怪物。英文版在战斗中对它的说明，模仿了现实食品标签上的常见文字。具体来说，这段说明还提到了美国农业部：

source.text:
Serving Size: 1 Monster
Not monitored by the USDA

translation.text:
Serving Size: 1 Monster（每份：1 只怪物）
Not monitored by the USDA（不受美国农业部监管）

source.text: Note: this label appearing in this book does not mean this book is USDA approved

translation.text: 注意：这枚标志出现在本书中，并不表示本书获得了 USDA 的认可。

source.text: The meaning of “USDA” would be lost on most players in Japan, so the translator adjusted the description to say:

translation.text: 日本的大多数玩家并不了解 USDA 的含义，因此译者调整了说明，日版大意是：

source.text:
Serves: 1 Monster
Not registered with the Food Safety Bureau

translation.text:
Serves: 1 Monster（份量：1 只怪物）
Not registered with the Food Safety Bureau（未在食品安全局登记）

source.text: Generalizing the description like this makes the original “in-group joke” more accessible to Japanese players. In fact, this new description could conceivably work in any country in the world!

translation.text: 把说明改得更通用后，日本玩家也更容易理解原先的“圈内笑话”。事实上，这段新说明大概放在世界上任何国家都能成立！

source.text: Healthy Eating

translation.text: 健康饮食

source.text: Pop culture references are always a problem, even before translation gets involved – not everyone will get them to begin with, and they grow more dated with every passing minute

translation.text: 流行文化典故总会带来麻烦，甚至还没到翻译这一步就已经如此：本来就不是人人都懂，而且时间每过一分，它们就又过时了一点。

source.text: During the battle with Vegetoid, the battle narration occasionally states:

translation.text: 与 Vegetoid 战斗时，战斗旁白偶尔会说：

source.text: Vegetoid’s here for your health.

translation.text: Vegetoid’s here for your health.（Vegetoid 为你的健康而来。）

source.text: Toby pointed out in his notes that “for your health” is a reference to Dr. Steve Brule’s catchphrase from the American comedy television programs Tim and Eric Awesome Show, Great Job! and Check It Out! with Dr. Steve Brule. He also noted that it wasn’t important to include a similar reference in the Japanese script, so the translator gave the line a straightforward translation:

translation.text: Toby 在备注中指出，“for your health”是美国喜剧节目 Tim and Eric Awesome Show, Great Job! 及 Check It Out! with Dr. Steve Brule 中，Dr. Steve Brule 的口头禅。他也说明，日文稿不必加入类似的典故，所以译者采用直译，日版大意是：

source.text: Vegetoid supports your health.

translation.text: Vegetoid supports your health.（Vegetoid 支持你的健康。）

source.text: Even without the original reference, the primary joke about Vegetoid attacking you while “supporting your health” still works perfectly in Japanese.

translation.text: 即使没有原来的典故，Vegetoid 一边攻击你，一边“支持你的健康”，这个核心笑点在日语里仍然完全成立。

source.text: Fictional doctor Steve Brule offers ridiculous health tips like “put vinegar on your armpits if they stink” and ends by saying “…for your health!”

translation.text: 虚构医生 Steve Brule 会给出“腋窝臭就涂点醋”之类荒唐的健康建议，末了再补一句：“……为了你的健康！”

source.text: Sticking to It

translation.text: 棍子的文字游戏

source.text: Another Japanese semi-proverb that I really like is “the weaker the dog, the more it barks”

translation.text: 还有一句近似谚语的日语说法，我也很喜欢：“越弱的狗，叫得越凶。”

source.text: The main character’s initial weapon is a simple wooden stick. In English, the stick’s description is:

translation.text: 主角最初的武器是一根普通木棍。英文版对它的说明是：

source.text: Its bark is worse than its bite.

translation.text: Its bark is worse than its bite.（叫声比咬人更凶。）

source.text: This is a groaningly simple pun on the word “bark” – as in “tree bark” – and the dog-themed English idiom, “its bark is worse than its bite”.

translation.text: 这是个简单得让人想叹气的双关：bark 既指“树皮”，也指“狗叫”，而 its bark is worse than its bite 是一句形容“叫得凶、咬得轻”的英语习语。

source.text: This English-language joke would be lost in a straightforward translation, so the localizers replaced it with a simple joke about a Japanese proverb:

translation.text: 这个英文笑话直译成日文就会失效，因此译者换成了一个取材于日语谚语的小笑话，日版大意是：

source.text: Dogs on walks often run into these.

translation.text: Dogs on walks often run into these.（散步的狗经常撞上它们。）

source.text: This is a comedic reference to one of the most famous proverbs in the Japanese language: “even a dog runs into a stick/pole when walking”. Originally, this proverb meant something like “if you’re too forward, you’ll meet with disaster”, but it has since gained the separate meaning of “nothing ventured, nothing gained”.

translation.text: 这里打趣的是日语中最有名的谚语之一：“狗走路也会撞到棍子／柱子。”它原本的意思近似于“过于冒进，就会遭殃”，后来又衍生出了另一层意思：“不去冒险，就不会有所收获。”

source.text: This dog proverb is why so many things in Japan show dogs walking into sticks and poles

translation.text: 正因为这句关于狗的谚语，日本才有那么多狗走路撞上棍子和柱子的形象。

source.text: I don’t think I’ve ever seen a dog walk into a stick or pole in real life, now that I think about it

translation.text: 仔细想想，我在现实中好像从没见过狗走路撞上棍子或柱子。

source.text: Ruins

translation.text: 遗迹

source.text: Peculiar Pies

translation.text: 奇特的派

source.text: I wonder if any ~ especially zealous fans have made snail pie after seeing it referenced in Undertale, similar to how EarthBound fans have made real-life trout yogurt

translation.text: 不知道有没有特别热情的粉丝在 Undertale 中见到蜗牛派后，真的动手做了一份，就像 EarthBound 的粉丝做出了现实版鳟鱼酸奶一样。

source.text: Toriel suggests that she was considering baking "snail pie" to celebrate the main character’s arrival. This outlandish-sounding dish is a reference to Illusion of Gaia, one of Toby’s favorite Japanese games from the mid-1990s.

translation.text: Toriel 说，她原本考虑烤一个“蜗牛派”来庆祝主角的到来。这道听起来很古怪的菜，出自 Toby 喜爱的日本游戏 Illusion of Gaia，发行于20世纪90年代中期。

source.text: The Undertale translator encountered an unexpected problem when translating this line, however: the original Japanese version of Illusion of Gaia never mentioned "snail pie" - it was originally just "meat pie", which doesn't sound nearly as bizarre or memorable.

translation.text: 不过，Undertale 的译者翻译这句台词时遇到了意想不到的问题：Illusion of Gaia 的日文原版根本没有“蜗牛派”，原本只是“肉派”，远没有那么古怪，也没那么令人难忘。

source.text: I feel that calling it ~ "meat pie with whipped cream on top" would make the Illusion of Gaia reference recognizable, but then the snail connection to Toriel's book later on would be lost

translation.text: 我觉得叫它“上面浇了鲜奶油的肉派”，或许能让人认出 Illusion of Gaia 的梗，但这样就失去了与 Toriel 后面那本书之间的蜗牛联系。

source.text: Because Toby's original "snail pie" reference would be lost on Japanese Undertale players, the translator had to make a choice:

translation.text: 日本 Undertale 玩家无法领会 Toby 原本的“蜗牛派”梗，因此译者需要作出选择：

source.text: Leave it as "snail pie" in Japanese, which would avoid the need to write all-new text when Torie! later quotes a book called 72 Uses for Snails

translation.text: 日文继续用“蜗牛派”，这样 Toriel 后面引用《蜗牛的72种用途》时，就不用重写那些引文。

source.text: Use "meat pie" to stay consistent with the original Illusion ofG aia reference and write all-new text for the 72 Uses for Snails quotes, even though the reference would be almost impossible to recognize

translation.text: 改用“肉派”，与 Illusion of Gaia 的原始出处一致，并重写《蜗牛的72种用途》的引文——尽管玩家几乎不可能认出这个梗。

source.text: Force some other bizarre food reference into the line and write all-new text for the 72 Uses for Snails quotes

translation.text: 硬塞入另一种古怪食物的梗，并重写《蜗牛的72种用途》的引文。

source.text: The localization team weighed the options and chose to keep it "snail pie" in the Japanese script.

translation.text: 本地化团队权衡各个方案后，决定在日文剧本中保留“蜗牛派”。

source.text: As a translation student, I was taught the importance of studying influential literature to broaden my knowledge base. I think the same is equally as important for entertainment translation, except you'd have to study hundreds of movies, play hundreds of games, and so on. I wonder if any universities out there study game translations the same way they study literary translations.

translation.text: 学习翻译时，老师告诉我，要阅读有影响力的文学作品，拓宽知识面。我觉得娱乐作品的翻译也一样重要，只不过需要研究几百部电影、玩几百款游戏，诸如此类。不知道有没有大学会像研究文学翻译那样，研究游戏翻译。

source.text: Inspiration Spotlight: Illusion of Gaia

translation.text: 灵感聚焦：Illusion of Gaia

source.text: In 1993, Enix released a Super Famicom action role-playing game known as Gaia Gensōki ("Gaia Fantasy Chronicle") in Japan. An English version debuted as Illusion of Gaia in North America in 1994, and as Illusion of Time in Europe in 1995. The English script features many translation mishaps and unusual localization choices that remain memorable to this day.

translation.text: 1993年，Enix 在日本推出了 Super Famicom 动作角色扮演游戏 Gaia Gensōki（《盖亚幻想纪》）。英语版于1994年以 Illusion of Gaia 为名在北美发行，1995年又以 Illusion of Time 为名在欧洲发行。英文剧本中有不少翻译失误和不寻常的本地化选择，至今仍令人难忘。

source.text: The game sends the teenage hero to many real-world locations in his quest to save humankind from a great evil. The hero gains abilities and powerful alter egos, leading to a climactic battle in space.

translation.text: 少年英雄为战胜邪恶、拯救人类，前往许多现实地点，获得新能力与强大的变身形态，最终在太空决战。

source.text: Ruins

translation.text: 遗迹

source.text: Another Skeleton Pun

translation.text: 又一个骷髅双关

source.text: You know how in ~ fighting games, characters have different stats like speed, strength, etc.? Translators have stats too, and one is "good at translating bad jokes"

translation.text: 格斗游戏里的角色都有速度、力量等不同属性，对吧？译者也有属性，其中一项就是“擅长翻译冷笑话”。

source.text: Another skeleton pun is found in Toriel's home. In English, the joke replaces the word "lonely" with a bone-themed rhyme:

translation.text: Toriel 家里还有一个骷髅双关。英语笑话把 lonely（孤独）换成了一个押韵、又带有 bone（骨头）的词：

source.text: Why did the skeleton want a friend? Because she was feeling BONELY ..

translation.text:
Why did the skeleton want a friend? Because she was feeling BONELY...
骷髅为什么想交朋友？因为她觉得 BONELY……

source.text: This joke would be lost in a literal translation, so the translator replaced it with a different Japanese joke:

translation.text: 直译会丢掉这个笑话，所以译者换了一个日语笑话：

source.text: Why'd the skeleton want a friend? Because the loneliness pierced to the bone ...

translation.text: 骷髅为什么想交朋友？因为寂寞已经深入骨髓……

source.text: As we can see, the setup to the joke is the same in Japanese, and the punchline manages to stay groaningly close to the original.

translation.text: 日语保留了相同的铺垫，包袱也紧贴原作，一样冷得令人叹气。

source.text: Snake Snack

translation.text: 蛇点心

source.text: To access the game's Hard Mode, start a new game, then give yourself a certain human's name ...

translation.text: 想进入游戏的困难模式，就新开一局，再给自己取某个人类的名字……

source.text: A snake-haired enemy named Parsnik appears in the ruins during Underta/e's secret Hard Mode. In the English version, a battle option titled "Snack" becomes available during this encounter. Occasionally, Parsnik mishears this "snack" as "snake", then aggressively offers "tasty snakes" to the player.

translation.text: Undertale 隐藏的困难模式中，遗迹会出现蛇发敌人 Parsnik。英语版战斗中有“Snack”（点心）选项。Parsnik 偶尔听成 snake（蛇），便气势汹汹地向玩家奉上“美味的蛇”。

source.text: The translator localized this wordplay by having Parsnik offer "Hebi Star Noodles" in Japanese. This name plays with the words hebi ("snake") and bebī ("baby") to humorously refer to Baby Star Ramen, a famous Japanese snack. Second, the noodles in Baby Star Ramen roughly look like countless baby snakes. The result is a snake-themed snack joke that parallels the original line in a uniquely Japanese way.

translation.text: 日文中，译者让 Parsnik 奉上“Hebi Star Noodles”（蛇星面），用 hebi（蛇）和 bebī（婴儿）的近音，打趣日本知名零食 Baby Star Ramen（童星拉面）。这种点心的面条也像无数条小蛇。这样便以日本特有的方式，重现了原文的蛇点心笑话。

source.text: Baby Star Ramen, popular since the 1950s, is made of squiggly, crunchy noodles

translation.text: Baby Star Ramen 自20世纪50年代流行至今，是一种弯曲酥脆的面条零食。

source.text: Possessive Parsnik Pun

translation.text: Parsnik 的所有格双关

source.text: Given Toby's fondness for including Internet jokes in the English script, this Japanese localization choice turned out to be surprisingly fitting

translation.text: Toby 本来就喜欢在英文剧本中塞入网络笑话，因此这个日语本地化选择意外地合拍。

source.text: In the English game, Parsnik utters snake sounds such as "hissss" during battle. On rare occasion, though, Parsnik will instead say "herssss" - a surprise play on the words "his" and "hers". This joke would be lost in a literal translation, so the translator replaced it with a completely different Japanese joke.

translation.text: 英语版中，Parsnik 战斗时会发出“hissss”一类的蛇嘶声。但偶尔它会改说“herssss”，突然拿 his（他的）和 hers（她的）开个玩笑。直译会丢掉这个笑话，于是译者换成了一个完全不同的日语笑话。

source.text: In Japanese, snakes make a "shaaaa" sound when they hiss, so Parsnik normally says shaaaa during battle. Parsnik's alternate hissing sound was localized as pyaaaa, which rhymes with shaaaa and refers to a legendary Japanese message board post involving a funny face shouting "pyaaaa" for no clear reason.

translation.text: 日语中，蛇的嘶声是 shaaaa，Parsnik 战斗时也通常如此。另一声则译成 pyaaaa，与 shaaaa 押韵，还引用了日本论坛上的传奇帖子：一个滑稽表情莫名其妙地大喊“pyaaaa”。

source.text: The Power of Pyaaaa

translation.text: Pyaaaa 的威力

source.text: In 2009, a user on a popular Japanese message board started a new message thread titled "Let's Reveal Our Real Names in this Thread". The thread began with this post:

translation.text: 2009年，日本一个热门论坛的用户发起了题为“在这个帖子里公布我们的真名吧”的讨论，开场是这样一条帖子：

source.text: Okay, here goes! I’m Yuya Sato （｀ェ´） pyaaa!

translation.text:
好，那我先来！
我叫 Yuya Sato（｀ェ´）pyaaa！

source.text: Because staying anonymous was central to this message board's culture, the very premise of the thread was ridiculous. The result: over a thousand replies of "I'm Yuya Sato too, pyaaaa!", "What a coincidence, I'm Yuya Sato too!", and other sarcastic remarks.

translation.text: 匿名是这个论坛文化的核心，因此帖子的出发点本身就很荒唐。结果出现了上千条“我也叫 Yuya Sato，pyaaaa！”“真巧，我也叫 Yuya Sato！”之类的调侃回复。

source.text: The sheer silliness of the thread, its content, and its enormous response transformed the original post into a Japanese Internet legend. To this day, comical references to Yuya Sato's post and nonsensical shout can be seen on Japanese websites and in Japanese entertainment.

translation.text: 帖子及内容的荒诞，加上海量回应，让原帖成了日本网络传奇。直到今天，日本网站和娱乐作品仍会拿 Yuya Sato 的帖子和那声莫名其妙的喊叫开玩笑。

source.text: Ruins

translation.text: 遗迹

source.text: Abbreviated Items

translation.text: 物品名称的缩写

source.text: "Butterscotch Pie" is ~ humorously abbreviated as "ButtsPie" in English, but is left full-length in Japanese

translation.text: “Butterscotch Pie”（奶油糖派）在英语中被戏谑地缩成“ButtsPie”（屁股派），日语则保留全名。

source.text: In the English version of Undertale, every item has three names: a standard name that can be quite long, an abbreviated name for battle menus, and an abbreviated name for battle menus during serious scenes.

translation.text: 英语版 Undertale 中，每件物品都有三个名字：可能很长的标准名、战斗菜单中的缩写名，以及严肃场景下战斗菜单专用的缩写名。

source.text: It's not obvious at first, but these abbreviated names serve multiple functions:

translation.text: 这些缩写名乍看不起眼，其实有多种用途：

source.text: l. Some names need to be shortened to fit in the limited text space

translation.text: 1. 有些名字需要缩短，才能放进有限的文字空间。

source.text: 2. The shortened names are a parody of the odd name abbreviations found in old Japanese-to-English game localizations

translation.text: 2. 缩写名模仿了早期日本游戏英文本地化中那些古怪的名称缩写。

source.text: 3. Toby wanted some items to have intentionally funny abbreviations

translation.text: 3. Toby 想让某些物品的缩写名故意显得滑稽。

source.text: As an example of the third function, "Butterscotch Pie" is normally abbreviated as the humorous "ButtsPie" in battle. But to avoid ruining the mood during serious scenes, Toby implemented the second set of "serious" abbreviations. Thus "ButtsPie" becomes "Pie" during important battles.

translation.text: 第三种用途的例子是“Butterscotch Pie”：通常战斗中会缩成滑稽的“ButtsPie”。但为了不破坏严肃场景的气氛，Toby 又做了第二套“严肃”缩写。因此在重要战斗中，“ButtsPie”就变成了“Pie”（派）。

source.text: In serious battles, ~ "Butterscotch Pie" is instead abbreviated as "Pie" in English, while the name remains its full length in Japanese

translation.text: 严肃战斗中，“Butterscotch Pie”在英语里改缩为“Pie”，而日语依然保留全名。

source.text: Although name abbreviations were common in old games localized into English, such abbreviations weren't as pervasive in Japanese-language games - after all, it's easy to say a lot in Japanese with only a few characters. So although the two extra sets of abbreviated names made sense for the English release, there was no strong reason to implement them in the Japanese version.

translation.text: 名称缩写在旧游戏的英语本地化中很常见，日语游戏却没有这么普遍，毕竟日语用几个字就很容易表达许多信息。因此，两套额外的缩写名在英语版中有意义，日语版却没有充分的理由照搬。

source.text: With this in mind, Toby and the localization team decided to only use one set of full-length Japanese item names. This new approach meant that the original two-column item menu needed to be reprogrammed into a one-column item menu with a scrollbar. And because the player can switch between the English and Japanese versions of the game at any time, all of this new program code needed to safely coexist with the original game's code.

translation.text: 考虑到这一点，Toby 和本地化团队决定，日文物品名称只保留一套全名。这就需要重新编程，把原来的双栏物品菜单改成带滚动条的单栏菜单。而玩家又可以随时切换游戏的英语版和日语版，所以所有新增代码都必须能与原版代码安全共存。

source.text: In short, the English and Japanese versions of Undertale treat item names quite differently, while also following the expectations of their specific audiences.

translation.text: 总的来说，Undertale 的英语版和日语版以截然不同的方式处理物品名称，也都符合各自玩家的预期。

pages.title: 老游戏翻译中的文字缩写

source.text: Text Abbreviations in Retro Game Translations

translation.text: 老游戏翻译中的文字缩写

source.text: In general, Japanese words can be written with fewer characters than English words. This difference often requires English text to be abbreviated in Japanese-to-English game translations. Such abbreviation filled games were especially common in Japanese RPGs translated during the 1990s. Naturally, heavy text abbreviations can lead to confusion, unintentional laughs, or even complete loss of meaning.

translation.text: 一般来说，日语词汇所需的字符比英语少。因此，日本游戏译成英语时，经常不得不缩写英文。这种满是缩写的游戏，在20世纪90年代翻译的日本 RPG 中尤其常见。大量缩写自然可能造成困惑、无心的笑料，甚至让原意完全丢失。

source.text: Phantasy Star (Master System, 1988)

translation.text:
Phantasy Star
（Master System，1988）

source.text: Final Fantasy (NES, 1990)

translation.text:
Final Fantasy
（NES，1990）

source.text: The 7th Saga (Super NE S, 1993)

source.text: Presenting Sans

translation.text: Sans 登场

source.text: Random trivia: A web comic about a skeleton named "Helvetica" inspired Toby to name Undertale's skeletons after fonts too

translation.text: 冷知识：一部以名为“Helvetica”的骷髅为主角的网络漫画，启发 Toby 也用字体给 Undertale 的骷髅命名。

source.text: A goofy skeleton named Sans plays a major role in Undertale. His name comes from a popular - and notorious - English computer font known as "Comic Sans". Unsurprisingly, Sans' English dialogue text uses the Comic Sans font.

translation.text: 名叫 Sans 的滑稽骷髅在 Undertale 中扮演着重要角色。他的名字来自一种很流行、也臭名昭著的英文电脑字体“Comic Sans”。不出所料，Sans 的英语台词用的正是 Comic Sans 字体。

source.text: Before he released Undertale in English, Toby already hoped to release a Japanese version of the game someday. But he was concerned that the connection between the name "Sans" and the English "Comic Sans" font might be lost on Japanese players. For this reason, 8-4’s localization team initially suggested naming Sans "Pop", in reference to a similarly popular-but-notorious Japanese font known as "Sōeikaku Pop-tai".

translation.text: 在 Undertale 英语版发行之前，Toby 就希望有朝一日推出日语版。但他担心日本玩家无法理解“Sans”这个名字与英文字体“Comic Sans”之间的联系。因此，8-4 的本地化团队最初建议把 Sans 改名为“Pop”，对应同样流行、同样恶名在外的日文字体“Sōeikaku Pop-tai”。

source.text: LEFT: Toby asks me about bad Japanese fonts in 2015, before Undertale's English release

translation.text: 左：2015年，Undertale 英语版发行前，Toby 向我打听难看的日文字体。

source.text: RIGHT: Sans is referred to as "Pop" in an early draft of the Japanese localization

translation.text: 右：日语本地化早期稿件中的 Sans 被叫作“Pop”。

source.text: The name "Pop" had drawbacks, however: early fans were already attached to Sans' name, the Siieikaku Pop-tai font was a slightly more professional font than Comic Sans, and the name had a very different ring to it. So it wasn't too surprising when the team decided to revert "Pop" back to "Sans" a few months before the Japanese game's release.

translation.text: 不过，“Pop”也有缺点：早期粉丝已经对 Sans 的名字产生了感情，Sōeikaku Pop-tai 比 Comic Sans 略显专业，而且新名字听起来很不一样。因此，团队在日语版发行前几个月决定把“Pop”改回“Sans”，也就并不令人意外了。

source.text: Because Undertale relies so much on different fonts and font-related jokes, Japanese fans have had a lot to say about the official localization's font choices. This is good example of how the localization process, by its very nature, can produce new, significant debate over matters that never concerned the original audience.

translation.text: Undertale 大量运用不同字体及字体相关的笑话，因此日本粉丝对官方本地化的字体选择有许多意见。这很好地说明，本地化过程本身就可能让原版受众从未在意的问题，变成新的重大争论。

source.text: The Comic Sans computer font was designed to approximate the lettering style used in English-language comic books such as this one

translation.text: Comic Sans 电脑字体的设计，模仿了这类英语漫画中的手写字风格。

source.text: Casual use of Comic Sans is rampant and can sometimes come across as wildly unsuitable

translation.text: Comic Sans 被随意滥用，有时显得极不合适。

source.text: The Sōeikaku Pop-tai font was designed for Japanese POP (point of purchase) signs and in-store promo materials.

translation.text: Sōeikaku Pop-tai 字体为日本的 POP（卖场广告）标牌及店内宣传材料而设计。

source.text: Sōeikaku Pop-tai is often poorly used - here it’s on a city notice about a recent series of arsons and crimes.

translation.text: Sōeikaku Pop-tai 也经常用得不妥，例如这里一则涉及近期接连发生的纵火和犯罪的市政告示。

translation.text: 雪镇

pages.title: Sans 一开口，日本震惊了

source.text: Sans Speaks, Japan is Shocked

translation.text: Sans 一开口，日本震惊了

source.text: Sans uses the personal pronoun オイラ (oira) in the final Japanese script.

translation.text: 最终日文剧本中，Sans 用“オイラ”（oira，我）自称。

source.text: Before translating Sans' dialogue into Japanese, the translator had to decide which of the many Japanese personal pronouns best fit Sans' character.

translation.text: 把 Sans 的台词译成日语之前，译者必须先从众多日语人称代词中，选出最适合他的一个。

source.text: After consulting with Toby, the translator settled on oira for Sans' pronoun. In everyday Japanese, oira gives off a "rural, unsophisticated bumpkin" vibe, but in entertainment it's also used by aloof, happy-go-lucky characters. It's important to note that this choice clashed with the existing fan-made translations, in which Sans used the more assertive pronoun ore.

translation.text: 与 Toby 商量后，译者选择让 Sans 用 oira 自称。在日常日语中，oira 带有“来自乡下、不谙世故的乡巴佬”的感觉，但娱乐作品里也会让超然、随和的角色使用它。这与已有的粉丝翻译产生了冲突：那些版本让 Sans 用语气更强势的 ore（我）。

source.text: In 2017, 8-4 announced details about Underta/e's upcoming Japanese release. This announcement included a video of Sans using oira. Fans accustomed to the fan-made translations reacted loudly to this unexpected pronoun choice - some responded with intense negativity, some responded with bewilderment, and others responded with humor. Online reactions grew so intense that the incident was quickly dubbed the "Oira Shock".

translation.text: 2017年，8-4 公布了 Undertale 即将推出日语版的详情，其中有一段 Sans 使用 oira 的视频。习惯了粉丝译版的玩家对这个出人意料的自称反应强烈：有人激烈反对，有人困惑，也有人拿它开玩笑。网上反响越来越大，这件事很快被称为“Oira Shock”（Oira 冲击）。

source.text: Despite the massive response to Sans' new pronoun, the team stuck with oira for several reasons:

translation.text: 尽管 Sans 的新自称引发了巨大反响，团队还是坚持使用 oira，理由有几个：

source.text: Oira seems fitting for Sans' normal, laid-back, wisecracking personality

translation.text: • oira 似乎很适合 Sans 平时悠闲、爱说俏皮话的性格。

source.text: Sans' all-lowercase text gives him a distinctive, carefree vibe that's lost in translation, so giving him a similarly distinctive pronoun felt like a natural replacement

translation.text: • Sans 全小写的台词营造出独特、无拘无束的感觉，翻成日语会丢失这一点；给他一个同样特别的自称，是自然的弥补。

source.text: Using oira in normal situations allows Sans to switch to the more intense ore when he turns deadly serious later on

translation.text: • 平时用 oira，后面变得极其严肃时，就能切换成更有力度的 ore。

source.text: Sans' use of oira in the final Japanese release actually came as two simultaneous shocks. First, it indicated that Toby had indeed given oira his stamp of approval. Second, it conflicted with Toby's statement from years earlier that Sans seemed like the type of character to use the pronoun boku. As a result of all of this, Sans' pronoun was - and still is - a serious and unique issue among Japanese fans.

translation.text: Sans 在最终日语版中使用 oira，其实同时带来了两重冲击。首先，这表明 Toby 确实认可了 oira。其次，这与 Toby 几年前的说法相矛盾：他当时觉得 Sans 像是会用 boku（我）自称的角色。因此，Sans 的自称在日本粉丝中成了一个严肃而独特的话题，直到现在仍是如此。

source.text: Reactions to Sans' use of oira made waves online almost immediately - here we see "oira" and "sans' pronoun" trending across all of Japan (left), in Tokyo (middle), and in Osaka (right)

translation.text: Sans 用 oira（我）自称的消息几乎立刻在网上掀起波澜。这里的“oira”和“Sans 的自称”同时登上日本全国（左）、东京（中）和大阪（右）的热门话题榜。

source.text: The phrase "Oira Shock" was mostly a joke name that went viral - genuine "shock" events in Japanese include the "Lehman Shock" (the 2008 global financial crisis) and the "Corona Shock" (the rise of the 2020 coronavirus pandemic)

translation.text: “Oira 冲击”主要是个广为传播的戏称。日语里真正被称为“冲击”的事件包括“雷曼冲击”（2008年全球金融危机）和“新冠冲击”（2020年新冠疫情暴发）。

source.text: The news of Sans' oira pronoun led to a deluge of fan art depicting Sans as a country bumpkin or farmer

translation.text: Sans 使用 oira 的消息，催生了大量把他画成乡巴佬或农民的同人画。

source.text: Reports of Japanese fan reactions even hit English-language video game news sites

translation.text: 日本粉丝的反应甚至登上了英语游戏新闻网站。

source.text: Snowdin

translation.text: 雪镇

pages.title: 玩家对 Oira 冲击的反应

source.text: Oira Shock Reactions

translation.text: 玩家对 Oira 冲击的反应

source.text: Japanese Undertale fans responded with fervor after learning that Sans uses the pronoun oira in the official Japanese release. Here are a handful of randomly selected fan comments, translated into English:

translation.text: 得知日语官方版中 Sans 用 oira（我）自称后，日本 Undertale 粉丝反应激烈。下面随机摘选了几条粉丝评论，由作者译为英语：

source.text: '' Guess I'll have to stick with the unofficial translation. Oh, my dear Sans, usingoira ...

translation.text: 看来我只能继续用非官方翻译了。唉，我亲爱的 Sans 居然用 oira……

source.text: '' After watching the controversy over Sans' pronoun, I've come to the conclusion that "oira Sans" might be pretty cool after all. In fact, maybe Sans could be the leading example ofc ool guys who use oira!

translation.text: 看完围绕 Sans 自称的争论，我觉得“oira Sans”说不定挺酷的。甚至可以让 Sans 成为使用 oira 的帅哥代表！

source.text: '' No, this isn't right, Sans can't use oira. He's not Sans-like unless he uses ore.

translation.text: 不，不对，Sans 不能用 oira。他不用 ore（我），就不像 Sans。

source.text: '' That's some good work from the translation team! I think having oira as his normal pronoun works great with his personality shift later.

translation.text: 翻译团队干得好！我觉得平时用 oira，与他后来的性格变化配合得很棒。

source.text: '' I'm really happy an official translation is being released. But I don't think I'll ever get used to Sans saying oira

translation.text: 能出官方翻译我真的很高兴。但我觉得自己永远习惯不了 Sans 说 oira。

source.text: '' At first I was shocked when I learned that he uses oira, but after seeing him use it in official screenshots it really clicked with me

translation.text: 刚知道他用 oira 时，我很震惊；但在官方截图里看到他这样说，就觉得完全说得通了。

source.text: Sans Laughs

translation.text: Sans 的笑声

source.text: Laughter doesn't always translate perfectly between languages, so localizers sometimes need to adjust the way characters laugh to sound more natural in the target language. As an example, Sans' standard "heheh" laugh in the English script was tweaked on a per-scene basis to match the different moods Toby had intended:

translation.text: 笑声并不总能在语言之间直接照搬，所以本地化人员有时需要调整角色的笑法，让它在目标语言中更自然。例如，英语剧本中 Sans 惯常的“heheh”，就按场景逐一调整，以贴合 Toby 想要的不同气氛：

source.text: Sans' friendly "heheh" was localized into Japanese with a friendly "haha"

translation.text: Sans 友善的“heheh”（嘿嘿），在日语中改成了同样友善的“haha”（哈哈）。

source.text: Sans' less friendly "heh heh heh" was left as-is, because it shares the same vibe in tenser scenes

translation.text: Sans 不太友善的“heh heh heh”（嘿、嘿、嘿）原样保留，因为在紧张场景中，两种语言给人的感觉相同。

source.text: Sans' gleefully dark "heheheh" was localized as "hee hee hee hee" in Japanese to match the tone of the scene

translation.text: Sans 带着阴暗快意的“heheheh”，在日语中改成“hee hee hee hee”（嘻嘻嘻嘻），以符合场景的基调。

source.text: Other characters had their laughter similarly fine-tuned for tone and context too, as we'll continue to see.

translation.text: 其他角色的笑声也根据语气和语境作了类似的微调，后面还会见到。

source.text: Japanese Personal Pronouns: oira

translation.text: 日语人称代词：oira

source.text: Traditionally, the Japanese personal pronoun oira suggests that the speaker is from a rural or uncultured area. Oira is slowly fading from everyday use, however, and is used far less commonly than pronouns like watashi, boku, and ore.

translation.text: 传统上，日语人称代词 oira（我）暗示说话者来自乡下或文化不发达的地方。不过，oira 正逐渐淡出日常用语，远不如 watashi、boku、ore 这些表示“我”的代词常用。

source.text: In modern Japanese entertainment, oira can still be used to lend characters a rural, unsophisticated vibe, but oira is more commonly associated with lovable rascals, rambunctious pranksters, and friendly mascots. Other fictional characters who use oira include:

translation.text: 现代日本娱乐作品仍会用 oira 赋予角色乡土、质朴的气息，但它更常让人想到讨人喜欢的小淘气、活泼的捣蛋鬼和亲切的吉祥物。其他用 oira 自称的虚构角色包括：

source.text: Shishimaru (Oira wa Shishimaru)

translation.text:
Shishimaru
（Oira wa Shishimaru）
