source.text: Canine Clowning

translation.text: 狗狗的玩笑

source.text: We've seen how easy it ~ is for things to get lost in translation, so this line's localization is a truly impressive feat!

translation.text: 我们已经见过，信息在翻译中多么容易丢失。因此，这句台词的本地化实在令人佩服！

source.text: During the battle against the two lovey-dovey guard dogs, Dogamy says:

translation.text: 与那对卿卿我我的守卫犬战斗时，Dogamy 说：

source.text: Take my wife. .. 's fleas.

translation.text: Take my wife...’s fleas.（把我老婆……身上的跳蚤带走。）

source.text: This is a parody of a classic joke by Henny Youngman that has remained in the public consciousness for nearly a century:

translation.text: 这改写了 Henny Youngman 一个流传近百年的经典笑话：

source.text: I can never understand women. Now, take my wife ... please!

translation.text:
我永远搞不懂女人。就拿我老婆来说……请把她带走吧！
（take my wife：拿老婆举例／把老婆带走；please“请”近 fleas“跳蚤”。）

source.text: In other words, the original English line contains a joke and a reference, is marriage-themed, and involves dogs.

translation.text: 原版台词既有笑话又有典故，围绕婚姻，也与狗有关。

source.text: LEFT: Dogamy's English line is a reference to a 1930s joke

translation.text: 左：Dogamy 的英语台词引用了一个20世纪30年代的笑话。

source.text: RIGHT: Dogamy's Japanese line is a reference to a 201 Os manga about a wife whose husband reincarnates as a dog, and together they solve crimes

translation.text: 右：日语台词引用了一部2010年代的漫画：一位妻子的丈夫转世成狗，两人一起破案。

source.text: This multi-layered line of dialogue would be flattened in a literal translation into Japanese, so the translator replaced the original reference with the Japanese phrase teishu genki de inu ga ii ("it’s good to have a husband who is healthy and a dog"). This new phrase is a reference to a Japanese manga series of the same name and is a play on the idiom teishu genki de rusu ga ii ("it’s good to have a husband who is healthy and away").

translation.text: 这句有多层含义的台词直译成日语，就会失去层次。因此译者把原本的典故换成日语 teishu genki de inu ga ii（丈夫健康、又是条狗就好）。这句话来自同名日本漫画，又改写了惯用语 teishu genki de rusu ga ii（丈夫健康、不在家就好）。

source.text: By replacing the original reference, the translator was able to preserve every layer of meaning found in Dogamy's English line. In other words, the .Japanese line also contains a joke and a reference, is marriage-themed, and involves dogs.

translation.text: 更换典故后，译者保住了 Dogamy 英语台词中的每一层含义。日语台词同样既有笑话又有典故，既涉及婚姻，又与狗有关。

source.text: Raisin Brand

translation.text: 葡萄干的牌子

source.text: They don't train you for raisin puns in translation school, you just have to master it on your own for some raisin

translation.text: 翻译学校可不教你葡萄干双关。不知出于什么“raisin”（葡萄干，谐音 reason“原因”），你只能靠自己掌握。

source.text: A sentry station belonging to a guard dog is empty, except for a strange box of raisins. The English script refers to this box as a "box of pomeraisins", a play on the words "Pomeranian" and "raisin".

translation.text: 某只守卫犬的哨所空空荡荡，只留着一盒奇怪的葡萄干。英文剧本把它叫作“a box of pomeraisins”，将 Pomeranian（博美犬）与 raisin（葡萄干）拼在一起。

source.text: Although the words "Pomeranian" and "raisin" exist in Japanese too, the "ra" parts are pronounced differently:

translation.text: 日语也借用了“Pomeranian”和“raisin”，但两者中“ra”的读音不同：

source.text: The "ra" in "Pomeranian" is pronounced like "rah" in Japanese

translation.text: • “Pomeranian”的“ra”，在日语中读作近似“rah”的音。

source.text: The "ra" in "raisin" is pronounced like "reh" in Japanese

translation.text: • “raisin”的“ra”，在日语中读作近似“reh”的音。

source.text: This is a non-raisin-related Pomeranian

translation.text: 这是一只与葡萄干无关的博美犬。

source.text: The localization team debated whether or not to keep this slightly broken Japanese wordplay as-is, even with the inconsistent vowel sounds. The team eventually chose the name inu jirushi rēzun ("dog-labeled raisins") to ensure that players will know exactly what the item is.

translation.text: 本地化团队讨论过，要不要无视元音差异，原样保留这个在日语里略显不顺的文字游戏。最终，团队选择了 inu jirushi rēzun（狗牌葡萄干），确保玩家清楚这究竟是什么物品。

source.text: The original "pomeraisin" pun probably would've worked pretty well in Japanese, but the localization team went with a different approach

translation.text: 原本的“pomeraisin”双关在日语里大概也能有不错的效果，不过本地化团队选了另一条路。

source.text: This "pomeraisin" issue comes up one other time in the English script, when un-decorating a monster named Gyftrot:

translation.text: 英文剧本还有一处“pomeraisin”相关的台词：为名叫 Gyftrot 的怪物拆掉身上的装饰时，会出现：

source.text: You remove the box of non-dog-related raisins.

translation.text: 你取下了那盒与狗无关的葡萄干。

source.text: Because this is a box of raisins rather than a box of pomeraisins, the Japanese line became:

translation.text: 因为这是一盒普通 raisins，而不是 pomeraisins，所以日语台词变成了：

source.text: You removed the box of" non-dog-labeled raisins".

translation.text: 你取下了那盒“非狗牌葡萄干”。

source.text: Understandably, the choice to remove the original Pomeranian/raisin joke surprised some Japanese players, particularly those already familiar with the English script.

translation.text: 移除原本博美犬与葡萄干双关的决定，让一些日本玩家感到意外，尤其是那些已经熟悉英文剧本的玩家。这也不难理解。

source.text: Snowdin

translation.text: 雪镇

source.text: Snow Much Fun

translation.text: 雪趣横生

source.text: "Snowful" is an • example of how a single name change can lead to a domino effect that requires a variety of other changes in other places

translation.text: “Snowful”说明，改一个名字也可能引发连锁反应，迫使其他地方跟着作出种种调整。

source.text: The first town in Undertale is known as "Snowdin" in the English script. Toby chose this name for several reasons:

translation.text: Undertale 中的第一座小镇，在英文剧本中叫“Snowdin”。Toby 选择这个名字，有几个原因：

source.text: It's a play on the phrase "snowed in"

translation.text: • 它谐音 snowed in（被雪困住）。

source.text: It allows the inn to be called "Snowed Inn", another play on "snowed in"

translation.text: • 旅馆因而可以叫“Snowed Inn”，以 inn（旅馆）再玩一次 snowed in 的双关。

source.text: The "din" part at the end gives it a town-like feeling

translation.text: • 末尾的“din”让它听起来像个镇名。

source.text: Because this "Snowdin" name carries extra meanings that would be lost in Japanese, the localization team renamed the town "Snowful". This new name seems like an arbitrary change at first, but it offered its own unique wordplay:

translation.text: “Snowdin”这些额外含义在日语中会丢失，因此本地化团队把小镇改名为“Snowful”。乍看像是随意改名，却有自己独特的文字游戏：

source.text: Japanese players would recognize the play on the words "snow" and "full"

translation.text: • 日本玩家可以看出 snow（雪）与 full（满）的组合。

source.text: In Japanese, "Snowful" is written sunofuru, a combination of the English word "snow" and the Japanese verb furu ("to rain/snow/fall from the sky")

translation.text: • “Snowful”用日语读写为 sunōfuru，由英语 snow 与日语动词 furu（下雨、下雪、从天而降）组合而成。

source.text: This small localization change required more work than one might expect, however, as the town's welcome sign exists as part of the game's map data rather than the game's text data. The progTammer had to account for this to ensure that the proper sign is loaded based on the user's language preference.

translation.text: 不过，这个小小的本地化改动，工作量比想象中更大。小镇的欢迎标牌属于地图数据，而非文字数据。程序员必须处理这一点，才能根据玩家选择的语言加载正确的标牌。

source.text: Get Inn or Get Out

translation.text: 进店还是出门

source.text: Reader Challenge #4: • Come up with an alternate name for the "Snowed Inn" that retains the snowy theme and contains a pun!

translation.text: 读者挑战④：给“Snowed Inn”想一个替代名字，既保留雪的主题，又包含双关！

source.text: In the English version of Undertale, Snowdin's inn is aptly named the "Snowed Inn". Toby knew this pun would likely be lost in translation, so he suggested an alternative name: "Snowtel". The translator agreed that this combination of the English words "snow" and "hotel" would be more recognizable to Japanese players. However, this change also meant that that English-speaking players and Japanese-speaking players would know the same place by a different name.

translation.text: 英语版 Undertale 中，Snowdin 的旅馆恰如其分地叫作“Snowed Inn”。Toby 知道这个双关很可能在翻译中丢失，于是建议替代名称“Snowtel”。译者也认为，把英语 snow（雪）与 hotel（旅馆）组合起来，更容易让日本玩家理解。不过，这一改动也意味着，英语玩家和日语玩家会用不同名字称呼同一个地方。

source.text: Overdue-ing It

translation.text: 图书馆的错字

source.text: Similar to the "Snowdin" town sign, the localization team had to add extra programming to make this sign switch between English and Japanese based on the player's language setting

translation.text: 和“Snowdin”的镇名标牌一样，本地化团队需要增加程序代码，让这个招牌按照玩家的语言设置切换英日文。

source.text: Snowdin’s library is denoted by a large sign that says "LIBRARBY". This is a simple, childish misspelling of the English word "library" that some hasty players might not notice immediately. To achieve the same effect in Japanese, the localizers replaced the misspelled English sign with a similarly misspelled Japanese sign. Instead of としょかん (toshokan, "library"), the new sign says としょんか (toshonka), a hilariously bad misspelling that means nothing.

translation.text: Snowdin 图书馆的大招牌写着“LIBRARBY”，把英语 library（图书馆）拼错了。这是个简单、幼稚的拼写错误，匆匆经过的玩家可能一时都注意不到。为了在日语中产生相同效果，本地化人员换上了同样写错的日文招牌：不写“としょかん”（toshokan，图书馆），而写“としょんか”（toshonka），一个毫无意义、错得很好笑的词。

source.text: Originally, the Japanese version of this sign said としよかん (toshiyokan), which isn’t a real word either. The misspelling was less blatant than "LIBRARBY" though, so it was changed a few months before Undertale’s Japanese release.

translation.text: 最初，日文招牌写的是“としよかん”（toshiyokan），同样不是个真正的词。但这个错误不如“LIBRARBY”明显，因此在 Undertale 日语版发行前几个月又作了修改。

source.text: The library sign used to say としよかん (toshiyokan) instead of としょんか (toshonka), both are nonsense words though.

translation.text: 图书馆招牌过去写的是“としよかん”（toshiyokan），后来改为“としょんか”（toshonka）；不过两者都没有实际含义。

source.text: Making History

translation.text: 书写历史

source.text: This Japanese line is a good example of an external influence changing a translation, just as we saw back in the "What is Localization?" chapter

translation.text: 这句日文很好地说明，外部因素也会改变翻译，正如“什么是本地化？”一章中的例子。

source.text: Several books in the library reveal the Underground's dark history. One book begins to discuss death and murder, then suddenly ends with:

translation.text: 图书馆里的几本书揭示了地下世界的黑暗历史。其中一本刚谈到死亡和谋杀，便突然以这句话结尾：

source.text: Um, let's end the chapter here ...

translation.text: 呃，这一章就到这里吧……

source.text: Toby noted that this is the author avoiding the subject of "gruesome death". He then suggested that it might be funnier in Japanese if the author changed the subject by sharing a recipe instead. Thus the same line in Japanese says:

translation.text: Toby 指出，这是书中作者在回避“惨死”这个话题。他又建议，日语中让作者改谈食谱来岔开话题，可能更好笑。因此日版相应的台词成了：

source.text: ... Perhaps I should set this depressing topic aside and share a cake recipe instead ...

translation.text: ……或许该把这个沉重的话题放一放，改写个蛋糕食谱……

source.text: In short, the Japanese version of this line differs from the original English line. Not because anything would be lost in translation, but because of Toby himself.

translation.text: 这句日文与英文原文不同，并不是因为直译会丢失什么，而是 Toby 本人提出了改动。

source.text: Snowdin

translation.text: 雪镇

source.text: Double the Dessert

translation.text: 双份甜点

source.text: "Popsicle" is one of ~ those weird words that's technically a brand name, but has transformed over time into a general-use word

translation.text: 严格来说，“Popsicle”是一个商标名，后来逐渐成了冰棒的通称。

source.text: A food item called the "Bisicle" is available for purchase in Snowdin. In English, the item is described as a "two-pronged popsicle, so you can eat it twice".

translation.text: Snowdin 商店出售一种叫“Bisicle”的食物，说明写着：“双头冰棒，所以可以吃两次。”

source.text: Normally, a food item disappears after being used, but the Bisicle becomes the "Unisicle" after one use. As we can see, there's wordplay at work here: the two item names sound like the words "bicycle" and "unicycle'', while also sounding like the word "popsicle".

translation.text: 食物一般用过就会消失，Bisicle 吃过一次却会变成“Unisicle”。这两个名称既像 bicycle（自行车）与 unicycle（独轮车），也像 popsicle（冰棒）。

source.text: The Bisicle item before being used

translation.text: 使用前的 Bisicle

source.text: The Bisicle item after being used

translation.text: 使用后的 Bisicle

source.text: This wordplay would be lost in a literal translation into Japanese, so the translator compensated by referring to a different, but similar Japanese ice cream treat known as "Papico". Papico packages generally contain two plastic, ice cream-filled bottles. And just like double popsicles, they're designed to be broken apart and eaten separately or shared with someone else.

translation.text: 直译会让日语失去这个文字游戏，因此译者换成了一种不同却相似的日本冰品：Papico。每包 Papico 有两个装着冰淇淋的塑料瓶，和双头冰棒一样，可以掰开分别吃，也可以分给别人。

source.text: LEFT: A "two- ~ pronged" popsicle

translation.text: 左：双头冰棒。

source.text: RIGHT: A "two pronged" Papico ice cream treat

translation.text: 右：双支装的 Papico。

source.text: However, because "Pa pico" is a trademarked name in Japan, the translator chose a parody name rather than a direct reference. Thus the original "Bisicle" and "Unisicle" items are known as the "Babico" and "Single Babico" in Japanese.

translation.text: Papico 是商标名，因此日版没有直接照用，而是作了戏仿。Bisicle 和 Unisicle 分别成了“Babico”和“Single Babico”（单支 Babico）。

source.text: Cinnamon Challenge

translation.text: 肉桂挑战

source.text: Under normal circumstances, the CinnaBun's new Japanese name would've resulted in different fan art from Japanese fans, but the new item description nullifies this side effect

translation.text: 通常，CinnaBun 的这个新日文名称可能让日本玩家画出不同的同人图；不过，道具说明消除了这种副作用。

source.text: A "CinnaBun" item is available in Snowdin, but it turns out its name isn't an abbreviation for "Cinnamon Bun":

translation.text: Snowdin 出售一种叫“CinnaBun”的食物，乍看像 cinnamon bun（肉桂卷）的缩写，实际却是：

source.text: "Cinnamon Bunny" Heals 22 HP. A cinnamon roll in the shape of a bunny.

translation.text:
“Cinnamon Bunny”（肉桂兔兔）
回复 22 HP。做成兔子模样的肉桂卷。

source.text: Basically, the item's name and description form a multi-layered joke:

translation.text: 名称与说明构成了几层笑点：

source.text: 1. Most players will assume "CinnaBun" stands for "Cinnamon Bun" at first 2. But it turns out that "Bun" actually stands for "bunny" 3. Even though "Bun" means "bunny", the item is a cinnamon bun after all

translation.text:
• 大多数人会以为 CinnaBun 是 cinnamon bun（肉桂卷）的缩写。
• 但这里的 Bun 其实是 bunny（兔子）。
• 尽管 Bun 指的是兔子，它又确实是个肉桂卷。

source.text: The translator localized this joke by changing the item's name and description:

translation.text: 译者修改了名称与说明：

source.text: "Cinnamonkey" Heals 22 HP. Despite the "monkey" in its name, it's a bun that clearly looks like a bunny.

translation.text:
“Cinnamonkey”（肉桂猴）
回复 22 HP。名字里虽然有猴子，却明显是兔子形状的面包。

source.text: As we can see, this "Cinnamonkey" name parallels the English "CinnaBun" name by tricking the player into assuming something about the item, then using the item's description to throw that assumption out the window.

translation.text: “Cinnamonkey”把 cinnamon（肉桂）与 monkey（猴子）连在一起，和“CinnaBun”一样，先让玩家产生一种猜想，再用说明推翻它。

source.text: Smiling Carefully

translation.text: 微笑也要留心

source.text: As a translator, I find that the shorter a reference is, the harder it becomes to recognize it

translation.text: 典故越短，译者越难认出来。

source.text: A character in Snowdin discusses why smiling is important. Talking to this character a second time in the English version results in the text:

translation.text: Snowdin 有个角色谈到微笑的重要性。第二次与其交谈，英文台词是：

source.text: Smile smile.

translation.text: “Smile smile.”（笑一笑，笑一笑。）

source.text: Preserving obscure references is always a tough call in localization - after all, when does "obscure" become "unrecognizable"?

translation.text: 要不要保留冷门典故很难抉择。冷门到什么程度，才算已经无人认得出来？

source.text: Toby noted that this short line is actually a quote from EarthBound. The translator used this information to preserve the EarthBound reference in the Japanese script, but noted that because the Earth.Bound quote is even more unremarkable in Japanese, the reference would be lost in translation.

translation.text: Toby 的注释说，这短短一句引用了 EarthBound。译者保留了这个典故，采用 EarthBound 日语版对应的台词。不过，那句日语更不起眼，典故也就更容易在翻译中失落。

source.text: Snowdin

translation.text: 雪镇

source.text: Playing With a Full Deck

translation.text: 独自打牌

source.text: This scene is a parody ~ of the famous Dogs Playing Poker painting, which is known in Japan too

translation.text: 这也在戏仿名画 Dogs Playing Poker（《玩扑克的狗》）；这幅画在日本也有知名度。

source.text: Inside Snowdin's local restaurant, a dog sits at a table all alone. At first, the dog plays poker against itself, but it switches to other card games as Underta/e's story unfolds. Eventually, in the English script, the dog starts to play Go Fish against itself.

translation.text: Snowdin 餐馆里，一只狗独自坐在桌前，跟自己玩扑克。故事推进后，它会换着玩别的纸牌游戏。英语版中，它后来会独自玩 Go Fish（钓鱼）。

source.text: Go Fish is a card game usually played by two to five players, so the idea of playing it alone is slightly comical. And because Go Fish is so simple to play, it's particularly popular as a children's card game.

translation.text: Go Fish 通常要两到五个人玩，一只狗独自玩自然有些好笑。这种游戏规则简单，在孩子中很流行。

source.text: Although card games are popular in Japan, Go Fish isn't as widely known there as it is elsewhere in the world. For that reason, the Undertale translator replaced the Go Fish reference with a different card game that some Japanese children do play: Daihinmin.

translation.text: 纸牌游戏在日本也很受欢迎，但 Go Fish 没那么有名。因此，译者把它换成了“大贫民”（Daihinmin）。

source.text: LEFT: Go Fish usually ~ uses a standard card deck, but fish-themed Go Fish decks are common

translation.text: Go Fish 用普通扑克牌就能玩，不过市面上也常见鱼类图案的专用牌。

source.text: RIGHT: Daihinmin and Daifugo also usually use a standard card deck, but custom sets exist too - some cities even have their own local rules!

translation.text: “大贫民”或“大富豪”也可以用普通扑克牌玩，同时也有专用牌。各地还流传着不同的地方规则。

source.text: Daihinmin ("Great Pauper"), more commonly known as Daifugo ("Great Millionaire"), is similar to the card games known as "Tycoon" and "President" in English. The goal of the game is to get rid of all your cards as quickly as possible. The winner of each round is declared the daifugo and the loser is called the daihinmin, so it's somewhat funny to imagine this goofy dog being both things at the same time.

translation.text: Daihinmin 的意思是“大贫民”，不过更常用的名称是“大富豪”（Daifugō），类似英语中的 Tycoon 或 President。玩家要尽快打光手中的牌，赢家成为“大富豪”，输家成为“大贫民”。于是，独自玩牌的狗既是大富豪，又是大贫民，笑点便保留了下来。

source.text: Man's Best Friend

translation.text: 人类最好的朋友

source.text: Japanese counter words like these are a good example of how even the most basic thing in one language can be much more complicated in another

translation.text: 日语量词说明了一件事：一种语言里很简单的表达，换到另一种语言里也许会复杂得多。

source.text: Defeating Dogamy and Dogaressa in battle will cause a bear in Snowdin to wonder where they went. In English, the bear says:

translation.text: 打败 Dogamy 和 Dogaressa 后，Snowdin 的一只熊会纳闷它们去了哪里。英文台词是：

source.text: Those two married dogs always put presents under the tree for each other. It's always the same. A single bone. But every time, they act like it's the first time they've gotten it. Then Papyrus comes to take his bones back. Anyway, where are those two. .. ?

translation.text: 那对狗夫妻总在树下给彼此放礼物。每次都只是一根骨头，却每次都表现得像头一回收到似的。然后 Papyrus 就来把骨头捡走。话说，那两个去哪儿了？

source.text: This would be relatively straightforward to translate into Japanese, except for one problem: counter words.

translation.text: 这些话译成日语并不难，只有一个问题：量词。

source.text: In English, we usually count objects by giving a number followed the name of the object: two dogs, 420 cats, seven farts. Sometimes, though, we use special "counter words" to count objects or groups of objects: three "heads" of!ettuce, a "n1urder" of crows, a "tank" of gas.

translation.text: 英语中，通常用数字加名词就能计数，比如“two dogs”（两只狗）、“420 cats”（420 只猫）、“7 farts”（7 个屁）。有时也会用类似量词的表达，如三“棵”生菜（three heads of lettuce）、一“群”乌鸦（a murder of crows）、一“箱”汽油（a tank of gas）。

source.text: In Japanese, when counting objects, everything requires a counter word. For example:

translation.text: 日语中，数什么都需要量词。例如：

source.text: People: 人 (nin). Small animals: 匹 (hiki). Large animals: 頭 (tō). Butterflies, for some reason: 頭 (tō). Cylindrical objects: 本 (hon). Flat objects: 枚 (mai).

translation.text:
• 人：人（nin）
• 小动物：匹（hiki）
• 大动物：頭（tō）
• 蝴蝶：不知为何也用頭（tō）
• 圆柱状物体：本（hon）
• 扁平物体：枚（mai）

source.text: In the English Undertale script, the bear says "those two married dogs" and "those two" when referring to Dogamy and Dogaressa, but how should they be counted in Japanese? The dogs walk and talk like people, which would warrant the counter word nin. But you can also pet them and play fetch with them like ordinary dogs, which would warrant hiki. So which should it be? And, perhaps more importantly, how would the Underground's denizens count them?

translation.text: 英文中，这只熊用“那对狗夫妻”和“那两个”指代 Dogamy 与 Dogaressa。日语该用哪个量词呢？它们像人一样走路、说话，似乎该用“人”；但它们又会让人抚摸、玩捡东西的游戏，似乎该用“匹”。更重要的是，地下世界的居民会怎样看待它们？

source.text: In the earliest drafts of the Japanese script, the translator chose hiki when referring to Dogamy and Dogaressa. Another team member later argued for using nin instead, given that they act overall more like people than dogs. The translator agreed and changed every instance of hiki to nin ... but accidentally missed one. As a result, the bear refers to the dogs as people and as small animals in the final draft of the Japanese script.

translation.text: 最早的译稿用了“匹”。后来，有位团队成员认为它们更像人，应该用“人”。团队于是作了替换，却漏改了一处。最终版里，这只熊既把它们当作人来数，也把它们当作小动物来数。

source.text: Snowdin

translation.text: 雪镇

source.text: Take My Word For It

translation.text: 自造词怎么译

source.text: Having direct ~ input from Toby helped limit misinterpretations of his invented English words

translation.text: 有 Toby 直接提供意见，团队便较少误解他自造的英语词。

source.text: Language dictionaries are an essential tool for any translator, but what happens when an author invents completely new words never seen before? This was a consistent issue during Underta/e's localization. Some problematic words included:

translation.text: 词典是译者不可或缺的工具，但作者要是造出了前所未见的新词，又该怎么办？这个问题贯穿了 Undertale 的本地化过程。下面这些词都曾给团队出难题：

source.text: Jippity jumpity joodle Low jinks Dapsolutely Passioneer Poff Sparkular Water sausage

translation.text:
• Jippity jumpity joodle
• Low jinks
• Dapsolutely
• Passioneer
• Poff
• Sparkular
• Water sausage

source.text: Fabuful Persistenester Aclog Freakadacious Japers Hotbaby Gentlebeauties

translation.text:
• Fabuful
• Persistenester
• Aclog
• Freakadacious
• Japers
• Hotbaby
• Gentlebeauties

source.text: Toby knew these invented words wouldn't translate well, so he always included helpful notes whenever they appeared in the script. He also answered the localization team's follow-up questions regarding these unique words.

translation.text: Toby 知道这些自造词很难翻译，因此只要剧本里出现，就会附上说明。本地化团队进一步询问这些特殊词语时，他也会解答。

source.text: Even with Toby's input, however, each invented word became its own translation challenge. The localization team's general solution was to translate each invented word's intended meaning while adjusting the encompassing line to match the word's "feeling".

translation.text: 不过，即便有 Toby 帮忙，每个自造词仍是独立的翻译难题。团队通常会译出它原本想表达的意思，再调整整句台词，传达这个词的“感觉”。

source.text: In one scene, for example, Papyrus leaves a letter for the main character. The letter ends with the message:

translation.text: 例如，有一幕中，Papyrus 给主角留下一封信，结尾写道：

source.text: - SLIGHTLY BONETROUSLED, PAPYRUS

translation.text:
——有点 BONETROUSLED 的
Papyrus

source.text: In his translation notes, Toby explained "bonetrousled" with:

translation.text: Toby 在翻译注释中这样解释“bonetrousled”：

source.text: '' Bonetrousle is the name ofP apyrus's boss theme. It's also a completely made up word that has absolutely no meaning but probably something akin to "bothered" or "troubled"?

translation.text: Bonetrousle 是 Papyrus 首领战主题曲的名字。它也是一个完全编出来、没有实际意义的词，不过大概接近“烦恼”或“困扰”吧？

source.text: With this helpful information, the translator rephrased the Japanese line to say:

translation.text: 有了这条线索，译者把日文改写为：

source.text: A bit bugged to the bone From Papyrus

translation.text:
有点烦到骨头里的
Papyrus 敬上

source.text: Other made-up words were handled in a similar way, with varying results.

translation.text: 其他自造词也采用了类似的处理方式，效果各不相同。

source.text: Dust in the Wind

translation.text: 风中的尘埃

source.text: Never in my life did I imagine I'd be writing a book that explains how to translate dust

translation.text: 我这辈子也没想到，自己会写一本书，解释尘埃应该怎么翻译。

source.text: It's explained throughout Underta/e's story that when monsters die, they turn into dust. This simple fact became a little more complicated during the localization process, because there are multiple words in Japanese that mean "dust'', each with its slightly different nuances. The localization team narrowed the choices down to three:

translation.text: Undertale 的故事多次说明，怪物死后会化为尘埃。这个简单的事实，到了本地化时却稍微复杂了一点：日语中有好几个表示“dust”的词，细微含义各不相同。团队最后把候选词缩小到三个：

source.text: chiri (dust that Aoats in the air and thinly covers things) hokori (small, possibly fluffy clumps of dust) kona ("powder")

translation.text:
• chiri（尘埃）：飘浮在空气中、薄薄落在物体表面的灰尘。
• hokori（灰尘）：聚成小团、有时带绒絮的灰尘。
• kona（粉）：粉末。

source.text: After a lot of internal discussion, and after consulting with Toby, the team settled on using the term chiri to describe what monsters turn into after death.

translation.text: 团队内部反复讨论，又征询了 Toby 的意见，最终决定用 chiri（尘埃）描述怪物死后化成的东西。

source.text: Bug Busting

translation.text: 修复漏洞

source.text: Sometimes, localization can strengthen the author's original work. This bug in the English version of Underta/e was found and fixed during its Japanese localization, for example

translation.text: 本地化有时也能完善作者的原作。比如，Undertale 英语版的这个漏洞，就是在日语本地化过程中发现并修好的。

source.text: After the original English version of Underta/e was released, intrepid fans dissected the game's data and found a treasure trove of unused text, graphics, and more. As the localization team discovered, though, some of this unused text only went unused due to programming mistakes in the original release.

translation.text: Undertale 原版英语游戏发行后，勇于探索的粉丝剖析了游戏数据，找出大量未使用的文本、图像等内容。但本地化团队发现，其中有些文字没能用上，只是因为原版程序出了错。

source.text: One such mistake occurs during the dramatic pre-battle encounter with Papyrus. If the player has spared Papryus in a previous run through the game, Papyrus is designed to have alternate dialogue about their previous meeting. It turns out that this line had a bug in it, though, so it didn't trigger during normal gameplay.

translation.text: 其中一处出现在与 Papyrus 开战前的戏剧性对峙。如果玩家在之前一轮游戏中饶恕过 Papyrus，按设计，他应该说出另一段台词，谈到两人之前的相遇。然而，这段台词存在漏洞，正常游玩时不会触发。

source.text: Although the localization team members knew how to fix this bug, they waited until Toby gave his approval to implement it. Thus, Papyrus' alternate dialogue now appears as designed in all versions of the game, on all platforms, in both English and in Japanese.

translation.text: 本地化团队虽然知道怎么修，仍然等 Toby 同意后才动手。因此，现在各平台的所有版本，无论英语还是日语，都会按原本的设计显示 Papyrus 的这段替代台词。

source.text: Snowdin

translation.text: 雪镇

source.text: Translation Collision

translation.text: 翻译与碰撞判定

source.text: During this battle, the player must dodge bones that scroll by quickly and spell a funny phrase

translation.text: 在这场战斗中，玩家必须躲开快速掠过的骨头；这些骨头还拼成了一句有趣的话。

source.text: In battle, Papyrus repeatedly and humorously states that he has a special attack that he’s prepared to use if need be. Eventually, he unleashes his special attack, which is flashy, strange, and funny all at once. In the English version of Undertale, this attack ends with the eight-character message “COOL DUDE” spelled out in bones. The player must then dodge this text as it quickly scrolls by.

translation.text: 战斗中，Papyrus 一再以诙谐的方式宣称，自己备有一招特殊攻击，必要时就会使出来。最后，他终于使出了这招既华丽、又古怪、还很好笑的攻击。在英文版 Undertale 中，攻击最后会出现用骨头拼出的八个字符：“COOL DUDE”（酷哥）。这行字会快速掠过，玩家必须躲开。

source.text: Because this English bone text is somewhat difficult to read and scrolls by quickly, the translator felt it would benefit the gameplay experience to localize the bone text into Japanese. But as Toby noted, any changes to “COOL DUDE” would likely change the difficulty of avoiding the scrolling text. With this in mind, the translator looked for a phrase that could say roughly the same thing in Japanese using the exact same number of characters as the English message.

translation.text: 这些英文骨头字有些难读，移动又快，因此译者认为，将它们本地化成日文会改善游玩体验。但正如 Toby 所指出的，任何对“COOL DUDE”的改动，都可能改变躲避这行移动文字的难度。考虑到这一点，译者开始寻找一个日文短语：意思大致相同，字符数也必须与英文完全一致。

source.text: Papyrus has a “COOL DUDE” attack and wears a “COOL DUDE” outfit at one point, but localizing the attack text into Japanese broke this connection

translation.text: Papyrus 有一招“COOL DUDE”攻击，还曾穿过写着“COOL DUDE”的衣服。不过，把攻击文字本地化成日文后，两者之间的呼应就消失了。

source.text: After some brainstorming for a replacement message, the translator chose the phrase イカした こうげき (ikashita kōgeki), which roughly means “cool attack” or “totally sweet attack”. This phrase was then given to the game art studio 256graph to transform into graphical form. 256graph not only created all-new Japanese bone text, but also ensured that its height and width closely matched the height and width of the original English bone text.

translation.text: 经过一番构思，译者选定了“イカした こうげき”（ikashita kōgeki），大意是“很酷的攻击”或“超棒的攻击”。随后，这个短语交给游戏美术工作室 256graph 制作成图像。256graph 不仅制作了全新的日文骨头字，还确保其高度和宽度与原英文骨头字尽量接近。

source.text: They definitely don’t teach hit box localization in textbooks or school, this is uncharted territory for almost everyone

translation.text: 教科书或学校里肯定不会教你如何本地化碰撞判定框；对几乎所有人来说，这都是陌生的领域。

source.text: The localized Japanese bone text closely matches the dimensions of the original English bone text

translation.text: 本地化后的日文骨头字，尺寸与原英文骨头字十分接近。

source.text: All of this teamwork resulted in a Japanese phrase with the same number of characters as the English phrase, hitboxes that closely match the original game’s hitboxes, and all-new bone graphics that look just like the original English bone graphics. Even more impressive is that all of this work was done for one short message that stays on the screen for less than five seconds!

translation.text: 经过这番协作，最终的日文短语与英文拥有相同的字符数，碰撞判定框也与原版十分接近；全新制作的骨头字图像，看起来仍与原英文版本风格一致。更令人佩服的是，这一切工作，只是为了屏幕上一句停留不到五秒钟的短语！

source.text: Just Ahead

translation.text: 只剩个头

source.text: An Undertafe themed retelling of Shakespeare plays would be interesting to see

translation.text: 要是用 Undertale 的角色重演莎士比亚戏剧，一定很有意思。

source.text: If Papyrus is defeated in battle, his head falls in his hand and he says in English:

translation.text: Papyrus 在战斗中落败后，脑袋掉进自己手里，英语版中他说：

source.text: ALAS, POOR PAPYRUS!

translation.text: 唉，可怜的 Papyrus！

source.text: Toby noted that this is a reference to the famous Shakespeare quote, "Alas, poor Yorick!", which Hamlet says while holding a skull. The translator preserved this reference by quoting the same line from a Japanese translation of Hamlet. However, the translator also noted that the quote is less recognizable in Japanese and thus more likely to be missed by Japanese players.

translation.text: Toby 指出，这引用了莎士比亚的名句“唉，可怜的约里克！”——哈姆雷特手持头骨时说的话。译者采用《哈姆雷特》日译本中对应的台词，保留了这个典故。不过，译者也指出，这句名言在日语中没那么耳熟，因此日本玩家更容易错过。

source.text: Hamlet holds Yorick's skull before not saying "I knew him well"

translation.text: 哈姆雷特拿着约里克的头骨；但接下来，他可没有说那句常被误引的“I knew him well”（我很了解他）。

source.text: Grammar Explosion

translation.text: 语法大爆炸

source.text: Papyrus' non-stop weird vocabulary and grammar made him particularly tricky but fun to localize into Japanese

translation.text: Papyrus 古怪的用词和语法层出不穷，让他的日语本地化格外棘手，也格外有趣。

source.text: After losing to Papyrus three times, Papyrus will say in English:

translation.text: 玩家连输给 Papyrus 三次后，他会在英语版里说：

source.text: I AM THE PERSISTENTEST! AND IF YOU THINK YOU ARE PERSISTENESTER ... THAT IS WRONG! GRAMATICALLY WRONG! BECAUSE THE CORRECT FORM WOULD BE. .. "NOT AS PERSISTENTEST AS PAPYRUS, THE PERSISTENTESTEST!"

translation.text: 我才是最坚持的（PERSISTENTEST）！要是你以为自己更最坚持（PERSISTENESTER）……那就错了！语法错了！正确的说法应该是……“比不上最最坚持的（PERSISTENTESTEST）Papyrus 那么最坚持！”

source.text: To retain this bizarre grammar abuse, the translator rephrased the text a bit:

translation.text: 为了保留这种胡乱糟蹋语法的效果，译者稍作改写：

source.text: I AM MORE INTENSELY PERSISTENT! IF YOU'RE THINKING "I'M WAY MORE PERSISTENT". .. THEN THAT'S WRONG. .. GRAMMATICALLY WRONG! THE CORRECT FORM WOULD BE ... "IT'S NOT UN-NON-REASONABLE TO SAY YOU'RE WAY MORE UN PERSISTENT!"

translation.text: 我才是更加坚持的！如果你想说“我更更坚持”……那就错了……语法错了！正确的说法应该是……“说你更不坚持，也不是不没有道理的！”

source.text: This new line emulates the English line's bizarre gran1mar by using a flurry of negatives in a row. This keeps the line comical, nonsensical, and very Papyrus-like.

translation.text: 新版台词用一连串否定来模仿英语原文古怪的语法。这样一来，它仍然好笑、莫名其妙，也很有 Papyrus 的风格。

source.text: Snowdin

translation.text: 雪镇

source.text: Making the Grade

translation.text: 评个等级

source.text: The Japanese word ~ tegami ("a postal letter") combines the words te ("hand") with kami ("piece of paper")

translation.text: 日语 tegami（信）由 te（手）和 kami（纸）组成，写作“手紙”。

source.text: Papyrus laments that Undyne, his boss and friend, doesn't write him letters:

translation.text: Papyrus 抱怨上司兼朋友 Undyne 不给他写信：

source.text: Papyrus: WHY DIDN'T SHE WRITE A LETTER TO ME INSTEAD? Undyne: Fine, you want a letter!? I'll give you a letter!!! YOU GET AN "F"! Papyrus: OH NO!!! WHAT'S THE F FOR? Undyne: Friendship!!!

translation.text:
Papyrus：她怎么不给我写封 letter（信）？
Undyne：好，想要 letter（字母）？给你个 F（不及格）！
Papyrus：噢不！！！F 代表什么？
Undyne：Friendship（友谊）！！！

source.text: The translator replicated this joke by splitting the compound word tegami:

translation.text: 译者拆开复合词 tegami（信），重现了这个笑话：

source.text: Papyrus: WHY WON'T UNDYNE WRITE ME A LETTER!? Undyne: Oh, you want a letter, huh!? Then take THIS! Papyrus: WI-IA--!? WHAT IS THIS LETTER? IT'S SHAPED FUNNY. .. Undyne: It's a tegami ("letter') ... Ate ("hand')-shaped kami ("piece ofp aper')!

translation.text:
Papyrus：Undyne 为什么不给我写信！？
Undyne：哦，想要信是吧！？那就拿着！
Papyrus：什——！？这信怎么长得这么奇怪？
Undyne：这是 tegami（信），te（手）形的 kami（纸）！

source.text: Japanese fans are asked to imagine a strangely shaped letter that looks like this

translation.text: 日本玩家需要想象的，就是这样一封形状奇特的信。

source.text: This new Japanese line remains letter-themed and includes Undyne teasing Papyrus. The gag about getting an "F" and "friendship" is lost, however.

translation.text: 日文仍谈信件，也保留了 Undyne 对 Papyrus 的调侃，却失去了“不及格 F”和 Friendship（友谊）的笑点。

source.text: Shed Head

translation.text: 酷棚子

source.text: This game has so many weird lines only accessible under weird circumstances, I'll never be able to cover everything in this book

translation.text: 这游戏有太多奇怪台词，只有在奇怪条件下才能看到。本书恐怕永远也讲不完。

source.text: After Papyrus talks about his shed, Undyne makes a simple shed pun:

translation.text: Papyrus 谈起自家棚子后，Undyne 用 shed（棚子）开了个简单的玩笑：

source.text: Papyrus: THAT'S JUST MY COOL TOOLSHED. Undyne: Do you call it your COOLSHED!?

translation.text:
Papyrus：那只是我很酷的工具棚（COOL TOOLSHED）。
Undyne：所以你叫它“酷棚”（COOLSHED）！？

source.text: Because this English wordplay would be lost in a straightforward translation, the translator replaced it with a .Japanese play on the words mono-sugoku ("extremely") and mono-oki ("shed"):

translation.text: 英语双关无法直译，译者便改用日语 mono-sugoku（非常）和 mono-oki（储物棚）共有的 mono：

source.text: Papyrus: THAT'S MY EXTREMELY COOL SHED. Undyne: Your "mono-sugoku" coo/ "mono-oki", huh ...

translation.text:
Papyrus：那是我非常酷的储物棚。
Undyne：“mono-sugoku”酷的“mono-oki”，是吧……

source.text: The resulting Japanese joke works differently than the English joke, but remains mildly amusing through the use of this new wordplay.

translation.text: 日语笑话的手法与英语不同，但借着这个新的文字游戏，仍然带着一点逗趣。

source.text: Home Sweet Home

translation.text: 甜蜜的家

source.text: The English grammar here almost feels broken at first, but it turns out it's just Papyrus being weird

translation.text: 这句英语乍看像语法有问题，实际上只是 Papyrus 又在说怪话。

source.text: Papyrus gives the main character a tour of his home. In English, he begins by saying:

translation.text: Papyrus 带主角参观自己的家。英语版中，他开场便说：

source.text: WELCOME TO SCENIC MY HOUSE!

translation.text: 欢迎来到风景秀丽的我家！

source.text: This is a humorous reference to the stereotypical signs found at American tourist destinations, such as "Welcome to historic Licking, Missouri" and "Welcome to scenic Boogertown, North Carolina". Naturally, referring to the inside of one's home as a scenic tourist destination sounds ridiculous. The entire English sentence sounds off-kilter at first, too.

translation.text: 这句玩笑模仿了美国旅游景点常见的欢迎标语，例如“欢迎来到历史悠久的密苏里州利金市”和“欢迎来到风景秀丽的北卡罗来纳州 Boogertown”。把自己家里说成景色优美的旅游胜地，自然很荒唐。而且整句英语一开始听起来也有点别扭。

source.text: Japanese tourist spots don't follow the same phrasing pattern to welcome visitors, so the original cultural reference was lost in translation. The core joke of calling one's home "scenic" works in any language, though, so this line was given a simple, straightforward translation into Japanese.

translation.text: 日本景点欢迎游客时不用相同的句式，所以这个文化典故在翻译中丢失了。但把自家称为“风景秀丽”的核心笑点，在任何语言里都成立，因此日文直接译出了这句话。

source.text: The "Welcome to (Adjective) Place Name" pattern is a common sight at American tourist spots

translation.text: “欢迎来到＋形容词＋地名”是美国旅游景点常见的标语格式。

source.text: I wonder if anyone has ever made their own Undertale-themed "Welcome to Scenic My House" doormats or signs

translation.text: 不知道有没有人自制过 Undertale 主题的门垫或招牌，上面写着“欢迎来到风景秀丽的我家”。

source.text: Snowdin

translation.text: 雪镇

source.text: Vacation Dedication

translation.text: 欢迎随时来访

source.text: Is Papyrus being ~ sarcastic or serious? It's for you to decide!

translation.text: Papyrus 是在挖苦人，还是认真的？由你来判断！

source.text: During his bizarre house tour, Papyrus points at his garbage can and says:

translation.text: 在这场古怪的家中导览里，Papyrus 指着垃圾桶说：

source.text: THAT'S THE TRASH CAN. FEEL FREE TO VISIT IT ANY TIME.

translation.text: 那是垃圾桶。欢迎随时来访。

source.text: In his notes, Toby emphasized that "people love to copy and paste this line to tell pp\ they have bad taste ... hopefully we can maintain this quotability".

translation.text: Toby 在注释中特别强调：“大家很喜欢复制粘贴这句话，嘲讽别人品味差……希望我们能保留这种让人爱引用的效果。”

source.text: This Papyrus quote ~ has led to a ton of English-language fan art, but not nearly as much Japanese fan art

translation.text: Papyrus 的这句台词催生了大量英语同人图，日语同人图却远没有那么多。

source.text: Although this line did receive extra attention during Undertale's localization, it basically became a literal translation of the English text. Japanese fans do quote it from time to time, but it's not nearly as popular as the original English quote.

translation.text: Undertale 本地化时，团队虽然格外留意了这句台词，最后基本还是采用直译。日本粉丝也偶尔会引用它，但热度远远不及原版英语台词。

source.text: Translation Memorability

translation.text: 译文是否令人难忘

source.text: The "quotability" of a line is hard to control during translation, as it's the audience who ultimately decides what's memorable and what isn't. The classic Japanese RPG Final Fantasy IV provides a great example of this:

translation.text: 一句话能否被反复引用，很难由译者控制：最终决定它是否令人难忘的，还是观众。经典日式角色扮演游戏 Final Fantasy IV 就有很好的例子：

source.text: ii desu to mo! (roughly "Indubitably!") is a famous game quote in Japan, but the same line is forgettable in English

translation.text: ii desu to mo!（大意为“当然没问题！”）在日本是句游戏名言，但对应的英文台词却毫不起眼。

source.text: "You spoony bard!" is a very famous English-language game quote, but the same line is forgettable in Japanese

translation.text: “You spoony bard!”（你这痴情的吟游诗人！）是著名的英语游戏台词，日语原句却并不令人难忘。

source.text: Absolute Units

translation.text: 单位的分寸

source.text: I mean, technically, it should be localized as "YOU MOVED IT 5.08 CENTIMETERS!" but please don't tell the math police

translation.text: 严格说，应该译成“你只挪了 5.08 厘米！”不过，请别告诉数学警察。

source.text: As part of his tour, Papyrus shows off Sans' sock collection. This collection includes a series of back-and-forth notes between the two brothers:

translation.text: 导览中，Papyrus 展示了 Sans 的袜子收藏，其中还有兄弟俩来来回回写的几张纸条：

source.text: SANS! PLEASE PICK UP YOUR SOCK! ok. DON'T PUT IT BACK DOWN! MOVE IT! ok. YOU MOVED IT TWO INCHES! MOVE IT TO YOUR ROOM!

translation.text:
Sans！请捡起你的袜子！
好。
别又放回去！挪走！
好。
你只挪了两英寸！挪到你房间去！

source.text: Japan uses the metric system, so the translator converted the measurement of "two inches" to "five centimeters". This is an understandable translation change that hardly seems noteworthy on its own, but it's also a nice example of how math - and not just text - can play a part in the localization process too.

translation.text: 日本使用公制，因此译者把“两英寸”换算成了“五厘米”。这个改动很容易理解，单独看似乎没什么值得一提，但它也说明：本地化过程中，除了文字，数学也可能派上用场。

source.text: Reader Challenge #5: Calculate how many millimeters there are in an inch, but without using technology!

translation.text: 读者挑战 5：不用科技工具，算算一英寸等于多少毫米！

source.text: Similar measurement changes can be found throughout Undertale's Japanese script. In some cases, when the measurements aren't meant to be taken literally to begin with, the translator chose a suitable replacement. For example, a character in Snowdin shares this remark:

translation.text: Undertale 的日文剧本中，这样的单位变更随处可见。有些长度本来就不是实指，译者便选择合适的替代说法。例如，Snowdin 有个角色说：

source.text: That lady over there's been going for a walk for a while now. ... but she hasn't moved an inch from where she's standing.

translation.text: 那边那位女士已经散步好一会儿了……可她站在原地，连一英寸都没挪过。

source.text: This reference to "an inch" wasn't meant to be taken literally, so the translator replaced it with "one millimeter". This is a terribly inaccurate conversion, of course, but by straying from the literal meaning of the source text, the translator was able to retain the intended, functional meaning instead.

translation.text: 这里的“一英寸”并不是精确长度，因此译者将它换成了“一毫米”。这当然不是准确的换算，但偏离原文的字面数值，反而保留了它实际要表达的意思。

source.text: Matters that involve length, area, volume, temperature, and money come up all the time during translation, so as a translator/localizer it's helpful to have a basic understanding of mathematics and units of measurement.

translation.text: 翻译经常涉及长度、面积、体积、温度和金钱。所以，掌握一些基础数学和计量单位知识，对翻译与本地化工作很有帮助。

source.text: Snowdin

translation.text: 雪镇

source.text: Blue Collar Crime

translation.text: 蓝色爪印之谜

source.text: There's some argument ~ that "pawprint" should be a legitimate spelling given that "fingerprint" is okay. It looks like Toby is part of Team Pawprint and not Team Paw Print

translation.text: 有人认为，既然 fingerprint（指纹）可以连写，pawprint（爪印）也该是合法拼法。看来 Toby 属于“pawprint 派”，而不是“paw print 派”。

source.text: The PlayStation 4 and PlayStation Vita versions of Undertale include a secret dog shrine. Donating money at the shrine will unlock various unusual decorations. One such decoration is a piece of white paper covered in blue pawprints.

translation.text: Undertale 的 PlayStation 4 和 PlayStation Vita 版藏有狗神社，捐款可解锁各种古怪装饰，包括一张印满蓝色爪印的白纸。

source.text: In English, checking this piece of paper produces the message:

translation.text: 英语版中，调查这张纸会显示：

source.text: (Huh!? Blueprints ... !?) (Literally. It's white paper, but covered in little blue pawprints ... ) (Wait ... Blue pawprints ... Could it be a clue!?)

translation.text:
（咦！？Blueprints，蓝图……！？）
（字面意思。这是张白纸，不过印满了蓝色小爪印……）
（等等……蓝色爪印……难道是条线索！？）

source.text: This line is a simple pun on the English word "blueprints", but it also contains a reference to Blue's Clues, an American educational television series intended for children. Each episode features a puzzle, and a dog named Blue marks clues with a blue pawprint. The viewer is then asked to locate these clues and use them to solve the puzzle.

translation.text: 这里既用 blueprints（蓝图／蓝色印记）开了个简单的玩笑，也引用了美国儿童教育节目 Blue’s Clues。每集节目都有一道谜题，名叫 Blue 的狗会用蓝色爪印标出线索，再请观众找出这些线索，解开谜题。

source.text: The long-running Blue's ~ Clues series has an insanely popular TV show, books, computer games, and more

translation.text: 长寿系列 Blue’s Clues 不仅有极受欢迎的电视节目，还有图书、电脑游戏等作品。

source.text: Both the "blueprints" joke and the Blue's Clues reference would be lost in a literal translation, so the translator adjusted things in the Japanese script:

translation.text: 无论“蓝图”的玩笑还是 Blue’s Clues 的典故，直译都会丢失，所以译者调整了日文剧本：

source.text: (An important document...!?) (No, it's just ordinary piece ofp aper. It's covered with tiny paw prints.) ( ...P aw prints? Then, could they be ... dog thumbprints? Which would mean ... it's an important document after all!?) (. .. No. It really is just an ordinary piece ofp aper.)

translation.text:
（重要文件……！？）
（不，只是普通的纸。上面印满了小爪印。）
（……爪印？难道是……狗的手印？那岂不是……果然是重要文件！？）
（……不，真的只是普通的纸。）

source.text: The translator explained the idea behind this localization change in the translation spreadsheet. Basically, in Japan, it's more common to stamp an important document with a hanko (a personalized ink seal) than with a signature. But if a hanlw isn't available when filling out an important document, a thumbprint is usually an acceptable alternative.

translation.text: 译者在翻译表格中解释了改动的思路：日本的重要文件通常盖 hanko（个人印章），而不只是签名。如果填写重要文件时手头没有印章，一般也可以用拇指印代替。

source.text: Personalized ink seals are commonly used to sign documents in Japan, although that trend seems to be changing lately

translation.text: 日本签署文件时，常用个人印章。不过，近来这种习惯似乎正在改变。

source.text: As we can see, the translator prioritized the core purpose of this text over the need to include a cultural reference. As a result, this scene probably won't hold as much meaning for Jap:rnese players as it holds for English-speaking players, but the scene will still make sense in Japanese.

translation.text: 可以看出，译者优先保留了这段文字的核心作用，而没有执着于文化典故。因此，日本玩家从这幕中读到的意味，可能不如英语玩家那么丰富，但场景在日语中依然说得通。

source.text: Totally Rad

translation.text: 酷毙了

source.text: Toby continues to show his fondness for retro games with this English text, but that's lost in the Japanese text

translation.text: 这段英语再次显露了 Toby 对老游戏的喜爱，不过这一点在日文中丢失了。

source.text: Undertale's Nintendo Switch release includes an exclusive boss battle against Mad Mew Mew. During the battle, Mad Mew Mew says:

translation.text: Undertale 的 Nintendo Switch 版有一场独占首领战，对手是 Mad Mew Mew。战斗中，她会说：

source.text: That was Gnarly! Tubular! Way Cool! Awesome! Groovy! Mondo! Outrageous! Funky!

translation.text: 刚才真是 Gnarly！Tubular！Way Cool！Awesome！Groovy！Mondo！Outrageous！Funky！（这些都是“太酷、太棒”的俚语。）

source.text: Toby didn't note it at the time, but these phrases are references to the English version of Super Mario World, a classic Super Nintendo game released in 1991. Specifically, these are the names of eight secret stages that require great expertise to complete. Unfortunately, the original Japanese version of Super Mario World used much simpler - and milder - names for these same stages:

translation.text: Toby 当时没有标注，但这些词引用了 1991 年发行的超级任天堂经典游戏 Super Mario World 的英语版。具体来说，它们是八个高难度隐藏关卡的名称。遗憾的是，Super Mario World 日语原版给这些关卡起的名字要简单、温和得多：

source.text: The secret stages in Super Mario World have very different names in Japanese and English - this sort of "make it sound less bland" approach is one of many different entertainment localization philosophies

translation.text: Super Mario World 的隐藏关卡，英日文名称差别很大。这种“让它听起来别那么平淡”的思路，也是娱乐作品本地化的诸多理念之一。

source.text: Japanese Stage Name (roughly translated)

translation.text: 日文关卡名大意

source.text: English Stage Name

translation.text: 英文关卡名

source.text: Fun Course

translation.text: 趣味关卡

source.text: Gnarly

translation.text: Gnarly（酷毙了）

source.text: Fun Course

translation.text: 趣味关卡

source.text: Tubular

translation.text: Tubular（太棒了）

source.text: Even the Mario Staff will be Surprised Course

translation.text: 连马力欧制作人员也会吃惊的关卡

source.text: Way Cool

translation.text: Way Cool（超酷）

source.text: Even the Mario Staff will be Surprised Course

translation.text: 连马力欧制作人员也会吃惊的关卡

source.text: Awesome

translation.text: Awesome（棒极了）

source.text: Specialists' Course

translation.text: 高手关卡

source.text: Groovy

translation.text: Groovy（酷极了）

source.text: Specialists' Course

translation.text: 高手关卡

source.text: Mondo

translation.text: Mondo（超级棒）

source.text: Championship Course

translation.text: 冠军关卡

source.text: Outrageous

translation.text: Outrageous（绝了）

source.text: Championship Course

translation.text: 冠军关卡

source.text: Funky

translation.text: Funky（真带劲）

source.text: Because these Super Mario World references would be lost in a literal translation, the translator replaced the English stage names with similar Japanese slang that sounds "hip" but is actually cheesy. Thus, the resulting translation prioritizes the scene's flow over the need to include any references.

translation.text: 直接翻译会丢掉这些 Super Mario World 典故，于是译者把英文关卡名换成了相似的日语俚语，听着“时髦”，其实颇有些土气。最后的译文优先照顾场景的流畅感，而没有一定要加入典故。

source.text: Snowdin

translation.text: 雪镇

source.text: Dating Game

translation.text: 约会游戏

source.text: I don't need to date • a skeleton, I already have one of my own

translation.text: 我用不着和骷髅约会，我自己就有一副。

source.text: Eventually, the main character goes on a date with Papyrus, although it's actually more like a silly, date-themed battle.

translation.text: 后来，主角与 Papyrus 来了一场约会——不过，实际上更像一场以约会为主题的胡闹战斗。

source.text: When this Papyrus dating sequence begins, the English version of Undertale displays the text "DATI G START!". Toby noted that this is another reference to Super Matio World, in which each stage begins with the messages "MARIO START!" or "LUIGI START!".

translation.text: 与 Papyrus 的约会环节开始时，Undertale 英语版会显示“DATING START!”（约会开始！）。Toby 指出，这又引用了 Super Mario World：每个关卡开头都会显示“MARIO START!”或“LUIGI START!”。

source.text: The Japanese version • of Super Mario World always displays this message in English text

translation.text: Super Mario World 日语版也一直用英文显示这条提示。

source.text: With this information in hand, the translator checked the Japanese version of Super Mario World and found that it also displays "MARIO START!" and "LUIGI START!" in English. For this reason, the translator chose to leave this dating message in English. The phrase was changed to "DATE START!", however, as the English word "date" already exists in the Japanese language and would be more recognizable to Japanese players.

translation.text: 有了这条信息，译者检查了 Super Mario World 的日语版，发现其中同样用英文显示“MARIO START!”和“LUIGI START!”。因此，约会开始的提示也保留英文，不过改成了“DATE START!”。英语 date（约会）已经作为外来词进入日语，日本玩家更容易认得。

source.text: We can see that "THU" remained unchanged during the localization process - this is because the English abbreviations for the days of the week are semi-common knowledge in Japan

translation.text: 可以看到，“THU”（星期四）在本地化时没有改动，因为星期的英语缩写在日本也算比较常见的知识。

source.text: This Super Mario World reference also appears in an alternate scene, when the main character and Papyrus hang out in Papyrus' room instead of going on a date.

translation.text: 这个 Super Mario World 典故也出现在另一条剧情中：主角不和 Papyrus 约会，而是在他的房间里一起消磨时光。

source.text: The English version of this sequence begins with the message "HANGOUT START!". The words "hang out" and "hangout" aren't well known in Japan, though, so "hangout" was replaced with the equivalent Japanese word mattari. Thus the Japanese game displays "MATTARI START!" in English before this scene begins.

translation.text: 英语版的这一环节以“HANGOUT START!”（一起玩耍开始！）开场。不过，hang out 和 hangout 在日本并不常见，所以译者把 hangout 换成意思相近的日语 mattari（悠闲放松）。因此，日语版在这一幕开头，会用罗马字显示“MATTARI START!”。

pages.title: 日本游戏里的简化英语

source.text: Simplified English in Japanese Games

translation.text: 日本游戏里的简化英语

source.text: As we've seen, English words appear all the time in Japanese games. Over the years, these English words have formed a limited "English game vocabulary" that Japanese gamers naturally absorb. However, it's still common for English phrases to be simplified during English-to Japanese game localization.

translation.text: 前面已经看到，日本游戏中经常出现英语词。多年来，它们形成了一套范围有限的“游戏英语词汇”，日本玩家玩着玩着就熟悉了。不过，英语游戏本地化成日语时，简化英文措辞仍然十分常见。

source.text: The English word "flawless" was replaced with the more recognizable English word "perfect" in the Japanese version of Valorant (2020)

translation.text: Valorant（2020）日语版把 flawless（完美无缺）换成了日本玩家更容易认得的 perfect（完美）。

source.text: Conversely, "flawless" was kept intact in the Japanese version of One Step From Eden (2020), but the phrase "battle won" was simplified to "victory"

translation.text: 相反，One Step From Eden（2020）日语版保留了 flawless，却把 battle won（战斗获胜）简化成了 victory（胜利）。

source.text: The reverse of this practice can happen too. Sometimes overly simplified English text in a Japanese game will be rewritten with more complicated English during the Japanese-to-English localization process.

translation.text: 反过来的情况也会发生。日本游戏中有时会出现过分简化的英语，日译英本地化时，又会把它们改写成更复杂的英语。

source.text: This victory message in the original Japanese version of Dark Souls (2011) uses very simple English intended for Japanese players, while the English localization uses a larger vocabulary to rephrase the message in a more natural way

translation.text: Dark Souls（2011）日语原版的胜利提示“YOU DEFEATED”使用很简单的英语，方便日本玩家理解。英语本地化则采用更丰富的词汇，改成较自然的“VICTORY ACHIEVED”（取得胜利）。

source.text: Snowdin

translation.text: 雪镇

source.text: Spelling Master

translation.text: 拼写大师

source.text: For no reason at all, • here are some anagrams of "Papyrus": Pa Syrup, Spray Up, Ray Pups, and Rap Yups

translation.text: 毫无缘由地，列几个重排“Papyrus”字母得到的词组：Pa Syrup（老爹糖浆）、Spray Up（向上喷）、Ray Pups（雷的小狗）、Rap Yups（说唱“是的”）。

source.text: Papyrus starts the date by showing off his "official dating rulebook", then says:

translation.text: Papyrus 展示自己的“官方约会指南”，作为约会的开场，然后说：

source.text: YOU CAN'T SPELL 'PREPARED' WITHOUT SEVERAL LETTERS FROM MY NAME!!!

translation.text: 少了我名字里的几个字母，你就拼不出 PREPARED（准备好了）！！！

source.text: Because this line involves the spelling of an English word and the spelling of Papyrus' English name, the joke would be lost in a literal translation. After struggling with this line for some time, the translator decided to instead focus on the core meaning and purpose of the statement. Thus, Papyrus' line became:

translation.text: 这句笑话涉及英语单词和 Papyrus 英文名字的拼写，直接翻译便不成立。译者为此苦恼了一阵，最后决定聚焦这句话的核心意思和作用。因此，Papyrus 的台词改成了：

source.text: "FL1lly prepared" is my motto!

translation.text: “准备周全”就是我的座右铭！

source.text: Although the original joke was lost in translation, the translator did try to reintroduce some humor by using a slightly fancy phrase for "fully prepared", which fits Papyrus' tendency to use comically unexpected wording.

translation.text: 虽然原来的笑话在翻译中丢失了，译者还是试着加回一点幽默，用略带文气的措辞表达“准备周全”，也符合 Papyrus 总爱出其不意地用词、惹人发笑的习惯。

source.text: Flipping Out

translation.text: 转个方向

source.text: I guess you have a big choice to make now: rotate your body or rotate the book

translation.text: 现在你大概要作个重大决定：转自己的身体，还是转这本书。

source.text: As we've already seen, Papyrus' Japanese text is written vertically from top to bottom, moving from right to left. This style of writing Japanese has been around for centuries. But what happens when foreign characters and symbols appear in vertical Japanese text?

translation.text: 前面已经看到，Papyrus 的日文采用竖排，从上往下读，再从右向左移列。日语沿用这种写法已有几百年。不过，竖排日文中出现外文字母和符号时，该怎么办？

source.text: There are different methods of handling vertical foreign text - one common practice is to rotate the foreign characters before displaying them vertically, even though the surrounding Japanese characters aren't rotated. This is why the English word "COOL" appears sideways during the date with Papyrus.

translation.text: 竖排中的外文有不同处理方法。常见的一种是先把外文字母旋转，再排进竖行，周围的日文则保持原方向。这也就是约会时英文“COOL”（酷）会侧着出现的原因。

source.text: Incidentally, all of • Papyrus' text was written horizontally in the spreadsheet

translation.text: 顺带一提，翻译表格中 Papyrus 的所有台词都是横排的。

source.text: Getting Sneaky

translation.text: 鞋里的秘密

source.text: Toby mentioned in his translation notes that this part of the game is "super inspired by Phoenix Wright"

translation.text: Toby 在翻译注释中说，游戏这一段“深受《逆转裁判》启发”。

source.text: During the date and hangout sequences, Papyrus mentions that his outfit contains a special secret. The player is then asked to identify that secret. If the player checks Papyrus' shoes in the English game, Papyrus responds with:

translation.text: 约会和一起玩耍时，Papyrus 会说自己的装束里藏着一个特别的秘密，请玩家找出来。英语版中，如果调查他的鞋子，他会回答：

source.text: HUMAN SOULS ARE STRONGER THAN MONSTER SOULS. .. BUT THE SOLES OF OUR SHOES ON THE OTHER HAND. .. ! ARE ABOUT THE SAME.

translation.text:
人类的 SOULS（灵魂）比怪物的更强大……
但是，我们鞋子的 SOLES（鞋底）……！
倒是差不多。

source.text: This line includes a pun on the English words "soul" and "sole". The Japanese equivalents of these words don't share the same pronunciation, though, so the joke would be lost in a straightforward translation.

translation.text: 这句台词利用了英语 soul（灵魂）与 sole（鞋底）的同音。相应的日语词发音并不相同，所以直译会丢掉这个笑话。

source.text: To get around this untranslatable English pun, the translator replaced the English shoe joke with a Japanese shoe joke:

translation.text: 为了绕过这个无法照译的英语双关，译者把英语鞋子笑话换成了日语鞋子笑话：

source.text: The secret is in my shoes, you say ...? Heh heh ... Sorry to break it to you, but "secret shoes" these are not!

translation.text:
你说秘密藏在鞋子里……？
嘿嘿……
抱歉让你失望了，这可不是“秘密鞋”！

source.text: At first glance, this Japanese response seems to be devoid of any jokes at all. However, the English phrase "secret shoes" is used in Japanese to refer to what are known elsewhere as "elevator shoes" - shoes designed to make the wearer look taller, in other words.

translation.text: 乍看之下，这段日文似乎根本没有笑点。但英语词组“secret shoes”（秘密鞋）在日语中指的正是“内增高鞋”——也就是让穿鞋的人看起来更高的鞋。

source.text: I apologize for occupying some of your brain cells for the next several years with this random Japanese shoe fact

translation.text: 抱歉，这条无关紧要的日本鞋类知识，恐怕要占用你未来好几年的一部分脑细胞了。

source.text: I really like this Japanese shoe joke - it fits the context, it's shoe-themed, it uses the word "secret", and it doesn't feel forced. It all comes down to personal opinion, but I feel this is a good example of a localization surpassing the original. It does lose the discussion about souls, though.

translation.text: 我很喜欢这个日语鞋子笑话：它符合上下文，以鞋为主题，用到了“秘密”这个词，又不显得牵强。好坏当然见仁见智，但我认为，这是一个本地化超越原文的好例子。不过，关于灵魂的那段话确实没有了。

source.text: Mystery Call

translation.text: 神秘来电

source.text: Some English-speaking ~ fans went straight to this line in the Japanese script to see if it revealed any more details about "G", but Toby had already anticipated them

translation.text: 有些英语粉丝直接去查日文剧本里的这句台词，想看看能不能得到更多关于“G”的线索。不过，Toby 早已料到。

source.text: Under very rare conditions, the player might receive a strange phone call from an unknown caller:

translation.text: 在极少见的条件下，玩家可能接到一个陌生人的奇怪电话：

source.text: Hello! Can I speak to G. .. Wait a second. Is this the wrong number?

translation.text:
你好！请问 G……在吗？
等等，我是不是打错电话了？

source.text: It appears that the speaker starts to say someone's name, then stops before saying too much. There are several characters in Undertale with names that start with "G", including Grillby, Gerson, Gyftrot, and Glyde. But the prevailing theory among English-speaking fans is that "G" is actually referring to an incredibly mysterious and eerie character named Gaster.

translation.text: 来电者似乎刚说出某个人名字的开头，就在透露更多之前停住了。Undertale 有几个角色的名字以“G”开头，包括 Grillby、Gerson、Gyftrot 和 Glyde。不过，英语粉丝中最流行的猜测是：“G”指的是那个极为神秘、诡异的角色 Gaster。

source.text: Toby has been notoriously quiet when fans ask about certain details in Undertale. As a creator, he wants certain mysteries to remain mysteries, so he only left one short note about this line in the translation spreadsheet:

translation.text: 粉丝问起 Undertale 的某些细节时，Toby 向来守口如瓶。作为作者，他希望某些谜团始终保持神秘。因此，他只在翻译表格里为这句台词留下一条简短注释：

source.text: '' Character's name beginning with "G". .. Actually, it might be suitably bizarre ify ou leave this line completely intact in English

translation.text: 角色名字以“G”开头……其实，如果这句完整保留英文，或许会怪得恰到好处。

source.text: As we've already seen, the translation process can reveal details not found in the original work. In this case, because the Japanese language is based on syllables and not sounds, a standard translation of "can I speak to G?" into Japanese would result in a vowel appearing after "G". This would reveal more information about G's identity - enough for fans to solve this mystery. Toby understood this, and eventually firmly requested that this text remain completely in English. And, as he suggested, leaving it in English would make the line feel even stranger for Japanese players.

translation.text: 前面已经看到，翻译有时会透露原作里没有的信息。在这里，日语假名表示音节，而非单个音素，按通常方式翻译“请问 G 在吗”，就会在“G”后加上一个元音。这会透露更多关于 G 身份的信息，足以让粉丝解开谜团。Toby 明白这一点，后来明确要求这段文字全部保留英文。而且正如他所说，保留英文会让日本玩家觉得这句台词更加古怪。

source.text: Before Toby insisted that this phone call remain entirely in English, the localization team assumed - like many other fans - that "G" referred to this secretive Gaster character. As such, early drafts of the Japanese translation had this line say "Hello? May I speak to Ga--" in English, but written using Japanese pronunciation.

translation.text: 在 Toby 坚持这通电话必须完全保留英文之前，本地化团队和许多粉丝一样，以为“G”指的是神秘的 Gaster。因此，早期日文译稿写的是英语“Hello? May I speak to Ga—”（你好？请问 Ga——在吗），但用日语假名标出英语发音。

source.text: Toby didn’t explain "G" in his translation notes, so the localizers originally assumed it was meant to refer to Gaster, thus "G" became ガ (Ga) for a short time.

translation.text: Toby 没有在注释里解释“G”，团队起初以为指的是 Gaster。因此，“G”曾一度变成“ガ”（Ga）。

source.text: "Is your refrigerator running?" is a classic telephone prank in some English speaking regions. The prank follows this pattern:

translation.text: “你的冰箱在 running 吗？”是一些英语地区经典的电话恶作剧，利用 running 既指“运转”又指“跑”的双关，套路如下：

source.text: Receiver: Hello? Caller: Hey, is your refrigerator running? Receiver: Yes. Caller: Then you better go catch it!

translation.text:
接电话的人：喂？
打电话的人：嘿，你的冰箱在跑吗？
接电话的人：是啊。
打电话的人：那还不快去追！

source.text: In his translation notes, Toby explains that the joke in this scene is an anti-joke: it has no point, there's no punchline, and Sans just takes everything literally.

translation.text: Toby 在翻译注释里解释，这一幕是个“反笑话”：没有寓意，也没有包袱，Sans 只是把一切都当真了。

source.text: This prank call based on an English pun wouldn't work in Japanese, so the translator replaced it with a reference to Licca-chan, a classic Japanese toy doll famous for having a real-life telephone hotline. But instead of answering as Licca-chan, he asks if he's Licca-chan. And just like in the English scene, Sans isn't calling as a prank - he's asking a genuine question. Thus, through creative localization, Sans' English, pun-based anti-joke became a phone-themed anti joke with a cultural reference that Japanese players could recognize.

translation.text: 这个基于英语双关的电话恶作剧，在日语中行不通，于是译者改为引用日本经典玩偶莉卡（Licca-chan），它以现实中的电话热线而闻名。但 Sans 并不是以莉卡的身份接电话，而是在问自己是不是莉卡。和英语版一样，他没有恶作剧，而是在认真提问。经过这样的创造性本地化，原本以英语双关构成的反笑话，变成了以电话为主题、包含日本玩家熟悉典故的反笑话。

source.text: Meet Licca-chan

translation.text: 认识莉卡娃娃

source.text: Licca-chan is a classic dress-up doll series in Japan that debuted in the late 1960s. In simple terms, Licca-chan is the Japanese equivalent of the United States' popular Barbie doll series.

translation.text: 莉卡（Licca-chan）是20世纪60年代末推出的日本经典换装娃娃，相当于美国流行的芭比娃娃。

source.text: Licca-chan's popularity among Japanese children spawned a "Talk to Licca-chan" phone service that began operating in 1968. Being old enough to call Licca-chan is almost like a generational rite of passage in some parents' eyes.

translation.text: 莉卡深受日本儿童喜爱，催生了 1968 年开通的“与莉卡通话”电话服务。在一些家长眼中，孩子长到能给莉卡打电话的年纪，几乎是代代相传的成长仪式。

source.text: When someone calls the Licca-chan hotline - which is just a pre-recorded message that changes monthly - Licca-chan answers with:

translation.text: 拨打莉卡热线时——其实只是每月更新的预录留言——莉卡会这样接听：

source.text: Hello, this is Licca-chan !

translation.text: 你好，我是莉卡！

source.text: This opening sentence, which also serves as the hotline's catchphrase, has been featured in countless commercials and advertisements for decades.

translation.text: 这句开场白也是热线的招牌台词，几十年来出现在无数电视广告及其他宣传中。

source.text: The main character heads for a distant castle to find the Underground's exit. The journey leads through a winding, watery path filled with dangers and delights.

translation.text: 主角朝远方的城堡前进，寻找地下世界的出口。旅程穿过蜿蜒的水路，沿途既有危险，也有惊喜。

translation.text: 落下的水

source.text: Translation and localization are very subjective processes - it's like asking a group of people to draw a clown and then seeing a bunch of different styles of clowns

translation.text: 翻译和本地化都很主观——就像让一群人画小丑，最后会看到各种不同风格的小丑。

source.text: After leaving Snowdin, the main character reaches a region named "Waterfall" in the English version of Undertale. Note that "Waterfall" is the actual name of the place - it isn't simply "a waterfall" in the general sense.

translation.text: 离开 Snowdin 后，主角来到 Waterfall。Undertale 英语版以此为正式地名，并非泛指“一道瀑布”。

source.text: Because of this intentional ambiguity - and the fact that the English word "waterfall" isn't commonly known in Japanese - this location was named ''Waterland" as a temporary placeholder. The localization tean1 later settled on the name ''Waterfell", which brought it closer to the original name, while "sounding" like the name of a place.

translation.text: 由于这种有意为之的歧义，再加上英语 waterfall（瀑布）在日语中并不常见，团队最初暂用“Waterland”（水之地）这个名字。后来，他们确定采用“Waterfell”，既更接近原名，又“听起来”像个地名。

source.text: The temporary "Waterland" name in Japanese paralleled "Hotland", the name of another region in Underta/e

translation.text: 日语暂名“Waterland”与 Undertale 另一个区域的名称“Hotland”（热域）相呼应。

source.text: Subjective Name Changes in Localization

translation.text: 本地化中的主观改名

source.text: It's somewhat common for names to change during the localization process if their original names sound "off". Some past examples include:

translation.text: 如果原名听起来“不太对”，本地化时改名是比较常见的事。过去的例子包括：

source.text: Princess Peach was renamed "Princess Toadstool" in Super Mario Bros.' English localization, presumably because "Peach" sounded "off" for a princess of the Mushroom Kingdom

translation.text: Super Mario Bros. 英译把 Princess Peach 改名为 Princess Toadstool（毒蘑菇公主），大概觉得蘑菇王国公主叫 Peach（桃子）不太对。

source.text: Tina was renamed "Terra" in the English localization of Final Fantasy VJ, supposedly because "Tina" doesn't sound "exotic" in English

translation.text: Final Fantasy VI 英语本地化把 Tina 改成了 Terra，据说是因为“Tina”在英语中不够有异域色彩。

source.text: Monster Kid Speaks

translation.text: Monster Kid 的说话方式

source.text: Although Monster Kid uses the masculine pronoun オレ (ore) in Japanese, Toby designed the character to have no clear gender.

translation.text: Monster Kid 在日语中虽然用偏男性的“オレ”（ore，我），但 Toby 设计这个角色时，并没有明确其性别。

source.text: In the English script, a character called "Monster Kid" speaks like an energetic youth who loves to use slang. The translator preserved these attributes in Japanese, but this led to a problem: Monster Kid's gender is never specified in the original script, yet this Japanese speaking style makes the character sound like a teenage boy. After consulting with Toby, the translator gave Monster Kid the assertive, masculine pronoun ore.

translation.text: 英文剧本中，Monster Kid 像个精力旺盛、爱说俚语的孩子。译者在日语里保留了这些特征，却遇到了问题：原文从未说明 Monster Kid 的性别，但这种日语说话风格，会让角色听起来像个少年。征询 Toby 后，译者为 Monster Kid 选用了态度鲜明、偏男性的第一人称 ore（我）。

source.text: In early drafts of the Japanese script, Monster Kid's laughter was denoted by the letter "w", which is the Japanese equivalent of "LOL" (laughing out loud) in English. Eventually, the localization team agreed that "w" felt too out of place, and gave the character a normal laugh instead.

translation.text: 早期日文译稿用字母“w”表示 Monster Kid 的笑声，相当于英语的“LOL”（放声大笑）。后来，团队一致认为“w”太突兀，便改成普通的笑声。

source.text: This use of Japanese Internet slang was meant to emphasize the Monster Kid's excitable youthfulness

translation.text: 使用这种日语网络用语，本来是想突出 Monster Kid 年轻又容易兴奋的性格。

source.text: Out Darned Spot

translation.text: 滚开，可恶的污点

source.text: Wow, what do you know, my high school English literature classes did come in handy for my future job!

translation.text: 哇，没想到我高中上的英国文学课，还真在未来的工作中派上用场了！

source.text: A local monster named Woshua lives to clean. Just before attacking the main character, Woshua sometimes says in English:

translation.text: 这里有个名叫 Woshua 的怪物，毕生热爱清洁。攻击主角之前，它有时会在英语版里说：

source.text: Out!!! Darned spot

translation.text: 滚开！！！可恶的污点。

source.text: Toby noted that this is reference to the famous quote from Shakespeare's Macbeth, "Out, damned spot! Out, I say!". Naturally, the translator consulted a Japanese translation of Macbeth and adapted the equivalent quote for Woshua's battle text. Although the reference is less recognizable in Japanese, the line fortunately still fits Woshua's dirt despising personality.

translation.text: Toby 指出，这引用了莎士比亚《麦克白》的名句：“滚开，该死的污点！滚开，我说！”译者自然去查了日译本，把对应台词改写为 Woshua 的战斗文字。虽然日本玩家未必那么容易认出典故，但这句话仍然符合 Woshua 痛恨污垢的性格。

source.text: Lady Macbeth shouts this famous line while trying to wash imaginary blood from her hands

translation.text: 麦克白夫人试图洗掉手上想象中的血迹时，喊出了这句名言。
