translation.text: 瀑布

source.text: Aaron Speaks

translation.text: Aaron 的说话方式

source.text: Today, emoticons like (^_-)☆ feel outdated and associated with middle-aged guys desperately trying to flirt with girls online.

translation.text: 如今，(^_-)☆ 之类的表情已经有些过时，容易让人想到在网上拼命撩女孩的中年男人。

source.text: A seahorse monster named Aaron loves bodybuilding, muscles, and flirting with other characters. In his notes, Toby describes Aaron as "a buff horse whose Airty actions border on creepy".

translation.text: 海马怪物 Aaron 热爱健身、肌肉，也喜欢和其他角色调情。Toby 在注释里把他形容为“一匹肌肉发达的马，调情举动已经接近让人发毛的程度”。

source.text: In Japanese, Aaron uses the friendly, boyish pronoun boku rather than the more "manly" pronoun ore. Although he doesn't use pronouns very often, this uncharacteristic use of boku was intended to accentuate his "creepy" vibe.

translation.text: 日语中，Aaron 用亲切、带少年感的 boku（我），而不是更有“男子气概”的 ore。虽然他不常用代词，但这种与外表不太相符的 boku，正是为了突出他让人不舒服的感觉。

source.text: In English, Aaron often ends his text with ;), which is a common Western emoticon of someone winking. Japanese emoticons are generally quite different, however, so the original winking face was replaced with a Japanese-style winking face: (^_-)☆

translation.text: 英语版中，Aaron 常在句尾加上 ;)。这是西方常见的眨眼表情。但日式表情通常很不一样，所以原来的眨眼脸换成了日式版本：(^_-)☆

source.text: Pumping Fire

translation.text: 练肌肉的火焰

source.text: Entertainment translators need to be well-versed in many different fields of study to accurately recognize references without supplemental notes

translation.text: 娱乐作品译者需要涉猎许多领域，才能在没有附加注释时准确认出典故。

source.text: During battle, Aaron sometimes says in English:

translation.text: 战斗中，Aaron 有时会在英语版里说：

source.text: Education? Hobby? Talent?

translation.text: 学历？爱好？特长？

source.text: Toby not d that this this seemingly random line is actually a direct quote from a bodybuilding character in Breath ofF ire II. The translator used Toby's notes to find the equivalent Japanese line from Breath ofF ire II in order to preserve the reference in the Japanese Undertale script. Fortunately, the Breath ofF ire II line is the same in Japanese and English, so no extra adaptation work was needed.

translation.text: Toby 指出，这句看似随意的话，实际上直接引用了 Breath of Fire II 中一个健美角色的台词。译者根据注释找到原作对应的日语台词，将典故保留在 Undertale 的日文剧本中。幸运的是，Breath of Fire II 的这句台词英日文一致，不需要额外改编。

source.text: In Breath of Fire II, this musclebound Director of HR repeats the same three questions during battle, as if giving a job interview

translation.text: Breath of Fire II 中，这位浑身肌肉的人事主管在战斗时反复问这三个问题，像是在主持招聘面试。

pages.title: 灵感聚焦：Breath of Fire II

source.text: Inspiration Spotlight: Breath of Fire II

translation.text: 灵感聚焦：Breath of Fire II

source.text: In 1994, Capcom released a Super Famicom role-playing game known as Breath of Fire II in Japan. A North American version was released in 1995, and a European version was released in 1996. Although it boasts solid game design and a memorable story, Breath of Fire II has also earned notoriety for its poor English-language localization.

translation.text: 1994 年，Capcom 在日本为 Super Famicom 发行了角色扮演游戏 Breath of Fire II。北美版于 1995 年发行，欧洲版于 1996 年发行。游戏设计扎实、故事令人难忘，不过它糟糕的英语本地化也出了名。

source.text: The game's story sets an orphan and a band of unique characters on a quest to destroy a corrupt religious cult, solve the mystery surrounding a giant sleeping dragon, and ultimately save the world from destruction.

translation.text: 故事讲述一个孤儿与一群各具特色的伙伴踏上旅途，摧毁腐败的宗教组织，解开沉睡巨龙之谜，最终拯救即将毁灭的世界。

source.text: Waterfall

translation.text: 瀑布

source.text: Onionsan Speaks

translation.text: Onionsan 的说话方式

source.text: In Japanese, Onionsan pronounces his sentences like a big, goofy-sounding character

translation.text: 日语中，Onionsan 说话的腔调像个傻乎乎的大块头。

source.text: A giant, onion-like creature named Onionsan appears in Waterfall. Toby described Onionsan's speaking style by saying "no one talks like this Joi" and "no one says 'big favorite' Joi". The overall effect is that Onionsan sounds lonely and insecure, but also goofy and upbeat.

translation.text: 瀑布地区出现了一个巨大、形似洋葱的生物 Onionsan。Toby 形容其说话方式时写道：“没人会这么说话哈哈”“没人会说 big favorite（大最爱）哈哈”。整体听来，Onionsan 既孤独、缺乏安全感，又有些傻气而乐观。

source.text: In Japanese, Onionsan ends sentences in a way that's associated with childishness, silliness, and awkward nerdiness. The Japanese script also treats the "san" part of"Onionsan" as the Japanese name suffix -san, which is roughly equivalent to "Mr." or "Ms." In English. However, it's improper to add -san when saying your own name, so this localization choice adds another layer of social awkwardness to the character.

translation.text: 日语中，Onionsan 的句尾带着孩子气、傻乎乎又不擅交际的宅气。译文还把“Onionsan”里的 san 视作日语姓名后缀 -san，大致相当于英语的 Mr. 或 Ms.（先生／女士）。然而，说自己的名字时不应加 -san，所以这一处理又给角色添了一层不通人情世故的感觉。

source.text: As with several other characters in Undertale, Onionsan's gender is meant to be unclear. As such, Onionsan usually uses the polite, somewhat gender neutral Japanese pronoun watashi. On other occasions, Onionsan simply says "Onionsan" instead of using a pronoun, which lends the character even more of a childish vibe.

translation.text: 和 Undertale 的其他几个角色一样，Onionsan 的性别有意保持模糊。因此，其日语通常采用礼貌、相对中性的第一人称 watashi（我）。有时又不用代词，直接以“Onionsan”自称，令角色更显孩子气。

source.text: Japanese Personal Pronouns: {own name)

translation.text: 日语人称表达：用自己的名字自称

source.text: In Japanese entertainment, characters sometimes refer to themselves by using their own name rather than a pronoun. This happens in other languages too, of course, but it's extraordinarily common in Japanese media. The use of one's own name instead of a pronoun can make a character seem childish, endearing, or uncivilized. Examples of such pronoun-less characters include:

translation.text: 日本娱乐作品中的角色，有时会不用代词，而用自己的名字自称。其他语言当然也有这种情况，但在日本作品里尤其常见。用名字代替“我”，会让角色显得孩子气、惹人喜爱，或带点未开化的感觉。采用这种自称的角色包括：

source.text: Relm (Final Fantasy VI)

translation.text:
Relm
（Final Fantasy VI）

source.text: Ayla (C hrono Trigger)

translation.text:
Ayla
（Chrono Trigger）

source.text: Playing Onion Games

translation.text: 洋葱游戏

source.text: Other characters say "hum hum hum" as a gameplay hint, but Toby's notes paint this particular "hum hum hum" as more of a fun reference than a hint

translation.text: 其他角色说“hum hum hum”是为了提示玩法，但按 Toby 的注释，这一处更偏向有趣的典故。

source.text: If the player calls Papyrus' cell phone twice while in Onionsan's room, Papyrus will say in English:

translation.text: 玩家在 Onionsan 所在房间里连续两次拨打 Papyrus 的手机，Papyrus 会在英语版里说：

source.text: HUM HUM HUM. ..

translation.text: HUM HUM HUM……（哼哼哼……）

source.text: In his translation notes, Toby explained that this is an indirect gameplay hint and a reference to the game development studio Onion Games. More specifically, it's a reference to what Onion Games' avatar often says in English language messages online. Toby wasn't sure if this reference would work in Japanese, however, so the translator revised Onionsan's line to say:

translation.text: Toby 在翻译注释里解释，这既是间接的玩法提示，也引用了游戏开发工作室 Onion Games。具体来说，Onion Games 的形象角色常在网上发布的英语消息里这么说。不过，Toby 不确定这个典故对日本玩家是否有效，所以译者把这句台词改为：

source.text: Yamada-kun ... ?

translation.text: Yamada-kun……？（山田君……？）

source.text: This new line is a reference to one of Onion Games' most popular games, known in Japan as Yiisha Yamada-kun ("Yamada the Hero") and elsewhere as Dandy Dungeon. This localization change has two effects: it makes the reference recognizable in Japanese, and it strengthens the original line's connection between Onionsan and Onion Games.

translation.text: 新版台词引用了 Onion Games 最受欢迎的游戏之一：日本名为 Yūsha Yamada-kun（《勇者山田君》），海外名为 Dandy Dungeon。这个本地化改动有两个效果：让日本玩家认得出典故，也加强了原句中 Onionsan 与 Onion Games 的联系。

source.text: LEFT: The "hum hum hum" in an Onion Games tweet

translation.text: 左：Onion Games 推文中的“hum hum hum”。

source.text: RIGHT: Yusha Yamada kun!Dandy Dungeon is about a programmer who aims to create his own ideal game

translation.text: 右：《勇者山田君》（Dandy Dungeon）讲的是一名程序员想要制作自己理想中的游戏。

source.text: Waterfall

translation.text: 瀑布

source.text: Money Minded

translation.text: 金钱的方向

source.text: Translation spreadsheets are usually enormous walls of text without context, which makes lines like this very easy to get wrong in translation

translation.text: 翻译表格通常堆满海量文字，却缺乏情境信息，因此这种台词很容易译错。

source.text: A purple monster offers to give the main character a ferry ride. In English, it says:

translation.text: 一个紫色怪物愿意载主角渡河。英语里，它说：

source.text: Three gold for the ferry.

translation.text: 渡河，三个金币。

source.text: Toby worded this line to fool players into thinking that the purple monster charges three gold pieces per ferry ride. In actuality, the purple monster gives the player three gold pieces after the ferry ride. It's a small, unexpected gag that pokes fun at veteran gamers' expectations.

translation.text: Toby 故意这样写，让玩家以为紫色怪物每次渡河收三个金币。实际上，渡河后它反而会给玩家三个金币。这个小小的意外笑话，戏弄了老玩家的惯性预期。

source.text: Because this line plays with vagueness and expectations, and because Toby didn't mention this line in his translation notes, a rushed translator or an automated translator would've almost certainly mistranslated it as "it costs three gold to ride the ferry". Fortunately, Underta/e's localization team did recognize the joke and was able to properly preserve it in the Japanese script.

translation.text: 这句话靠含糊措辞与预期落差制造笑点，Toby 又没有专门作注释，因此匆忙赶工的译者或自动翻译几乎一定会误译成“渡河要花三个金币”。幸运的是，Undertale 的本地化团队看出了笑话，并在日文剧本中妥善保留。

source.text: Music Ghost Z

translation.text: 音乐幽灵 Z

source.text: Papyrus continually messes up Napstablook’s name and accidentally hits upon the name ナッパブー (nappa bū).

translation.text: Papyrus 总叫错 Napstablook 的名字，无意间叫出了“ナッパブー”（nappa bū，那巴布欧）。

source.text: Papyrus struggles with Napstablook's name and calls the character "Napper Hog". He corrupts Napstablook's name in a similar way in Japanese, resulting in the name Nappa Buu. The translator noted that this wasn't intentional at first, but both "Nappa" and "Buu" are characters from the Dragon Ball Z series.

translation.text: Papyrus 记不住 Napstablook 的名字，管这个角色叫“Napper Hog”（打盹猪）。日语里也有类似的叫错，结果变成了 Nappa Buu。译者指出，最初并不是有意为之，但“Nappa”（那巴）与“Buu”（布欧）恰好都是《龙珠 Z》的角色。

source.text: LEFT: Nappa is an early foe in Dragon Ball l

translation.text: 左：Nappa 是《龙珠 Z》早期的敌人。

source.text: RIGHT: Buu is a major enemy much later in Dragon Ball I

translation.text: 右：Buu 是《龙珠 Z》后期的重要敌人。

source.text: When Napstablook was still named "Winnybore" in early drafts of the Japanese script, Papyrus corrupted "Winnybore" into ウィンナーボー (winnābō), which can be humorously interpreted as "Weiner Stick", among other things.

translation.text: 早期日文译稿中，Napstablook 还叫“Winnybore”时，Papyrus 会把它叫成“ウィンナーボー”（winnābō），可以让人联想到“香肠棒”等好笑的意思。

source.text: Bootiful Music

translation.text: 美妙的鬼音乐

source.text: If someone handed me a song like this and asked me to translate it, I'd assume it's a trick question at first

translation.text: 如果有人拿这样的歌来让我翻译，我起初一定会以为对方在故意考我。

source.text: Napstablook enjoys some ghostly "spooktunes" with the main character. In the English script, the lyrics to one song are simply:

translation.text: Napstablook 和主角一起欣赏幽灵的“spooktunes”（鬼曲）。英语剧本里，有首歌的歌词只是：

source.text:
ooo ooo oooo
ooo ooo oooo
oo oo ooo oo ooo

translation.text:
ooo ooo oooo
ooo ooo oooo
oo oo ooo oo ooo

source.text: Actual music - accompanied by spooky vocal sounds - plays while these lyrics are displayed. The song seems like random, meaningless nonsense at first, but Toby noted that the song is actually "Jingle Bells", the classic popular Christmas song.

translation.text: 显示这些歌词时，游戏会播放音乐，伴着经典的幽灵叫声。起初，这首歌看似随意、毫无意义，但 Toby 指出，它其实是流行的经典圣诞歌曲《铃儿响叮当》。

source.text: In English, ghosts sometimes say "oo" as a stereotypical spooky sound. Hoping to preserve this idea in Japanese, the translator gave the song new lyrics:

translation.text: 英语中的鬼魂有时会发出“oo”（呜——）这样的吓人叫声。为了在日语中保留这个想法，译者重新填了歌词：

source.text:
u~ra~me~
shi~ya~u~
ra~me~shi~~ya u~

translation.text:
u～ra～me～
shi～ya～u～
ra～me～shi～～ya u～

source.text: In Japanese, urameshiya (roughly "oh, how I begn1dge you" or "I curse you") is a stereotypical phrase that ghosts say, similar to how ghosts say "boo" or "oo" in some English speaking regions. Even with these new Japanese lyrics, however, the song was crafted to follow the tune of "Jingle Bells".

translation.text: 日语中的 urameshiya，大意为“我好恨你啊”或“我诅咒你”，是鬼魂常说的固定台词，类似一些英语地区的“boo”或“oo”。即使用了这套新日文歌词，歌曲仍然配合《铃儿响叮当》的旋律。

source.text: As we've already seen, classic Christmas songs are known in Japan, and many of them have received multiple translations into Japanese. I wonder if there are ever heated arguments about which version of "Jingle Bells" is the "truer" translation

translation.text: 前面说过，经典圣诞歌曲在日本也很有名，许多还有多个日语译本。不知道人们会不会为哪个《铃儿响叮当》译本更“忠实”而争个面红耳赤。

source.text: In early drafts of the translation, Napstablook sang all new Japanese lyrics when listening to this spooktune

translation.text: 早期译稿中，Napstablook 听这首鬼曲时，唱的是全新日文歌词。

source.text: As the final draft of the Japanese translation began to solidify, Toby requested that the uremishiya lyrics be changed back to "oo" sounds to properly match the actual "oo" sound effects that accompany the music.

translation.text: 日语译稿逐渐定稿时，Toby 要求把 urameshiya 歌词改回“oo”的叫声，好与音乐中实际播放的“oo”音效一致。

source.text: Waterfall

translation.text: 瀑布

source.text: Gerson Speaks

translation.text: Gerson 的说话方式

source.text: Gerson uses the pronoun ワシ (washi), which is associated with elderly characters in Japanese entertainment.

translation.text: Gerson 使用“ワシ”（washi，我），这是日本娱乐作品中常与老年角色联系在一起的自称。

source.text: An elderly turtle named Gerson runs a shop in Waterfall. In English, he speaks like a kooky old man. This attribute was retained in Japanese by giving him an equivalent "stereotypical old person" speaking style. Gerson also uses the Japanese pronoun washi, which is commonly used by old characters in Japanese entertainment.

translation.text: 年迈的乌龟 Gerson 在瀑布开店。英语里，他像个古怪老头一样说话。日语通过相应的“典型老人”口吻保留了这个特点。Gerson 还使用日语第一人称 washi（我），这也是日本娱乐作品中老年角色常用的自称。

source.text: Japanese Personal Pronouns: washi

translation.text: 日语人称代词：washi

source.text: In everyday Japanese, the personal pronoun washi is strongly associated with older people and parts of western Japan. In Japanese entertainment, washi can also lend a very "traditional Japanese culture" vibe to samurai warriors, sumo wrestlers, etc. Some familiar washi users include:

translation.text: 日常日语中，washi（我）与老年人及日本西部部分地区的说话习惯联系紧密。在日本娱乐作品里，武士、相扑力士等角色用 washi 自称，还能带出浓厚的“日本传统文化”气息。熟悉的例子包括：

source.text: Master Roshi (Dragon Ball series)

translation.text:
Master Roshi（龟仙人）
（《龙珠》系列）

source.text: Cranky Kong (Super Donkey Kong/ Donkey Kong Country series)

translation.text:
Cranky Kong（Super Donkey Kong／
Donkey Kong Country 系列）

source.text: Old Woman in Kakariko Village (The Legend of Zelda series)

translation.text:
卡卡利科村的老妇人
（《塞尔达传说》系列）

source.text: E. Honda (Street Fighter series)

translation.text:
E. Honda
（《街头霸王》系列）

source.text: Delta Force

translation.text: Delta 的力量

source.text: Here's hoping we see Underta/e 11: UNRELATED and Underta/e 17: NUDER TALE someday!

translation.text: 希望有朝一日能玩到 Undertale 11: UNRELATED（无关）和 Undertale 17: NUDER TALE（更裸的故事）！这两个名字也都是 Undertale 的字母重排。

source.text: Gerson also explains that a reoccurring symbol in the game is called the "Delta Rune". In the translation spreadsheet, Toby left only one short note for the localization team:

translation.text: Gerson 还会解释，游戏中反复出现的标志叫作“Delta Rune”。Toby 在翻译表格里只给团队留了一条简短注释：

source.text: Delta Rune= anagrnm for Under tale

translation.text: Delta Rune＝Undertale 的字母重排。

source.text: At first, the translator paralleled this wordplay by scrambling the word アンダーテイル (andāteiru, "Undertale") to create a new Japanese anagram: テアイダ・ルーン (teaida rūn, "Teaida Rune"). It’s unclear if the name holds any specific meaning, however, as teaida isn’t a standard Japanese word.

translation.text: 起初，译者模仿这个文字游戏，把“アンダーテイル”（andāteiru，Undertale 的日语音译）重新排列，造出“テアイダ・ルーン”（teaida rūn，Teaida Rune）。不过，teaida 并不是标准日语词，因此不清楚这个名字是否有特定含义。

source.text: Although it’s not a real word, テアイダ (teaida) could potentially mean "between hands" or "a match-up between two competitors", among other things.

translation.text: “テアイダ”（teaida）虽然不是现成的词，但也可以让人联想到“手之间”“双方的对阵”等意思。

source.text: Before Underta/e's Japanese release, Toby emphatically requested that "Teida Rune" be changed back to "Delta Rune" and left in English text. This choice preserved the original English anagram. For added measure, and for the Japanese audience's sake, the translator included the Japanese pronunciation of "DELTA RUNE" in parentheses the first time the term is introduced.

translation.text: Undertale 日语版发行前，Toby 强烈要求把“Teaida Rune”改回“Delta Rune”，并保留英文字母。这样，原版的字母重排关系就保住了。为方便日本玩家，译者又在这个词首次出现时，用括号附上“DELTA RUNE”的日语读音。

source.text: Deltarune is a sort of alternate universe version of Undertale that tells a different story, or something like that

translation.text: Deltarune 大概算是 Undertale 的平行世界，讲述另一段故事，或者类似这么回事。

source.text: In late 2018, Toby released Chapter 1 of a new game he called Delta rune. Suddenly, the anagram connection between "Undertale" and "Delta Rune" became clear to many more fans around the world. Had the Japanese translation of Undertale stuck with "Teaida Rune", though, this after-the-fact connection might've been lost in translation.

translation.text: 2018 年末，Toby 发布了新游戏 Deltarune 的第一章。突然间，全球更多粉丝看明白了“Undertale”与“Delta Rune”的字母重排关系。倘若 Undertale 日译版当初坚持用“Teaida Rune”，这个事后才显露的联系可能就会在翻译中丢失。

source.text: Waterfall

translation.text: 瀑布

source.text: Hot Stuff

translation.text: 火热甩卖

source.text: "Stop, drop, and roll" is one of those phrases every kid in America learns over and over at an early age, along with "stranger danger"

translation.text: “停下、趴下、打滚”和“小心陌生人”一样，是美国孩子从小反复学的口诀。

source.text: In English, Papyrus suggests that the player visit Gerson's shop by saying:

translation.text: 英语版中，Papyrus 这样建议玩家去 Gerson 的商店看看：

source.text: IF YOU SEE A SHOP, YOU SHOULD STOP. .. DROP, AND ROLL... INTO SOME GREAT DEALS!! BECAUSE WE'RE HAVING A FIRE SALE!! AT MY IMAGINARY STORE, WHICH SELLS FLAMES.

translation.text: 看到商店，你就该停下……趴下，然后滚……进超值优惠里！！我们正在举办 FIRE SALE（火灾后大甩卖）！！就在我那家想象中的、专卖火焰的店里。

source.text: In some English-speaking regions, children are taught the phrase "stop, drop, and roll" as a way to remember what to do if their clothes catch on fire. This reference and Papyrus' fire puns would be lost in a literal translation, so the translator adjusted the line:

translation.text: 一些英语地区会教孩子 stop, drop, and roll（停下、趴下、打滚），记住衣服着火时的应对方法。这一典故和 Papyrus 的火焰双关直译就没了，因此译者改成：

source.text: I heard "stop, drop, and roll" so often as a kid that it almost felt like catching on fire was a common problem we'd all face daily when we grew up - same with quicksand, too

translation.text: 我小时候听“停下、趴下、打滚”听得太多，差点以为长大后身上着火会是天天遇到的问题——流沙也是一样。

source.text: IF YOU SHOULD SPOT A SHOP. .. GO IN WITHOUT A SECOND THOUGHT! YOU'RE SURE TO FIND A GREAT BARGAIN! A BARGAIN ON WHAT? HOW SHOULD I KNOW?! BUT ANY BARGAIN IS A MUST-BUY IN MY BOOK!

translation.text: 看见商店……就别犹豫，进去吧！你一定能找到好划算的东西！什么东西划算？我怎么知道？！反正只要划算，在我看来就必须买！

source.text: This new line lacks the multiple comedic punches of the original English line, but it still sounds silly and fits Papyrus' "weird yet happy-go-lucky" personality.

translation.text: 新版台词没有原版层层推进的笑点，但仍然傻乎乎的，也符合 Papyrus 古怪却乐天的性格。

source.text: Sea of Creativi-Tea

translation.text: 海茶的创意

source.text: I've seen Japanese fans praise this minor, unimportant item name, which shows that even the smallest things do matter and do get noticed in a localization!

translation.text: 我见过日本粉丝称赞这件不起眼的小道具的译名。这说明，本地化中再小的细节，也有意义，也会有人留意！

source.text: Gerson sells a Waterfall-exclusive item named "Sea Tea" in the English script. This name contains a basic rhyme, but no wordplay beyond that.

translation.text: Gerson 出售一种瀑布特产，英语名为“Sea Tea”（海茶）。这个名字简单地押了韵，没有其他文字游戏。

source.text: After some brainstorming, the localization team chose a new name for "Sea Tea": Bichabi-cha. This is a play on the Japanese words cha ("tea") and bichabicha ("sopping wet; soggy"), and was intended to sound like real-life tea brands such as Sokenbicha. Thus, the Japanese name for "Sea Tea" has a level of wordplay that goes beyond the simple rhyme of the original English name.

translation.text: 团队集思广益后，为“Sea Tea”取了新名字：Bichabi-cha。它结合了日语 cha（茶）与 bichabicha（湿漉漉、湿透了），同时有意模仿 Sōkenbicha（爽健美茶）等现实茶饮品牌。因此，日文名的文字游戏比英文原名的简单押韵又多了一层。

source.text: I am a Sokenbicha bottle

translation.text: 我是一瓶爽健美茶。

source.text: Getting Crabby

translation.text: 螃蟹苹果

source.text: The "Crab Apple" item was renamed to stay funny and understandable for Japanese players

translation.text: “Crab Apple”改了名字，好让日本玩家也能看懂并觉得好笑。

source.text: Gerson also sells an item known as the "Crab Apple" in the English script. The item's description is:

translation.text: Gerson 还出售一种英语名为“Crab Apple”的道具，说明写着：

source.text: An aquatic fruit that resembles a crustacean.

translation.text: 一种形似甲壳动物的水生水果。

source.text: Crab apples (sometimes spelled "crabapples") are a real thing - they're essentially a type of wild apple. They look like smaller versions of regular apples and tend to be very sour or bitter. So the joke here is that Crab Apples in Undertale are literal crab-shaped apples, rather than the real-life crab apples that savvy players might envision.

translation.text: Crab apple（也拼作 crabapple）在现实中确有其物，基本上是一类野生苹果，模样像缩小的普通苹果，通常很酸或很苦。笑点在于，Undertale 里的 Crab Apple 真的是螃蟹形状的苹果，而不是熟悉这个词的玩家想象中的现实水果。

source.text: The English wordplay that connects the "Crab Apple" name and its description would be lost in a literal translation, so the localization team relied on a more creative solution: combining the wordsfujimi ("immortality") and ringo ("apple"). The resulting name, Fujiringo, usually means "Fuji apple" in everyday Japanese, but instead means "immortality apple" in this specific, unexpected context.

translation.text: 名称与道具说明之间的英语文字游戏，直译会丢失。团队于是采用更有创意的办法，把日语 fujimi（不死）和 ringo（苹果）结合起来。得到的名字 Fujiringo，平时指“富士苹果”，但在这个出人意料的特定语境里，却变成了“不死苹果”。

source.text: LEFT: Crab apples do seem to have a fitting name

translation.text: 左：Crab apple 的名字看起来还真有点贴切。

source.text: RIGHT: Fuji apples are named after Fujisaki, the city they originate from

translation.text: 右：富士苹果以其发源地藤崎命名。

source.text: Naturally, changing the item's name meant that the original item description would no longer make sense, so the translator gave it an all-new description:

translation.text: 名字改了，原来的道具说明自然就不再合适，因此译者另写了一段：

source.text: Rumored to grant immortality when eaten. But it's actually just a normal apple.

translation.text: 据说吃了便能长生不死。其实只是普通苹果。

source.text: From all of this, we can see that the localized item name follows the ideas of the original item name: it contains wordplay, remains apple-themed, and matches the name of a type of real-life apple. At the same time, however, the Japanese name lacks the original's aquatic theme shared by many items found in Waterfall.

translation.text: 可见，本地化后的名称沿用了原名的思路：有文字游戏，仍然与苹果有关，又与现实中的苹果品种同名。但另一方面，日文名失去了原版的水生主题，而这恰好是瀑布地区许多道具共有的特点。

source.text: Temmies Speak

translation.text: Temmie 们的说话方式

source.text: Although both names are pronounced temī in Japanese, Temmies humorously misspell their names 手ミー instead of テミー.

translation.text: 两种日文写法都读 temī。Temmie 们却把“テミー”写成了滑稽的“手ミー”。

source.text: A strange area named Temmie Village exists in Waterfall. Unsurprisingly, almost every monster living in Temmie Village is named "Temmie''. These Temmie characters look unusual, behave strangely, and speak in a unique way.

translation.text: 瀑布中藏着一个奇怪的地方：Temmie Village（Temmie 村）。不出所料，村里的怪物几乎都叫“Temmie”。这些角色模样奇特，行为古怪，说话方式也与众不同。

source.text: In the English script, Temmies often call themselves "temmie", "TEMMIE", or "tEMMIE" - capitalization seemingly has no meaning for them. In other instances, Temmies simply call themselves "tem". To replicate this unusual English wordplay, the translator devised a simple system:

translation.text: 英文剧本里，Temmie 们常称自己为“temmie”“TEMMIE”或“tEMMIE”，大小写似乎对它们毫无意义。有时它们干脆叫自己“tem”。为了模仿这种特殊的英语文字游戏，译者定了一个简单规则：

source.text: 1. When "Temmie" is spelled correctly in the English script, the Japanese script should use the properly spelled name テミー (temī).

translation.text: 1. 英文中“Temmie”拼写正确时，日文使用正确写法“テミー”（temī）。

source.text: 2. When "Temmie" is misspelled, the Japanese script should use the misspelled name 手ミー (temī) instead.

translation.text: 2. 英文中“Temmie”拼错时，日文改用错误写法“手ミー”（temī）。

source.text: Basically, both Japanese names for "Temmie" are pronounced the same, but the misspelled name mixes two Japanese writing systems in an unexpected way. The resulting misspelling, which combines the kanji character 手 (te, "hand") with the katakana characters ミー (mī), is bizarre, funny, and memorable.

translation.text: 两种日文名字读音相同，但错误写法出人意料地混合了两种文字：把汉字“手”（te，手）与片假名“ミー”（mī）拼在一起。这样的错字古怪、好笑，又让人记得住。

source.text: Temmies use the feminine pronoun あちし (achishi).

translation.text: Temmie 们使用偏女性的自称“あちし”（achishi，我）。

source.text: In English, Temmies sound like hyperactive, energetic girls. In Japanese, Temmies use a variety of unique speech patterns to sound equally hyperactive and energetic. And although they don't use pronouns very often, Temmies in the Japanese script use the youthful and feminine personal pronoun achishi.

translation.text: 英语版的 Temmie 们听起来像过分兴奋、活力十足的女孩。日文也用了多种独特的说话习惯，传达同样的亢奋与活力。虽然它们不常用代词，但需要时，会采用年轻、偏女性的第一人称 achishi（我）。

source.text: In the English script, one unusual Temmie uses proper grammar and introduces himself as "Bob". For the Japanese script, the translator left Bob's name as-is, and gave him a polite, grammatically correct speech pattern. As part of this, Bob uses the boyish pronoun boku.

translation.text: 英文剧本里有一只与众不同的 Temmie，语法完全正确，还自称“Bob”。日语版保留了 Bob 的名字，并让他说礼貌、语法正确的话。他也相应使用带少年感的第一人称 boku（我）。

source.text: Bob speaks more like a normal person in Japanese and uses the boyish pronoun ぼく (boku).

translation.text: Bob 在日语中说话比较像正常人，使用少年式的自称“ぼく”（boku，我）。

source.text: Japanese Personal Pronouns: achishi

translation.text: 日语人称代词：achishi

source.text: In standard Japanese, the informal personal pronoun achishi is a part of some regional dialects, but has generally begun to fall out of use. In Japanese entertainment, achishi is commonly associated with feminine characters with youthful energy. Other fictional characters who use achishi include:

translation.text: 日语中，非正式自称 achishi（我）见于一些地方方言，但总体上已逐渐少用。在日本娱乐作品里，它通常与活力充沛、偏女性的角色相联系。其他使用 achishi 的虚构角色包括：

source.text: Gramatically Temmie

translation.text: Temmie 式语法

source.text: Note that "Temminese" is just an unofficial name I made up for convenience's sake - I've never heard anyone say it before, not even Toby

translation.text: 注意，“Temminese”（Temmie 语）只是我为方便讨论而起的非正式名称。我从没听过别人这么说，包括 Toby。

source.text: In English, the Temmies speak in "Temminese" - an extremely unique dialect that can be described as an absolute disaster of the English language. Toby's explanation to the localization staff offers some details:

translation.text: 英语版中，Temmie 们说着“Temmie 语”：一种极其独特的方言，简直是英语的大灾难。Toby 给本地化人员的说明提供了一些细节：

source.text: Temmies are based off of how my friend Temmie talks, which is to say with a lot of typos and weird phrases. Kind ofl ike Mr. Saturn I guess but more like chatspeak. Temmies are generally all girls besides Bob I think.

translation.text: Temmie 们的说话方式，参考了我的朋友 Temmie：错字很多，措辞也很奇怪。大概有点像 Mr. Saturn，但更接近网络聊天语言。除了 Bob 之外，Temmie 应该基本都是女孩。

source.text: In short, Temminese makes Temmies sounds hyper-energetic, excitable, upbeat, and positive. These qualities, combined with their butchering of the English language, make the Temmies' dialogue funny, endearing, and quotable.

translation.text: Temmie 语让这些角色显得精力过剩、容易兴奋、乐观积极。再加上它们对英语的胡乱糟蹋，台词便既好笑、惹人喜欢，又让人忍不住引用。

source.text: This unique butchery of the English language would be lost in a straightforward translation into Japanese. But because Temmies are so memorable and strange, the localization team spent weeks on creating a solid, Japanese equivalent of English Temminese. The resulting Japanese speech style included:

translation.text: 这种糟蹋英语的独特方式，直接翻译成日语就会消失。但 Temmie 们实在古怪而令人难忘，本地化团队为此花了好几周，打磨出与英语 Temmie 语相当的日语风格，包括：

source.text: In EarthBound, beings known as "Mr. Saturn" speak strangely and with a weird font

translation.text: EarthBound 中，名为 Mr. Saturn 的生物说话很奇怪，字体也很奇怪。

source.text: Having Temmies use hyper, cute, teenage girl-like speech styles Having Temmies make amusing and bizarre word choices Breaking Japanese grammar non-stop Misspelling things in amusing and surprising ways Unexpectedly switching between the hiragana and katakana writing systems Using hiragana and katakana in ways that no normal person would use them Using hiragana and katakana in ways that are potentially unpronounceable Mixing half-width Japanese characters with full-width Japanese characters

translation.text:
• 使用亢奋、可爱、少女式的语气。
• 选择好笑而古怪的词。
• 不断破坏日语语法。
• 把字写得出人意料地好笑。
• 出其不意地切换平假名与片假名。
• 以正常人不会采用的方式使用平假名与片假名。
• 把平假名与片假名组合成可能根本念不出来的写法。
• 混用半角和全角日文字符。

source.text: By incorporating these language quirks into the Temmies' dialogue, the localization team ensured that Temmies sound hyper, cute, upbeat, earnest, and unique in Japanese, while also sounding weird, goofy, slightly annoying, and unintelligent. In short, Temmies are as memorable in the Japanese version of Undertale as they are in the English release.

translation.text: 把这些语言怪癖融入台词后，团队让日语 Temmie 们既亢奋、可爱、乐观、认真、独特，也古怪、傻气、有点烦人，还不太聪明。结果是：在 Undertale 日语版里，Temmie 们和英语版一样令人难忘。

source.text: The Japanese script combines a variety of language tricks to reinforce the idea that Temmies speak unlike any other character in the game

translation.text: 日文剧本结合多种语言手法，突出 Temmie 们与游戏中其他所有角色截然不同的说话方式。

source.text: typo/wrong character

translation.text: 错字／错用字

source.text: typo/wrong character/wrong writing system

translation.text:
错字／错用字／
错用文字体系

source.text: half-width characters

translation.text: 半角字符

source.text: By making up new words and distorting existing words, Temmies come across as hyperactive girls in Japanese - in this example, a Temmie says kyawawa instead of kawaii ("cute")

translation.text: 通过自造词和扭曲现成词语，日语 Temmie 们听起来像过分兴奋的女孩。比如这里把 kawaii（可爱）说成 kyawawa，一种故意变形的“可爱”。

source.text: Temmies use unusual spelling choices, such as using ぢ (ji) instead of じ (ji). Both are pronounced the same, but the former isn’t commonly seen in written Japanese these days, outside of a few specific situations.

translation.text: Temmie 们会用不寻常的写法，比如用“ぢ”（ji）代替“じ”（ji）。两者读音相同，但如今除了少数特定情况，书面日语很少使用前者。

source.text: In early drafts of the translation, the English Temmie greeting of "hOI" became ai in Japanese, which isn’t a normal word in this context. On Toby’s request, the team changed every ai back to hoi—but missed this single ai in battle.

translation.text: 早期译稿把英语问候语“hOI”译成 ai，这并不是正常的招呼用语。应 Toby 要求，团队把所有 ai 改回 hoi，却漏掉了战斗中的这一处 ai。

source.text: In English, Temmies say "bOI!!" when saying goodbye. In Japanese, they say "Bye-nara!", a combination of the English word "bye" and the Japanese word sayōnara.

translation.text: 英语版中，Temmie 们用“bOI!!”告别。日语则说“Bye-nara!”，把英语 bye 与日语 sayōnara 这两个“再见”拼在一起。

source.text: Waterfall

translation.text: 瀑布

source.text: Determination Migration

translation.text: 决心的变形

source.text: As per Temminese grammar rules, the word ケツイ (ketsui) in this line is spelled improperly as ケッィ. It’s such a weird spelling that I’m not even sure how to pronounce it!

translation.text: 按照 Temmie 语的规则，这句中的“ケツイ”（ketsui，决心）被写错成“ケッィ”。这写法太怪，我都不确定该怎么念！

source.text: In English, using the save point in Temmie Village results in the message:

translation.text: 英语版中，使用 Temmie 村的存档点，会看到：

source.text: (You feel ... something.) (You're filled with detemmienation.)

translation.text:
（你感觉到了……某种东西。）
（你充满了 detemmienation。）

source.text: The word "detemmienation" in this message is a combination of the word "determination" - a key term in Underta/e's story - and the name "Temmie".

translation.text: 这里的“detemmienation”结合了 Undertale 故事的关键词 determination（决心），以及名字 Temmie。

source.text: Because the Japanese script translates "determination" as ketsui, this line's wordplay would be lost in a straightforward translation. To get around this obstacle, the translator replaced "you're filled with detemmienation" with the Japanese Temminese equivalent of "you're filled with determination". The resulting Japanese line no longer relies on wordplay, but it does remain humorous and Temmie-themed.

translation.text: 日文把 determination 译作 ketsui（决心），因此直接翻译就会失去文字游戏。为解决这个问题，译者把“你充满了 detemmienation”换成了用日语 Temmie 语写的“你充满了决心”。新版不再依赖双关，却仍然好笑，也仍然与 Temmie 有关。

source.text: Flaking Out

translation.text: 麦片没讨到

source.text: This English text is ~ actually a hand-drawn image and not normal text, so a Japanese image had to be created and added to the game too

translation.text: 这里的英文其实是一张手绘图片，而不是普通文字。因此还得另做一张日文图片，加入游戏。

source.text: If the player refuses to give Temmie Flakes to a Temmie in battle, Temmie says "can't blame a BARK for tryin' ..." in English as a funny tune plays. In his notes, Toby explained this line and his vision for the Japanese equivalent:

translation.text: 战斗中，如果玩家拒绝给 Temmie 吃 Temmie Flakes（Temmie 麦片），它会伴着滑稽的曲调说“can’t blame a BARK for tryin’…”（不能怪一声“汪”想试试嘛……）。Toby 在注释中解释了这句话，以及他对日文版本的设想：

source.text: '' Pretty much a meaningless/nonsense phrase, though the idea is "you can't blame me for trying (to get those temmie flakes)." temmie makes a special face during this action. Honestly it might be interesting if this was completely changed, including her face,for absolutely no reason, as one of those translation mysteries like, if her face became very manly and she just says "You have entered the pit ofh ell ..."

translation.text: 基本上是句没什么意义的胡话，不过意思是“不能怪我想试着弄到那些 Temmie 麦片”。Temmie 做这个动作时会露出特殊表情。说真的，要是毫无理由地把它全改了，连表情一起改，或许挺有趣，变成那种让人摸不着头脑的翻译谜团。比如她突然长出一张特别硬汉的脸，只说：“你已踏入地狱深渊……”

source.text: Using this information, the translator changed the Temrnie line to say "heh ... you've just opened the gates to hell" in an assertive, masculine tone in Japanese.

translation.text: 根据这段说明，译者把日文台词改成了“呵……你刚刚打开了地狱之门”，用强硬、男性化的语气说出。

source.text: Japanese Half-width Characters

translation.text: 日文半角字符

source.text: In standard written Japanese, most characters share the same size and adhere to a grid format. In computer lingo, these are sometimes referred to as "full-width characters".

translation.text: 在规范的日文书写中，大多数字符大小相同，排列成整齐的方格。用计算机术语来说，这些字符有时叫作“全角字符”。

source.text: For various technical and historical reasons, early Japanese computing systems used "half-width characters". These squished characters allowed two characters to fit in the space of one standard character. This came at a cost, however: the half-width character set only supports one Japanese writing system: katakana.

translation.text: 由于技术和历史方面的原因，早期日文计算机系统采用了“半角字符”。字符被压窄后，一个标准字符的空间就能容纳两个字符。不过，这也有代价：半角字符集只支持一种日文文字——片假名。

source.text: Here, we see the name "Super Mario" written in full-width Japanese and in half-width Japanese

translation.text: “Super Mario”的日文全角写法与半角写法

source.text: Today, modern technology and robust text encoding standards have made half-width characters mostly obsolete, although they still appear in a handful of ways:

translation.text: 如今，现代技术和完善的文字编码标准已使半角字符基本过时，不过仍可在少数场合见到：

source.text: Older mobile phones and devices with small screens

translation.text: 早期手机及其他小屏幕设备

source.text: Internet slang, particularly during the 2000s

translation.text: 网络用语，尤其在 2000 年代

source.text: half-width characters

translation.text: 半角字符

source.text: same word, full-width characters

translation.text: 同一个词的全角写法

source.text: Cash register receipts

translation.text: 收银小票

source.text: Video subtitles

translation.text: 视频字幕

source.text: Given the limited use of half-width characters today, it's fascinating to see them being used to stylize character dialogue in a video game!

translation.text: 如今半角字符用途有限，却被用来塑造游戏角色的说话风格，实在有趣！

translation.text: 大学与红薯

source.text: Here's hoping they release Underta/e-brand cool legs and sweet potatoes someday

translation.text: 真希望哪天能买到 Undertale 牌的酷腿和红薯。

source.text: One Temmie has opened a shop to earn enough money to attend college someday. But, because Temmies are scatterbrained and speak oddly, this Temmie regularly misspells the English word "college".

translation.text: 有只 Temmie 开了商店，想攒钱上大学。但 Temmie 们迷迷糊糊，说话又古怪，因此这只 Temmie 经常拼错 college（大学）。

source.text: In one scene, purchasing an expensive item results in this text:

translation.text: 在一段情节中，买下昂贵的商品后，会看到这些台词：

source.text: WOA!! thas ALOT o muns... can tem realy acepts... OKs!!!! tem go to colleg and make u prouds!!! [...] tem bak from cool leg, tem learn MANY THINs, learn to sell new ITEM! yayA!!!

translation.text:
哇！！这么多钱……tem 真的能收吗……
好哒！！！！tem 要去 colleg（大学），让你骄傲！！！
［……］
tem 从 cool leg（酷腿）回来啦，tem 学了好多东西，学会卖新商品！
耶呀！！！

source.text: This bizarre misspelling of "college" as "cool leg" quickly became a fan favorite quote among English-speaking players. The joke would be lost in a straightforward translation, however, so the translator replaced it with a funny cultural reference that would make sense to Japanese players:

translation.text: 把 college（大学）错拼成 cool leg（酷腿），很快成了英语玩家津津乐道的台词。不过，直接翻译就会失去笑点，于是译者换成了日本玩家能理解的文化笑料：

source.text: wENt to co/LEge. poTAtOes not there.

translation.text: 去大学了。没有红薯。

source.text: This is a humorous reference to a famous food in Japan called daigaku imo, which translates as "college potato" or "university potato". Daigaku imo is basically deep-fried sweet potato covered with a hard sugar coating. It first gained popularity in the 1900s as an inexpensive, but filling meal for Japanese university students, and has since become a standard dish that can be found in countless recipe books, restaurants, and food stalls throughout Japan.

translation.text: 这句打趣的是日本名吃“大学芋”（daigaku imo），字面意思就是“大学的薯”。它是炸过后裹上硬糖衣的红薯。20 世纪初，这种便宜又顶饱的食物在日本大学生中流行起来，此后成为常见小吃，日本各地无数食谱、餐馆和摊位上都能见到。

source.text: LEFT: Daigaku imo is a type of candied sweet potato that can be found all over Japan

translation.text: 左：大学芋是一种裹糖的红薯，日本各地都有。

source.text: RIGHT: Daigaku imo is popular enough that daigaku imo-flavored snacks and candies exist

translation.text: 右：大学芋非常受欢迎，甚至有这种口味的零食和糖果。

source.text: As we can see, although this "cool leg" line is completely different in Japanese, it remains as silly as the original line. This change is also why fans outside of Japan draw art about Temmie and legs, while fans in Japan draw Temmie and sweet potatoes.

translation.text: 可见，日文这句虽然与“cool leg”完全不同，却同样傻气。也正因为这处改动，日本以外的爱好者会画 Temmie 和腿，日本爱好者则画 Temmie 和红薯。

source.text: English-speaking Undertale fans sometimes draw Temmie with unusual legs as a reference to this "cool leg" scene

translation.text: 英语圈的 Undertale 爱好者有时会给 Temmie 画上奇怪的腿，呼应“cool leg”（酷腿）这段情节。

source.text: If you've ever seen Japanese drawings of Temmie eating weird potato things, now you know why!

translation.text: 如果你见过日本画师笔下的 Temmie 吃着奇怪的薯块，现在就知道原因了！

source.text: Waterfall

translation.text: 瀑布

source.text: Undyne Speaks

translation.text: Undyne 的说话方式

source.text: Undyne uses the mostly neutral personal pronoun わたし (watashi) in Japanese

translation.text: 日语版中，Undyne 用比较中性的人称代词“わたし”（watashi，我）自称。

source.text: An intimidating knight named Undyne first appears in Waterfall. She loathes the main character at first, but the player can change her attitude over time. As such, Undyne sounds scary and ferocious in some situations, polite and friendly in others, and sometimes all of these things at once. Luckily, Toby provided many notes about Undyne's constant attitude changes.

translation.text: 令人畏惧的骑士 Undyne 首次登场于瀑布。起初她厌恶主角，但玩家可以逐渐改变她的态度。因此，Undyne 有时凶狠可怕，有时礼貌友好，有时甚至兼而有之。幸好，Toby 对她不断变化的态度留下了许多说明。

source.text: In Japanese, Undyne uses the pronoun watashi. This suits her in several ways:

translation.text: 日语中，Undyne 使用 watashi（我）自称，在几个方面都很合适：

source.text: It conveys a sense of neutral courtesy, professionalism, and honor In some contexts it can give off a sense of femininity It can be safely used in a wide variety of situations

translation.text:
• 传达中性、礼貌、专业、重荣誉的感觉。
• 某些语境下，也能显出女性气质。
• 适用范围广，在各种场合都不容易出错。

source.text: Of course, other pronouns could've suited Undyne too - one interesting solution might've been to give her a different pronoun to match her different attitudes.

translation.text: 当然，其他人称代词也可能适合 Undyne。有个有趣的办法，或许是让她随态度变化，使用不同的自称。

source.text: Similar to Papyrus' laugh, Undyne's sound of aggravation was changed slightly for the Japanese script

translation.text: 与 Papyrus 的笑声一样，Undyne 发怒时的吼声在日文剧本里也稍作了调整。

source.text: In the English script, Undyne often shouts "ngaaaah" when frustrated. Because grunts, growls, and other sounds often "feel" different in different languages, Undyne's growls were translated as nuaaaa throughout the Japanese script.

translation.text: 英语剧本中，Undyne 恼火时经常大吼“ngaaaah”。哼声、吼声等声音在不同语言中，往往给人不同的“感觉”，因此日文剧本把她的吼声统一译成 nuaaaa。

source.text: I feel like an analysis of the zillion different sounds of Japanese laughter could fill its own little textbook

translation.text: 我觉得，光分析日语里千奇百怪的笑声，就够写一本小教材了。

source.text: Undyne also tends to laugh when she's confident. In English, this laugh is spelled "fuhuhu". In Japanese,fuhuhu is sometimes associated with polite, friendly laughter and cordial giggling, so the translator localizedfuhuhu as kukukuku, which carries a sense of confidence, stubbornness, and/or cunning.

translation.text: Undyne 信心十足时也常会大笑。英语把这笑声写作“fuhuhu”。但在日语中，fuhuhu 有时让人想到礼貌、友好的笑声或亲切的轻笑。于是译者改用了 kukukuku，这种笑声带有自信、倔强或狡黠的意味。

source.text: Fatal Fall

translation.text: 把你打倒

source.text: Toby didn't note this reference, so the translator initially missed it, but luckily an American member of the localization team was there to point it out

translation.text: Toby 没有注明这处引用，因此译者最初没有发现。幸好，本地化团队的一位美国成员指出了出处。

source.text: In the English version of Undertale, Undyne shouts at the main character:

translation.text: Undertale 英语版中，Undyne 冲主角大喊：

source.text: I, Undyne, will knock you down!

translation.text: I, Undyne, will knock you down!（我，Undyne，要把你打倒！）

source.text: This laughable threat comes from a famous line in the 1990 English translation of Final Fantasy: "I, Garland, will knock you all down!".

translation.text: 这句好笑的威胁出自 Final Fantasy 1990 年英译版的名句：“I, Garland, will knock you all down!”（我，Garland，要把你们全都打倒！）

source.text: In Japanese, Garland roughly says "I, Garland, will vanquish you!", which makes it less memorable than the awkwardly phrased English translation

translation.text: 日文中，Garland 大致是在说“我，Garland，要消灭你们！”不像措辞别扭的英译那样令人难忘。

source.text: Undertale's translator retained this reference by quoting the same line from the original Japanese version of Final Fantasy.

translation.text: 日版译者引用 Final Fantasy 日文原句，保留这处致敬。

source.text: However, this Final Fantasy quote is famous because of its odd translation - the original Japanese line was normal and unremarkable. For this reason, the Final Fantasy reference is less recognizable in Japanese than in English.

translation.text: 这句台词因英译古怪而出名，日文原句却平淡无奇。因此，日语版的 Final Fantasy 致敬比英语版更难认出来。

source.text: Fishy Ideas

translation.text: 鱼腥味的笑料

source.text: In Japanese, sushi technically refers to a type of vinegared rice rather than raw fish, meaning there are genuine, authentic, non-fish types of sushi if you don't like fish (inari is my favorite!)

translation.text: 严格说来，日语 sushi（寿司）指的是一种醋饭，并非生鱼。因此，不喜欢鱼的人也能吃到正宗的无鱼寿司——我最喜欢稻荷寿司！

source.text: The text "smells like sushi" will occasionally appear while fighting Undyne. This humorous reference to raw fish makes sense, given that Undyne is a fish monster.

translation.text: 与 Undyne 战斗时，偶尔会出现“闻起来像寿司”。Undyne 是鱼形怪物，用生鱼的气味打趣她自然说得通。

source.text: At first, the translator changed "smells like sushi" to "smells like a fish market" and explained that Japanese players are more likely to associate the smell of sushi with vinegared rice rather than raw fish. Much later, Toby noted that "smells like sushi" is a fan-favorite quote and asked that it be reinstated in Japanese.

translation.text: 最初，译者把“闻起来像寿司”改成了“闻起来像鱼市”，并解释说，日本玩家闻到寿司，更容易想到醋饭，而不是生鱼。很久以后，Toby 指出“闻起来像寿司”是玩家很喜欢的台词，要求日文也恢复这一说法。

source.text: This line was originally localized as "smells like a fish market" to better retain the joke about Undyne being a fish monster, but it was un-localized due to external influences

translation.text: 最初译作“闻起来像鱼市”，是为了更好地保留 Undyne 是鱼形怪物的笑点。后来由于游戏以外的影响，这处本地化改动又被撤回。

source.text: Waterfall

translation.text: 瀑布

source.text: Dinner for Two

translation.text: 双人晚餐

source.text: Note that these screenshots are mock ups and not real

translation.text: 这些画面是示意图，并非真实游戏截图。

source.text: The translation spreadsheet includes an odd line related to the Undyne battle that simply says "Hamburger Helpers". Toby noted that this line seems to be unused in the actual game. It's likely an old error message he used while developing Underta/e. Still, the translator localized it just to be safe.

translation.text: 翻译表里有一句与 Undyne 战斗有关的怪话，只有“Hamburger Helpers”。Toby 注明，这句话似乎没有在实际游戏中使用，可能是开发 Undertale 时遗留的错误提示。不过，为保险起见，译者还是做了本地化。

source.text: Hamburger Helper is a popular meal preparation kit with a weird hand for a mascot

translation.text: Hamburger Helper 是一种很受欢迎的方便料理包，吉祥物是一只奇怪的手。

source.text: Hamburger Helper is an American packaged food product meant to simplify the meal-cooking process - the purchaser only needs to add hamburger meat before cooking. Because Hamburger Helper isn't widely known in Japan, however, the Undertale translator changed this line to say "Instant Food" instead.

translation.text: Hamburger Helper 是美国的包装食品，用来简化做饭过程：只需加入汉堡肉末，就能下锅烹饪。但这个品牌在日本并不知名，因此 Undertale 译者把这句改成了“方便食品”。

source.text: Ominous Wind

translation.text: 不祥的风

source.text: The villainous Magus can be befriended in Chrono Trigger, just as the antagonistic Undyne can be befriended in Underta/e - maybe this is partly what inspired Toby to quote Magus here

translation.text: 在 Chrono Trigger 中，玩家可以与反派 Magus 结为同伴，就像在 Undertale 中可以与敌对的 Undyne 交朋友。也许这也是 Toby 在此引用 Magus 台词的原因之一。

source.text: The phrase "the wind is howling" appears before, during, and after the battle with Undyne. Toby included this short, ominous message as a reference to the classic Japanese RPG Chrono Trigger. In the game, a villain named Magus shares two memorable lines: "the black wind begins to blow" and "the black wind howls".

translation.text: 与 Undyne 战斗前、战斗中以及战斗后，都会出现“风在呼啸”。Toby 加入这句简短而不祥的提示，是在致敬经典日式 RPG Chrono Trigger。该作反派 Magus 有两句令人难忘的台词：“黑风开始吹起”与“黑风在呼啸”。

source.text: Chrono Trigger features memorable lines about howling black wind

translation.text: Chrono Trigger 中有关黑风呼啸的台词令人难忘。

source.text: Chrono Trigger (Japan)

translation.text: Chrono Trigger（日版）

source.text: Chrono Trigger (North America)

translation.text: Chrono Trigger（北美版）

source.text: Because Magus' lines are slightly different in Japanese and English, the Undertale translator replaced Toby's indirect reference with a direct quote to keep the reference recognizable for Japanese players.

translation.text: Magus 的台词在日文与英文中略有不同，因此 Undertale 的译者把 Toby 的间接致敬换成了直接引用，让日本玩家也能认出出处。

source.text: Inspiration Spotlight: Chrono Trigger

translation.text: 灵感聚焦：Chrono Trigger

source.text: In 1995, Square released Chrono Trigger for the Japanese Super Famicom and the North American Super NES. This classic, influential Japanese RPG introduced new gameplay concepts not found in its contemporaries, including time-travel mechanics, branching storylines, and multi character battle techniques. As the product of a dream team of game developers, Chrono Trigger enjoyed commercial and critical success upon release, and remains well regarded to this day.

translation.text: 1995 年，Square 在日本 Super Famicom 与北美 Super NES 平台发行了 Chrono Trigger。这部经典日式 RPG 影响深远，加入了当时同类作品未见的玩法构想，包括时间旅行机制、分支剧情，以及多人合体战技。它由游戏开发者组成的梦之队打造，上市时销量与口碑俱佳，至今仍备受推崇。

source.text: Waterfall

translation.text: 瀑布

source.text: Power of Sugar

translation.text: 糖的力量

source.text: Reader Challenge #6: ~ Create your own "death to the enemy" lyrics for an ice cream truck song

translation.text: 读者挑战 6：给冰淇淋车的曲子填一段自己的“消灭敌人”歌词。

source.text: Undyne offers the main character a drink. Options include tea, hot chocolate, soda, and a cup of sugar. If the player selects the cup of sugar, Undyne says in English:

translation.text: Undyne 请主角喝点东西，可选茶、热巧克力、汽水和一杯糖。如果选那杯糖，英语版中 Undyne 会说：

source.text: I'm not gonna give you a cup ofs ugar! What do I look like, the ice-cream woman? Do human ice-cream women TERRORIZE HUMANITY with ENERGY SPEARS? Are their ice-cream songs a PRELUDE TO DESTRUCTION?

translation.text: 我才不会给你一杯糖！你当我是卖冰淇淋的女人吗？人类世界卖冰淇淋的女人，会用能量长矛让全人类闻风丧胆吗？她们的冰淇淋歌，是毁灭的序曲吗？

source.text: The joke here is part of a larger running gag: Undyne imagines the human world to be just like what's depicted in fiction-based anime and manga. And in this scene, she equates happy ice cream truck music with a human warrior's "death to the enemy" song.

translation.text: 这处笑料延续了游戏里反复出现的一个梗：Undyne 以为，人类世界就像虚构的动画和漫画描绘的那样。因此在这里，她把冰淇淋车欢快的音乐，当成了人类战士的“消灭敌人”之歌。

source.text: Although ice cream trucks represent a commonly shared cultural experience in many Western countries, they're culturally insignificant in Japan. This left the localization team in a tough situation: Undyne's line needs to be related to sugar, a literal translation wouldn't make much sense, and there's no strong equivalent to musical ice cream trucks in Japanese culture. For this reason, early drafts of the Japanese scripts had Undyne talk about how warriors in the human world surely sell ice cream and work in ice cream shops.

translation.text: 冰淇淋车在许多西方国家是共同的文化记忆，在日本却没什么文化分量。这给本地化团队出了难题：Undyne 的台词必须与糖有关，直译说不通，日本文化里也找不到足以对应音乐冰淇淋车的事物。因此，日文剧本的早期译稿让 Undyne 说，人类世界的战士一定会卖冰淇淋、在冰淇淋店工作。

source.text: Later, a localization team member noted that Undyne's new line felt too plain in comparison to the original. The line was then updated to suggest that human warriors surely eat ice cream before charging into battle.

translation.text: 后来，一位团队成员觉得，新台词与原文相比太平淡，于是又改成了人类战士一定会在冲上战场前吃冰淇淋。

source.text: Soon after, another team member suggested replacing the ice cream truck with a food vehicle that is more common in Japan: a yakiimo ("roasted sweet potato") truck. This idea was dropped, however, because it lacked a clear, logical connection to normal sugar.

translation.text: 不久，另一位成员提议，把冰淇淋车换成日本更常见的 yakiimo（烤红薯）车。不过，烤红薯与普通砂糖之间没有清楚、合理的联系，这个方案也被放弃了。

source.text: After even more discussion, the translator changed Undyne's line to reference a classic Japanese snack instead of ice cream trucks:

translation.text: 经过更多讨论，译者最终用日本经典零食，取代了冰淇淋车的典故：

source.text: Who the hell pours sugar into a cup and offers it to a guest?! What, do you plan on sipping it with a spoon or something? I mean, I've heard ofp eople with a sweet-tooth before, but this is on a different level. Or do sweets on the surface world make you strong, let you sprint for 300 meters, and other stuff like that?

translation.text: 谁会把糖倒进杯子里招待客人啊？！怎么，你还打算拿勺子一点点喝掉？我也听说过爱吃甜食的人，可你这完全是另一个程度。难道地上世界的甜食，吃了就能变强、能一口气冲刺 300 米什么的？

source.text: This new text refers to Japanese Glico-brand snacks and their two timeless slogans: "makes you strong" and "300 meters in a single piece".

translation.text: 新台词提到的是日本 Glico（格力高）的零食，以及两句经久不衰的广告词：“让你强壮”和“一粒跑 300 米”。

pages.title: 冰淇淋车、烤红薯车与格力高

source.text: Nothing stops kids in their tracks like an approaching ice cream truck or the sound of someone yelling "ice cream truck!"

translation.text: 没有什么比驶近的冰淇淋车，或者一声“冰淇淋车来了！”，更能让孩子们立刻停下脚步。

source.text: In Japan, some yakiimo trucks drive around and sell roasted sweet potatoes to passersby

translation.text: 在日本，一些 yakiimo（烤红薯）车会沿街行驶，向路人售卖烤红薯。

source.text: This classic Glico slogan says "300 meters in a single piece"

translation.text: 格力高这句经典广告词是“一粒跑 300 米”。

source.text: This other classic slogan says "delicious, and makes you strong"

translation.text: 另一句经典广告词是“美味，让你强壮”。

source.text: Hotland

translation.text: 热域

source.text: Human Intruder Encounters Monster Machines

translation.text: 人类闯入者遇上怪物机器

source.text: The next step of the journey takes the main character to a lava-filled region packed with new characters, new surprises, and a pitch-dark laboratory.

translation.text: 旅程的下一站把主角带到一片满是熔岩的区域。这里有新角色、新惊喜，还有一间漆黑的实验室。

source.text: A Stab in the Dark

translation.text: 黑暗中的线索

source.text: Toby really liked this line from Brandish and included multiple notes about it in the translation spreadsheet

translation.text: Toby 很喜欢《Brandish》里的这句台词，在翻译表格中多次提到它。

source.text: If the player checks the lab's dark walls in the English version of Undertale, the game will state that "it's too dark to see near the walls".

translation.text: 在英文版《Undertale》中调查实验室黑暗的墙壁，游戏会提示：“太暗了，看不清墙边。”

source.text: Toby noted that this generic "there's nothing here" line is actually a direct quote from Brandish. He also mentioned that it wasn't important to retain the quote in the Japanese Undertale script. Even so, the translator did some research and included the equivalent quote from a Japanese version of Brandish.

translation.text: Toby 指出，这句寻常的“这里没东西”式提示，其实直接引用了《Brandish》。他也说，日文版《Undertale》不必保留这个引用。即便如此，译者还是查找了资料，采用了日文版《Brandish》中对应的台词。

source.text: The Japanese version of Brandish has been re-released many times over the past thirty years. Because each version has slightly different text, there is no single "too dark to see" line in Japanese - the line is different in each release. Of these, the Japanese version of Undertale quotes the PC Engine port of Brandish:

translation.text: 过去三十年间，日文版《Brandish》多次再版，各版文本略有不同，所以日语并没有一句统一的“太暗了看不见”，每版措辞都不一样。《Undertale》日文版引用的是 PC Engine 移植版：

source.text: "Can't identify due to the darkness!" (PC98, 1991)

translation.text:
“太暗了，无法辨认！”
（PC98，1991）

source.text: "Can't identify due to the darkness." (Super Famicom, 1994)

translation.text:
“太暗了，无法辨认。”
（Super Famicom，1994）

source.text: "It's too dark to see well" (PC Engine, 1994)

translation.text:
“太暗了，看不清。”
（PC Engine，1994）

source.text: "Nothing unusual here." (PSP, 2009)

translation.text:
“这里没什么异常。”
（PSP，2009）

source.text: In short, it's clear that this generic English line is very important to Toby, and that the localization team took that importance seriously.

translation.text: 可见，这句平平无奇的英文对 Toby 很重要，本地化团队也认真对待了他的重视。

source.text: Inspiration Spotlight: Brandish

translation.text: 灵感聚焦：Brandish

source.text: In 1991, Ni hon Falcom released Brandish for the NEC PC-98 series of Japanese home computers. The game's solid popularity among its niche audience led to multiple re-releases, ports, and sequels in Japan. Outside of Japan, the Brandish series remains largely unknown.

translation.text: 1991 年，日本 Falcom 为 NEC PC-98 系列家用电脑推出了《Brandish》。它在小众受众中拥有稳定的人气，于是在日本陆续推出了多个再版、移植版和续作。不过在日本以外，这个系列始终鲜为人知。

source.text: In simple terms, Brandish is a top-down "dungeon crawler" that combines the gameplay mechanics of action, puzzle, and role-playing games. Players are tasked with navigating 45 increasingly complex dungeons filled with monsters, traps, and secrets.

translation.text: 简单说，《Brandish》是一款俯视视角的“地牢探索”游戏，结合了动作、解谜和角色扮演游戏的机制。玩家要穿过 45 座越来越复杂的地牢，里面满是怪物、陷阱和秘密。

pages.title: Alphys 与 Mettaton 的说话方式

source.text: Alphys Speaks

translation.text: Alphys 的说话方式

source.text: Alphys switches ~ between being confident and being out of her comfort zone, so Toby included many notes about how individual lines should "feel" to the player

translation.text: Alphys 时而自信，时而局促不安，所以 Toby 写了许多说明，交代每句台词应该给玩家什么“感觉”。

source.text: In the English script, a scientist named Al phys comes across as smart and professional when it comes to her work, but becomes shy, nerdy, and insecure when holding a casual conversation. The translator conveyed these qualities in Japanese by giving Al phys a mixture of casual speech patterns and polite speech patterns that fit her character. Alphys also uses the polite and somewhat feminine pronoun watashi when referring to herself.

translation.text: 英文剧本中的科学家 Alphys 谈到工作时聪明而专业，闲聊时却害羞、宅气又不自信。译者把符合她性格的随意说法和礼貌说法混合起来，在日语中表现这些特点。Alphys 自称时还使用礼貌、略带女性色彩的代词 watashi（我）。

source.text: Early on, Toby noted that "Alphys" should be pronounced "al-feez", which he imagined would be spelled in Japanese as アルフィーズ (arufīzu). He also understood that this six-character name could cause problems with Papyrus’ vertical text box, which only comfortably allows five characters per line. Thus, per Toby’s personal suggestion, Alphys is now known as アルフィー (arufī, roughly: "Alphy") in the Japanese script. Naturally, this name change surprised early Japanese fans who were accustomed to seeing Alphys’ full name in the fan-made translations.

translation.text: Toby 很早就说明，“Alphys”应读作“al-feez”，他设想的日文写法是「アルフィーズ」（arufīzu）。他也明白，这个六字符的名字可能不适合 Papyrus 的竖排对话框，因为那里每行只能轻松容纳五个字符。因此，按照 Toby 本人的建议，日文剧本采用了「アルフィー」（arufī，大致相当于“Alphy”）。早期日本玩家已习惯民间译版中的完整名字，看到改名自然很吃惊。

source.text: Alphys' name change had an unintended side effect: online searches for her Japanese name mostly bring up The Allee, a 1974 Japanese folk rock band

translation.text: Alphys 改名还带来了意外后果：上网搜索她的日文名字，大多会搜到 1974 年成立的日本民谣摇滚乐队 The Alfee。

source.text: Mettaton Speaks

translation.text: Mettaton 的说话方式

source.text: Mettaton usually uses the good-natured pronoun boku to refer to himself, but switches to the more feminine watashi when dressed up as a robot bride later on

translation.text: Mettaton 通常用温和的 boku（我）自称；后来扮成机器人新娘时，则换成更有女性色彩的 watashi（我）。

source.text: A killer robot named Mettaton appears and repeatedly attempts to stop the main character in unusual ways. In English, Mettaton usually speaks like a game show host. He speaks similarly in Japanese, and usually uses the boyish pronoun boku to refer to himself.

translation.text: 杀人机器人 Mettaton 登场后，不断用奇怪的方式阻拦主角。在英语中，他通常像电视游戏节目的主持人一样说话。日语也保留了这种风格，通常用带有少年气的 boku自称。

source.text: Mettaton's catchphrase in English is "OHHHH YES!!", and he often refers to the main character as "Darling''. In the Japanese script, he still says "OHHHH YES'!" in English and calls the main character koneko-chan ("kitten").

translation.text: Mettaton 的英语口头禅是“OHHHH YES!!”（噢——没错！！），还常称主角为“Darling”（亲爱的）。日文剧本中，他仍用英语说“OHHHH YES!!”，但把主角叫作 koneko-chan（小猫咪）。

source.text: Mettaton's catchphrase ~ is unchanged in Japanese, but was never simply copy-and-pasted during translation

translation.text: Mettaton 的口头禅在日文版中没有变，但翻译时并不是直接复制粘贴过去的。

source.text: Robot Rebranding

translation.text: 机器人的节目改名

source.text: Mettaton refers to this game show as a "quiz show" in English, so the updated Japanese sign is actually more consistent with the game's dialogue

translation.text: Mettaton 在英文台词里也把节目称作“quiz show”（问答节目），因此日版的新招牌反而与台词更一致。

source.text: Mettaton forces the main character to participate in a television game show. In the English version of Underta/e, the game show begins with a flashing sign that says "GAME SHOW''. Game shows are usually called "quiz shows" in Japan, though, so the sign was updated to say "QUIZ SHOW" in the Japanese release.

translation.text: Mettaton 强迫主角参加电视游戏节目。在英文版《Undertale》中，节目开场有一块闪烁的“GAME SHOW”（游戏节目）招牌。不过日本通常把这类节目叫作“quiz show”（问答节目），因此日文版把招牌改成了“QUIZ SHOW”。

source.text: Toby's Japanese friend Moa (the developer behind Hatoful Boyfriend) drew this Japanese game show title card and helped check Underta/e's localization in general

translation.text: Toby 的日本朋友 Moa（《Hatoful Boyfriend》的开发者）绘制了这张日文节目标题画面，也帮助检查了《Undertale》的整体本地化。

source.text: Later, Mettaton forces the main character to participate in a cooking show. This show begins with a hand-drawn title card that says "COOKING WITH A KILLER ROBOT''. Toby asked a Japanese artist named Moa to redraw this title card with a new, localized Japanese name that roughly translates as "The Killer Robot's Kitchen of Sparkles".

translation.text: 后来，Mettaton 又强迫主角参加烹饪节目。开场手绘标题写着“COOKING WITH A KILLER ROBOT”（和杀人机器人一起做饭）。Toby 请日本画师 Moa 重新绘制标题，换上本地化后的日文名字，大意是“杀人机器人的闪亮厨房”。

source.text: On the Fly

translation.text: 苍蝇双关

source.text: Reader Challenge #7: Come up with a different English pun that could fit this fly counting game show scene!

translation.text: 读者挑战 7：再想一个适合这场数苍蝇节目的英语双关吧！

source.text: Mettaton challenges the player to count the number of flies in a jar, then says:

translation.text: Mettaton 让玩家数罐子里有多少只苍蝇，然后说：

source.text: DON'T 'COUNT' ON YOUR VICTORY ..

translation.text: 别“指望”（COUNT ON）自己会赢……

source.text: This pun on the English word "count" is lost in a literal translation, so the translator adjusted it slightly:

translation.text: 这里的 count 既可指“数数”，count on 又是“指望”。直译会丢掉双关，所以译者稍作调整：

source.text: But a "hae aru" victory won't be so easy to achieve.

translation.text: 不过，想取得“hae aru”的胜利可没那么容易。

source.text: The joke here is that hae aru usually means "glorious" or "honorable", but hae by itself can mean "fly" or "flies". Additionally, hae aru can be interpreted as a way of saying "there are flies". The result is a Japanese pun that uses completely different words to fit the scene seamlessly.

translation.text: 笑点在于，hae aru 通常表示“光荣的”或“荣耀的”，但 hae 单独也可以指“苍蝇”。此外，hae aru 还可以理解为“有苍蝇”。日语用了完全不同的词，构成了同样贴合场景的双关。

source.text: Dr. Al phys regularly posts on the Undernet, the Underground's version of the Internet. As such, she often includes smilies, emoticons, and Internet slang in her social media messages.

source.text: Polarizing Vocabulary

translation.text: 表里不一的词

source.text: Tsundere characters stereotypically say things like "it's not like I like you or anything, dummy"

translation.text: 傲娇角色的典型台词是：“才不是喜欢你呢，笨蛋。”

source.text: Underta/e's English script sometimes uses the Japanese word tsundere. In broad terms, tsundere - roughly pronounced "tsoon deh reh" - describes the trait of having an unfriendly attitude on the outside that gives way to an affectionate inner attitude over time.

translation.text: 《Undertale》的英文剧本偶尔会用日语词 tsundere（傲娇，读音大致是“tsoon deh reh”）。广义上，它形容一种性格：表面不友善，内心的亲昵却随着时间渐渐显露。

source.text: Twndere is a common word in Japanese entertainment, but is notoriously troublesome to translate into English because it has no solid equivalent. For this reason, English-speaking fans of Japanese entertainment - such as Toby - tend to leave the word untranslated. Basically, tsundere is in the process of becoming a loan word in English like "karate" and "karaoke", but it hasn't yet reached mainstream recognition. As such, the word tsundere might confuse some English-speaking players, but it poses little problem for Japanese players.

translation.text: Tsundere 在日本娱乐作品中很常见，却因英语没有确切的对应词而出了名地难译。因此，像 Toby 这样的英语圈日本娱乐爱好者，通常直接保留原词。它正在像 karate（空手道）、karaoke（卡拉 OK）那样成为英语借词，但还没被主流广泛认识。所以它可能让一些英语玩家困惑，日本玩家却很容易理解。

source.text: Toby also included jokes about how the cactus is a tsundere plant because of its sharp exterior needles

translation.text: Toby 还拿仙人掌开玩笑，说它外表长满尖刺，是一种傲娇植物。

source.text: Unhelping Hands

translation.text: 洗手也成秀

source.text: This localization change points to a level of cultural knowledge that's beyond the reach of inexperienced translators and machine translation systems

translation.text: 这项本地化改动体现出的文化知识，是缺乏经验的译者和机器翻译系统难以企及的。

source.text: During Metta ton's cooking show, the player is asked to find ingredients. If the player checks the sink, Mettaton will remark:

translation.text: Mettaton 的烹饪节目要求玩家寻找食材。如果调查水槽，他就会说：

source.text: THIS ISN'T A SHOW ABOUT WASHING YOUR HANDS, DARLING.

translation.text: 亲爱的，这可不是教你洗手的节目。

source.text: This relatively straightforward line received a boost of creativity in Japanese:

translation.text: 这句相当直白的台词，在日语中多了些创意：

source.text: This show's title isn't "Teo AraimaSHOW"!

translation.text: 这节目的名字可不是“Te o AraimaSHOW”（一起洗手秀）！

source.text: Normally, this would be written in Japanese as te o araimasho, which means "let's wash our hands". But in Japanese entertainment, titles that end in sho are sometimes replaced with the English word "show". This wordplay adds an extra layer of flair to the title in question, so this practice is particularly common with flashy entertainment. And, of course, Mettaton is all about being flashy.

translation.text: 这句话在日语里通常写作 te o araimashō，意思是“一起洗手吧”。不过，日本娱乐节目有时会把标题末尾的 shō 换成英语 show（秀）。这个文字游戏让标题更俏皮，所以特别常见于花哨的娱乐节目。Mettaton 当然最爱花哨。

source.text: Replacing the Japanese verb fragment sho with the English word "SHOW" is very common on Japanese TV

translation.text: 把日语动词末尾的 shō 换成英语“SHOW”，在日本电视节目中很常见。

source.text: In short, this Japanese line adds an extra level of natural, customary humor that isn't present in the original English text. In doing so, it arguably improves upon the original text.

translation.text: 这句日语加入了原英文没有、却自然又符合当地习惯的幽默。从这个角度说，或许还胜过了原文。

source.text: Meme Temperature

translation.text: 网络梗的温度

source.text: Sometimes, things that seem like references aren't references at all - it's like "seeing" faces in clouds and carpet patterns

translation.text: 有些看似引用的东西其实并没有出处，就像在云朵和地毯花纹里“看见”人脸一样。

source.text: During the robot cooking show, Mettaton offers details about the oven:

translation.text: 在机器人的烹饪节目里，Mettaton 介绍烤箱：

source.text: OH YES! MTT-BRAND OVENS CAN REACH TEMPERATURES UP TO NINE-THOUSAND DEGREES!

translation.text: 噢，没错！MTT 牌烤箱最高能达到九千度！

source.text: Toby confirmed with the localization team that this reference to the number 9000 isn't a reference to the famous "it's over 9000!" Internet joke. He even included a note in the translation spreadsheet that said "Don't localize this as an over 9000 meme. Wait, that doesn't exist in Japan, does it...?". With this information in mind, the translator gave Mettaton's line a simple, straightforward translation into Japanese.

translation.text: Toby 向本地化团队确认，这里的 9000 不是在玩著名网络梗“it’s over 9000!”（超过九千了！）。他甚至在翻译表格里写道：“别把这句本地化成‘超过九千’的梗。等等，日本没有这个梗吧……？”知道这一点后，译者就直接把 Mettaton 的台词译成了日语。

source.text: "It's Over 9000!" Explained

translation.text: “超过九千！”的来历

source.text: In a 1997 English dub of a Dragon Ball Z episode, a villain angrily shouts, "It's over 9000!" after checking his opponent's power level. In 2006, the humorous delivery of this English line transformed the quote into an online meme. The quote "It's over 9000!" could suddenly be found in countless articles, videos, message boards, and chat rooms. Over time, the quote also began to appear in mainstream English-language entertainment. It also began to appear in video games, including:

translation.text: 在《龙珠 Z》1997 年的一集英语配音中，反派测完对手的战斗力后，愤怒地大喊：“It’s over 9000!”（超过九千了！）2006 年，这句英语台词滑稽的演绎让它变成了网络梗。一时间，无数文章、视频、论坛和聊天室都能看到这句话。后来，它也逐渐出现在英语主流娱乐作品中，包括以下电子游戏：

translation.text: 《Ninjatown》（2008）

Fate/Grand Order (2017)
