source.text: Should've replaced ~ the hot dogs with jelly doughnuts

translation.text: 真该把热狗换成果酱甜甜圈。

source.text: Sans runs a hot dog stand in Hotland. If the player buys enough hot dogs, Sans invents new replacements for the word "hot dog". Because these silly name variations play with English punctuation and spelling, the translator tweaked them to work smoothly in Japanese:

translation.text: Sans 在热域经营热狗摊。玩家买得够多，他就会不断为“hot dog”（热狗）发明新叫法。这些傻乎乎的名字玩的是英语标点和拼写，所以译者做了调整，让它们在日语里也说得通：

source.text: Original English Joke

translation.text: 英语原梗

source.text: Approximate Japanese Localization

translation.text: 日版本地化大意

source.text: here's your 'dog. yeah, 'dog. apostrophe-dog. it's short for hot-dog.

translation.text: 给，你的 ’dog。没错，’dog。撇号加 dog。这是 hot-dog的缩写。

source.text: here's your dog. that's right, "dog". it's my abbreviation for "hot dog".

translation.text: 给，你的 dog。没错，“dog”，这是我给“hot dog”起的缩写。

source.text: another h'dog? here you go ...

translation.text: 还要个 h’dog？给你……

source.text: another hodog? you got it.

translation.text: 还要个 hodog？没问题。

source.text: cool. here's that "dog. apostrophe- apostrophe dog. it's short for apostrophe-dog.

translation.text: 好，给你的 ’’dog。撇号—撇号 dog。是“撇号 dog”的缩写。

source.text: want another D.O.G.? you got it. that's right. D.O.G. they're initials. they stand for "dog".

translation.text: 还要个 D.O.G.？没问题。对，D.O.G.，首字母缩写。全称是“dog”。

source.text: During the game’s localization process, Toby often wrote notes to himself to later share with the localization team. In one such note, Toby came up with an idea for a comical "hot dog" abbreviation in Japanese: ットdog (tto dog). Essentially, the "ho" part of "hot dog" would be dropped, and the word "dog" would be left in English.

translation.text: 本地化期间，Toby 经常给自己写笔记，准备之后分享给团队。其中一条设想了日语里一个滑稽的“热狗”缩写：「ットdog」（tto dog）。也就是删掉 hot dog 开头的“ho”，而 dog 仍保留英语。

source.text: Toby's private notes ~ included a handful of localization ideas he had considered but never shared with anyone

translation.text: Toby 的私人笔记里，有几条他考虑过却从未向别人提起的本地化点子。

source.text: The idea behind Toby's new "hot dog" word was quite clever - the consonant extending character "/ almost never appears at the beginning of a Japanese word, and the decision to keep "dog" in English makes the Japanese abbreviation even sillier. Although he never pitched this suggestion to the localization team, it's another clear sign that Toby was actively involved in the localization process of his own game.

translation.text: Toby 这个新“热狗”词的想法很巧妙：表示辅音延长的「ッ」几乎不会出现在日语词开头，而 dog 保留英语又让这个缩写更傻气。虽然他从未向本地化团队提出这个建议，但它再次清楚表明，他一直在积极参与自己游戏的本地化。

source.text: Version Juggling

translation.text: 兼顾不同版本

source.text: Different versions of Undertale have slightly different text than other versions - sometimes the differences are as tiny as this

translation.text: 《Undertale》各版本的文本略有不同，有时差异就像这样细小。

source.text: As we've seen, not every version of Under tale is the same - for example, the PlayStation 4 version has content not found in the Nintendo Switch version, and vice-versa. These differences range in size, from secret rooms with new content to minor text changes that rely on alternate programming.

translation.text: 我们已经看到，《Undertale》的各版本并不完全相同。例如 PlayStation 4 版有 Nintendo Switch 版没有的内容，反过来也一样。差别有大有小，从装着新内容的隐藏房间，到因程序不同而产生的细微文字变化。

source.text: The fact that there are so many different·versions of Undertale means that there are multiple English scripts that need to be managed, organized, and actively maintained. This holds true on the Japanese side of things too, meaning that Toby and 8-4 currently have to keep track of ten or so versions of the game. Understandably, this is a level of support not offered by most generic translation companies.

translation.text: 《Undertale》版本众多，就意味着有好几套英语剧本需要管理、整理并持续维护。日语这边也是如此，所以 Toby 和 8-4 目前得同时照管大约十个版本。可以想见，一般翻译公司大多不会提供这种程度的支持。

source.text: What's more, each time Toby adds new content or fixes a bug, all of these separate versions need to be updated, which can lead to even more versions to keep track of. All of this illustrates how game localization can be an ongoing process rather than a one-and-done affair.

translation.text: 而且，每次 Toby 增添内容或修复错误，都得更新各个版本，这又可能产生更多需要追踪的版本。这说明游戏本地化可以是一项持续的工作，而非一次交付就结束。

source.text: Fun with Letters

translation.text: 字母的趣味

source.text: This secret enemy creates two new enemies named Doodlebog. Because there are three enemies total, the second Doodlebog is automatically (and unintentionally) called Doodlebog C

translation.text: 这个隐藏敌人会创造两个叫 Doodlebog 的新敌人。由于场上总共有三个敌人，第二个 Doodlebog 被自动——也意外地——叫作 Doodlebog C。

source.text: A secret battle features an artist and two "Doodlebog" enemies. In his translation notes, Toby explained that the second Doodlebog is automatically named "Doodle bog C" instead of "Doodle bog B" due to a programming bug. He liked this bug enough to give Doodlebog C its own pun-based description:

translation.text: 一场隐藏战斗中有一名画家和两个“Doodlebog”敌人。Toby 在翻译说明中解释，由于程序错误，第二个 Doodlebog 会被自动叫作“Doodlebog C”，而不是“Doodlebog B”。他很喜欢这个错误，于是给 Doodlebog C 写了一条专门的双关说明：

source.text: The "C" stands for "seafaring:" It likes to ride in a boat.

translation.text: “C”代表“seafaring”（航海；sea 与 C 同音）。它喜欢坐船。

source.text: This wordplay would be lost in a literal translation, so the description became:

translation.text: 直译会失去这个文字游戏，所以日文说明变成了：

source.text: The "C'' stands for "Vitamin C". It helps your skin look more supple.

translation.text: “C”代表“维生素 C”。它能让你的皮肤更有弹性。

source.text: This change was actually Toby's idea - he understood that the pun would be lost in translation and prepared this suggestion ahead of time.

translation.text: 这个改动其实是 Toby 的主意。他知道双关在翻译中会消失，因此事先准备了这个建议。

source.text: Hotland

translation.text: 热域

source.text: Tying it Together

translation.text: 绳索双关

source.text: Incidentally, Pyropes ~ use the assertive, masculine pronoun ore in Japanese

translation.text: 顺带一提，Pyrope 在日语里用强势、男性化的 ore（我）自称。

source.text: Flaming rope monsters known as "Pyropes" appear in Hotland. During battle, the player can invite each Pyrope to "hang out". In the English script, the Pyrope will respond with:

translation.text: 热域里会出现叫作 Pyrope 的燃烧绳索怪物。战斗中，玩家可以邀它“hang out”（一起玩，也有悬挂之意）。英文剧本里，它会回答：

source.text: Sorry!! I'm all tied up!!

translation.text: 抱歉！！我忙得脱不开身（tied up，也指被绑住）！！

source.text: Toby understood that these rope-themed English puns would be lost in a literal translation, so he left a note in the translation spreadsheet:

translation.text: Toby 明白，这些围绕绳索的英语双关无法直接译出来，于是在翻译表格里留下说明：

source.text: '' TIED UP??? GET IT??? ITS A JOKE BECAUSE HE'S A ROPE!!! btw since all this command does is trigger a pun,feelfree to change it to anything you like

translation.text:
TIED UP？？？懂了吗？？？这是个笑话，因为它是根绳子！！！
对了，这个指令唯一的作用就是引出双关，所以你想改成什么都行。

source.text: To make these rope puns work in Japanese, the translator adjusted the lines slightly:

translation.text: 为了让绳索双关在日语里成立，译者稍微调整了台词：

source.text: "Hang out" became burabura wru ("to loiter/idle about; to dangle/ hang down")

translation.text: “Hang out”改成了 burabura suru（闲逛／无所事事；悬着／垂着）。

source.text: "Tied up" became yotei ni shibararete ("to be bound/tied up by one's schedule")

translation.text: “Tied up”改成了 yotei ni shibararete（被日程束缚／缠住）。

source.text: These two screenshots are actually mock-ups I had to make, as a game bug appears to make this text inaccessible under normal circumstances

translation.text: 这两张截图其实是我制作的示意图，因为游戏里的一个错误似乎让这些文字无法在正常游玩时出现。

source.text: A similar rope pun appears outside of battle, in a block of text that appears to be unused due to a programming issue. In English, a Pyrope character is supposed to say:

translation.text: 战斗外也有类似的绳索双关，不过这段文本似乎因为程序问题而没有用上。英文原本要让一个 Pyrope 说：

source.text: Haha, ha ha ha. Ya wanna "hang" out?

translation.text: 哈哈，哈哈哈。想一起“hang out”（玩玩／挂着）吗？

source.text: Although this line seems to be inaccessible through normal play, the translator localized it into Japanese for completeness' sake. In this case, the translator replaced the phrase "hang out" with tanomi no tsww, which literally means "a rope of reliance", but functionally means "a mainstay" or "something you can depend on". Thus the final Japanese line drops the invitation and instead roughly says "Hehe ... Hehehe ... I'm a real reliable 'lifeline', y'know?".

translation.text: 虽然正常游玩似乎看不到这句，译者还是为了完整性把它译成了日语。这回，“hang out”换成了 tanomi no tsuna，字面是“依靠之绳”，实际指“支柱”或“可以依赖的东西”。因此，最终日文去掉了邀请，大意变成：“嘿嘿……嘿嘿嘿……我可是可靠的‘救命绳’，对吧？”

source.text: A Frayed Knot

translation.text: 磨损的绳结

source.text: My theory is that the "Double Davis" here is somehow related to the "Double Davy" knot, but who knows anymore

translation.text: 我猜这里的“Double Davis”可能与“Double Davy”绳结有关，不过谁又说得准呢。

source.text: In some cases, two Pyrope monsters will appear in battle at the same time. When this happens, the battle begins with the English message:

translation.text: 有时两个 Pyrope 会同时出现在战斗中。此时英文版的开场提示是：

source.text: The rare and threatening Double Davis.

translation.text: 罕见而危险的 Double Davis。

source.text: From the player's perspective, this line appears to be a reference to something, but that "something" is never made clear. Fans have shared multiple theories over the years, but the truth remains a mystery. During this book's production, Toby privately stated that it was something he probably just made up at the time.

translation.text: 在玩家看来，这句话像是在引用什么，但究竟指什么，一直不明。多年来，粉丝提出过各种猜测，真相却仍是谜。本书制作期间，Toby 私下说，这大概只是他当时随手编的。

source.text: Unfortunately, Toby didn't provide any extra information about this line during the localization process, so the translator was left as puzzled as fans are. So, without any clear information to work from, the translator interpreted "Double Davis" as a potential reference to the "Double Dutch" jump-rope game that children play, just with added danger. The Japanese line thus became:

translation.text: 遗憾的是，本地化时 Toby 没有提供进一步解释，译者也和粉丝一样困惑。没有明确线索可循，译者便把“Double Davis”理解为可能在指儿童玩的“Double Dutch”（交互绳）游戏，只是多了一份危险。日版大意是：

source.text: Two ropes... So begins a hellish game of Double Dutch.

translation.text: 两根绳子……地狱般的交互绳游戏开始了。

source.text: As a result of this localization decision, the mysterious, indecipherable English line was given a clear, understandable meaning in Japanese.

translation.text: 这项本地化决定，让神秘而难以解读的英语台词在日语中有了明确易懂的意思。

source.text: The Double Dutch jump rope game involves two jump ropes that turn in opposite directions at the same time

translation.text: Double Dutch 交互绳游戏同时使用两根跳绳，朝相反方向转动。

source.text: Hotland

translation.text: 热域

source.text: Backwards Talk

translation.text: 倒着说

source.text: On a related but different note, Toby mentioned that "spicey" is purposely misspelled everywhere in the game, so the Japanese script uses slight misspellings too

translation.text: 顺便一提，Toby 说游戏中所有“spicey”（spicy，辣的）的错拼都是故意的，因此日文也用了些小小的错拼。

source.text: The possibly unused Pyrope dialogue includes two more lines of text:

translation.text: Pyrope 那段可能没有用上的对话，还有两句：

source.text: Haha, ha ha ha. Sorry, I'm all TIED UP!!! Psyche! Owned! No one wants to be MY friend!!!

translation.text:
哈哈，哈哈哈。抱歉，我忙得脱不开身（TIED UP，也指被绑住）！！！
骗你的！上当了吧！根本没人想和我交朋友！！！

source.text: In Japanese, this became:

translation.text: 日文版变成了：

source.text: Hehe. .. Hehehe ... After all, I am a ropii - a puro in other words! Yeah, right! Just kidding! I'm actually just an ordinary toshiro!

translation.text:
嘿嘿……嘿嘿嘿……毕竟我是 rōpū（绳子）——也就是 puro（专业人士）啊！
才怪！开玩笑的！我其实只是个普通的 tōshiro（外行）！

source.text: To retain the rope pun in this dialogue, the translator used a form of Japanese wordplay referred to as gyokai yoga ("[entertainment] industry lingo") to make a pun on the words ropu ("rope") and puro ("pro; professional"). The translator again used gyokai yoga to change shiroto ("amateur") into the nonsensical word toshiro in the following line.

translation.text: 为了保住绳索双关，译者运用了日语里叫作 gyōkai yōgo（娱乐行业行话）的文字游戏，把 rōpu（绳子）和 puro（专业人士）联系起来。下一句又用同样的方法，把 shirōto（外行）倒成了本无意义的 tōshiro。

source.text: Because the same Pyrope character does properly appear at the end of the game with even more rope puns, it made sense for the translator to localize this inaccessible line too. By not skipping it, the translator ensured that Japanese players can appreciate this character's internal consistency if the original programming issues ever get fixed someday.

translation.text: 同一个 Pyrope 在游戏结尾确实会出现，还会讲更多绳索双关，因此把这句暂时看不到的台词也本地化很有道理。译者没有跳过它，就能确保将来若修复了原程序问题，日本玩家也能体会这个角色前后一致的风格。

source.text: Insert your own fire pun here

translation.text: 请在此自行补上一个火焰双关。

source.text: Overview of Japanese gyokai yogo

translation.text: 日语行业行话一览

source.text: In simple terms, Japanese gyokai yoga, sometimes referred to as zujago, is similar to English "Pig Latin" -you basically shuffle and move the characters in a word to create a new, funny-sounding "secret code word".

translation.text: 简单说，这种行话有时也叫 zūjago，类似英语的 Pig Latin（儿童黑话）：调换词内字符，造出一个听起来好笑的新“暗号词”。

source.text: In basic gyōkai yōgo, the final character in a word is moved to the front, and certain vowels are elongated. For example, トマト (tomato) might become トートマ (tōtoma), while スシ (sushi) might become シースー (shīsū).

translation.text: 最基本的做法是把词尾字符挪到前面，再拉长某些元音。例如「トマト」（tomato，番茄）可能变成「トートマ」（tōtoma）；「スシ」（sushi，寿司）则可能变成「シースー」（shīsū）。

source.text: Going Bananas

translation.text: Banana 的引用

source.text: Toby wasn't picky about this Japanese text being an exact quote from Kitchen

translation.text: Toby 并不要求这些日文逐字引用《厨房》。

source.text: Two royal guards in Hotland block the way forward. Using patience and the proper choices, the player can convince the guards to reveal their hidden feelings for each other. During this process, using the "Check" command on the guards reveals two new descriptions:

translation.text: 热域的两名皇家卫兵挡住了去路。只要耐心选择合适的行动，玩家就能让他们坦白对彼此隐藏的感情。过程中使用“查看”指令，会出现两条新描述：

source.text: I see two lovers staring over the edge of the cauldron of hell.

translation.text: 我看见两个恋人，正探头望向地狱大锅的边缘。

source.text: Do they both wish for death? That means their love will end in hell. I couldn't stop laughing.

translation.text: 他们都想死吗？那他们的爱情就会在地狱里结束。我笑个不停。

source.text: Toby noted that these are indirect, inaccurate quotes from the English translation of Kitchen, a famous novel by Japanese author Banana Yoshimoto. The exact English quote from Kitchen is:

translation.text: Toby 说明，这些是对日本作家 Banana Yoshimoto 的名作《厨房》英译本的间接、不精确引用。英译本的准确原文大意是：

source.text: I didn't know we could put our nickname for our first name on stuff, I guess that makes me Tomato Mandelin!

translation.text: 原来可以把昵称当名字印在书上，那我就是 Tomato Mandelin（番茄 Mandelin）啦！

source.text: '' Although I had been earnestly daydreaming until then, I suddenly started to laugh. "I see two lovers looking over the edge of the cauldron of hell. Are they contemplating a double suicide? This means their love will end in hell." I couldn't stop laughing.

translation.text: 此前我还认真地做着白日梦，却突然笑了起来。“我看见两个恋人，正探头望向地狱大锅的边缘。他们在考虑殉情吗？那他们的爱情就会在地狱里结束。”我笑个不停。

source.text: Under normal circumstances, a professional translator would've immediately looked for the equivalent lines from the Japanese version of Kitchen. However, Toby specifically noted that he considered this text an "in-joke between friends" and that "since it's just a joke, you don't have to find the original". He further emphasized this attitude elsewhere in the spreadsheet by saying "Another Banana Yoshimoto reference. Again, I don't care that much".

translation.text: 通常，专业译者会立刻去日文版《厨房》里寻找对应原句。但 Toby 特别说明，他把这段当成“朋友之间的内部笑话”，“既然只是个玩笑，就不用找原文了”。他在表格另一处又强调：“又是个吉本芭娜娜的引用。我还是没那么在意。”

source.text: Undertale's translator honored Toby's unusual wish and translated the guards' indirect English quotes back into Japanese as-is. This resulted in Japanese text that is recognizable as a Kitchen reference, but with noticeably different wording.

translation.text: 《Undertale》的译者尊重了 Toby 这个不寻常的愿望，把卫兵那几句不精确的英文照样译回日语。结果仍能看出是在引用《厨房》，但措辞明显不同。

source.text: Normally, skilled translators will go out of their way to retain jokes and references, as it's assumed that the original author considered them important enough to use. As such, it's rare to encounter a situation like this, in which the author is actually so unattached to a reference that the translators are asked to skip it! Toby truly is the king of crazy exceptions.

translation.text: 熟练的译者通常会特意保留笑话和引用，因为原作者既然用了，就应该认为它们值得保留。因此，这种情况很罕见：作者对某处引用竟如此不在意，反而要求译者跳过它！Toby 真是各种离奇例外之王。

source.text: Hotland

translation.text: 热域

source.text: Water Matters

translation.text: 一杯水引发的灾难

source.text: As we've seen ~ several times before, it's unclear if this localized reference is as recognizable in Japanese as it is in English

translation.text: 像前面几次一样，我们很难判断，这个本地化后的引用在日语里是否与英语一样容易认出来。

source.text: Mettaton forces the main character to participate in a live news broadcast. If the player chooses to report on a nearby a glass of water, Metta ton will shout:

translation.text: Mettaton 强迫主角参加新闻直播。如果玩家选择报道附近一杯水，他就会大喊：

source.text: WAIT A SECOND. THAT'S NOT A GLASS OF WATER!!! THAT'S. .. A BOMB!!! OH NO!!! THIS NEWS REPORT. .. IS TURNING INTO A DISASTER REPORT!!!

translation.text:
等一下。那不是一杯水！！！
那是……炸弹！！！噢，不！！！这场新闻报道……
要变成灾难报道（DISASTER REPORT）了！！！

source.text: Toby noted that this line includes a reference to Disaster Report, a PlayStation 2 game from 2003. This led to an unexpected issue, though - Disaster Report originally went by a very different name in Japan: Zettai Zetsumei Toshi ("City of Certain Doom").

translation.text: Toby 指出，这里引用了 2003 年的 PlayStation 2 游戏《Disaster Report》。但问题意外出现了：它原本的日文名字完全不同，叫 Zettai Zetsumei Toshi（绝体绝命都市，意即“必死绝境中的城市”）。

source.text: Disaster Report went by a different name in Japan - even the game's box was quite different

translation.text: 《Disaster Report》在日本的名字不同，连包装盒都差别很大。

source.text: To keep Toby's Disaster Report reference intact, the translator rephrased Mettaton's line:

translation.text: 为了保留 Toby 对《Disaster Report》的引用，译者改写了 Mettaton 的台词：

source.text: WAIT. .. THAT'S NOT A GLASS OF WATER! IT'SA BOMB! OH, NO! WHAT WAS SUPPOSED TO BE A NEWS REPORT. .. HAS BECOME A REPORT OF CERTAIN DOOM!

translation.text:
等等……那不是一杯水！是炸弹！
噢，不！本来是新闻报道……
结果变成绝体绝命的报道了！

source.text: In the original English script, Toby's game reference is unobtrusive enough to sound like ordinary text to players unfamiliar with Disaster Report. The translator recognized this fact and phrased the Japanese line to work similarly.

translation.text: 原英文里的游戏引用很不显眼，不熟悉《Disaster Report》的玩家只会把它当成普通台词。译者注意到了这一点，也让日语的措辞达到类似效果。

source.text: Explosive Prohibition

translation.text: 炸弹与租赁禁令

source.text: It's funny how we can say "that game is the bomb!" as a good thing but then also say "that game bombed!" as a bad thing

translation.text: 真有意思，“that game is the bomb!”可以夸游戏“棒极了”，而“that game bombed!”却是在说它“惨败了”。

source.text: If the player reports on a nearby video game, the video game turns out to be a bomb too. In the English script, the game-bomb's description is:

translation.text: 如果玩家报道附近的电子游戏，它也会被揭穿是一颗炸弹。英文版的说明是：

source.text: GAME BOMB You really should have rented it first.

translation.text:
游戏炸弹
你真该先租来试试。

source.text: Although common in many Western countries for decades, game rentals have generally been prohibited in Japan by law since 1984. With this in mind, the translator rephrased the game's Japanese description to say:

translation.text: 虽然几十年来，游戏租赁在许多西方国家很常见，日本法律自 1984 年起却基本禁止这项业务。因此，译者把日文说明改成：

source.text: GAME BOMB You really should've read the shopping site reviews first.

translation.text:
游戏炸弹
你真该先看购物网站上的评价。

source.text: Game rentals have been prohibited by Japanese law since the 1980s, although there have been attempts to legitimize the market from time to time

translation.text: 日本法律自 20 世纪 80 年代起禁止游戏租赁，但其间不时有人尝试让这个市场合法化。

source.text: As minor as it is, this localization choice points to a level of cultural knowledge that goes beyond what an inexperienced translator or a machine can currently provide.

translation.text: 改动虽小，却显示了缺乏经验的译者或当前机器翻译难以具备的文化知识。

source.text: Muffet Speaks

translation.text: Muffet 的说话方式

source.text: If you're curious, the classic Little Miss Muffet nursery rhyme isn't widely known in Japan, but it has received multiple translations into Japanese over the years

translation.text: 如果你好奇，经典童谣《Little Miss Muffet》在日本并不广为人知，不过这些年已有多个日译版本。

source.text: A spider monster named Muffet appears in Hotland. In English, Muffet tends to call the main character "dearie", but not in Japanese. This is because the sentiment is already conveyed by her cordial, feminine speech pattern in Japanese - including the use of the polite, feminine pronoun watashi.

translation.text: 热域里会出现蜘蛛怪物 Muffet。英语里，她常把主角叫作“dearie”（亲爱的），日语却不会这样叫，因为亲切、女性化的说话方式已经传达了这种感觉，其中还包括用礼貌、女性化的 watashi（我）自称。

source.text: In English, Muffet uses tildes (the squiggly - mark) at the end of words to denote a cute, upbeat tone of voice. This use of tildes is still uncommon in English, which lends Muffet a distinctive vibe. Tilde-like characters are extremely common in Japanese entertainment, so Muffet retains her squiggles in the Japanese script. Basically, this tilde use is a good example of how Toby blended certain Japanese language quirks into Undertale's original English script.

translation.text: 在英语中，Muffet 会在词尾加波浪号“~”，表现可爱、轻快的语气。英语里这种用法仍不常见，因此显得她很有特色。类似波浪号的符号在日本娱乐作品中却极为普遍，所以日文保留了这些弯弯的符号。这也很好地说明，Toby 如何把日语的一些特点融进《Undertale》的英语原剧本。

source.text: Hotland

translation.text: 热域

source.text: Opera Floozy

translation.text: 歌剧俏佳人

source.text: In his notes, Toby said ~ "this whole sequence is a reference to the opera in FF6 but it's just a parody so I don't care about having the tone being identical or being overly referential"

translation.text: Toby 在说明里说：“这一整段是在模仿《FF6》的歌剧，但只是恶搞，所以我不在乎语气是否一模一样，也不必太执着于对应原作。”

source.text: Mettaton forces the main character to participate in an opera scene that includes a song with lyrics. But as we've already seen, songs don't work well when translated literally. For this reason, the translator revised the lyrics to be singable in Japanese while remaining as faithful to the original lyrics as possible:

pages.title: 灵感聚焦：最终幻想 VI

source.text: Inspiration Spotlight: Final Fantasy VI

translation.text: 灵感聚焦：最终幻想 VI

source.text: In 1994, Square released Final Fantasy VI for the Japanese Super Famicom and the North American Super NES. As another of Square's classic Japanese RPGs, Final Fantasy VI combined established game design with entertaining innovations and surprises. Like many of Square's games from the 1990s, Final Fantasy VI enjoyed great critical success and inspired a new generation of game designers.

translation.text: 1994 年，Square 在日本 Super Famicom 和北美 Super NES 上推出《最终幻想 VI》。这款经典日式 RPG 在成熟的游戏设计中加入有趣的创新与惊喜。和 Square 在 20 世纪 90 年代的许多作品一样，它大获好评，并启发了新一代游戏设计师。

source.text: Meeting Bratty and Catty

translation.text: 认识 Bratty 与 Catty

source.text: Bratty and Catty speak ~ at the same time, which is so unusual that it required the localizers to jump through extra technical hoops to nail down

translation.text: Bratty 和 Catty 同时说话，这种独特设计让本地化人员必须额外解决一些技术难题。

source.text: A cat monster named "Catty" and an alligator monster named "Bratty" run a shop in a back alley. Because the English word "bratty" isn’t well known in Japan, Bratty was renamed "Alligetty" in Japanese. Early on, Toby was informed that ブラッティ (buratti, "Bratty") might also look confusingly similar to ブラッディ (buraddi, "bloody"), which is a well-known English word in Japan.

translation.text: 猫怪物 Catty 和鳄鱼怪物 Bratty 在后巷经营商店。英语 bratty（顽劣、任性）在日本不太为人所知，所以日版把 Bratty 改名为“Alligetty”。Toby 很早就被告知，「ブラッティ」（buratti，Bratty）还可能与「ブラッディ」（buraddi，bloody，血腥的）看起来太像，令人混淆；后者是日本人很熟悉的英语词。

source.text: The English word "cat" ~ is widely known in Japan, so Catty's name didn't need any updates

translation.text: 英语 cat（猫）在日本广为人知，因此 Catty 的名字不用改。

source.text: Bra tty's name happens to appear on a faint background banner in one scene. To reflect her new name in Japanese, the localization team crafted a new banner that spells "Alligetty", then modified the game's core programming to display the proper banner based on the player's language settings.

translation.text: 某个场景的背景里有条不起眼的横幅，恰好写着 Bratty 的名字。为了配合日文改名，团队制作了写着“Alligetty”的新横幅，又修改游戏底层程序，让它按玩家的语言设置显示正确版本。

source.text: Bratty and Catty Speak

translation.text: Bratty 与 Catty 的说话方式

source.text: Bratty and Catty ~ generally use the feminine Japanese pronoun iY.>tc L,, (atashi) to refer to themselves

translation.text: Bratty 和 Catty 通常用女性化的日语代词「あたし」（atashi，我）自称。

source.text: In English, Bratty and Catty use Valleyspeak, an American social dialect that's associated with teenage girls. The translator replicated this in Japanese by giving the characters a similar speech pattern associated with the Japanese gyaru subculture. Both characters use the feminine pronoun atashi.

translation.text: 在英语中，Bratty 和 Catty 使用 Valleyspeak，这是与美国少女群体相关的社会方言。译者用日本 gyaru（辣妹）亚文化中类似的说话方式重现了这一特点。两人都用女性化的 atashi（我）自称。

source.text: Bratty and Catty are unique in that both start speaking and stop speaking at the same time. Toby noted that some of these simultaneous lines might cause the game to "mess up" unless Bratty and Catty use an equal number of letters when speaking. Naturally, the translation process demolished this synchronization, so Bratty and Catty's lines required extra fine-tuning to display properly in Japanese.

translation.text: 她们独特之处在于，总是同时开始说话，也同时停下。Toby 指出，有些同步台词必须让两人的字母数相等，否则游戏可能“出乱子”。翻译自然会打乱这种同步，所以她们的日语台词还得格外细调，才能正常显示。

source.text: Because Valleyspeak and "Gyaru-speak" speech share similar demographics, histories, and usages, it's very common to see one localized into the other

translation.text: Valleyspeak 与“辣妹话”的使用群体、历史和用途相近，所以本地化时经常用其中一种对应另一种。

source.text: Yellow Front

translation.text: 黄色的机关

source.text: During another encounter with Mettaton, the unique battle option "Yell" doesn't seem to do anything. Eventually, though, a yellow button appears on the main character's cell phone. The useless "Yell" option then quietly becomes the "Yellow" option.

translation.text: 再一次遭遇 Mettaton 时，特殊战斗指令“Yell”（大喊）似乎毫无作用。后来，主角手机上出现黄色按钮，原本无用的“Yell”便悄悄变成了“Yellow”（黄色）。

source.text: One of the toughest • ch a ll e ng e s i n localization i s h a n d lin g important wordplay that must adhere to specific, scene-based restrictions

translation.text: 重要的文字游戏又必须符合场景的特定限制，是本地化最难应付的挑战之一。

source.text: Because this scene plays with how "yell" and "yellow" are spelled in English, the wordplay would be lost a straightforward translation into Japanese. What's more, this scene requires the mention of a yellow button, so any new wordplay would need to revolve around "yellow" or "button" in some way.

translation.text: 这场戏利用了英语 yell 与 yellow 拼写相近的特点，直接译成日语就会失去趣味。而场景又必须提到黄色按钮，因此新文字游戏必须围绕“黄色”或“按钮”来做。

source.text: Getting the "yell" • and "yellow" joke to work in Japanese took creativity to figure out

translation.text: 要让 yell／yellow 的笑话在日语里成立，需要发挥创意。

source.text: To preserve this scene's logic, the translator localized "Yell" as ki iroi koe o ageru, which literally means "to let out a yellow voice" but functionally means "to cry out in a shrill voice". The translator then localized "Yellow" as ki iroi botan ("yellow button"). So although it uses slightly different wording, the Japanese scene closely parallels the English script in tone and intent.

translation.text: 为了保住场景逻辑，译者把“Yell”译成 ki iroi koe o ageru，字面是“发出黄色的声音”，实际指“尖声喊叫”；再把“Yellow”译成 ki iroi botan（黄色按钮）。虽然措辞略有变化，日版的语气和用意却与英文十分接近。

source.text: Getting Meta

translation.text: 从 MTT 到 META

source.text: As we've seen, it's not • too rare for different languages to use different abbreviations for the same thing

translation.text: 正如前面所见，不同语言为同一事物采用不同缩写，并不罕见。

source.text: Throughout the English version of Undertale, the name "Mettaton" is abbreviated as "MTT". The localizers were concerned that this abbreviation's meaning might be lost in translation, so the team used a different abbreviation in the Japanese script: "META". Some examples include:

translation.text: 英文版《Undertale》常把“Mettaton”缩写为“MTT”。本地化团队担心日本玩家看不懂这个缩写，因此改用了“META”。例如：

source.text: "MTT News" became "META News"

translation.text: “MTT News”变成“META News”（新闻）。

source.text: "MTT-Brand" became "META-Brand"

translation.text: “MTT-Brand”变成“META-Brand”（品牌）。

source.text: "MTT Resort" became "META Hotel"

translation.text: “MTT Resort”（MTT 度假村）变成“META Hotel”（META 酒店）。

source.text: This change from "MTT" to "META" wasn't applied everywhere, however - "MTT" still appears in several graphical assets in the Japanese version.

translation.text: 不过，MTT 并没有处处改成 META；日版的一些图像素材仍保留着“MTT”。

source.text: A Mettaton-themed restaurant inside the MTT Resort sells four different Mettaton-therned items:

translation.text: MTT 度假村里的 Mettaton 主题餐厅，出售四种以他为主题的食物：

source.text: • A hamburger called the "Glamburger"

translation.text: Glamburger（华丽汉堡）。

translation.text: Legendary Hero（传奇英雄）长条三明治（hero／submarine）。

source.text: • A steak shaped like Metta ton's face, called the "Face Steak"

translation.text: 做成 Mettaton 脸形的 Face Steak 牛排。

source.text: • A parfait called the "Starfait"

translation.text: Starfait（星星芭菲）甜品。

source.text: In the English version of Undertale, the Mettaton-themed restaurant sells four Mettaton-themed food items

translation.text: 在英文版《Undertale》中，这家主题餐厅出售四种 Mettaton 主题食物。

source.text: These items are meant to represent how fabulous and popular Mettaton considers himself to be: a glamorous, legendary, heroic star with an incredible face.

translation.text: 这些食物都体现了 Mettaton 自认为的魅力和人气：华丽、传奇、英雄般的大明星，还有一张无与伦比的脸。

source.text: I w o n de r i f f a n s h av e m a d e a c t u al Starfaits and Sunday Sundaes - if so, it'd be cool to see if they differ at all

translation.text: 不知道粉丝有没有真的做出 Starfait 和 Sunday Sundae；如果有，看看它们是否不同一定很有趣。

source.text: In Japanese, the Glamburger, Legendary Hero, and Face Steak items remain unchanged. However, the Starfait - which is short for "Star Parfait" - became the "Sunday Sundae" and received a new Japanese description:

translation.text: 日文版的 Glamburger、Legendary Hero 和 Face Steak 没有变化。不过，Starfait 是 Star Parfait（星星芭菲）的缩写，日版改成了 Sunday Sundae（星期日圣代），还换上了新说明：

source.text: English Text

translation.text: 英文版

source.text: Japanese Text (roughly translated)

translation.text: 日文版大意

source.text: A sweet treat made of sparkling stars.

translation.text: 用闪亮星星做成的甜点。

source.text: The perfect sweet for a snack on your day off.

translation.text: 休息日享用的绝佳甜点。

source.text: The Starfait received this new name and description early in Underta/e's localization, when Toby and the translation team were still getting accustomed to the project's workflow and with working with each other. During this time, Toby explained his vision for the Japanese script:

translation.text: Starfait 的新名字和说明在《Undertale》本地化早期就定下了，当时 Toby 与翻译团队还在熟悉项目流程、磨合彼此的合作。那时，他这样描述自己对日语剧本的期待：

source.text: '' Undertale is fir/I of weird things and jokes. If tl1ere's afimny line in the EN version that doesn't work in the .JP version, it's obviously better to change it to somethingfi1nny rather than try to make it faithful. I'd be glad to help with any of these changes if necessary.

translation.text: 《Undertale》里满是怪事和笑话。如果英文里有句笑话在日语中不成立，显然把它改成别的好笑的话，比勉强忠实原文更好。必要时，我很乐意帮忙一起改。

source.text: With this note in mind, the team played around with various item names in early versions of the Japanese script. Thus, at some point, the "Starfait" became the -t}-/-T'--ij-/·'f'- (sande sande, "Sunday Sundae") and remained that way. This "Sunday Sundae" change does have drawbacks, however: the new name and description are no longer Metta ton-themed or star-themed.

translation.text: 有了这条说明，团队在早期日语剧本中尝试了各种物品名。于是，Starfait 在某个阶段变成了「サンデーサンデー」（sandē sandē，Sunday Sundae，星期日圣代），并一直沿用下来。但这项改动也有缺点：新名字和说明不再与 Mettaton 或星星有关。

translation.text: 热域

source.text: Burgerpants Speaks

translation.text: Burgerpants 的说话方式

source.text: Burgerpants tends to ._ call the main character "little buddy" in English, and anta (a casual form of "you") in Japanese

translation.text: Burgerpants 在英语里常叫主角“little buddy”（小老弟），日语则叫 anta（一种随意的“你”）。

source.text: A character named Burgerpants works at the Mettaton-themed restaurant in Hotland. In English, Burgerpants speaks in a cheerful and polite manner when speaking as an employee, but quickly shifts to a variety of hyper-casual speech styles whenever he drops his professional persona.

translation.text: Burgerpants 在热域的 Mettaton 主题餐厅工作。英语里，以店员身份说话时他开朗又礼貌；一旦放下职业面具，就立刻切换到各种极其随意的口吻。

source.text: Burgerpants speaks in a similar way in Japanese too - he uses proper and polite speech when speaking as an employee, but switches to different casual speaking styles in other situations. Burgerpants never uses personal pronouns when speaking formally in Japanese, but he does use the informal, masculine pronoun ore during more casual moments.

translation.text: 日语也保留了类似风格：工作时得体有礼，其他时候则换用不同的随意说法。正式说话时他从不用人称代词，但放松时会用非正式、男性化的 ore（我）自称。

source.text: Come on Down

translation.text: 价格正合适

source.text: The Price Is Right is a simple English idiom and the name of a popular TV game show

translation.text: The Price Is Right 既是“价格合适”的普通英语说法，也是一档热门电视游戏节目的名字。

source.text: Under certain conditions, Papyrus will describe the MTT Hotel with one short English phrase:

translation.text: 在特定条件下，Papyrus 会用一句简短的英语形容 MTT 酒店：

source.text: THE PRICE IS RIGHT!!

translation.text:
THE PRICE IS RIGHT!!
价格正合适！！

source.text: Toby noted that this can be taken either as a reference to the classic American game show The Price Is Right, or just as a simple English idiom. Because the game show reference would be lost in a literal translation, the translator chose to follow the idiom option. Thus, the new Japanese line became:

translation.text: Toby 说明，这既可以看成引用美国经典游戏节目《The Price Is Right》，也可以只是普通习语。直接翻译会让节目引用消失，所以译者选择按习语处理。新的日语台词是：

source.text: Story idea: only people who are ill can see this show, the TV screen is random static otherwise

translation.text: 故事点子：只有生病的人才能看见这档节目，其他人看电视只能看到雪花。

source.text: Providing service worth more than its price!

translation.text: 提供超值服务！

source.text: Variations of this phrase often appear in Japanese slogans and advertisements. So although this localization choice lacks a clear pop culture reference, it does keep the logic behind Papyrus' line intact.

translation.text: 这种说法的变体常见于日本标语和广告。因此，虽然这项本地化没保留明确的流行文化引用，却完整保住了 Papyrus 这句话的逻辑。

source.text: Fatherly Humor

translation.text: 父亲的幽默

source.text: Both Snowdrake and his father speak with an Osaka accent in Japanese, which makes sense - like father, like son

translation.text: Snowdrake 和父亲在日语里都讲大阪口音，合情合理——有其父必有其子。

source.text: Previously, a teenage comedian monster named Snowdrake appeared in the Snowdin area. It turns out that his is father is the in-house comedian at the MTT Hotel in Hotland.

translation.text: 前面在雪镇出现过名叫 Snowdrake 的少年喜剧怪物。原来，他父亲是热域 MTT 酒店的驻场喜剧演员。

source.text: In English, Snowdrake's father has an unusual accent - he uses the word "fathah" instead of "father", for example. Toby explained in his translation notes that this character "talks like a weird Jewish dad, in a stilted way". This unique speech pattern suggests that the father might not be from the Hotland region to begin with.

translation.text: 英语里，Snowdrake 的父亲口音很特别，例如他把 father（父亲）说成 fathah。Toby 在翻译说明中说，这个角色“像个古怪的犹太老爸，说话不太自然”。这种独特腔调暗示他可能原本并非热域居民。

source.text: To retain this sense of "outsider-ness", the translator gave Snowdrake's father a thick Osaka accent. This makes perfect sense for two reasons: Osaka is the comedy capital of Japan, and Snowdrake already has an Osaka accent. The result: Snowdrake's father sounds like a .Japanese comedian who has passed on some of his traits and ambitions to his son.

translation.text: 为保留这种“外来者”的感觉，译者让他讲浓重的大阪口音。这样做有两重道理：大阪是日本的喜剧之都，Snowdrake 本来也讲大阪口音。结果，父亲听起来像个日本喜剧演员，把自己的部分特点与志向传给了儿子。

source.text: Japanese Manzai Comedy

translation.text: 日本漫才

source.text: Manzai is a long-established form of Japanese stand-up comedy that traditionally features a team of two comedians. Much like the double-act comedy routines found in other countries, manzai usually involves one bokeh ("funny man") and one tsukkomi ("straight man") playing off of each other as ridiculous situations unfold.

translation.text: Manzai（漫才）是日本历史悠久的舞台喜剧形式，传统上由两名演员搭档。与其他国家的双人喜剧相似，漫才通常由 bokeh（装傻逗趣者）与 tsukkomi（吐槽纠正者）相互配合，演出荒唐情境。

source.text: Historically, manzai is approximately 1000 years old, but modern-day manzai emerged from Osaka in the early 1900s. From there, Osaka-style manzai spread to the rest of Japan via stage, radio, and other forms of entertainment.

translation.text: 漫才的历史约有一千年，不过现代漫才是在 20 世纪初的大阪成形的。此后，大阪式漫才通过舞台、广播等娱乐形式传遍日本。

source.text: Today, manzai corporations play a major part in the Japanese entertainment industry by cultivating and introducing new talent. As such, many Japanese actors, singers, television hosts, and other celebrities begin their careers by making a name for themselves on the national manzai circuit.

translation.text: 如今，漫才公司通过培养、推出新人，在日本娱乐业扮演重要角色。因此，不少日本演员、歌手、电视主持人和其他名人，都是先在全国漫才舞台上闯出名气，再展开事业。

source.text: Dishing Out Comedy

translation.text: 端上一道笑话

source.text: In his translation notes ., for this scene, Toby said, "I heard there are no knock knock jokes in JP. I can try to think of some alternate takes on this"

translation.text: Toby 为这场戏写的说明是：“听说日本没有敲门笑话。我可以试着想几个替代方案。”

source.text: Sans reveals important background information during a story scene. At one point in the English script, he retells a knock-knock joke:

translation.text: Sans 在一段剧情中透露重要背景，其中复述了一个英语敲门笑话：

source.text: English Text

translation.text: 英文版

source.text: Japanese Text (roughly translated)

translation.text: 日文版大意

source.text: fortunately, deep in the forest... there's this HUGE locked door. and it's perfect for practicing knock knock jokes.

translation.text: 幸好，森林深处……有扇锁着的巨大门，用来练敲门笑话正合适。

source.text: but deep in the forest is a huge locked door, perfect for practicing my comedy with.

translation.text: 不过森林深处有扇锁着的巨大门，正适合练习我的笑话。

source.text: so one day, i'm knocking 'em out, like usual. i knock on the door and say "knock knock." and suddenly, from the other side ... i hear a woman's voice.

translation.text: 某天，我像往常一样接连讲笑话。我敲门说“咚咚”。突然，从另一边……传来一个女人的声音。

source.text: one day, i was practicing my latest jokes while pretending the door was the audience. suddenly, from behind the door, a woman's voice butted in with a sharp retort:

source.text: "who is there?" so, naturally, I respond: "dishes."

“谁呀？”
我自然回答：“dishes（盘子）。”

source.text: "what are ya, an idiot or somethin'?!" without skipping a beat, i replied: "if i'm such an idiot, why are you play- ing the straight-man during a solo comedy routine Ji"

“你是不是傻啊？！”
我立刻回道：“说我傻？我这单口表演，你跑来当什么吐槽役啊？！”

source.text: "dishes who?"

translation.text: “dishes who（哪个盘子）？”

source.text: the voice replied: "well, if i'm such an idiot, why the heck are you, the fun- ny-man, insulting the straight-man in a duo comedy routine?!"

translation.text: 那声音回答：“说我傻？我们这双人漫才，你这个装傻的干吗骂吐槽的？！”

source.text: "dishes a very bad joke."

translation.text:
“dishes a very bad joke.”
“这是个很烂的笑话。”

translation.text: 我说：“我根本就没在装傻啊！”

translation.text: 然后她笑得停不下来。

source.text: Because knock-knock jokes don't exist in Japan, and because the English joke in this scene plays with how "this is" and "dishes" are pronounced, the scene would've made little sense in a literal translation. To get around this problem, the translator replaced the knock-knock joke with a joke related to two common forms of Japanese comedy: solo acts and duo manzai acts.

translation.text: 日本没有敲门笑话，而这里又利用了 this is（这是）与 dishes（盘子）读音相近的特点，所以直接翻译几乎毫无意义。为解决这一问题，译者改用了围绕日本两种常见喜剧形式——单口表演和双人漫才——的笑话。

source.text: Although this new Japanese text parallels the humor of the original text, it does carry one minor side effect: it makes some level of sense for a comedian to practice knock-knock jokes while standing in front of a giant door, but it makes less sense to practice generic comedy in the same situation.

translation.text: 新日文重现了原文的幽默，却也带来一个小副作用：喜剧演员站在大门前练敲门笑话，还算说得通；同样站在那里练一般笑话，就不那么自然了。

source.text: Knockabout Solution

translation.text: 另解敲门笑话

source.text: In my experience, pronunciation-based jokes are almost always too slippery to be translatable between languages

translation.text: 以我的经验，靠发音构成的笑话几乎总是太难捉摸，无法直接跨语言翻译。

source.text: Sans continues to discuss his unusual experience at the giant door. This time, the person behind the door makes a knock-knock joke. Naturally, the translator had to rephrase this scene in Japanese too:

translation.text: Sans 继续讲述在大门前的奇遇。这回，门后的人讲了个敲门笑话，译者自然也必须改写：

source.text: English Text

translation.text: 英文版

source.text: Japanese Text (roughly translated)

translation.text: 日文版大意

source.text: then, after a dozen of 'em, SHE knocks and says ..

translation.text: 讲了十几个后，换她敲门说……

source.text: then, the woman says

translation.text: 然后，那女人说……

source.text: "knock knock!"

translation.text: “咚咚！”

source.text: "can I tell a joke too?"

translation.text: “我也能讲个笑话吗？”

source.text: i say "whos there?"

translation.text: 我问：“谁呀？”

source.text: "sure!" i say.

translation.text: “当然！”我说。

source.text: "old lady!"

translation.text: “old lady（老太太）！”

source.text: "say, doesn't it seem strange?" she asks.

translation.text: “你说，奇不奇怪？”她问。

source.text: "old lady who?"

translation.text: “old lady who（哪位老太太）？”

source.text: "what do you mean?" i reply.

translation.text: “怎么说？”我问。

source.text: "oh! I did not know you could yodel!"

translation.text: “噢！没想到你会唱约德尔！”

source.text: "we're talking so close to each other, but we're so 'toku' away."

translation.text: “我们靠这么近说话，却还是这么 tōku（远／聊天）。”

source.text: This dialogue contains two main points of interest. First, astute players will realize that the "old lady" in Sans' story is actually Torie!, although the two have yet to meet in person.

translation.text: 这段对话有两个看点。首先，细心的玩家会意识到，Sans 故事里的“老太太”其实是 Toriel，尽管两人还没真正见过面。

source.text: Second, and more importantly, Toriel's knock-knock joke plays with how the phrase "old lady who" sounds like the shout that yodelers make, "yodel-ay-ee-oo". But again, because knock-knock jokes don't exist in Japanese, and because this joke plays with English pronunciation, a literal translation of the scene would lose all meaning.

translation.text: 其次，更重要的是，Toriel 的敲门笑话利用了“old lady who”听起来像约德尔唱法中的“yodel-ay-ee-oo”。但日本没有敲门笑话，笑点又依赖英语发音，因此直译会完全失去意义。

source.text: Yodeling is a traditional form of singing that originated in rural regions of Europe. It involves quickly switching back and forth between super-high and super-low notes

translation.text: 约德尔是源自欧洲乡村的传统唱法，需要在极高与极低的音之间快速切换。

source.text: To get around these linguistic and cultural barriers, the translator replaced the English knock-knock joke with a pun on the Japanese word toku, which can mean both "far away" and "talk". The result is a cheesy joke in Japanese that perfectly matches Toriel's character.

translation.text: 为了绕过语言和文化障碍，译者把英语敲门笑话换成日语 tōku 的双关：它既可指“远”，也可指“聊天”（英语 talk 的借词）。这个日语冷笑话与 Toriel 的性格非常贴合。

source.text: Hotland

translation.text: 热域

source.text: Sans Surprise

translation.text: Sans 突然变脸

source.text: Imagine being longtime ~ friends with the kindest, funniest person alive - like maybe Mr. Rogers from American TV - then suddenly hearing them say, ''I'll kill you if I have to."

translation.text: 想象一下，你多年的好友是世上最友善、最风趣的人——比如美国电视上的 Mr. Rogers——却突然听见他说：“必要的话，我会杀了你。”

source.text: Throughout the story so far, Sans has been a friendly, joke-loving goofball. But suddenly, with a terrifying look on his face, he says in a completely different font and tone of voice:

translation.text: 到目前为止，Sans 一直是友善、爱讲笑话的活宝。但他突然露出可怕的神情，用完全不同的字体和语气说：

source.text: that promise i made to her. .. you /mow what would have happened ifs he hadn't said anything? ... buddy. You'd be dead where you stand.

translation.text: 我答应过她……你知道，要是她什么都没说，会发生什么吗？……伙计。你现在就死在这里了。

source.text: Toby intended this line to emotionally shock the player, as it's the first real time that Sans shows that he has a dark, frightening side. Naturally, Toby considers this scene - and this specific line - very important to the Undertale experience. As such, he was very particular about how this line was handled in translation. After a lot of trial-and-error, Toby and the translation team went with a straightforward approach:

translation.text: Toby 希望这句话让玩家受到震动，因为这是 Sans 第一次真正展露黑暗、可怕的一面。因此，他认为这场戏，尤其是这句台词，对《Undertale》的体验非常重要，翻译时也格外讲究。经过多次尝试，Toby 与团队最终选择了直接的处理：

source.text: おまえは いまごろ とっくに しんでいた。 [Literally: "You’d be long dead by now." or "You’d already be dead by now."]

translation.text:
おまえは いまごろ とっくに しんでいた。
［直译：“你现在早就死了。”或“到现在你已经死了。”］

source.text: The original English line leaves it unclear why the main character would be dead by now. It's left to the player's interpretation: would Sans have killed the main character himself, would he have captured the main character for the king to kill later, or possibly something else? This Japanese line achieves a similar vagueness through careful wording.

translation.text: 英文原句没有说明主角为什么会死，留给玩家自行理解：Sans 会亲手杀死主角，还是抓住主角交给国王杀掉，又或者另有原因？日语通过谨慎措辞，保住了相近的模糊性。

source.text: After the official translation's release, Japanese players indeed found this scene shocking, and the vagueness of the translated line left players with different interpretations. Given this, there's no doubt that Toby's persistence with this line led to a superior, more faithful translation in the end.

translation.text: 官方译版发行后，日本玩家确实被这一幕震住了，模糊的台词也引发了不同解读。由此可见，Toby 对这句话的坚持，最终带来了更出色、更忠实的翻译。

source.text: ~ From some of his personal notes-to-self, we can see that Toby cared a great deal about this Sans scene in particular

translation.text: 从 Toby 写给自己的几条私人笔记可以看出，他格外重视 Sans 的这场戏。

source.text: Toby actively consulted ~ outside sources for second opinions about the nuances of localized lines

translation.text: Toby 主动向团队之外的人征求意见，核对本地化台词的细微含义。

source.text: Hotland

translation.text: 热域

source.text: The Core

translation.text: 核心

pages.title: 核心：不屈的人类威胁重要设施

source.text: The Core

translation.text: 核心

source.text: Relentless Human Threatens Vital Infrastructure

translation.text: 不屈的人类威胁重要设施

source.text: The main character now enters the Core, an advanced energy generation facility. Extreme temperatures and enhanced foes wait inside.

translation.text: 主角现在进入了核心，一座先进的能源设施。极端高温和更强的敌人正在里面等待。

source.text: Works Like a Charm

translation.text: 咒语也要本地化

source.text: Localizing magic spells ~ into other languages sounds like a fictional Hogwarts class or something, but nope, it's a real thing

translation.text: 把魔法咒语本地化成别的语言，听起来像霍格沃茨的虚构课程，但这确实是一项真实工作。

source.text: A monster named Madjick occasionally chants magic words during battle. Some of these magic words remained unchanged during the translation process, while others were localized to make more sense for Japanese players.

translation.text: 怪物 Madjick 会在战斗中偶尔念出咒语。翻译时，一部分咒语保持不变，另一部分则经过本地化，让日本玩家更容易理解。

source.text: Abra Cadabra

translation.text: Abra Cadabra

source.text: In English, "abracadabra" is a customary, well-known magic word that can be used in just about any magic-related situation. Because "abracadabra" is well known in Japan too, this magic word remained the same in Underta/e's Japanese script.

translation.text: 英语中的 abra cadabra 是耳熟能详的常见咒语，几乎任何与魔法有关的场合都能用。日本也熟悉这个咒语，因此《Undertale》日文版保留了它。

source.text: Alakazam

translation.text: Alakazam

source.text: In English, "alakazam" is another standard, well-known magic word. This word is less known in Japan, however, so the localization team replaced "alakazam" with chichinpui, a magic-like Japanese phrase often said to children to soothe their pain after getting hurt.

translation.text: Alakazam 也是英语里熟悉的标准咒语。不过日本人对它较陌生，所以团队换成了 chichinpui——一种像咒语的日语说法，常用来安抚受伤的孩子，意在让疼痛消失。

source.text: Tinkle Tinkle Hoy

translation.text: Tinkle Tinkle Hoy

source.text: Another of Madjick's phrases, "tinkle tinkle hoy", isn't a commonly known magic word in English. In the translation spreadsheet, Toby noted that "tinkle tinkle hoy" is actually a reference to a magic phrase in the Japanese manga series, Oyasumi Pun Pun. Naturally, the localization team ensured that this reference remained intact in the Japanese script.

translation.text: Madjick 的另一句“tinkle tinkle hoy”并不是英语里常见的咒语。Toby 在翻译表格中注明，它其实引用了日本漫画《Oyasumi Pun Pun》（晚安，布布）里的魔法短句。团队自然确保日文版保留了这个引用。

source.text: Toby included the magic phrase "tinkle tinkle hoy" as a reference to the Oyasumi Pun Pun series

translation.text: Toby 用“tinkle tinkle hoy”这句咒语引用了《晚安，布布》。

source.text: Hocus Pocus

translation.text: Hocus Pocus

source.text: "Hocus pocus" is one of the most classic magic phrases in English. Although it's less known in Japan, it does appear occasionally in Japanese entertainment. For this reason, "hocus pocus" remained as-is in the Japanese script.

translation.text: Hocus pocus 是英语中最经典的咒语之一。虽然日本人不太熟悉，但日本娱乐作品中偶尔也会出现，所以日文剧本仍保留原样。

source.text: Please and Thank You

translation.text: 请与谢谢

source.text: Children in English-speaking regions are taught that "please" and "thank you" are "magic words" that should be used when making a request or after receiving something. The joke here is that "please" and "thank you" are out of place in this situation - they aren't actual "magic words" that magicians chant.

translation.text: 英语地区的孩子从小会被教导：“please”（请）和“thank you”（谢谢）是提出请求、接受东西后该说的“魔法词”。这里的笑点在于，这两句话放在这种场合不合适——它们可不是魔法师真正念的咒语。

source.text: Because "please" and "thank you" aren't traditionally called "magic words" in Japanese, the translator changed Madjick's "please and thank you" to popopopo-n. This mostly meaningless word is a reference to Aisatsu no Maha ("Greetings Are Magic"), a magic-themed public service announcement that constantly aired on Japanese television in 2011.

translation.text: 日语传统上不把“请”和“谢谢”叫作“魔法词”，因此译者把 Madjick 的“please and thank you”改成 popopopo~n。这个词本身基本没有意义，引用的是 2011 年在日本电视上反复播出的魔法主题公益广告《Aisatsu no Mahō》（问候的魔法）。

source.text: Aisatsu no Maha on Japanese Television

translation.text: 日本电视上的《问候的魔法》

source.text: In 2011, several regions of Japan were hit by devastating natural and manmade disasters. During this painful and turbulent time, many Japanese companies felt it would be inappropriate and tone-deaf to advertise their products on television between the constant news programs about the disasters. For this reason, ordinary commercials on television were often replaced with simple filler material.

translation.text: 2011 年，日本多地遭受严重天灾与人祸。在这段痛苦、动荡的时期，许多企业觉得，在不断播报灾情的新闻之间插入商品广告很不合适，也显得不懂人情。因此，电视上的普通广告常被简单的填充节目取代。

source.text: One such "filler video" was Aisatsu no Maha ("Greetings Are Magic"), a 2010 children's song and television public service announcement that aired with brain-searing regularity in 2011. Aisatsu no Maha repeated on Japanese television so often that it became a widely shared cultural experience. The video grew so grating over time that it spawned hate memes, spooky urban legends, and elaborate conspiracy theories.

translation.text: 其中一段就是《问候的魔法》：这首 2010 年制作的儿歌兼电视公益广告，在 2011 年以令人洗脑的频率播出。它反复出现，成为日本人广泛共有的文化记忆。时间久了，视频令人越来越烦，催生了恶搞、恐怖都市传说，以及复杂的阴谋论。

source.text: Aisatsu no Maha teaches children to be polite and friendly by using various "magic words"

translation.text: 《问候的魔法》教孩子用各种“魔法词”礼貌友善地待人。

source.text: The made-up sound effect word popopopo-n became closely tied with magic through excessive repetition

translation.text: 虚构拟声词 popopopo~n 因反复出现，与魔法紧密联系起来。

source.text: As a song, Aisatsu no Maha was intended to teach children the importance of words like konnichi wa ("hello"), itadakimasu ("I humbly accept this food"), and arigata ("thank you"). In the song, these phrases are referred to as "magic words" that can help you make friends. The lyrics also include the occasional popopopo-n, a made-up sound effect word that was intended to represent "the sound of lots of friends appearing". Popopopo-n was such an unavoidable phrase that it won first place in 2011 's Japanese Internet Buzzword Awards.

translation.text: 这首歌原本想让孩子明白 konnichi wa（你好）、itadakimasu（我怀着感激接受这顿饭）和 arigatō（谢谢）等用语的重要性。歌词称它们为能帮你交朋友的“魔法词”，还不时穿插 popopopo~n——一个虚构的音效词，表示“许多朋友出现的声音”。它变得无处不在，甚至获得了 2011 年日本网络流行语大奖第一名。

source.text: The Core

translation.text: 核心

source.text: Midknight Hour

translation.text: 骑士与晚安

source.text: On a side note, Knight ~ Knight sometimes says "adieu" in the English game, which became "adios" in the Japanese script

translation.text: 顺便说一句，Knight Knight 在英文版有时说“adieu”（法语“再见”），日文版改成了“adios”（西班牙语“再见”）。

source.text: A sleep-themed monster named "Knight Knight" appears in the Core. This name is a play on the phrase "night-night", which is a common way of saying "good night" to children.

translation.text: 核心里有一个以睡眠为主题的怪物，名叫 Knight Knight。这个名字用 knight（骑士）谐音 night，模仿英语中常对孩子说的“night-night”（晚安）。

source.text: While the English phrase "night-night" isn't well known in Japan, the English phrase "good night" has been absorbed into the Japanese language. Because of this, the translator renamed the monster "Good Knight" in Japanese.

translation.text: 日本人不太熟悉 night-night，但英语 good night 已成为日语借用的说法。因此，译者把这个怪物改名为“Good Knight”。

source.text: Not Losing It

translation.text: 不让引用迷路

source.text: As a translator, my ~ internal "this is probably a reference to something" sense activates when I run across lone, carefully crafted lines like this

translation.text: 作为译者，每逢这种独立出现、措辞精心的句子，我内心“这大概在引用什么”的直觉就会启动。

source.text: In the English script, a sign in the Core taunts the player with the message:

translation.text: 英语剧本中，核心的一块牌子用下面的话嘲弄玩家：

source.text: (Get lost. .. ) (And stay that way.)

translation.text:
（迷路去吧……）
（永远别找回来。）

source.text: Toby noted that this is another direct quote from the English version of Brandish. With this obscure information in hand, the translator looked up the original Japanese Brandish quote, which translates as:

translation.text: Toby 说明，这又是直接引用英文版《Brandish》。掌握这条冷门线索后，译者找出了它的日文原句，大意是：

source.text: (May you wander continuously.)

translation.text: （你就一直徘徊下去吧。）

source.text: Random Life Tip: if ~ you lose something in your house, look in a 3-foot radius around where you normally expect it to be, it's likely there somewhere

translation.text: 随手生活小贴士：如果在家找不到东西，就在平时放它的位置周围三英尺（约一米）内找找，多半就在那里。

source.text: Fortunately, this quote is consistent across the many Japanese versions of Brandish. This potentially makes it more recognizable than other Brandish references that were retained in Underta/e's Japanese script.

translation.text: 幸好，《Brandish》的多个日文版本都用了同一句话，因此这项引用可能比《Undertale》日版保留的其他《Brandish》引用更容易辨认。

source.text: Getting Burned

translation.text: 从燃烧到转身

source.text: Toby noted: "Burn becomes Turn so if you can think of something else that can turn into 'turn' that's a funnier pun that has to do with dying etc that'd be cool"

translation.text: Toby 写道：“Burn 要变成 Turn，所以如果你能想到别的词，既能变成‘转身’，又能和死亡之类构成更好笑的双关，那就太好了。”

source.text: Mettaton attempts to kill the main character again. As before, the player has few options while battling Mettaton - the only notable action available is "Burn", which simply produces the message:

translation.text: Mettaton 再次试图杀死主角。和之前一样，战斗中玩家可选的行动不多，唯一醒目的是“Burn”（燃烧），选了只会出现提示：

source.text: This is probably what you'll do ift hings continue in this manner.

translation.text: 如果一直这样下去，你大概就会变成这样。

source.text: Similar to the previous Mettaton encounter, this "Burn" command eventually transforms into the similarly spelled "Turn" command

translation.text: 与上次遭遇 Mettaton 类似，“Burn”最后会变成拼写相近的“Turn”。

source.text: Eventually, Al phys informs the player that Mettaton has a switch on his back. The "Burn" menu option is then quietly replaced with the "Turn" option. This option will turn Mettaton around and reveal his power switch.

translation.text: 后来 Alphys 告诉玩家，Mettaton 背上有个开关。“Burn”选项便悄悄被“Turn”（转身）替换。选它就能让 Mettaton 转过去，露出电源开关。

source.text: Because this subtle text change relies on "Burn" and "Turn" having similar spellings in English, this wordplay would be lost in a literal translation into Japanese. To compensate, the translator first replaced "Burn" with hikkuri kaeru ("to topple over; to fall down"). The translator then altered the original battle message to fit the new menu option:

translation.text: 这处细微变化依靠 Burn 和 Turn 在英语中拼写相近，直接译成日语会丢失文字游戏。为此，译者先把 Burn 换成 hikkuri kaeru（翻倒、倒下），再调整原提示，与新选项相配：

source.text: If this keeps up, you will definitely topple over and die.

translation.text: 再这样下去，你肯定会翻倒死去。

source.text: Even if you don't know Japanese, you can see how the right hand menu option changes very slightly during this scene

translation.text: 即便不懂日语，也能看出右侧选项在这一幕中只有极细微的变化。

source.text: After this, the translator changed the "Turn" command into hikkuri kaesu ("to flip over or around"). The resulting Japanese localization closely parallels Toby's original design: the first Japanese command does nothing, the second command looks similar to the first command at first glance, and the second command also causes Mettaton to be turned around.

translation.text: 接着，译者把 Turn 译成 hikkuri kaesu（把东西翻转过来）。这样，日版就紧贴 Toby 的原设计：第一个指令毫无作用，第二个乍看与第一个相似，而且确实能让 Mettaton 转身。

source.text: The Core

translation.text: 核心

source.text: Word Problems

translation.text: 文字难题

source.text: What DO you like most about Mettaton? Write your answer below for future generations to read:

translation.text: 你究竟最喜欢 Mettaton 的哪一点？请把答案写在下面，留给后人阅读：

source.text: During battle, Mettaton gains a humanoid body and becomes Mettaton EX. He then stops and asks the player a question:

translation.text: 战斗中，Mettaton 获得了人形身体，变成 Mettaton EX。随后，他停下来问玩家一个问题：

source.text: “What do you love most about Mettaton?”

translation.text: “你最喜欢 Mettaton 的哪一点？”

source.text: The player is then asked to type an essay on their computer keyboard that answers this question. Once the essay is finished – or if time runs out – Mettaton EX will scan the player’s essay for specific keywords and respond with appropriate dialogue. Toby originally designed this system to recognize English answers, so getting it to work properly in Japanese required all-new programming code and technical adjustments.

translation.text: 接下来，玩家需要用电脑键盘输入一篇短文来回答这个问题。写完之后，或者时间一到，Mettaton EX 就会扫描玩家的文章，寻找特定关键词，并给出对应的回应。Toby 最初把这套系统设计为识别英文答案，因此，要让它正常处理日文，就需要编写全新的代码并作出技术调整。

source.text: Keyboards

translation.text: 键盘

source.text: First, because Undertale was originally designed for home computers, players could simply use their computer keyboard to type an essay answer. Unfortunately, home consoles rarely come with keyboards. To get around this hardware issue, the localization team added new code to Undertale’s programming to display on-screen keyboards compatible with game controllers.

translation.text: 首先，Undertale 最初是为家用电脑设计的，玩家可以直接用电脑键盘输入答案。然而，家用游戏机很少配备键盘。为了解决这一硬件问题，本地化团队为 Undertale 添加了新代码，显示可以用游戏手柄操作的屏幕键盘。

source.text: Japanese Input

translation.text: 日文输入

source.text: The Japanese language includes three separate writing systems, which complicates the process of searching for keywords in the player’s essay. For example, the word bibō (“good looks”) can be written with a combination of all three systems, leading to multiple possible spellings:

translation.text: 日语包含三种书写系统，这使得在玩家文章中搜索关键词变得复杂。例如，bibō（“美貌”）可以用这三种书写系统组合写出，因而有多种可能的写法：

source.text:
びぼう (all hiragana)
ビボウ (all katakana)
美貌 (all kanji)
美ぼう (kanji + hiragana)
美ボウ (kanji + katakana)
び貌 (hiragana + kanji)
ビ貌 (katakana + kanji)

translation.text:
びぼう（全平假名）
ビボウ（全片假名）
美貌（全汉字）
美ぼう（汉字＋平假名）
美ボウ（汉字＋片假名）
び貌（平假名＋汉字）
ビ貌（片假名＋汉字）

source.text: To simplify this technical problem, the localization team disabled kanji support. The team then added new programming that internally converts every katakana character to hiragana.

translation.text: 为简化这一技术问题，本地化团队禁用了汉字支持，随后加入新程序，在内部把每个片假名字符转换成平假名。

source.text: This technical solution simplified matters greatly, but it had an unexpected flaw: the game’s core programming already uses the “Z” and “X” keys for other in-game functions. To get around this, the localization team made sure that no Japanese keywords required the “Z” or “X” keys. The team then added an on-screen message stating that “Z” and “X” are unavailable. Fortunately, these keys aren’t 100% vital for Japanese input to begin with – there are often multiple ways to type a single word in Japanese.

translation.text: 这项技术方案大大简化了问题，但也带来了一个意料之外的缺陷：游戏的核心程序已经把“Z”和“X”键用于其他游戏功能。为此，本地化团队确保所有日文关键词都不必用到“Z”或“X”键，并增加了提示，说明这两个键不可用。幸好，日文输入并非一定需要它们——同一个日语词往往有多种输入方式。

source.text: Each home console version of Undertale required re-programming to support on-screen keyboards Here we see the English and Japanese keyboard layouts for the Nintendo Switch release

translation.text: 《Undertale》每个家用主机版都必须重新编程，以支持屏幕键盘。这里展示的是 Nintendo Switch 版的英语与日语键盘布局。

source.text: ~ Here we see the English and Japanese keyboard layouts for the PlayStation 4 release of Undertale

translation.text: 这里展示的是《Undertale》PlayStation 4 版的英语与日语键盘布局。

source.text: The Core

translation.text: 核心

source.text: Key Words

translation.text: 关键词

source.text: Video game • homework sounds fun and terrifying at the same time

translation.text: 电子游戏作业听起来既有趣，又可怕。

source.text: In the English version of Undertale, the game's programming searches for 69 keywords in the player's essay. In the Japanese version, there are 81 keywords. There are several reasons for this mismatch:

translation.text: 英文版《Undertale》的程序会在玩家作文中搜索 69 个关键词；日文版则有 81 个。数量不同有几个原因：

source.text: The English language separates words with spaces, but spaces aren't required in Japanese - this complicates the keyword searching process and can result in false positives unless extra precautions are taken

translation.text: 英语用空格分词，日语却不必。这使关键词搜索更复杂，不采取额外措施就可能误判。

source.text: The Japanese language includes a dizzying number of homophones (words with the same pronunciation but different meanings), and the lack of kanji support makes it difficult to differentiate them

translation.text: 日语有数量惊人的同音词，即读音相同、意思不同的词；这里不支持汉字，因而很难区分。

source.text: The Japanese language has its own words for things, but it's also absorbed countless English words - this combination results in a slightly larger pool of available keywords

translation.text: 日语既有自己的词汇，又吸收了大量英语词，两者结合使可用的关键词稍多。

source.text: The Japanese version of Undertale also includes a new set of 14 keywords that result in all-new Mettaton EX responses. For example, if a Japanese player includes the word nihongo ("Japanese language") in the essay, Mettaton EX will respond with:

translation.text: 日版《Undertale》还加入了 14 个新关键词，触发 Mettaton EX 全新的回应。例如，作文写到 nihongo（日语）时，他会回答：

source.text: But ofc ourse! Any true star is well-versed in the language arts!

translation.text: 那当然！真正的明星都精通语言艺术！

source.text: When Toby originally designed this essay scene, he put a lot of thought into how it should work and how Mettaton EX should react as ifhe were an actual, living character. As we can see, the localization team put just as much care into how the Japanese scene should work technically and linguistically.

translation.text: Toby 最初设计作文场景时，仔细考虑了它的运作方式，以及如何让 Mettaton EX 像真实、鲜活的角色一样回应。可以看出，本地化团队也同样用心，兼顾了日语场景的技术与语言表现。

source.text: And for no real reason, here is what Japanese computer keyboards look like if you've never seen one before

translation.text: 没什么特别原因，给没见过的人看看日本电脑键盘长什么样。

source.text: If the player includes the word omoshiroi ("fun; funny; interesting"), Mettaton EX responds by saying, "Being funny and cool is the secret to being popular!"

translation.text: 如果玩家写到 omoshiroi（有趣、好笑），Mettaton EX 会说：“又有趣又帅气，才是受欢迎的秘诀！”

source.text: If the player uses the wordyabai ("sick; crazy; awesome", can be used as slang to describe something good or bad}, Mettaton EX will reply, "Sick? You mean that in the positive sense, I assume?"

translation.text: 如果玩家用 yabai（不得了、疯狂、厉害，可褒可贬的俚语），Mettaton EX 会回答：“不得了？我想你说的当然是好的那种吧？”

source.text: If the player uses the slang word emoi ("emotional"), Mettaton EX will say, "Thanks! .. Uhh, you meant that as a compliment, right?"

translation.text: 如果玩家用俚语 emoi（触动情绪的、令人感慨的），Mettaton EX 会说：“谢谢！……呃，你是在夸我，对吧？”

source.text: If the player uses the word nihongo ("the Japanese language"}, Mettaton EX will respond with, "But of course! Any true star is well-versed in the language arts!"

translation.text: 如果玩家写到 nihongo（日语），Mettaton EX 会回答：“那当然！真正的明星都精通语言艺术！”

source.text: The Core

translation.text: 核心

source.text: New Home

translation.text: 新家

source.text: New Home

translation.text: 新家

source.text: Human Enters Royal Abode

translation.text: 人类走进王室居所

source.text: The main character passes through New Home, the royal capital of the Underground. A look around the castle reveals details about the royal family's tragic past.

translation.text: 主角来到地下世界的王都——新家。查看城堡里的物品，王室悲惨的往事也渐渐浮现。

source.text: Self Reflection

translation.text: 镜中的自己

source.text: A lot gets lost when translated back into English, but this Japanese line basically says "a lot of things have happened, but self is self after all"

translation.text: 回译成英文会损失许多意味，不过日文这句大致是说：“虽然发生了很多事，自己终究还是自己。”

source.text: In the English version of Undertale, checking a mirror in New Home produces the message:

translation.text: 在《Undertale》英文版里，查看新家的一面镜子，会出现这句话：

source.text: Despite everything, it's still you.

translation.text: Despite everything, it’s still you.（尽管如此，你依然是你。）

source.text: This short, five-word sentence is one of the most famous quotes in Underta/e's English script, largely because its intentional ambiguity can mean very different things to different players. Some possible interpretations include:

translation.text: 这句短短五个词的话，是《Undertale》英文剧本里最著名的台词之一。它刻意留下了模糊空间，不同玩家可以读出截然不同的意味。例如：

source.text: "A lot's happened, but you've made it this far intact"

translation.text: • “经历了这么多，你仍然好好地走到了这里。”

source.text: "The main character/player has endured a lot, yet is unchanged deep down"

translation.text: • “主角／玩家承受了许多，内心深处却没有改变。”

source.text: "The main character/player has caused a lot to happen, yet is the same deep down"

translation.text: • “主角／玩家造成了许多事，内心深处却仍然一样。”

source.text: This line could arguably be referencing the player's inner personality as well:

translation.text: 这句话也可以理解为在说玩家内在的性情：

source.text: "See, despite believing you're a good person, your choices show that you also have a dark side to you." (When a normally gentle player murders some monsters in the game just to see what happens)

translation.text: • “看吧，尽管你相信自己是好人，你的选择却说明你也有阴暗的一面。”（平时温和的玩家，只为看看结果而在游戏里杀害一些怪物。）

source.text: "See, despite acting like a tough guy on the exterior, you do have a caring side to you." (When a normally hot-tempered player spares every monster in the game)

translation.text: • “看吧，尽管你外表强硬，你也有温柔体贴的一面。”（平时脾气暴躁的玩家，在游戏里饶恕每一个怪物。）

source.text: Many other potential interpretations exist too, of course. In short, with its simplicity and emotional depth, this "despite everything, it's still you" line has spawned countless pieces of fan fiction, fan art, and even permanent tattoos.

translation.text: 当然，还可以有许多其他解读。“尽管如此，你依然是你”简单却情感深厚，因此催生了无数同人小说、同人画，甚至成了永不褪去的文身。

source.text: Naturally, Toby and the localization team put a lot of thought into this line to preserve its many potential nuances. In the end, the team decided to prioritize the content of the message over its sheer memorability. So although the resulting literal translation is less celebrated than its English counterpart, it does retain the intent of the original line, while still flowing naturally in Japanese.

translation.text: Toby 和本地化团队自然也在这句台词上花了很多心思，希望保留各种潜在含义。最后，他们决定优先传达这句话的内容，而非单纯追求令人难忘的表达。最终的直译虽然不像英文原句那样广受传颂，却保留了原意，日语读来也很自然。

source.text: English-speaking Underta/e fans often draw art related to this single line of text

translation.text: 英语圈的《Undertale》粉丝经常以这句台词为题作画。

source.text: Reader Challenge #8: Consider who you are as a person right now - would you want to be your own friend if you somehow met yourself?

translation.text: 读者挑战 #8：想想现在的你是怎样的人。假如你遇见另一个自己，你会愿意和自己交朋友吗？

source.text: Tattoos of this scene are a common sight among English speaking Undertale fan communities

translation.text: 在英语圈《Undertale》粉丝群体里，这个场景的文身并不少见。

source.text: Some English speaking fans even celebrate this memorable line with food

translation.text: 有些英语圈粉丝甚至用食物来纪念这句难忘的台词。

source.text: New Home

translation.text: 新家

pages.title: Asgore 的说话方式与 Mario 彩蛋

source.text: Asgore Speaks

translation.text: Asgore 的说话方式

source.text: King Asgore uses the polite pronoun わたし (watashi) in Japanese

translation.text: 日文中，Asgore 国王用较礼貌的第一人称「わたし」（watashi，“我”）。

source.text: The king of the Underground, Asgore Dreemur, lives in New Home. In the translation spreadsheet, Toby explained how Asgore switches between two different speech patterns in English:

translation.text: 地下世界的国王 Asgore Dreemur 住在新家。在翻译表格里，Toby 解释了 Asgore 在英文中如何切换两种说话方式：

source.text: '' King But his method of speech is kind of like "goo.fy,forgetful dad" with only certain points that he goes into "cold, distant/formal king:" He's not really great at being a king

translation.text: 国王。不过他说话更像个“傻乎乎、健忘的老爸”，只有某些时候才会变成“冷漠、疏远／一本正经的国王”。他其实不太擅长当国王。

source.text: With this information in hand, the translator gave Asgore a polite speech pattern for most of his Japanese dialogue, which includes the use of the polite pronoun watashi. For other situations, the translator made sure that Asgore switches to a colder, but still formal speech pattern.

translation.text: 根据这些说明，译者让 Asgore 的大部分日语台词都采用礼貌的说话方式，包括使用较礼貌的第一人称 watashi（我）。其他场合则让他转为更冷淡、但仍然正式的语气。

source.text: Mario Artist

translation.text: 手工作品里的 Mario 彩蛋

source.text: To be fair, this Mario ~ reference probably went unnoticed by a large portion of the English speaking audience

translation.text: 公平地说，恐怕也有许多英语玩家没发现这个 Mario 彩蛋。

source.text: In the king's home, a child's art project hangs on a wall with a short message:

translation.text: 国王家里的墙上挂着一件孩子做的手工作品，上面有一句短短的话：

source.text: For King Dad!

translation.text: 献给 King Dad（国王爸爸）！

source.text: Toby noted that the phrase "King Dad" is a reference to the Super Mario Bros. television cartoons that first aired in the late 1980s and early 1990s. Specifically, the phrase is from the Adventures of Super Mario Bros. 3 series, in which the villain's children regularly call their father "King Dad".

translation.text: Toby 指出，“King Dad”是在致敬 20 世纪 80 年代末至 90 年代初开播的《超级马力欧兄弟》电视动画。具体来说，它出自《超级马力欧兄弟 3 大冒险》：反派的孩子们经常这样称呼自己的父亲。

source.text: Some of King Koopa's children called him "King Dad" in the old American animated series, but later games would clarify that they're just his minions and not actually his children

translation.text: 在早年的美国动画里，King Koopa 的几个孩子叫他“国王爸爸”。但后来的游戏澄清，他们其实只是手下，并非他的孩子。

source.text: Because this animated series was produced for Western audiences, this reference would be missed by most .Japanese players. But rather than force a different reference into this important line, the translator focused on the key information and translated the line literally. Even without the reference, it's still clear in the Japanese script that Asgore and his child were part of a loving family.

translation.text: 这部动画面向西方观众制作，多数日本玩家大概不会明白这个典故。不过，译者没有硬往这句重要台词里塞进别的典故，而是抓住关键信息，直接翻译。即使看不出致敬对象，日本玩家仍能清楚感受到 Asgore 和孩子曾有一个充满爱的家。

source.text: The Importance of "The"

translation.text: “The”的重要性

source.text: The Japanese version of this line spells things out a tad more clearly for players, but it also keeps it vague enough for players to ponder the implication on their own

translation.text: 日文把意思说得稍明白了些，但仍保留足够的模糊空间，让玩家自行琢磨其中的暗示。

source.text: A very special locket is stored in a box in New Home. Inspecting the box during a standard playthrough will produce the message:

translation.text: 新家的一个盒子里放着一枚很特别的挂坠。正常游玩时查看盒子，会出现：

source.text: You got the Heart-shaped Locket.

translation.text: You got the Heart-shaped Locket.（你得到了心形挂坠。）

source.text: During a murderous No Mercy playthrough, it becomes clear that the player and the main character aren't one and the same. Further clues suggest that the locket and this other "entity" share a dark, complicated history. For these reasons, the standard locket message becomes:

translation.text: 在大开杀戒的屠杀路线中，玩家会明显发现，自己和主角并不是同一个存在。其他线索还暗示，这枚挂坠与另一个“存在”有着黑暗而复杂的过往。因此，通常的提示会变成：

source.text: You got The Locket.

translation.text: You got The Locket.（你得到了“那枚挂坠”。）

source.text: The capital "T" in "The Locket" might seem like a simple typo at first, making it easy for players - and translators - to overlook its importance. What's more, the Japanese language lacks both uppercase writing and articles like "a" and "the". Had Underta/e's localization been rushed, this combination of language quirks could've easily led to a generic-sounding game phrase:

translation.text: “The Locket”里大写的 T，乍看可能只是笔误，玩家和译者都很容易忽略它的重要性。日语既没有字母大小写，也没有 a、the 这样的冠词。假如《Undertale》的本地化赶工，这些语言差异凑在一起，很容易把它译成一句毫无特殊意味的游戏提示：

source.text: Got [a/the] locket.

translation.text: 得到了挂坠。

source.text: Fortunately, the team recognized the importance of the word "The" in this line. So, to preserve Toby's intention, the translator replaced the verb "got" with "took back". Thus, the Japanese version of this line became:

translation.text: 幸好，团队注意到了这句中“The”的分量。为了保留 Toby 的意图，译者把动词“得到”改成了“取回”。因此，日文这句话变成了：

source.text: Took back [a/the] locket.

translation.text: 取回了挂坠。

source.text: Basically, by prioritizing the intent of the line over its literal wording, the localization team was able to preserve this important piece of background lore for Japanese players to analyze.

translation.text: 本地化团队优先考虑台词的用意，而非拘泥于字面，从而保住了这条重要的背景线索，让日本玩家也能加以分析。

source.text: English Articles in Japanese Games

translation.text: 日本游戏里的英语冠词

source.text: Because the Japanese language lacks articles like "a", "an", or "the", it's common to see these words mishandled in Japanese entertainment. In some cases, these erratic articles can be funny, memorable, and endearing for players outside of Japan.

translation.text: 日语没有 a、an、the 这样的冠词，因此日本娱乐作品里经常用错它们。有时，这些古怪的用法会让海外玩家觉得好笑、难忘，甚至有点可爱。

translation.text: 真实验室

source.text: Human Accesses Secret Scientific Research!

translation.text: 人类接触到了秘密科学研究！

source.text: The human discovers a secret laboratory crawling with creepy creatures and twisted experiments. Beyond them lie the Underground's darkest secrets, waiting to be uncovered.

translation.text: 人类发现了一间秘密实验室，里面遍布诡异的生物和扭曲的实验。更深处，地下世界最黑暗的秘密正等待揭开。

source.text: Translation by Complication

translation.text: 让翻译更难读

source.text: Underta/e's English script contains many special lines of text that most players probably never see. A few of these special lines look like random, meaningless symbols when uncovered, but they're not meaningless at all. They simply use a computer font named "Wingdings" that contains nothing but symbols.

translation.text: 《Undertale》的英文剧本里有许多特殊文本，大部分玩家可能从未见过。其中一些看起来像是随机、无意义的符号，其实并非如此。它们只是用了名为 Wingdings 的电脑字体；这套字体里全是符号。

source.text: For example, the random sentence "I EAT BUGS EVERY DAY" looks like this in the Wingdings font:

translation.text: 随便举个例子，“I EAT BUGS EVERY DAY”（我每天都吃虫子）用 Wingdings 字体显示出来，是这样的：

source.text: Most players will probably never encounter these special messages in Underta/e because they only appear under extremely rare conditions. In addition, these messages look like gibberish unless the player has a Wingdings conversion chart handy. Thus, it almost feels like these messages contain dark secrets intended to confuse the player.

translation.text: 多数玩家可能永远不会在《Undertale》里遇见这些特殊消息，因为它们只在极其罕见的条件下出现。而且，除非手边恰好有 Wingdings 对照表，否则看起来就是一堆乱码。于是，它们仿佛藏着某种黑暗秘密，有意让玩家摸不着头脑。

source.text: Naturally, the localization team wanted to preserve the "dark, mysterious, and unreadable" vibe in Japanese too. There was one problem, though: the Wingdings font is incompatible with standard Japanese text.

translation.text: 本地化团队自然也想在日文里保留这种“黑暗、神秘、无法阅读”的感觉。但有个问题：Wingdings 字体不支持普通日文。

source.text: The localization team found a simple solution to this font problem: decode the Wingding messages into English, translate those messages into Japanese, transcribe the Japanese messages using English letters, then display the new messages with the Wingdings font.

translation.text: 团队找到一个简单办法：先把 Wingdings 消息解码成英文，再译成日文，把日文转写成英文字母，最后用 Wingdings 字体显示这段新消息。

source.text: Original English Line

translation.text: 英文原句

source.text: Japanese Translation

translation.text: 日语翻译

source.text: English Transcription

translation.text: 字母转写

translation.text: 游戏中的最终显示
