translation.text: I AM A HORSE（我是一匹马）

source.text: 私は馬だ

translation.text: 私は馬だ（我是一匹马）

source.text: WATASHI HA UMA DA

translation.text: WATASHI HA UMA DA（我是一匹马）

source.text: As a result of this localization change, the special Wingding messages look different in English and in Japanese. The content remains the same, though - inquisitive Japanese players who decipher the Japanese message will learn the same information as inquisitive English-speaking players.

translation.text: 经过这样的本地化处理，英文与日文中的 Wingdings 特殊消息看上去并不相同，内容却保持一致。好奇的日本玩家破解日文消息后，得到的信息与好奇的英语玩家完全一样。

pages.title: 符号对照表与面包彩蛋

source.text: Wingdings Symbol Chart

translation.text: Wingdings 符号对照表

source.text: The Wingdings font, which has come standard with Windows computers since the early 1990s, allows users to include symbols and icons in text documents

translation.text: Wingdings 从 20 世纪 90 年代初起就是 Windows 电脑的标配字体，用户可用它在文档中加入符号和图标。

source.text: Bread-Based Tribute

translation.text: 用面包致敬

source.text: Reader Challenge #9: Come up with a bread pun for this caption before you finish this page!

translation.text: 读者挑战 #9：读完这页之前，为这条图注想一个面包双关！

source.text: In the English version of Undertale, an enemy named "Lemon Bread" blocks the way forward. In his notes, Toby stated that this name is a reference to the classic 1993 game, Gunstar Heroes.

translation.text: 《Undertale》英文版里，一个名叫“Lemon Bread”（柠檬面包）的敌人挡住了去路。Toby 在笔记里说，这个名字是在致敬 1993 年的经典游戏《Gunstar Heroes》。

source.text: In the original Japanese version of Gunstar Heroes, players can fight "MELON PAN", a bizarre enemy whose name comes from a popular Japanese snack of the same name. In the English-language release of Gunstar Heroes, "MELON PAN" was translated literally as "MELON BREAD".

translation.text: 在《Gunstar Heroes》日文原版里，玩家会遇到一个古怪敌人“MELON PAN”（蜜瓜包），名字来自日本常见的同名点心。游戏推出英文版时，这个名字被直译成了“MELON BREAD”（蜜瓜面包）。

source.text: Japanese melon pan is a sweet bread roll topped with crispy cookie dough

translation.text: 日本的 melon pan（蜜瓜包）是一种甜面包，表面覆着酥脆的饼干面皮。

source.text: We can actually see one of Toby's early notes about this reference back in the Getting it Localized chapter

translation.text: 前面的“本地化过程”一章里，就能看到 Toby 关于这个彩蛋的一条早期笔记。

source.text: As a tribute to this localization choice in Gunstar Heroes, Toby requested that the "Lemon Bread" enemy in Undertale be renamed "LEMON PAN" in the Japanese script. This change ensures that Toby's Gunstar Heroes reference will remain intact and recognizable to Japanese players.

translation.text: 为了致敬《Gunstar Heroes》当年的本地化处理，Toby 要求把《Undertale》日文剧本里的“Lemon Bread”改名为“LEMON PAN”（柠檬面包）。这样，日本玩家也能认出这个致敬。

source.text: True Lab

translation.text: 真实验室

source.text: Comedy Clash

translation.text: 冷笑话交锋

source.text: Bad jokes can be tricky to localize because they have to fall under a certain threshold to be considered a bad joke, which paradoxically requires comedic ability to achieve

translation.text: 烂笑话也不好翻译：得差到一定程度才算烂笑话，偏偏要做到这一点，也需要幽默功力。

source.text: In an old recording, Torie! and Asgore talk about their new child. Because Tori el is fond of bad jokes, several bad puns appear in this recording.

translation.text: 一段旧录音里，Toriel 和 Asgore 谈起即将到来的孩子。Toriel 爱讲烂笑话，所以这段录音里有好几个冷双关。

source.text: In the first joke, a pun on the English words "mom" and "edamame" was replaced with a Japanese pun on mama ("mom; mama") and mamaredo ("marmalade"):

translation.text: 第一个笑话用 mom（妈妈）和 edamame（毛豆）做双关。日文则改用 mama（妈妈）与 māmaredo（橘子酱）：

source.text: English Text

translation.text: 英文台词

source.text: Japanese Text (roughly translated)

translation.text: 日文台词（大意）

source.text: Toriel: Gorey, dearest. What is my favorite vegetable?

translation.text: Toriel：亲爱的 Gorey，我最喜欢什么蔬菜？

source.text: Toriel: Say, Gorey. What is my favorite type of jam?

translation.text: Toriel：我说 Gorey，我最喜欢什么果酱？

source.text: Asgore: Hmmm ... Carrots, right?

translation.text: Asgore：嗯……胡萝卜，对吧？

source.text: Asgore: Hmm .. Strawberry, right?

translation.text: Asgore：嗯……草莓酱，对吧？

source.text: Toriel: No no no! My FAVORITE vegetable is ... Eda-MOM-e.

translation.text: Toriel：不不不！我最喜欢的蔬菜是……Eda-MOM-e！

source.text: Toriel: Bzz! Too bad! My favorite type of jam is ... "mama"lade!

translation.text: Toriel：答错啦！真可惜！我最喜欢的果酱是……“mama”lade！

source.text: In the second joke, a pun on the English words "mom" and "Pomeranian" was replaced with a Japanese pun on the words mama and amagaeru ("tree frog").

translation.text: 第二个笑话把 mom（妈妈）嵌进 Pomeranian（博美犬）。日文则改用 mama（妈妈）与 amagaeru（树蛙）做双关。

source.text: English Text

translation.text: 英文台词

source.text: Japanese Text (roughly translated)

translation.text: 日文台词（大意）

source.text: Toriel: Now, If I were a dog, what breed of dog would I be?

translation.text: Toriel：那么，假如我是一只狗，会是什么品种？

source.text: Toriel: Now, if I were a frog, what kind of frog would I be?

translation.text: Toriel：那么，假如我是一只青蛙，会是哪一种？

source.text: Asgore: Hmmm ... I don't know, honey. What kind of dog would you be?

translation.text: Asgore：嗯……亲爱的，我不知道。你会是什么狗？

source.text: Asgore: Hmm ... I don't know. What kind of frog would you be?

translation.text: Asgore：嗯……不知道。你会是什么蛙？

source.text: Toriel: I would be ... A MOM ERAN/AN.

translation.text: Toriel：我会是……MOMERANIAN！

source.text: Toriel: A "mama"gaeru.

translation.text: Toriel：“mama”gaeru！

source.text: In the third joke, which is spoken entirely by Asgore, a pun on the English words "mom" and "comedian" was replaced with a Japanese pun on the words mama and mama naranai ("unlikely, impossible"):

translation.text: 第三个笑话全由 Asgore 说出。英文以 mom（妈妈）和 comedian（喜剧演员）做双关，日文改用 mama（妈妈）和 mama naranai（难以做到、无法如愿）：

source.text: English Text

translation.text: 英文台词

source.text: Japanese Text (roughly translated)

translation.text: 日文台词（大意）

source.text: You sure are excited to have this child.

translation.text: 你真是迫不及待想要这个孩子了。

source.text: You really are happy to have this child.

translation.text: 有了这个孩子，你真高兴啊。

source.text: You know, if you keep making jokes like this ..

translation.text: 要是你一直这样讲笑话……

source.text: Honestly, though .. If I keep putting up with your jokes like this ...

translation.text: 不过说真的……要是我一直陪你听这些笑话……

source.text: One day, you could be .. a famous MO Median.

translation.text: 总有一天，你能成为……著名的 MOMedian。

source.text: Any chances of me sleeping will be .. mama naranai.

translation.text: 恐怕连睡觉都……mama naranai。

source.text: As we can see, the various mother-related puns in the English scene were paralleled in Japanese by using completely new jokes with completely new wording.

translation.text: 可以看到，日文用了全新的措辞和笑话，逐一对应英文场景里那些围绕“妈妈”展开的双关。

source.text: Context Extraction

translation.text: 从上下文中提取线索

source.text: The secret lab is equipped with an ominous device known as the "DT Extraction Machine" in English. The player is supposed to deduce that "DT" stands for "Determination".

translation.text: 秘密实验室里有一台不祥的装置，英文名为“DT Extraction Machine”（DT 提取机）。玩家需要自行推断，DT 代表 Determination（决心）。

source.text: Because "determination" was translated as ketsui elsewhere in the Japanese script, this machine was renamed the "KTI Extraction Machine". This peculiar abbreviation comes from how ketsui is spelled in the Japanese script: ケツイ (Ke Tsu I).

translation.text: 日文剧本的其他地方把 determination 译成了 ketsui（决心），因此这台机器也改名为“KTI 提取机”。这个特别的缩写来自游戏里 ketsui 的写法：「ケツイ」（Ke Tsu I），各取一个字母。

source.text: This simple localization change offers another example of how a single localization choice in one part of a script can unexpectedly affect other parts. Such unexpected side effects can easily be missed by machine translation systems, rushed translators using primitive "search-and-replace" tools, or inexperienced translators.

translation.text: 这个简单的改动再次说明，剧本某一处的翻译选择，可能意外影响其他地方。机器翻译、用简陋“查找替换”工具赶工的译者，或经验不足的译者，都很容易漏掉这类连带影响。

source.text: The Dangers of Search-and-Replace in Translation

translation.text: 翻译中查找替换的隐患

source.text: Someone searched for "magic" and replaced most instances with "spell", leading to unintended results like "spellian" instead of "magician" (Game: Yu-Gi-Oh! World Tournament 2004)

translation.text: 有人把大部分 magic（魔法）替换为 spell（咒语），结果连 magician（魔术师）也变成了不存在的“spellian”。（游戏：《游戏王 世界大赛 2004》）

source.text: Someone searched for "youth" at some point and replaced most instances with "kid", which somehow led to phrases like "you think" becoming "kidink" (Game: Ever 17: The Out of Infinity)

translation.text: 有人把大部分 youth（少年）替换成 kid（孩子），不知怎么连 you think（你认为）也变成了“kidink”。（游戏：《Ever 17: The Out of Infinity》）

source.text: In today's computer age, writers regularly rely on automatic spell-checking and search-and-replace tools to fix problematic text. Translators rely on these tools all the time, too. Of course, these tools can actually introduce new problems into a translation if used improperly. This phenomenon is rare, but when it occurs, it can harm the quality of the full, final product.

translation.text: 在电脑时代，作者经常用自动拼写检查、查找替换来修正文稿，译者也一样。不过，使用不当时，这些工具也会给译文引入新问题。这种情况不常见，但一旦发生，就会损害最终成品的整体质量。

source.text: True Lab

translation.text: 真实验室

source.text: Final Battles

translation.text: 最终战斗

pages.title: 最终战斗：再谈 Flowey 的说话方式

source.text: Final Battles

translation.text: 最终战斗

source.text: Unstoppable Human Encounters Last Line of Defense!

translation.text: 势不可挡的人类遇上最后一道防线！

source.text: At last, the main character reaches the barrier that separates the human world from the monster world. The player's choices over the course of the game now steer the player toward several different climactic battles.

translation.text: 主角终于来到分隔人类世界与怪物世界的结界。一路上的选择，将把玩家引向几场截然不同的最终战斗。

source.text: Flowey Speaks Again

translation.text: 再谈 Flowey 的说话方式

source.text: As we've already seen in the Japanese script, Flowey has used the boyish pronoun boku throughout the game so far. For first-time players, boku seems to reflect Flowey's friendly personality at the beginning of the game. However, there's another reason that Flowey uses boku: it turns out that he's actually the king's young son, stuck in the body of a flower.

translation.text: 前面已经看到，日文版的 Flowey 到目前为止一直用带男孩气的第一人称 boku（我）。第一次玩的玩家，会觉得这很符合他在游戏开头表现出的友善性格。不过，还有另一个原因：他其实是国王年幼的儿子，被困在了一朵花的身体里。

source.text: Flowey uses the boyish pronoun ボク (boku) at the start of the game

translation.text: 游戏开头，Flowey 用带男孩气的「ボク」（boku，我）自称。

source.text: Flowey was actually a little boy before he got transformed, so it makes perfect sense for him to keep using boku

translation.text: Flowey 变身前其实是个小男孩，因此一直用 boku完全说得通。

source.text: In Japanese entertainment, it's normal for characters to switch to an aggressive personal pronoun after turning evil or being corrupted by immense power. In this case, however, Flowey continues to use the timid pronoun boku even after becoming a god-like entity:

translation.text: 日本娱乐作品里，角色变坏或被强大力量腐蚀后，常会改用更咄咄逼人的自称。但 Flowey 即使变成近乎神明的存在，也仍用偏温弱的 boku：

source.text: Flowey continues to use boku even when he gets sinister

translation.text: 即使变得阴险，Flowey 仍用 boku。

source.text: Even when he's a terrifying creature of untold power, Flowey keeps using boku

translation.text: 即使化为力量深不可测的恐怖生物，Flowey 仍用 boku。

source.text: Because the Japanese language has a wider variety of personal pronouns than the English language, this unwavering use of boku gives Japanese players an extra layer of insight into Flowey's character that isn't seen in the English script.

translation.text: 日语人称代词比英语丰富得多，因此他始终不变的 boku，也让日本玩家多看见一层英文剧本无法直接体现的性格。

source.text: This scene offers another example of how the localization process can shine light on extra details that were there all along but were otherwise invisible. It's kind of like a microscope or a night-vision camera in that sense. In this chapter, we'll continue to see how pronouns enhance the Japanese dialogue.

translation.text: 这个场景再次说明，本地化能让原本一直存在、却不易察觉的细节显露出来。从这个意义上说，它有点像显微镜或夜视相机。本章还会继续看看，人称代词如何丰富日文台词。

source.text: Attitude Adjustment

translation.text: 态度转变

source.text: When Sans says this out-of-character line during a No Mercy playthrough, he also switches to a very different font and uses proper punctuation

translation.text: Sans 在屠杀路线说出这句一反常态的话时，字体也完全变了，并开始规范使用标点。

source.text: Sans suddenly stops acting like a goofball, turns deadly serious, and begins to speak in an intimidating tone of voice. To preserve this attitude change in the Japanese script, the translator replaced his normal Japanese speech patterns with harsher speech patterns. For example, instead of his usual, laid-back personal pronoun oira, Sans now uses the more assertive pronoun ore. And instead of referring to the main character with the casual second-person pronoun an ta, he now uses the more condescending pronoun omae.

translation.text: Sans 突然收起嬉皮笑脸，变得严肃而可怕，话语里满是威慑。为了保留这种态度转变，译者把他平时的日语说话方式改得更强硬。例如，原本随意的自称 oira（我）换成了更强势的 ore（我）；称呼主角时，也从较随便的 anta（你）变成了更居高临下的 omae（你）。

source.text: Abbreviation Revelation

translation.text: 缩写背后的真相

source.text: Technically, "execution points" were renamed "executor points" in Japanese, but the "EXP" abbreviation still works the same way

translation.text: 严格说来，日文把 execution points（处决点数）改成了 executor points（处决者点数），但缩写仍是 EXP。

source.text: In many role-playing games, the player must earn "EXP" (short for "Experience Points") to increase their "LV" (short for "Level"). These standard terms appear in Undertale too, but it's eventually revealed that "EXP" and "LV" actually stand for "execution points" and "level of violence" here in the Underground.

translation.text: 许多角色扮演游戏中，玩家要积累 EXP（Experience Points，经验值）来提升 LV（Level，等级）。《Undertale》也用了这些常见术语，但最后揭晓：在地下世界里，EXP 和 LV 其实分别代表 execution points（处决点数）和 level of violence（暴力等级）。

source.text: Flowey says "LV" stands for "Love" at the start of the game, but the true meaning of "LV" is only revealed now

translation.text: 游戏开头，Flowey 说 LV 代表 Love（爱）；直到这里，LV 的真正含义才揭晓。

source.text: Because both of these surprise meanings rely on English abbreviations and English spelling, this wordplay would likely be lost in a straightforward, literal translation. To compensate for this, the localization team kept the English words mostly as-is, then included their Japanese meanings afterward for clarification. This solution preserves Toby's original intent without forcing Japanese words to awkwardly fit the English abbreviations.

translation.text: 这两处反转都依赖英语缩写和拼写，直接照字面翻译，很可能丢掉文字游戏。为此，团队基本保留了英文词语，再附上日语解释。这样既保留了 Toby 的意图，也不用勉强拼出能对应英语缩写的日语词。

source.text: Final Battles

translation.text: 最终战斗

source.text: A Bad Time

translation.text: 一段坏时光

source.text: In the translation spreadsheet. Toby labeled this text the "Famous Meme Line Of Game"

translation.text: Toby 在翻译表格里把这句标为“游戏里那句著名的梗台词”。

source.text: Before Sans challenges the murderous main character in battle, he asks:

translation.text: 向杀戮成性的主角发起战斗前，Sans 会问：

source.text: do you wanna have a bad time?

translation.text: do you wanna have a bad time?（想度过一段坏时光吗？）

source.text: Despite his laid-back attitude throughout the game, it turns out that Sans is extremely powerful. In fact, Sans is so difficult to fight that it usually takes players dozens of attempts to defeat him. Sometimes, the battle is so tough that some players just give up entirely.

translation.text: Sans 虽然一路都懒懒散散，实力却极其强大。事实上，他难打到玩家通常要尝试几十次才能取胜。有时战斗太难，甚至有人干脆彻底放弃。

source.text: Players who murder every monster they see are rewarded with one of the most frustrating boss battles of all time

translation.text: 见到怪物就杀的玩家，得到的“奖励”是史上最令人抓狂的头目战之一。

source.text: This battle with Sans is memorable, epic, and frustrating, so his casual question has become one of the most famous lines in the game. As such, "do you wanna have a bad time" has spawned countless English-language fan drawings, videos, and meme images over the years.

translation.text: 这场 Sans 战气势十足、令人难忘，也令人抓狂，于是他这句随口的问话成了游戏最著名的台词之一。多年来，“do you wanna have a bad time”催生了无数英语圈同人画、视频和梗图。

source.text: Naturally, Toby commented on this line's importance and worked with the localization team to get it just right. Because Sans' English line isn't technically a direct threat, the Japanese line needed to achieve a similar "you have to read between the lines" effect. Eventually, the team settled on a relatively straightforward translation:

translation.text: Toby 自然也特地说明了这句的重要性，与本地化团队一同斟酌。严格说来，Sans 的英文台词并非直接威胁，日文也要让玩家自己听出弦外之音。团队最后采用了比较直接的译法：

source.text: omae saiaku na me ni awasaretai ka? (roughly, "do you want to suffer a terrible fate?" or "do you want to have a terrible time?")

translation.text: omae saiaku na me ni awasaretai ka?（大致是“你想遭遇最糟的下场吗？”或“你想尝尝最难熬的滋味吗？”）

source.text: This final Japanese line conveys everything found in the English line, but rolls off the tongue differently. Even so, Japanese fans do quote the line regularly, although it's usually only the saiaku name ("terrible time") portion rather than the full quote itself.

translation.text: 最终的日文传达了英文原句的全部内容，只是读起来的节奏不同。日本粉丝也常引用它，但通常只说 saiaku na me（最糟的遭遇）这一部分，而非整句。

source.text: On Days Like This

translation.text: 在这样的日子里

source.text: Sans suddenly starts speaking with dead eyes, a different font, and proper capitalization

translation.text: Sans 突然双眼空洞，换了一种字体，也开始规范使用大写字母。

source.text: Sans gives a short speech before the battle begins. His speech begins pleasantly enough, but takes a sudden turn at the end:

translation.text: 战斗开始前，Sans 会说一小段话。开头还很和气，末尾却陡然一转：

source.text: it's a beautiful day outside. birds are singing, flowers are blooming. .. on days like these, kids like you ... Should be burning in hell.

translation.text: 外面真是美好的一天。鸟儿歌唱，花儿绽放……在这样的日子里，像你这样的孩子……就该在地狱里焚烧。

source.text: This scene has two important elements to it. First, it contains an "extreme tonal shift", as Toby puts it. Second, the scene is an indirect reference to a popular quote from EarthBound:

translation.text: 这个场景有两个重点。一是 Toby 所说的“语气剧变”。二是它间接引用了《EarthBound》的一句著名台词：

source.text: At times like this, kids like you should be playing Nintendo games.

translation.text: 这种时候，像你这样的孩子就该去玩任天堂游戏。

source.text: To preserve Toby's intentional reference, the localization team replaced the English EarthBound reference with its equivalent Japanese line:

translation.text: 为保留 Toby 有意埋下的典故，团队找来了《EarthBound》对应的日文原句：

source.text: "There's an emergency going on. Kids like you should be playing Nintendo at home or something." (MOTHER 2, 1994)

translation.text: “现在可是紧急时刻。你们这些孩子就该待在家里玩任天堂什么的。”（《MOTHER 2》，1994）

source.text: "At times like this, kids like you should be playing Nintendo games." (EarthBound, 1995)

translation.text: “这种时候，像你这样的孩子就该去玩任天堂游戏。”（《EarthBound》，1995）

source.text: Unfortunately, the original Japanese version of this EarthBound quote is spoken by a cranky, middle-aged police chief with a different speech pattern than Sans', so the translator was forced to adjust the quote to match Sans' character. Thus, Toby's EarthBound reference still lives on in the Japanese script, just in a less recognizable form.

translation.text: 可惜，日文原句是个脾气暴躁的中年警察局长说的，语气和 Sans 不同。译者只好调整措辞，让它符合 Sans 的性格。因此，日文剧本仍保留了 Toby 对《EarthBound》的致敬，只是没那么容易认出来。

source.text: Sans has many intimidating lines during this scene in the game. What's more, most players probably end up seeing this scene dozens of times before defeating Sans. So it's no surprise that this section of the game is where some imprinted fan-translation players criticize the official translation the most, and vice-versa.

translation.text: Sans 在这个场景里有许多气势逼人的台词。多数玩家打败他之前，大概还得看上几十遍。因此，这一段往往是先入为主的民间译本玩家批评官译最多的地方；先接触官译的玩家也会反过来批评民间译本，并不奇怪。

source.text: Final Battles

translation.text: 最终战斗

source.text: Come On and Jam

translation.text: 来尝尝扣篮的滋味

source.text: The phrase "to I> get dunked on" is still new enough that many English speaking players have probably never heard of it before

translation.text: “get dunked on”还是个相当新的说法，许多英语玩家此前可能也没听过。

source.text: If the player can survive against Sans for long enough, Sans will grow visibly exhausted. At this point, the player can choose to spare Sans rather than defeat him. It's all a trick, though - Sans isn't actually tired and will launch a lethal surprise attack upon being spared. On the resulting game over screen, Sans shouts in English:

translation.text: 如果玩家能在 Sans 的攻击下撑得足够久，他就会显得疲惫不堪。这时，玩家可以选择饶恕他，而不是击败他。但这全是圈套：Sans 其实并没累，一被饶恕就会突然发动致命攻击。接着，在游戏结束画面里，他会用英文大喊：

source.text: geeettttttt dunked on!!!

translation.text: geeettttttt dunked on!!!（被——隔扣了吧！！！）

source.text: In basketball, it's humiliating if someone performs a slam dunk over you. Thus the phrase "to be dunked on" is a humorous way of saying "you've been completely dominated" or "you're nothing to me". As it's a relatively new slang phrase and isn't often seen in video games, this surprise appearance adds extra humor to the line.

translation.text: 篮球比赛中，被人隔着自己扣篮很丢脸。因此，“be dunked on”（被隔扣）也成了调侃人的说法，意思是“你被彻底碾压了”或“你在我眼里什么也不是”。这句俚语比较新，在游戏里又不常见，突然冒出来就更好笑了。

source.text: In his the translation spreadsheet, Toby included a note about Sans' "get dunked on" quote:

translation.text: Toby 在翻译表格中，为 Sans 的这句“get dunked on”写了说明：

source.text: '' Famous line, always makes people laugh really hard the first time

translation.text: 名台词，大家第一次看到总会笑得很厉害。

source.text: Getting "dunked on" is humiliating in the human sport of basketball

translation.text: 在人类的篮球运动中，被“隔扣”很丢脸。

source.text: Unfortunately, there's no direct equivalent of the phrase "get dunked on" in Japanese. The localization team cycled through a number of potential Japanese replacements, most of which were variations on "ha, I fooled you" or insults based on Internet slang. Nothing quite had the same "bite" as the original English quote, however.

translation.text: 可惜，日语没有直接对应“get dunked on”的说法。团队尝试了好几个替代方案，多半是“哈，被我骗了吧”的各种变体，或来自网络用语的嘲讽。但都没有英文原句那股损劲儿。

source.text: As the project neared completion, Toby worked with the localization team to finally solve this conundrum. At Toby's suggestion, the team dropped Sans' English quote entirely and replaced it with something different but still suitable:

translation.text: 项目临近完成时，Toby 和团队终于解决了这个难题。按照 Toby 的建议，他们完全舍弃英文原句，换成意思不同、但同样合适的一句：

source.text: Huh? You died? That's weird. All I did was try to hug you ...

translation.text: 咦？你死了？奇怪，我只是想抱抱你啊……

source.text: Even though this new line uses completely different wording to say something completely different, the reward is still the same for the player: a funny, memorable insult after a humiliating defeat.

translation.text: 新台词的措辞与内容都完全变了，玩家得到的效果却一样：惨遭羞辱性失败后，又听到一句好笑、难忘的嘲讽。

source.text: Incidentally, when translators and creators work together like this to invent something new, some professional circles refer to the process as "transcreation" rather than "localization".

translation.text: 顺带一提，译者和创作者像这样一起构思新内容，有些专业领域会称之为“创译”（transcreation），而不只是“本地化”。

source.text: English-speaking fans sometimes draw Sans dunking on the main character in a basketball game

translation.text: 英语圈粉丝有时会画 Sans 打篮球、隔着主角扣篮的场景。

source.text: Because Sans' line is completely different in the Japanese release, Japanese fans sometimes draw Sans hugging the main character to death instead

translation.text: 日版的台词完全不同，于是日本粉丝有时会改画 Sans 把主角抱死的场景。

source.text: Final Battles

translation.text: 最终战斗

source.text: Losing Over and Over

translation.text: 输了一次又一次

source.text: Sans is so powerful that he literally counts how many times he defeats the player. He uses this information to taunt the player with number-related jokes after each defeat. aturally, some of these jokes needed to be changed to make sense in Japanese.

translation.text: Sans 强大到还会专门数自己击败玩家的次数。每次获胜，他都会拿次数开玩笑，嘲讽玩家。其中一些笑话自然需要改动，才能在日语里说得通。

source.text: Three Losses

translation.text: 输三次

source.text: I don't th ink I've ever • used the word "thrice" in a normal, everyday English conversation. Have you?

translation.text: 我好像从没在普通英语日常对话里用过 thrice（三次）。你用过吗？

source.text: If the player speaks to Sans after losing three times, he says in English:

translation.text: 玩家输掉三次后再与 Sans 对话，他在英文里会说：

source.text: hey, what comes after "thrice," anyway?

translation.text: 喂，话说“thrice”（三次）再往后该怎么说？

source.text: The joke here is that the English word "thrice" is rarely ever used. Because this cultural joke would be lost in a literal translation, the quote was rephrased as:

translation.text: 笑点在于，thrice 这个英语词本来就很少用。照字面翻译会丢掉这种语言文化背景，因此日文改成了：

source.text: i guess the third time isn't always the charm.

translation.text: 看来第三次也未必能成啊。

source.text: To replicate the dry humor of the English line, the translator included a joke on a Japanese idiom that's equivalent to the phrase "the third time's the charm".

translation.text: 为再现原句的冷幽默，译者拿一句日语惯用语开了玩笑；它的意思相当于英语的“the third time’s the charm”（第三次就能成功）。

source.text: Four Losses

translation.text: 输四次

source.text: Four is an unlucky • number in Japanese because "four" and "death" can both be pronounced shi

translation.text: 在日本，四被视为不吉利的数字，因为“四”和“死”都可以读作 shi。

source.text: After the player loses four times in a row, Sans tries to figure out a fancy English word for "four times":

translation.text: 玩家连输四次后，Sans 试着给“四次”找一个文绉绉的英语说法：

source.text: quice? frice? welp, won't have to use it again anyways.

translation.text: quice？frice？（仿照 thrice 现编的“四次”。）算了，反正也不会再用到了。

source.text: Because this joke would be lost in translation, Toby provided a replacement line based on Japanese superstition about the number four:

translation.text: 这个笑话无法直接移植，Toby 便依据日本对“四”的忌讳提供了一句替代台词：

source.text: they say four is an unlucky number, you know. want to see ifi t's true or not?

translation.text: 听说四是个不吉利的数字。想验证一下吗？

source.text: Seven Losses

translation.text: 输七次

source.text: Pachinko is kind of like that Plinko game on The Price Is Right, but with bright lights and sounds to keep your brain addicted

translation.text: 柏青哥有点像《The Price Is Right》里的 Plinko 弹珠游戏，但配上了让人上瘾的闪亮灯光和音效。

source.text: Sans eventually makes a joke about seven being a lucky number:

translation.text: 随后，Sans 会拿幸运数字七开玩笑：

source.text: who knows, maybe you'll hit the jackpot and that number will multiply tenfold.

translation.text: 谁知道呢，说不定你会中大奖，让这个数字翻上十倍。

source.text: Seven is a lucky number in Japan too, so this line stayed similar in Japanese:

translation.text: 七在日本也是幸运数字，所以日文保留了类似的说法：

source.text: who knows, maybe you can get into "fever mode" and turn it into 70.

translation.text: 谁知道呢，说不定会进入“狂热模式”，变成七十次。

source.text: In the original English line, Sans refers to Western-style slot machines. In the Japanese line, he instead refers to Japanese pachinko and pachinko-related gambling machines.

translation.text: 英文原句说的是西式老虎机，日文则改为日本的柏青哥及相关赌博机。

source.text: Hitting the "fever mode" in a pachinko game usually activates various multipliers, bonuses, or payouts for a short time

translation.text: 柏青哥进入“狂热模式”后，通常会在短时间内触发各种倍率、奖励或出球收益。

source.text: Rough Romance

translation.text: 失意的感情

source.text: After Undyne learns that Torie! and Asgore were once married, she says:

translation.text: Undyne 得知 Toriel 和 Asgore 曾经结过婚后，说：

source.text: Hey ASGORE, is that your ex? Jeez. That's rough, buddy.

translation.text: 嘿，ASGORE，那是你前妻？哎，老兄，真够惨的。

source.text: Toby noted that this line is a direct quote from Avatar: The Last Airbender, an American animated series that debuted in 2005. Specifically, the quote comes from this scene:

translation.text: Toby 说明，这句直接引用了 2005 年开播的美国动画《降世神通：最后的气宗》，具体出自下面这段对话：

source.text: Sokka: My first girlfriend turned into the moon.

translation.text: Sokka：我的初恋女友变成了月亮。

source.text: Zuko: That's rough, buddy.

translation.text: Zuko：That’s rough, buddy.（老兄，真够惨的。）

source.text: This line became a popular Internet meme in English-speaking locales but not so much in Japan

translation.text: 这句话在英语圈成了热门网络梗，在日本却没那么出名。

source.text: The ridiculousness of this scene transformed "that's rough, buddy" into a popular Internet meme in the late 2000s. However, because this quote isn't as well-known in Japan, Toby asked the team to prioritize the content of Undyne's text over the need to retain the reference.

translation.text: 这段对话荒诞得让“that’s rough, buddy”在 2000 年代末成了热门网络梗。但日本玩家未必熟悉，所以 Toby 请团队优先传达 Undyne 台词的内容，不必强求保留典故。

source.text: Final Battles

translation.text: 最终战斗

source.text: Temporary Arrangement

translation.text: 一度采用的重排名字

source.text: Books and schools usually only prep you to translate old historical novels and stuff, not bad-guy anagrams

translation.text: 书本和学校通常只教你怎么翻译历史小说之类的东西，可不会教你怎么翻反派名字里的字母重排。

source.text: It turns out that Torie! and Asgore once had a kindhearted child named Asriel. But through a series of tragic events, Asriel was transformed into the wrathful Flowey. Now, near the end of the game, Asriel gains immense, godlike power - enough for him to destroy everything and everyone for good.

translation.text: 原来，Toriel 和 Asgore 曾有个心地善良的孩子，名叫 Asriel。一连串悲剧却把他变成了满怀怨恨的 Flowey。如今游戏将近结尾，Asriel 获得了近乎神明的强大力量，足以彻底摧毁一切。

source.text: As Asgore's son, Asriel's full name is "Asriel Dreemur". Keen-eyed players have noticed that "Asriel Dreemur" is an anagram of"Serial Murderer", and Toby has confirmed that this was intentional:

translation.text: 作为 Asgore 的儿子，Asriel 全名是“Asriel Dreemurr”。细心的玩家发现，把这些字母重新排列，就会得到“Serial Murderer”（连环杀人犯）。Toby 也确认，这是刻意设计的：

source.text: Toby's fondness for anagrams continues to reveal itself

translation.text: Toby 对字母重排的喜爱，又一次显露出来。

source.text: To preserve this hidden aspect of Asriel’s character, the localization team considered giving Asriel a new Japanese name with a similarly frightening anagram. Thus, in early drafts of the Japanese script, Asriel Dreemur was named アシリル・ラーキ (Ashiriru Rāki, roughly "Aseril Lerki"), which could be rearranged to spell シリアル・キラー (shiriaru kirā, "serial killer").

translation.text: 为了保留 Asriel 隐藏的这一面，团队曾考虑替他另取一个日文名字，同样暗藏骇人的重排结果。因此，日文早期草稿曾用「アシリル・ラーキ」（Ashiriru Rāki，约相当于“Aseril Lerki”），可以重排成「シリアル・キラー」（shiriaru kirā，连环杀手）。

source.text: Dots are sometimes used in Japanese to separate parts of names

translation.text: 日语有时会用间隔号分开姓名的不同部分。

source.text: This localization choice offered two benefits: it retained the murderous anagram, and it kept the first name roughly similar in both languages.

translation.text: 这个方案有两个好处：既保留了暗示杀人的重排，也让两种语言里的名字大致相近。

source.text: Of course, this localization choice had downsides too: players in Japan would know this important character by a very different last name, and the name Riiki doesn't evoke the same whimsical feeling that "Dreemur" does. More importantly, however, Toby chose the name "Asriel" with two other special meanings in mind:

translation.text: 但它也有缺点：日本玩家会以一个完全不同的姓氏认识这位重要角色，而 Rāki 也没有“Dreemurr”那种梦幻感。更重要的是，Toby 取名“Asriel”时，还考虑了另外两层特殊含义：

source.text: "Asriel" is a reference to Azrael, the mythological angel of death

translation.text: • “Asriel”呼应神话中的死亡天使 Azrael。

source.text: "Asriel" is a combination of the names "Asgore" and "Torie]"

translation.text: • “Asriel”由“Asgore”和“Toriel”两个名字组合而成。

source.text: Everyone agreed that localizing "Asriel Dreemur" into a Japanese anagram brought more downsides than benefits. For this reason, the localization team dropped the anagrnm aspect of Asriel's name and kept his name in line with his original English name.

translation.text: 大家一致认为，为“Asriel Dreemurr”另造日语重排名字弊大于利。因此，团队放弃了这一层文字游戏，让日文名与原来的英文名保持一致。

source.text: Asriel Speaks

translation.text: Asriel 的说话方式

source.text: During the big, final battle, Asriel speaks with strong conviction and disgust for the main character. To replicate this in Japanese, the translator gave Asriel a disrespectful speech pattern which includes the use of the assertive personal pronoun ore.

translation.text: 在最后的大战中，Asriel 说话非常笃定，对主角满怀厌恶。为在日语中再现这种感觉，译者让他采用无礼的语气，包括使用强势的第一人称 ore（我）。

source.text: In addition to using the first-person pronoun ore, Asriel uses the rude pronoun omae to say "you"

translation.text: 除了用 ore自称，Asriel 还用不客气的 omae 来称呼“你”。

source.text: Little by little, though, the player is able to chip away at Asriel's hatred. Eventually, Asriel begins to speak with hesitation and less confidence. This is then followed by strong regret and shame for his actions.

translation.text: 不过，玩家逐渐瓦解了 Asriel 的仇恨。他开始迟疑，不再那么自信，随后又对自己的行为深感懊悔和羞愧。

source.text: The translator paralleled this emotional change in Japanese by easing up on the disrespectful speech patterns. As part of this, Asriel eventually switches his personal pronoun to boku, which conveys a more innocent image befitting a scared young boy.

translation.text: 译者也在日文中逐步缓和无礼的语气，呼应这种情感变化。Asriel 最后改用 boku（我）自称，呈现出更天真、符合受惊小男孩的形象。

source.text: Asriel switches to using boku to refer to himself, and the more familiar pronoun kimi to say "you"

translation.text: Asriel 改用 boku自称，并用较亲近的 kimi 来称呼“你”。

source.text: Because the original English text didn't include any such pronoun changes at all, it's clear that the translator viewed Asriel's dialogue through Asriel's eyes when translating his text, much as an actor might slip into their character's mindset before performing a scene.

translation.text: 英文原文没有这些代词变化，可见译者翻译时是从 Asriel 自己的视角理解台词的，就像演员上场前先进入角色的心境。

source.text: Final Battles

translation.text: 最终战斗

source.text: Monument to Pre-Existence

translation.text: 向前作致敬

source.text: Without a high level of • cooperation between creator and localizer, references can easily be lost in translation

translation.text: 创作者与本地化人员如果缺乏密切合作，典故就很容易在翻译中丢失。

source.text: Asriel unleashes a powerful attack known as "Hyper Goner" in English. Toby noted that this is a reference to the final battle in Final Fantasy VI, in which the godlike villain uses his ultimate attack - known as "Goner" in English - when his defeat draws near. Toby also noted that it wasn't important to retain this reference in the Japanese script - he only asked that the Japanese name for "Hyper Goner" should sound "extremely powerful and cool".

translation.text: Asriel 会使出英文名为“Hyper Goner”的强力攻击。Toby 说明，这致敬的是《最终幻想 VI》的最终战：近乎神明的反派即将落败时，会使出英文名为“Goner”（意为“完蛋的人”）的终极攻击。Toby 也说，日文不一定要保留这个典故，只要求“Hyper Goner”的日文名听起来“强得不得了，而且很酷”。

source.text: The "Goner" attack in • Final Fantasy VI was originally known as "Missing" in Japanese

translation.text: 《最终幻想 VI》的“Goner”在日文原版里叫“Missing”（消失）。

source.text: Although it was unnecessary, the localizers did preserve this classic Final Fantasy reference. But because "Goner" was known in Japanese as "Missing", Asriel's "Hyper Goner" was localized into Japanese as "Hyper Missing".

translation.text: 虽然不是硬性要求，团队还是保留了这处对经典《最终幻想》的致敬。但因为“Goner”在日文里叫“Missing”，Asriel 的“Hyper Goner”便译成了“Hyper Missing”（超级消失）。

source.text: Umm ...

Perhaps I should set these depressing topics aside and share a Japanese recipe instead. One of the best down-home recipes in Japan is Japanese curry. It's basically a warm, hearty stew with vegetables or meat or anything else, but with a rich, mouthwatering flavor. I want it to finally be popular where I'm from, so I hope you'll try making some sometime!

translation.text: 或许该把这些沉重话题放一放，分享一道日本菜谱。日式咖喱是日本最棒的家常菜之一：把蔬菜、肉或其他食材炖成热腾腾、料足的浓汤，味道醇厚，叫人垂涎。我希望它也能在我的家乡流行起来，所以希望你有空也试着做一锅！

source.text: Find Japanese curry blocks at your local store and then drop them in any soup or stew

translation.text: 在当地商店找些日式咖喱块，放进汤或炖菜里就行。

source.text: Japanese curry is even better with steak, mashed potatoes, dipping bread, and/or rice!

translation.text: 日式咖喱配牛排、土豆泥、蘸汁面包或米饭，都更好吃！

source.text: Double Refusion

translation.text: 拒绝与重新融合

source.text: Again, we see Toby's fondness for phrases with extra meanings that are difficult to retain in translation

translation.text: 又一次看出 Toby 喜欢给短语藏上额外含义，而这些含义往往很难在翻译中保留。

source.text: Normally, if the player is defeated during battle, the character's soul - represented as a red heart - shatters into pieces. This is then followed by a standard game over screen:

translation.text: 通常，玩家在战斗中落败后，角色的灵魂——一颗红心——会碎成许多片，接着出现普通的游戏结束画面：

source.text: Upon defeat, the main character's soul is surrounded by darkness

translation.text: 落败后，主角的灵魂被黑暗包围。

source.text: The soul breaks apart and shatters

translation.text: 灵魂裂开，碎散。

source.text: The game over screen appears

translation.text: 出现游戏结束画面。

source.text: If Asriel defeats the main character in battle, this same heart-shattering scene plays out again. But instead of going to the usual game over screen, the heart pieces recombine and a new message appears:

translation.text: 主角被 Asriel 击败时，同样会出现心碎的画面。但接下来没有进入通常的游戏结束界面，红心碎片反而重新聚合，并出现一条新消息：

source.text: But it refused.

translation.text: But it refused.（但它拒绝了。）

source.text: Toby explained that this short sentence carries two separate meanings:

translation.text: Toby 解释，这句短话包含两层意思：

source.text: 1. "Refused" can mean "refused to die"

translation.text: 1. refused 意为“拒绝”，这里即“拒绝死亡”。

source.text: 2. "Refused" can mean "re-fused", referring to how the heart fragments fuse back together again

translation.text: 2. refused 也可拆成 re-fused（重新融合），呼应红心碎片再次聚合。

source.text: Toby understood that this pun would probably be difficult to retain in Japanese, so he noted that Meaning #l was more important to preserve. As a result, this line was given a straightforward to translation in early versions of the Japanese script:

translation.text: Toby 知道这个双关在日语中大概很难保留，因此说明第一层意思更重要。早期日文剧本便采用了直接的译法：

source.text: But the SOUL couldn't be broken.

translation.text: 但灵魂无法被击碎。

source.text: After some more internal discussion, the localization team switched the line from an outside narrator's explanation to a first-person exclamation:

translation.text: 经过进一步内部讨论，团队把旁观叙述者的解释，改成了第一人称的呼喊：

source.text: No! I won't be broken!

translation.text: 不！我才不会被击碎！

source.text: This Japanese wording - combined with the first-person perspective - evokes the sense of holding on to strong resolve against all odds, which is a common "final battle" theme in classic Japanese RPGs. Thus, the final Japanese line uses very different grammar and wording to parallel the meaning and intent of the original English line.

translation.text: 这套日语措辞配合第一人称视角，唤起了一种不论多大逆境也要坚持到底的决心，正是经典日式角色扮演游戏最终战中常见的主题。最终日文虽然采用了很不一样的语法与措辞，却对应了英文原句的含义和意图。

source.text: Final Battles

translation.text: 最终战斗

source.text: Multiple Saves

translation.text: SAVE 的多重含义

source.text: It's revealed that whoever has the most "determination" in the Underground is able to use the in-game save menu functions. In other words, the most determined person in the Underground can freely load and save their progress. This is what allows the player to save and load their progress, just like in any other game. Except here, it's the actual, physical player's determination that enables this ability. The main character is just along for the ride.

translation.text: 游戏揭晓，地下世界中“决心”最强的存在，能够使用存档菜单。换句话说，此人可以自由保存、读取进度。这也是玩家能像玩其他游戏一样存读档的原因；区别在于，这次赋予能力的是现实中玩家本人的决心，主角只是随之行动。

source.text: Toby begins by using "save" in a noun-like way related to computers

translation.text: Toby 起初把 save 用作与电脑相关的名词，指存档。

source.text: During this final battle, Asriel absorbs and corrupts the souls of Sans, Papyrus, Undyne, and every other important story character. With all this new power, Asriel immobilizes the main character and takes control over the save menu. This becomes clear when the player reaches out for the save file, only to fail.

translation.text: 这场最终战中，Asriel 吸收并扭曲了 Sans、Papyrus、Undyne 以及其他重要角色的灵魂。获得这些力量后，他让主角动弹不得，也夺走了存档菜单的控制权。玩家伸手试图触及存档却失败时，这一点便显露出来。

source.text: Toby switches to using "save" as a verb and with a very different meaning

translation.text: 随后，Toby 把 save 改作动词，意义也大不相同：拯救。

source.text: After the player fails to reach the save file a second time, the game offers a hint about focusing on saving the characters whose souls have been absorbed:

translation.text: 玩家第二次试图触及存档又失败后，游戏提示玩家转而拯救那些灵魂被吸收的角色：

source.text: You tried to reach your SAVE file. Nothing happened. You tried again to reach your SAVE file. Nothing happened.

translation.text: 你试图触及自己的 SAVE 文件（存档）。什么也没有发生。你再次试图触及自己的 SAVE 文件。什么也没有发生。

source.text: But. .. Maybe, with what little power you have. .. You can SAVE something else.

translation.text: 但是……也许，凭你仅剩的一点力量……你可以 SAVE（拯救）别的什么。

source.text: As we can see, the English word "save" in this scene carries multiple meanings:

translation.text: 可见，这里的英语词 save 承担了好几层含义：

source.text: "Save" is used to refer to the player's save file and the ability to load it

translation.text: • 指玩家的存档，以及读取存档的能力。

source.text: "Save" is used to mean "give salvation to someone's soul"

translation.text: • 指“救赎某人的灵魂”。

source.text: "Save" is used to mean "to physically rescue someone"

translation.text: • 指实际“救出某个人”。

source.text: Toby and the localization team spent a lot of time on preserving this wordplay in Japanese. After trying a number of solutions, the team settled on using the Japanese wordfukkatsu in place of"save". In general,fukkatsu means "to revive" or "to restore", but it can also be used to mean "to restore/load a saved file" and "to restore something back to how it should be".

translation.text: Toby 和本地化团队花了很多时间，试图在日语里保住这个文字游戏。尝试多种方案后，团队决定用日语 fukkatsu 替代 save。fukkatsu 通常表示“复活”或“恢复”，也可以用来表示“恢复／读取存档”以及“让事物恢复应有的状态”。

source.text: A new menu icon had ~ to be created to work properly with the new Japanese wording of this scene

translation.text: 为了配合这个场景的新日语措辞，还得制作一个新的菜单图标。

pages.title: SAVE 的翻译与后续影响

source.text: Although the choice to replace "save" withft1kkatsll solved most of the wordplay issues, it also slightly altered the logic of the scene. To compensate for this change, the team added an extra line that bridges the jump from "save" to ft1kkatst1. Thus, the final Japanese scene became:

translation.text: 用 fukkatsu（复活、恢复）替换 save，虽然解决了大部分文字游戏问题，却也稍稍改变了场景逻辑。团队因此补上一句，衔接从“存档”到“恢复”的转折。最终日文场景变成了：

source.text: Yot1 reached for yol.lr save file. Bllt nothing happened. Yot1 reached for yow· save file again. Nothing happened. It appears yol.1 can't restore yow· save file after all.

translation.text: 你向自己的存档伸出手。却什么也没有发生。你再次向存档伸出手。什么也没有发生。看来，终究无法恢复存档。

source.text: Bt1t ... Ify ol.1 gather what little power yol.1 have left ... Maybe yoll CAN restore something else.

translation.text: 但是……如果聚起你剩下的那一点力量……也许可以恢复别的什么。

source.text: This creative localization choice allowed the Japanese scene to approximate the wordplay in the original English scene. This choice did create new issues to be tackled, however:

translation.text: 这个有创意的方案，让日文场景接近了英文原场景的文字游戏。不过，它也带来了新问题：

source.text: 1. The in-game "SAVE" icon needed to be redrawn to say ft1kkatStl in Japanese

translation.text: 1. 游戏中的“SAVE”图标需要重画，改成日语 fukkatsu（复活）。

source.text: 2. The new icon needed extra programming to load properly based on the player's chosen language

translation.text: 2. 要额外编写程序，让新图标按玩家所选语言正确加载。

source.text: 3. Dropping the word "SAVE" from the scene broke the connection to "SAVE the World", the official English title of this scene's background music track

translation.text: 3. 场景中不再出现“SAVE”后，也就失去了与背景音乐官方英文曲名“SAVE the World”（拯救世界）的联系。

source.text: The localization team easily fixed the first two issues. The third issue came into play a year after Undertale's Japanese release, when the game's official soundtrack was set to be released in Japan. Because this track is so iconic and memorable, Toby requested that the Japanese soundtrack retain the "SAVE the World" name as-is rather than replace it with a less memorable pun onfukkatsl.1.

translation.text: 前两个问题很容易解决。第三个问题，则在《Undertale》日版推出一年后、官方原声带准备在日本发行时显现出来。因为这首曲子太有代表性、太令人难忘，Toby 要求日版原声带原样保留“SAVE the World”，不要换成一个不如原名好记的 fukkatsu 双关。

source.text: Every choice you ever make as a translator or localizer has the potential to bite you in the butt years later in unexpected ways

translation.text: 译者或本地化人员做出的每个选择，都可能几年后以意想不到的方式反过来给自己找麻烦。

source.text: Final Battles

translation.text: 最终战斗

source.text: Ending

translation.text: 结局

source.text: Ending

translation.text: 结局

source.text: Human Victorious! Underground Beholds New Under-Tale!

translation.text: 人类获胜！地下世界迎来新的“地下传说”！

source.text: At last, the main character reaches the end of the journey. All that lies ahead is freedom, destruction, delight, or death. The Underground's final fate rests in the player's hands.

translation.text: 主角终于走到旅程终点。前方可能是自由、毁灭、喜悦，也可能是死亡。地下世界最终的命运，就掌握在玩家手中。

source.text: In Big Trouble Now

translation.text: 这下惹麻烦了

source.text: Reader Challenge #10: Come up with three alternatives from your region that could replace "go to your room!"

translation.text: 读者挑战 #10：想出你所在地区的三种说法，替换“回你房间去！”

source.text: Undyne jokingly pretends to be Papyrus' mother. She scolds him in English by saying:

translation.text: Undyne 开玩笑扮演 Papyrus 的妈妈。在英文中，她训斥道：

source.text: Don't talk back to me like that! Go to your room, Papyrus!

translation.text: 不许这样顶嘴！回你房间去，Papyrus！

source.text: In some English-speaking cultures, it's common for parents to punish their children by sending them to their room. This punishment is less common in Japan, however, so Undyne gives Papyrus a slightly different punishment in Japanese:

translation.text: 在一些英语文化中，家长常用“回房间去”来惩罚孩子。但日本不太常用这种处罚，因此日文里的 Undyne 给 Papyrus 换了个稍有不同的惩罚：

source.text: Don't give me that back-talk! Go to your room and sit down seiza-style!

translation.text: 不许顶嘴！回房间正坐去！

source.text: In Japanese, seiza refers to a formal sitting style in which a person kneels on the floor, sits back on their heels, and pushes the tops of their feet fiat on the ground.

translation.text: 日语 seiza（正坐）是一种正式坐姿：双膝跪地，臀部坐在脚跟上，脚背平贴地面。

source.text: Sending a kid to their room is a common punishment in some Western cultures

translation.text: 在一些西方文化中，让孩子回房间是常见的处罚。

source.text: Sitting seiza-style for a while can be so painful that the Japanese government recently passed a law declaring it a "morally unacceptable form of punishment"

translation.text: 长时间正坐会疼痛难忍，以至于本书写作时，日本政府不久前通过法律，将其认定为“道德上不可接受的惩罚方式”。

source.text: Because this posture limits blood circulation and compresses nerves in the legs, sitting seiza-style becomes painful after a short time. This is why the seiza sitting style is sometimes used as a punishment for misbehaving children.

translation.text: 这种姿势会影响腿部血液循环、压迫神经，因此正坐一会儿就会疼。这也是它有时被用来惩罚不听话的孩子的原因。

source.text: Banding Together

translation.text: 一起组乐队

source.text: Now that I think about it, the "CHITEI NO OWARI" name nicely fits the context of nearing the end of Underta/e

translation.text: 现在想想，“CHITEI NO OWARI”（地下世界的终结）还挺契合《Undertale》即将结束的情境。

source.text: In the English script, Torie! sends the main character a bad joke via text message:

translation.text: 英文剧本中，Toriel 发短信给主角，讲了一个烂笑话：

source.text: If Sans and I started a band, do you know what we could call it? "Dreemurr" and "Femur." L-0-L! PS - That is only a joke. Do not refer to me as Dreenmrr

translation.text: 如果我和 Sans 组个乐队，你知道可以叫什么吗？“Dreemurr and Femur”（Dreemurr 与股骨）。笑—死—啦！附言：只是开玩笑。别叫我 Dreemurr。

source.text: The joke here is that Toriel's last name, "Dreemurr", rhymes with "Femur", which is a type oflarge bone. This joke would be lost in a literal translation into Japanese, so the translator replaced it with something new:

translation.text: 笑点在于，Toriel 的姓 Dreemurr 和 femur（股骨，一种大骨头）押韵。直译成日文就没了笑点，因此译者换了个新笑话：

source.text: If Sans and I started a band, what do you think its name would be? "CHITEI NO OWARI'' LOL! PS - I'm thinking of having Sans be our DJ.

translation.text: 如果我和 Sans 组个乐队，你觉得会叫什么？“CHITEI NO OWARI”（地下世界的终结）。哈哈哈！附言：我想让 Sans 当我们的 DJ。

source.text: The name "CHITEI NO OWARI" ("End of the Underground"), is a reference to "SEKAI NO OWARI" ("End of the World"), a Japanese band that achieved incredible popularity in the 2010s. In this way, the untranslatable joke of the original text was replaced with a comedic reference to a real-life band.

translation.text: “CHITEI NO OWARI”（地下世界的终结）是在致敬日本乐队“SEKAI NO OWARI”（世界末日）；这支乐队在 2010 年代大受欢迎。原本无法直译的笑话，就这样换成了对现实乐队的幽默引用。

source.text: This small change in this small line has resulted in an unexpected side effect: Japanese fans now associate Sans with being a DJ. So while English-speaking fans might draw Sans playing musical instruments as part of"Dreemur and Femur", Japanese fans often portray him as the DJ for "CHITEI NO OWARI".

translation.text: 这一小句里的小改动，产生了意想不到的影响：日本粉丝开始把 Sans 与 DJ 联系起来。因此，英语圈粉丝可能会画他作为“Dreemurr and Femur”的成员演奏乐器，日本粉丝却常把他画成“CHITEI NO OWARI”的 DJ。

source.text: Say hello to the members of SEKAI NO OWARI

translation.text: 来认识一下 SEKAI NO OWARI 的成员们。

source.text: LEFT: An illustration of "Dreemur and Femur" by an American fan

translation.text: 左：美国粉丝画的“Dreemurr and Femur”。

source.text: RIGHT: An illustration of "CHITEI NO OWARI" by a Japanese fan

translation.text: 右：日本粉丝画的“CHITEI NO OWARI”。

source.text: Ending

translation.text: 结局

source.text: Playing with Fire

translation.text: 玩火

source.text: Incidentally, Japanese ~ people love to cook Japanese-style "curry rice" over campfires, it's like the default camping meal - try it sometime!

translation.text: 顺带一提，日本人很爱用营火煮日式咖喱饭，几乎是露营的标配。不妨试试！

source.text: In the Core, a creepy monster explains its fondness for a creepy pit of fire:

translation.text: 核心区一个阴森的怪物，说起自己为何喜欢那口阴森的火坑：

source.text: Now it is my special place. It is nice for cooking s'mores and things like that.

translation.text: 现在它是我的专属地方了。很适合做 s’mores（烤棉花糖巧克力夹心饼）之类的东西。

source.text: Cooking s'mores over a campfire is a common tradition in some English speaking regions. This practice isn't as widespread in Japan, however, so the reference to s'mores was altered slightly:

translation.text: 在一些英语地区，用篝火做 s’mores 是常见传统。日本却没那么普遍，因此这处稍作了调整：

source.text: Traditional s'mores are made with graham crackers, chocolate, and marshmallow toasted over a campfire

translation.text: 传统的 s’mores 用全麦饼干、巧克力，以及在篝火上烤过的棉花糖制成。

source.text: It's a special place to me now. It's perfect for roasting marshmallows and stuff like that.

translation.text: 现在它对我来说是个特别的地方。用来烤棉花糖什么的，再合适不过了。

source.text: As we can see, the s'mores reference was replaced with a reference to roasting marshmallows over a campfire, which is a more common practice in Japan.

translation.text: 可见，原文的 s’mores 被换成了日本更常见的篝火烤棉花糖。

source.text: Jokes in Reserve

translation.text: “预订”好的笑话

source.text: The localization ~ team turned this untranslatable English pun into a Japanese joke that hits three goals simultaneously

translation.text: 团队把这个无法直译的英语双关，换成了一个同时达到三个目的的日语笑话。

source.text: The monsters in the Underground are now free to venture out into the human world. Back at the MTT Hotel, a reservation-obsessed receptionist says in English:

translation.text: 地下世界的怪物终于能自由前往人类世界。MTT 酒店那个满脑子都是预订的前台接待员，在英文中说：

source.text: Now we can live life without reservations.

translation.text: Now we can live life without reservations.（现在我们能毫无顾虑／无需预订地生活了。）

source.text: This line is a pun on the phrase "without reservations", which normally means "without any worries" but also means "without making advance arrangements" in this case. Because this English pun would be lost in a literal translation, the localization team replaced it with a Japanese pun on the words yōyaku ("finally") and yoyaku ("reservations; advance arrangements"):

translation.text: without reservations 通常表示“毫无顾虑”，在这里又指“不必提前预订”。这个英语双关无法直译，团队便换成日语 yōyaku（终于）与 yoyaku（预订）的近音双关：

source.text: We can finally go wherever we want without needing reservations.

translation.text: 我们终于（yōyaku）可以不必预订（yoyaku），想去哪儿就去哪儿了。

source.text: This new line accomplishes three things: it conveys the surface-level information of the original line, it parallels the wordplay of the original line, and it preserves this character's uniqueness as the hotel's "annoying reservation guy".

translation.text: 新台词一举三得：传达了原句表面的信息，再现了原句的文字游戏，也保住了这个“烦人的预订接待员”的独特性格。

source.text: Dual Core

translation.text: 双重“核心”

source.text: I wonder how many times apples have come up in this book so far

translation.text: 不知道本书到这里，苹果已经出现多少次了。

source.text: A construction monster in the Core laments his luck. In English, he says:

translation.text: 核心区一个搞建设的怪物，感叹自己运气不佳。英文中他说：

source.text: So, if we're leaving, will my job. .. ? Ugh, and I just got a raise! Well, guess every apple has its CORE, heheh.

translation.text: 所以，大家都要走了，我的工作会……？唉，我才刚加薪啊！算了，看来每个苹果都有它的 CORE（果核／核心），嘿嘿。

source.text: This final sentence uses figurative speech that means "all good things have a downside" or "you gotta take the good with the bad". The line also contains a pun on the phrase "apple core" and the place known as the "Core".

translation.text: 最后一句是个比喻，意思是“好事也有不如意的一面”，或“有好有坏，都得接受”。同时，apple core（苹果核）与地名 Core（核心）又构成了双关。

source.text: Because the Japanese language has its own word for apple cores, the wordplay in this line would be lost in a straightforward translation. To compensate, the translator replaced the apple core pun with something completely new:

translation.text: 日语另有表示“苹果核”的词，直接翻译便无法保留这层文字游戏。译者于是把苹果核双关换成了全新的说法：

source.text: If everyone's going to the surface world, what'll happen to my job ... ? Ugh! And I just got a pay raise, too! Boy, life sure is hardCORE. Heheheh.

translation.text: 如果大家都去地表，我的工作怎么办……？唉！我才刚加薪啊！人生真是 hardCORE（艰难／硬“核”）啊，嘿嘿嘿。

source.text: This new line closely parallels the original line in content and intent: the monster reluctantly accepts his situation while making a pun about his old job.

translation.text: 新台词的内容和意图都紧贴原文：怪物无奈接受现状，同时拿自己原来的工作地点开了个双关玩笑。

source.text: Small Business Donor

translation.text: 小生意的大赞助者

source.text: For reference, you need to spend over 100 Gold to get this message

translation.text: 供你参考：花费超过 100 金币才会触发这条消息。

source.text: Muffet thanks the player for spending so much money at her bake sales throughout the game:

translation.text: Muffet 感谢玩家一路上在她的糕点义卖中花了那么多钱：

source.text: It's all because ofy ou (r money).

translation.text:
It’s all because of you
(r money).
全都多亏了你（的钱）。

source.text: To make this spelling joke work in Japanese, the translator first gave the line a literal translation. Because this pushed the "(r money") part to the middle of the sentence instead of the end, the localization programmer then modified the game to display "(r money)" in its own tiny font. The result looks different from the original English line, but achieves a similar, comical effect.

translation.text: 原文把 you（你）接成 your money（你的钱）。为了让这个拼写笑话在日文中奏效，译者先照字面翻译。但“的钱”因此被挪到句子中间，不再位于句末。本地化程序员于是修改游戏，专门用极小的字体显示括号里的这部分。结果看起来与英文不同，却产生了相近的滑稽效果。

source.text: Ending

translation.text: 结局

source.text: Fashion Statement

translation.text: 时尚宣言

source.text: Ice Wolf also speaks ._ with fragmented Japanese grammar to mimic the phrasing of Ice Wolf's English dialogue

translation.text: Ice Wolf 的日语语法也断断续续，模仿了英文台词的措辞。

source.text: A monster named Ice Wolf is glad to finally have a break from throwing ice cubes all day as a job:

translation.text: 名叫 Ice Wolf 的怪物终于不用整天扔冰块，能歇一歇了，非常高兴：

source.text: Ice Wolf can take a break to buy some pants now. Ice Wolf thinking ofc hanging their name to Jimmy Hotpants.

translation.text: Ice Wolf 现在可以休息，去买裤子。Ice Wolf 考虑改名叫 Jimmy Hotpants（热裤 Jimmy）。

source.text: The name "Jimmy Hotpants" comes from a personal experience Toby had during a game of laser tag. Apparently, the top scorer at one point was named "Jimmy Hotpants", and the name was so ridiculous that it stuck with Toby long after.

translation.text: “Jimmy Hotpants”这个名字来自 Toby 玩镭射对战时的一次亲身经历。据说当时积分榜第一名就叫这个名字。它实在太荒唐，Toby 很久以后还记得。

source.text: In laser tag, you shoot light guns at other players and hope they don't shoot you first

translation.text: 镭射对战中，你用光枪射击其他玩家，同时希望他们别先射中你。

source.text: The name "Jimmy Hotpants" evokes the image of very short shorts like these

translation.text: “Jimmy Hotpants”让人想到这样短得不能再短的热裤。

source.text: The name "Jimmy Zubonski" evokes the image of ordinary, full-length pants

translation.text: “Jimmy Zubonski”让人想到普通的长裤。

source.text: The ridiculous sound and associated imagery of the name "Jimmy Hotpants" would be dulled in a literal transcription into Japanese. As such, the translator altered the name to "Jimmy Zubonski", which contains three levels of wordplay:

translation.text: 把“Jimmy Hotpants”直接音译成日语，会削弱它荒唐的音感与联想。译者于是改为“Jimmy Zubonski”，其中有三层文字游戏：

source.text: "Jimmy Zubonski" sounds like a plausible, real-life Russian name

translation.text: • “Jimmy Zubonski”听起来像个现实中可能存在的俄国人名。

source.text: "Zubonski" is a play on the Japanese word zubon ("pants")

translation.text: • Zubonski 里包含日语 zubon（裤子）。

source.text: "Zubonski" is also a play on the Japanese word suki ("to like; to love")

translation.text: • Zubonski 也呼应日语 suki（喜欢、喜爱）。

source.text: In this way, the Japanese version of this line preserves the original joke in tone and humor. At the same time, it arguably surpasses the humor of the original line.

translation.text: 这样，日文保住了原句的语气和幽默，甚至可以说更好笑。

source.text: On a mostly unrelated topic, a rare practice in localization is something I call "reverse localization". As an example, let's pretend you're translating a Japanese game into English. But instead of translating like normal, imagine that what you're looking at is actually a Japanese translation of something that was originally in English. It's then your job to get as close to that "original" text as possible. Naturally, this requires an incredible amount of experience and skill to accomplish successfully.

translation.text: 说个基本不相干的话题：本地化里有种少见的做法，我称为“反向本地化”。例如，你在把一款日本游戏译成英文，却不按通常思路翻译，而是假想眼前的日文原本就是从英文译来的。你的任务就是尽可能还原那个假想的“英文原文”。要做好这件事，自然需要极丰富的经验与技巧。

source.text: Clawful Cattitude

translation.text: 猫咪不好惹

source.text: Random trivia: I've noticed my cats tend to boop their noses on people as a way to say "Hey. You."

translation.text: 随手冷知识：我发现自家的猫常用鼻子碰人，像是在说：“喂，你。”

source.text: A secret monster named Mad Mew Mew appears in the Nintendo Switch version of Undertale. Mad Mew Mew is a catgirl doll possessed by the spirit of a revengeful enemy named Mad Dummy. During the game's ending credits, Mad Mew Mew's name is accompanied by the phrase:

translation.text: 《Undertale》的 Nintendo Switch 版里，有个隐藏怪物 Mad Mew Mew。她是一个猫娘玩偶，被满心复仇的敌人 Mad Dummy 的灵魂附身。游戏片尾名单里，她的名字旁配着一句：

source.text: Furiosity Wills The Cat

translation.text: Furiosity Wills The Cat（怒气驱动了猫）。

source.text: This line is a two-pronged play on the English proverb "curiosity killed the cat". It contains a comical rhyme on the classic proverb, and it points to the fact that Mad Mew Mew has been possessed by the spirit of Mad Dummy.

translation.text: 这句话从两处改写了英语谚语“curiosity killed the cat”（好奇心害死猫）：用怒气的 Furiosity 换掉好奇心 curiosity，用驱使的 wills 换掉害死的 killed。它既俏皮地呼应原谚语的音韵，也点出了 Mad Mew Mew 被 Mad Dummy 的灵魂附身。

source.text: Because this English wordplay would be lost in a straightforward translation into Japanese, the translator replaced it with something completely different:

translation.text: 把这个英语文字游戏直译成日语就会失效，因此译者换成了完全不同的表达：

source.text: namennayo

translation.text: namennayo（别小看我／别惹我）。

source.text: In this situation, namennayo could be translated as "don't screw with me" - it's the sort of thing you'd hear from a tough guy about to start a fight. The phrase comes from the word nameru, which can mean "to belittle" in some contexts and "to lick" in more ordinary situations. This line is also a reference to namennayo, a slogan of the Nameneko brand of cat-related entertainment.

translation.text: 在这里，namennayo 可以译作“别惹我”，像是硬汉动手前会放的话。它来自 nameru：在一些语境中意为“小看”，通常又表示“舔”。这句话还引用了猫主题娱乐品牌 Nameneko 的口号 namennayo。

source.text: Overview of Nameneko

translation.text: Nameneko 简介

source.text: In the early 1980s, a Japanese photographer became famous for his photos of cats acting like tough ruffians. These photos exploded in popularity and were packaged into books and merchandise under the Nameneko brand name. The Nameneko fad was so big that the brand was even released internationally, under names like "Pelorian" and "Don't Pelorian".

translation.text: 20 世纪 80 年代初，日本一位摄影师因拍摄装扮成凶悍不良少年的猫而出名。这些照片迅速走红，以 Nameneko 品牌推出图书与周边。热潮甚至传到国外，品牌以“Pelorian”“Don’t Pelorian”等名称发行。

source.text: I couldn't get the rights to any Nameneko photographs, so please enjoy these illustrated badass kitties instead

translation.text: 我没能取得 Nameneko 照片的使用权，请欣赏这些画出来的凶猫吧。

source.text: Ending

translation.text: 结局

source.text: Final Thoughts

translation.text: 结语

pages.title: 结语：关于翻译与本地化的收获

source.text: Final Thoughts

translation.text: 结语

source.text: Top-notch localization work can be hard to come by, so it's heartening to see an indie game like Undertale receive such lavish treatment

translation.text: 顶尖的本地化并不常见，看到《Undertale》这样的独立游戏获得如此用心的待遇，令人欣慰。

source.text: Over the past 240 pages or so, we've looked at the history behind Underta/e's localization and its official Japanese release. We've studied the changes that were made during the localization process, why those changes were made, and how those changes affected the player's experience.

translation.text: 在前面约 240 页中，我们回顾了《Undertale》本地化及官方日版背后的历史，研究了本地化过程中作出的改动、改动的原因，以及它们如何影响玩家体验。

source.text: We've also seen how culture and language are so closely tied together that sometimes a literal translation just isn't possible. We've examined how a single localization choice can affect the gameplay experience in surprising ways. And we've seen examples of how a localized piece of text can improve or surpass the original text. This look at Underta/e's English-to-Japanese localization has been a real learning experience.

translation.text: 我们也看到，文化与语言紧密相连，有时根本无法直译；一个本地化选择，也可能出乎意料地改变游戏体验。还有一些例子表明，译后的文字可以改进甚至超越原文。研究《Undertale》的英译日本地化，确实让人学到很多。

source.text: What We've Learned About Translation and Localization

translation.text: 我们对翻译与本地化有了哪些认识

source.text: In addition to learning about Underta/e's localization, we've learned a lot about translation and localization in general. Some key discoveries include:

translation.text: 除了《Undertale》本身，我们也进一步认识了翻译与本地化的一般规律。几个要点是：

source.text: Translation isn't simply replacing all the words in one language with all the words in another - it involves intent, figurative meaning, functional meaning, emotional impact, cultural background, artistic nuance, and more

translation.text: • 翻译不只是把一种语言的所有词换成另一种语言的词。它还涉及意图、比喻意义、实际功能、情感效果、文化背景、艺术韵味等。

source.text: When something will otherwise be lost in a literal or straightforward translation, localization can preserve the original intent for the target audience

translation.text: • 当直译无法传达某些内容时，本地化能为目标受众保留原作的意图。

source.text: Different forms of translation have different limitations - games, for example, have technical, computer-related limitations that sometimes affect the final product, just as movie subtitles must be short and simple enough to be read in the time allotted

translation.text: • 不同形式的翻译有不同限制。例如，游戏会受电脑和技术条件影响；电影字幕则必须足够简短易读，让观众能在规定时间内看完。

source.text: Translation also involves psychological biases like "imprinting" and notions that a translation can only ever be inferior to the source material

translation.text: • 翻译也涉及心理偏见，比如“先入为主”，或认定译文必然不如原文。

source.text: Translation theory is very different from translation reality - every translation decision has its own unique challenges with unique solutions

translation.text: • 翻译理论与实际操作差别很大。每个翻译选择都有独特的难题，也需要相应的解决办法。

source.text: I guess all of this is a fancy-pants way of saying that translation isn't black and white at all - it's more like red and green and yellow and smurple, all stuck together with melted bubble gum, motor oil, and that ball of tangled wires you keep in a box somewhere. Even so, a good translator can navigate the mess and make things work.

translation.text: 说了这么多，其实就是：翻译绝不是非黑即白。它更像红、绿、黄，再加上胡编的“什紫色”，被融化的泡泡糖、机油，还有你塞在某个盒子里的那团乱电线黏在一起。即便如此，优秀的译者依然能从这团乱麻中理出头绪，让作品顺利运转。

source.text: What I've Learned

translation.text: 我的收获

source.text: Although I was only on the sidelines during most of Underta/e's English-to Japanese localization, watching everything come together was an enlightening experience for me. I learned just as much while writing this book too.

translation.text: 《Undertale》从英文译成日文的过程中，我多数时候只是旁观者，但亲眼看着一切逐渐成形，仍让我大受启发。写这本书时，我也学到了同样多的东西。

source.text: My biggest challenge was finding a way to explain Underta/e's English-to Japanese translation for readers who know nothing about Undertale, video games, translation, the Japanese language, or Japanese culture. Packaging all of these complex topics in a clear, understandable way took so long that I basically ended up rewriting this book twice over the course of several years.

translation.text: 最大的挑战，是如何向完全不了解《Undertale》、电子游戏、翻译、日语或日本文化的读者，解释它的英译日。把这些复杂主题讲得清楚易懂，耗费了很长时间；几年下来，我基本把整本书重写了两遍。

source.text: Anyway, looking back now, it feels like I just finished taking and finished teaching a two-semester university course on media translation. Hopefully this look at Underta/e's localization has been educational and entertaining for you, too.

translation.text: 现在回头看，感觉像是刚上完、也刚教完一门持续两个学期的大学媒体翻译课。希望这次对《Undertale》本地化的考察，也让你有所收获，读得开心。

source.text: I also had to devise my own writing style guide, which I'll call the "Legends of Localization Style", or "LoL Style" for short. You basically ignore other style guides and just do whatever makes the most sense for your situation - but try to remain consistent throughout.

translation.text: 我还得自己制定写作规范，姑且叫它“Legends of Localization Style”，简称“LoL Style”。基本原则就是：先不管其他规范，按当前情况选最合理的做法，但尽量全书保持一致。

source.text: Loose Thoughts

translation.text: 零散感想

source.text: There were many other topics I had hoped to cover in this book, but could never find quite the right place to put them. So here are a few other points of interest if you've come this far:

translation.text: 原本还有许多话题想写进本书，却一直找不到合适的位置。既然你已经读到这里，就再补充几点：

source.text: Think of localization as redrawing an existing painting, but with different tools - it's like if you tried to redraw the Mona Lisa with crayons or markers instead of paint. You could do a really good job, but it's still going to be different in the end, no matter what

translation.text: • 可以把本地化想成换一种工具重画现有的画。比如不用颜料，而用蜡笔或马克笔重画《蒙娜丽莎》。你可能画得非常好，但无论如何，最终都不会一模一样。

source.text: Because most localization choices are essentially personal choices, and because different target audiences usually have different expectations, it's probably not possible for a "perfect, universal localization" to exist

translation.text: • 大多数本地化选择说到底是个人选择，不同目标受众的期待通常也不同，因此“完美、放之四海而皆准的本地化”大概并不存在。

source.text: I've only covered a hundred or so Undertale localization changes in this book, but there were actually thousands of other, smaller localization issues that had to be solved. Had I covered every localization issue at my usual level of detail, this book would be about 18,000 pages long and weigh approximately 128 pounds (56 kilograms)

translation.text: • 本书只谈了《Undertale》的一百多处本地化改动，实际还解决了成千上万个更小的问题。假如每个问题都按我惯常的细致程度来讲，这本书大约会有 18,000 页，重约 128 磅（56 千克）。

source.text: If you're fixated on only one or two lines in a full-scale localization, keep in mind you're probably only looking at like 0.01% of the entire thing

translation.text: • 如果你只盯着一部完整译作中的一两句，别忘了，你看到的可能只有全貌的 0.01%。

source.text: Note that "entertainment Japanese" is quite different from "real-life Japanese" and shouldn't be used in real life unless you know what you're doing

translation.text: • “娱乐作品里的日语”和“现实中的日语”很不一样。除非清楚自己在做什么，否则别直接搬到现实里用。

source.text: It could be fun to make a Japanese version of this book, but it would probably be a bit different, as I'd need to explain American culture everywhere instead of Japanese culture

translation.text: • 给本书做个日文版也许很有趣，但内容大概会有些变化：我得处处解释美国文化，而非日本文化。

source.text: I'm pretty sure I did the math right

translation.text: 我相当确定，自己没算错。

source.text: Final Thoughts

translation.text: 结语

source.text: Legacy

translation.text: 延续下去的影响

source.text: As we've seen, Underta/e's Japanese localization has impressed Japanese players, game developers, and critics alike. The localization's success has even inspired others to follow Toby's path of turning a simple hobby into a full fledged career, much as EarthBound's Japanese-to-English localization did for Toby nearly thirty years ago. Games are usually localized to make money, but now we're seeing how localization can start a cycle of inspiration that crosses the language barrier.

translation.text: 我们已经看到，《Undertale》的日文本地化赢得了日本玩家、开发者与评论者的赞赏。它的成功甚至鼓舞了其他人，让他们沿着 Toby 的道路，把普通爱好变成正式事业——正如近三十年前，《EarthBound》的日译英曾启发 Toby 一样。游戏本地化通常为了赚钱，但现在我们也看到了，它如何开启跨越语言障碍、不断传递灵感的循环。

source.text: Surprisingly, the legacy of Underta/e's localization doesn't end here. Undertale continues to grow and change as Toby adds new content, which 8-4 continues to localize into Japanese. Toby and 8-4 also continue to collaborate with the Japanese game industry and the Japanese fan community long after Underta/e's Japanese release. They're also working more closely than ever on new projects like Deltarune, Toby's latest game creation.

translation.text: 令人惊喜的是，这份影响并未止步于此。Toby 不断为《Undertale》添加新内容，8-4 继续将其本地化为日语。日版发行很久以后，Toby 和 8-4 仍与日本游戏业及粉丝社区保持合作。他们也在 Toby 的新作《Deltarune》等项目上，比以往合作得更加紧密。

source.text: In short, the teamwork that Toby and 8-4 developed during Underta/e's localization has transformed their basic business relationship into something greater: a genuine bond of friendship and trust.

translation.text: 《Undertale》本地化过程中培养的默契，让 Toby 与 8-4 的关系超出了普通商业合作，成为建立在友谊与信任上的纽带。

source.text: "Suck moss if you want water" was mistranslated as "Even moss drinks water" in Illusion of Gaia

translation.text: 《Illusion of Gaia》把“想喝水就吸吮苔藓”误译成了“连苔藓也喝水”。

source.text: The English version of this Deltarune line includes an indirect reference to a memorable mistranslation in the classic Japanese RPG, Illusion of Gaia. This reference would be lost on most Japanese Deltarune players, however, so the localization team gave the line a straightforward translation that still conveys the content and mood of the English line

translation.text: 《Deltarune》这句英文间接引用了经典日式角色扮演游戏《Illusion of Gaia》中的那处著名误译。多数日本玩家认不出这个典故，团队便直接翻译，仍保留英文台词的内容与气氛。

source.text: Lancer has a unique "ho ho ho" laugh in both the English and Japanese scripts. In English, "ho ho ho" is closely associated with Santa Claus' laugh, but in Japanese, "ho ho ho" is more closely associated with the laughter of snooty rich ladies. As such, Lancer is compared to Santa Claus in the English script and a snooty old hag in the Japanese script

translation.text: Lancer 在英日两版里都发出独特的“ho ho ho”笑声。英语里，这让人想到圣诞老人；日语里，却更像傲慢贵妇的笑声。因此，英文把 Lancer 比作圣诞老人，日文则说他像个装腔作势的老太婆。

source.text: The Power of Three

translation.text: 三的力量

source.text: In the world of Underta/e, important things come in threes. The monsters, the humans, and the player. The three members of the Dreemur family. The three entities vying for control of the main character's body. Three main story routes. Three triangles in the Delta Rune. And so on.

translation.text: 在《Undertale》的世界里，重要的事物常常以三为一组：怪物、人类和玩家；Dreemurr 家的三位成员；争夺主角身体控制权的三个存在；三条主要故事路线；Delta Rune 中的三个三角形，等等。

source.text: As I finish this book, I now see that the number three is important in localization too. Specifically, I see that there are three sides to any successful localization: the creator's side, the localizer's side, and the audience's side. Without all three sides, the final localization will be flawed, incomplete, or meaningless. If even one side is weak, the final localization will feel weak too. But if all three sides are present and solid, the resulting localization will shine brightly. I believe this holds true not just for games, but for any form of artistic transformation.

translation.text: 写到本书结尾，我发现“三”在本地化中也很重要。一次成功的本地化需要三方：创作者、本地化人员和受众。缺了任何一方，最终的本地化就会有缺陷、不完整，甚至失去意义。即使只有一方薄弱，成品也会显得薄弱。但如果三方齐备、各自扎实，最终的本地化就能大放异彩。我相信，这不仅适用于游戏，也适用于任何形式的艺术转化。

source.text: If you've read the entire book all the way through, then I sincerely thank you and congratulate you

translation.text: 如果你从头到尾读完了这本书，我由衷地感谢你，也向你道一声恭喜！

source.text: On occasion, I'll finish a lengthy localization analysis with some sort of final score or rating. I don't think that would be appropriate this time, given my personal involvement with the project. Instead, I'll just say that all three sides of Underta/e's Japanese localization are solid: the localization team brought experience and passion, Toby brought care and excitement, and the players brought support and respect. Without a doubt, Underta/e's Japanese localization is filled with DETERMINATION.

translation.text: 有时，我会在一篇长篇本地化分析的末尾给出评分或评价。但这次我亲自参与了项目，觉得这样做不太合适。我只想说，《Undertale》日语本地化的三方都很扎实：本地化团队带来了经验与热情，Toby 带来了用心与兴奋，玩家带来了支持与尊重。毫无疑问，《Undertale》的日语本地化充满了决心。

source.text: Your Turn

translation.text: 轮到你了

source.text: On a final note, I leave you two challenges before you close this book.

translation.text: 最后，在你合上这本书之前，我想留给你两道挑战。

source.text: First, why do you think it's called "localization" and not something else like "globalization", "regionalization", or "culturalization"? Is there a better name that would work instead? The term "localization" is still relatively new and in flux, so who knows, maybe it'll go by a different name someday.

translation.text: 第一，你觉得为什么叫“本地化”（localization），不叫“全球化”（globalization）、“地区化”（regionalization）或“文化化”（culturalization）？有没有更合适的名称？“本地化”这个术语还比较新，也在变化。谁知道呢，说不定将来会换个名字。

source.text: My second challenge to you is this: the next time you watch your favorite movie, read your favorite book, or listen to your favorite music, keep an eye out for things that would be lost in a straightforward, literal translation into another language. Then come up with a way to localize it somehow. Think of it as a game. Or a bad time. Nyehehe!

translation.text: 第二道挑战是：下次看你最喜欢的电影、读你最喜欢的书，或听你最喜欢的音乐时，留意哪些东西会在直白、逐字的外语翻译中丢失，再想办法把它们本地化。把这当成一场游戏吧。也可能是一段苦日子。捏嘿嘿！

source.text: But seriously, if you do come across any cool localization changes in a game or whatever, share it sometime. I live for this stuff, and I'm always looking for more legends of localization!

translation.text: 不过说真的，如果你在游戏或其他作品中发现了有趣的本地化改动，不妨分享出来。我就靠这些东西活着，也一直在寻找更多本地化传奇！
